If an EAID is not found, the officer shall take reasonable steps to notify a sponsor of the description and sex of the cat, and if available, the address or location where the cat was trapped. The sponsor shall then take all appropriate and available steps to identify the feral cat colony caretaker of the cat or a feral cat colony caretaker who will take responsibility for managing the cat.

If the feral cat colony caretaker is not able to immediately take custody of the cat, the officer shall transport the cat to MACC. The feral cat colony caretaker shall be responsible for retrieving the cat from the shelter within three (3) business days or advising the shelter if he or she does not intend to retrieve the cat; no fees will be charged for cats reclaimed within three (3) business days. In all other cases normal impound and kennel fees apply.

MACC, its designee, or a licensed veterinarian, in accordance with this title shall be the only persons permitted to destroy a feral cat. No person may knowingly cause physical harm to or cause the destruction by any means of a feral cat. The only exception will be by written permit from the Minnesota Department of Agriculture or the Minnesota Department of Health for the purpose of controlling diseases transmissible to humans or other animals and only when all other methods and means have been exhausted. Such a permit shall name a person or persons conducting the activities, specify the items and products to be used, give the boundaries of the area involved and specify the precautionary measures to be employed to ensure the safety of humans and other animals. Any drugs used for the euthanasia shall be administered by or under the direction of a licensed veterinarian. (Ord. No. 2016-009, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Enforcement
children.text:
(a) MACC or its designee, in order to encourage the stabilization and reduction of the feral cat population in the City of Minneapolis, shall have, in addition to any other rights and powers provided pursuant to this Code, state statute or applicable law, the powers enumerated in this section.

(1) MACC is authorized to trap in a humane manner and remove any feral cats that:

a. Have not been vaccinated against rabies or which are demonstrating signs of the disease.

b. Are not spayed or neutered.

c. Have bitten or injured a person or domestic pet.

d. Are not identifiable through an EAID as belonging to a feral cat colony that has a sponsor and a feral cat colony caretaker.

e. Belong to a colony that is illegally being managed within one-half (½) mile of the edge of any public lands encompassing a creek, river or body of water of six (6) acres or more in size.

f. Pose any other public health or public safety concerns.

g. If no issue of public health or safety exists, or if any issues of public health and safety can be addressed by the removal and relocation of the cat to another area, a sponsor may arrange to have the cat spayed or neutered, eartipped, and vaccinated against rabies by a licensed veterinarian, and have an EAID inserted. The sponsor may then arrange for the cat to be adopted or placed in a feral cat colony.

h. If a feral cat is demonstrating signs of having rabies, or has an illness or injury that presents an imminent danger to the public health or safety, or to its own person, the cat shall be humanely destroyed.

(2) MACC is authorized to direct that a sponsor remove a feral cat that is creating a nuisance or harm if the sponsor has failed to adequately resolve the issue within thirty (30) days (or such shorter time period as MACC may specify) after being given written notice thereof. In the event that MACC directs the sponsor to remove the cat, the sponsor shall have thirty (30) days (or a shorter period as MACC may specify) to do so. Failure of the sponsor to remove the cat within said time period as specified shall constitute grounds for MACC to remove the cat and/or remove the sponsor as a registered sponsor.

(b) Animal control officers or police officers shall investigate any nuisance or harm complaint allegedly caused by a feral cat.

(1) In the event that an animal control officer or police officer finds that a feral cat or feral cat colony has created a nuisance or harm, the animal control officer or police officer shall advise the sponsor in writing of the issue.

(2) The sponsor shall have the right to review the matter with MACC or MACC's designee. If the sponsor is not able to satisfy MACC or MACC's designee that the nuisance or other violation has not or is not occurring, the sponsor shall have thirty (30) days (or shorter time period as MACC may specify) to comply with the direction with respect to correcting the issue. If the sponsor fails to correct the issue, MACC shall have the right to remove the cat and/or remove the sponsor as a registered sponsor.

(c) If a sponsor fails to perform its responsibilities under this chapter, MACC may notify the sponsor that it must comply with the requirements of this chapter within thirty (30) days. If the sponsor fails to do so or repeatedly fails to comply with the requirements of this chapter, MACC may remove the sponsor from being a registered sponsor, and may reassign the feral cat colonies from the sponsor to another approved sponsor.

(d) If a feral cat colony caretaker regularly fails to comply with the requirements of this chapter, the sponsor may notify the feral cat colony caretaker that he or she has thirty (30) days to make all reasonable efforts to fulfill the responsibilities of this chapter. If the feral cat colony caretaker fails to comply within that time period or has received more than one (1) notification, the sponsor shall remove approval for the person from being a feral cat colony caretaker and may identify and obtain replacement feral cat colony caretakers for the feral cat colonies of the noncompliant feral cat colony caretaker. If no other feral cat colony caretaker can be found within thirty (30) days, the sponsor shall notify MACC and MACC may humanely remove all, or portions of, the feral cat colonies and dispose of them in accordance with this title.

(e) Any sponsor or feral cat colony caretaker that has been removed from being a registered sponsor or removed as an approved feral cat colony caretaker due to noncompliance issues shall not be allowed to be a sponsor or a feral cat colony caretaker for one (1) year from the date of their removal.

(f) Feral cats that were spayed or neutered and vaccinated for rabies prior to the commencement of the city's feral cat colony program, but did not have an EAID inserted or were marked as feral by some indication other than an eartip, such as but not limited to a tattoo, shall be deemed to be in compliance with this chapter if all other requirements are being met by their feral cat colony caretaker. Feral cat colony caretakers shall take all appropriate and available steps to bring these cats into compliance with the provisions of this article within three (3) years of its enactment or upon revaccination of the cats for rabies, whichever comes first. (Ord. No. 2016-009, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Abandonment of feral cats prohibited
children.text: No person having the care, custody, and control of any feral cats shall abandon said animals anywhere in the city, nor introduce said animals from outside the city into an existing feral cat colony inside the city. (Ord. No. 2016-009, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: In general
children.text: Title 5 of the Minneapolis Code of Ordinances shall be known and cited as the Minneapolis Building Code and shall apply to all parts of the city. The Minneapolis Code of Ordinances shall hereinafter be referred to as 'this Code'. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: State code adopted
children.text: The Minnesota State Building Code, hereinafter referred to as 'the building code', as adopted by the Department of Labor and Industry pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Chapter 326B including all of the amendments, rules and regulations established, adopted and published from time to time by the Department of Labor and Industry, through the Construction Codes and Licensing Division is hereby adopted by reference as if fully set out herein with the exception of the optional chapters, unless specifically adopted by this chapter. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Administration and application
children.text: The agency charged with the administration and application of Title 5 of this Code shall be under the direction of the Minnesota Certified Building Official designated by the city pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Section 326B.133 and Minn. Rule Part 1300.0090. References to the building official in Title 5 shall mean the building official or authorized representative(s). (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Compliance with the Minneapolis Building Code
children.text: All persons or entities shall comply with the requirements of Title 5, the other requirements of this Code, and the policies and procedures established by the city. The building official shall have the authority to modify requirements of Title 5 of this Code when public safety or other unforeseen circumstances require it. If activities regulated by Title 5 impact other operations of the city, the building official shall work in conjunction with other departments or divisions of the city to ensure compliance with all requirements of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Exemption from the Minneapolis Building Code
children.text: The building official shall determine exemption from Title 5 requirements pursuant to federal and state laws and this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permits
children.text:
The administration and issuance of permits shall be pursuant to Title 5 of this Code. For purposes of Title 5, a reference to a permit shall include documents issued as a license or other format in the land management system. All permits regulated by Title 5 shall be under the authority of the building official unless otherwise stated. In addition to the permit requirements in the building code, the following shall apply:

(1) If work authorized by a permit has not commenced within one hundred eighty (180) days of the date of permit issuance or has been stopped or abandoned for any consecutive one hundred eighty (180) day period, the permit shall be invalid. Work shall be considered stopped or abandoned if the permit applicant has not requested a required inspection, and the city has not performed such an inspection during any consecutive one hundred eighty (180) day period. Abandoned work that is determined to be a nuisance condition shall be subject to the applicable requirements of Minnesota State Statutes and this Code.

(2) An application for a permit to perform work to a building subject to the authority of the Minneapolis Heritage Preservation Commission shall be reviewed by the preservation and design staff prior to permit issuance except in situations where public safety is a concern as determined by the building official. The preservation and design review shall be completed within the time needed to complete the building code plan review for the purposes of issuing a building permit.

(3) No permit shall be issued pursuant to Title 5 for work to be done to a building subject to the requirements of Chapter 249 of this Code unless the permit is for performing work required by this Code, wrecking of the structure, or as otherwise required by the building official.

(4) No permit shall be issued pursuant to Title 5 for work to be done to a building that is required to obtain a certificate of code compliance as required by Chapter 87, Article II of this Code unless the permit is for work required by this Code, wrecking of the structure, or as otherwise required by the building official.

(5) No permit shall be issued for work that is already covered by a valid permit unless the permit is to satisfy the requirements of an order or as otherwise required by the building official.

(6) Permits are issued based on the assumption that the applicant has the necessary knowledge and skill to perform the work. The building official may require proof of the applicant's ability to perform the work prior to issuance of the permit. After a permit has been issued, if it is determined that an applicant does not have the necessary knowledge and skill to perform the work, the building official may require the permit applicant to hire someone with the necessary knowledge and skill to complete the work or revoke the permit and require a new permit be issued to someone with the necessary knowledge and skill.

(7) When a permit is not required by Title 5 and circumstances exist that require that a permit be issued, the building official shall have authority to require such permit.

(8) Permits are subject to cancellation due to any violation of statutes, rules, laws, or requirements of this Code.

(9) Work authorized by a permit shall not proceed beyond the scope of the permit. Work that exceeds the scope of a permit shall be considered unpermitted work and may be subject to an investigation/penalty fee pursuant to sections 91.1010 and 91.1020 of this Code. Subsequent permits may be obtained for additional work to be performed.

(10) Permits and requirements administered by other departments or divisions of the city may be required in addition to the permits and requirements in Title 5. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Licensing
children.text: When so required pursuant to applicable state statutes, rules, and this Code, permits shall only be issued to persons or entities properly licensed to perform the work. Licensing shall include state licenses and city licenses and certificates of competency. City issued licenses and certificates of competency shall be pursuant to Chapters 85 and 278 of this Code. All required licenses shall be obtained prior to any work being performed. No person or entity shall knowingly allow unlicensed persons or entities to perform work that requires a license or allow unlicensed persons or entities to perform work under their license. Violations of licensing requirements shall be deemed sufficient cause for the revocation of any city license or certificate issued. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: License exemption
children.text: An owner of a single-family detached or single-family attached dwelling may apply for permits to perform work on the dwelling they reside in without complying with the licensing and/or certificate of competency requirements in this Code. The exemption shall apply provided there exists legally established property lines separating the dwelling from any other habitable dwelling and where utility services on the subject property including but not limited to electric, gas, water, and sewer are not shared with any other habitable dwelling. If an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) exists on the property the owner may perform work on the dwelling or ADU and be exempt from licensing and certificate of competency requirements so long as the owner resides in the dwelling or ADU. If circumstances exist that require an owner to temporarily vacate the dwelling or ADU to perform the work they can still obtain permits and be entitled to the license exemption. Any person or company hired by the owner to perform work under the owner's permit shall possess the appropriate licenses and certifications for the type of work being performed. The license exemption shall not apply to gas work for environmental burners as defined in Chapter 278 of this Code. Exemption from state contractor licenses shall be pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Section 326B.805. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fees
children.text: Title 5 fees shall be pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Violations
children.text: Non-conformance with the provisions of Title 5 and other provisions of this Code shall be considered a violation pursuant to section 59.90 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Inspections
children.text: Pursuant to Title 5 of this Code, the building official may enter, examine, and survey at all reasonable times all premises after obtaining consent from an occupant or owner of the premises. In the event an occupant or owner of the premises does not consent to entry by the building official, and if there is probable cause to believe that an inspection is warranted, then application may be made to the court for an administrative or other search warrant for the purposes of inspecting the premises. Conditions that may be a violation of Title 5 that are visible from public property or public way shall be subject to investigation and may result in required corrective action by the owner. The cost of inspector time to perform inspections shall be covered by the permit fees charged except for other fees noted in Chapter 91 or when no permit is required, the fee for such inspections shall be as stated in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Orders and correction notices
children.text:
Orders and correction notices issued due to an inspection, investigation, complaint, or other process shall be complied with as stated in the order or notice.

Non-compliance with an order or notice shall be considered a violation pursuant to section 59.90 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Certificate of occupancy
children.text:
A certificate of occupancy shall be issued pursuant to the building code. No building or structure requiring a certificate of occupancy shall be occupied before issuance of the certificate of occupancy without the approval of the building official.

A temporary certificate of occupancy may be issued pursuant to Minn. Rule Part 1300.0220. A fee shall apply as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Building code appeals process
children.text: Any person aggrieved by a decision of building code requirements shall have the right to appeal the decision to the building official. The appeal shall be made on a form provided by the city and shall include any necessary supporting materials. Appeals shall be submitted pursuant to procedures established by the city. The building official shall hear all appeals related to the building code. The building official shall only make decisions relative to the suitability of alternate materials, methods of construction, or interpretation of the building code. Exceptions or variances to the building code are not permitted. Anyone aggrieved by a decision of the building official pursuant to this section shall have the right to appeal to the state appeals board as described in Minn. Rules Chapter 1300. For appeals that do not meet the submittal requirements of the state appeals board the decision of the building official shall be final. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Encroachment upon or projection into other property
children.text: Except for utility connections, no portion of any structure shall encroach upon or project into any adjacent property separated by legally established property or easement lines including but not limited to a street, alley, or park without approval of the adjoining property owner and the city. Encroachments and projections shall be pursuant to the requirements of Chapter 95 and Title 17 of this Code and the Minn. State Building Code, Chapter 33 of the International Building Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Structure maintenance and construction site management
children.text:
Structure maintenance and construction site management shall be pursuant to the International Building Code (IBC) including but not limited to Chapter 33 and this Code.

(1) Structure maintenance. The exterior of structures shall be maintained in a workman-like manner as intended when constructed. Features intended to prevent the intrusion of moisture, weather, pests, or other undesirable conditions shall be maintained. Structural elements shall be maintained to safely support the loads imposed. The standards used to determine when maintenance is required shall be all the standards of this Code as well as ensuring public safety and the prevention of nuisance conditions.

(2) Completion of exterior work. Any work to the exterior of any one- or two-family dwelling, including accessory structures, shall be completed within one (1) year from the date of issuance of the permit authorizing the work. A permit issued for exterior work or that includes exterior work is also subject to the requirements related to stopped or abandoned work pursuant to section 85.60 of this Code. One extension not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days may be requested from the building official prior to the expiration of a permit when weather conditions or other unforeseen circumstances prevent completion of the exterior work so long as acceptable work progress is being made. Public safety and nuisance conditions shall be considered when a request for an extension is presented.

(3) Dangerous construction conditions. Whenever any structure or property is suspected or found to be dangerous due to a construction condition, the building official shall cause the condition to be inspected and determine a course of action. When necessary, the building official shall confer with any affected department to verify the condition and determine a course of action. When a dangerous condition is found which is not an imminent danger to public safety, a notice shall be sent to the owner of the property or permit applicant identifying the dangerous condition and establishing a course of action which must be taken to abate the condition.

(4) Emergency abatement. Whenever any structure or property becomes unsafe for its intended purpose due to a construction condition and is determined to be an imminent danger to public safety, the building official shall determine if an emergency abatement through repair or demolition of all or part of the condition is warranted. When necessary, the building official shall confer with any affected department to determine a course of action. Notification to the owner is not required prior to any emergency abatement action when an imminent danger is determined. If the unsafe condition is such that notification to the owner can occur before any abatement action the building official may provide such notification. When an emergency abatement is ordered, the building official shall notify the owner of the structure in a timely manner after the emergency abatement as to the reasons for the actions taken. Any costs associated with an emergency abatement shall be paid by special assessment on the land where the condition exists. Such assessment shall be collected the same as special assessments made for other purposes under section 227.100 of this Code.

(5) Construction site management. Construction sites shall be managed by the owner or permit holder so they do not become a nuisance condition or a public safety concern pursuant to this Code. The building official shall cause construction sites to be inspected periodically for site management. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Scope
children.text: Building work shall include work regulated by Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050 including but not limited to Chapters 1305, 1309, 1311, 1322, 1323, and 1341. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Licensing
children.text: Licensing to perform building work shall include state and city issued contractor licenses. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit required
children.text: A permit shall be required for building work pursuant to the building code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit not required
children.text: A permit shall not be required for work exempted by Minn. Rule Part 1300.0120. If licensing is required for building work exempted by this section the work shall be performed by individuals or entities that possess the required license. Building work that does not require a permit shall be subject to any applicable requirements of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Administration and enforcement
children.text: The administration and enforcement of the electrical code is performed under the authority of the State of Minnesota. In the event the administration and enforcement of the electrical code by the state is interrupted, the city shall enter into an agreement with the state to maintain administration and enforcement. The agreement shall include the requirements set forth in Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050, Chapter 1315. Such agreement shall terminate upon reinstatement of state authority. Exterior electrical installations shall also be pursuant to Chapter 99, Articles IV, V, and VI of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Administration and enforcement
children.text:
The administration and enforcement of this code as it relates to elevators and conveyance devices is performed under the authority of the State of Minnesota. In the event the administration and enforcement of such code provisions by the state is interrupted, the city shall enter into an agreement with the state to maintain administration and enforcement. The agreement shall include any requirements set forth pursuant to the Minnesota Building Code. Such agreement shall terminate upon reinstatement of state authority. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19; Ord. No. 2021-007, § 1, 2-26-21)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 2021-007, § 1, adopted Feb. 26, 2021, amended the title of § 85.400 from "Scope" to "Administration and enforcement," as herein set out.

children.title: Scope
children.text: Mechanical work shall include work regulated by Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050 including but not limited to Chapter 1346. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Licensing
children.text: Licensing to perform mechanical work shall include city issued contractor licenses and certificates of competency. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit required
children.text: A permit shall be required for mechanical work pursuant to the building code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit not required
children.text: A permit shall not be required for work exempted by Minn. Rule Part 1300.0120. If licensing is required for mechanical work exempted by this section the work shall be performed by individuals or entities that possess the required license or certificate of competency. Mechanical work that does not require a permit shall be subject to any applicable code requirements. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: High-pressure pipefitting
children.text: High-pressure pipefitting shall be regulated pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Sections 326B.90 through 326B.925. The City of Minneapolis hereby agrees to abide by the state requirements and pursuant to section 326B.92 shall administer regulations, issue permits, and perform inspections of high-pressure piping installations in compliance with that section. The standards for high-pressure pipefitting work shall be pursuant to Minn. Rule 1300.0050, Chapter 5230. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: High-pressure pipefitting license
children.text: In addition to any other license or certification required by this Code, licenses and certifications for high-pressure pipefitting issued by the state of Minnesota, Department of Labor and Industry pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Section 326B.921 shall be required to obtain a permit for such work. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Scope
children.text: Plumbing work shall include work regulated by Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050 including but not limited to Chapter 4714 and Minn. Statutes, Chapter 326B. Gas piping work for other than environmental burners shall be considered plumbing work and shall be regulated by Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050, Chapter 1346. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Licensing
children.text: Licensing to perform plumbing work shall include state issued individual licenses and city issued contractor licenses and certificates of competency. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit required
children.text: A permit shall be required for plumbing work pursuant to the building code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit not required
children.text: A plumbing permit shall not be required for plumbing work according to Minn. Rule Part 1300.0215. If licensing is required for the plumbing work exempted by this section the work shall be performed by individuals or entities that possess the required license or certificate of competency. Plumbing work that does not require a permit shall be subject to any applicable code requirements. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Advertising to perform plumbing
children.text: Advertising to perform plumbing shall comply with Minn. Statutes, Section 325F.75. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit, license, certificate exception
children.text: There shall be no requirement for a plumbing permit, license, or certificate of competency when a person or entity possesses the required license and certificate of competency as a master or journey worker refrigeration installer and has a mechanical permit for the disconnecting or reconnecting of refrigeration systems or equipment that is connected to the water distribution system of any building or structure for the purposes of repairing or servicing such refrigeration system or equipment. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Administration and enforcement authorized
children.text: Administration and enforcement of the programs in this chapter shall be by the agency under the direction of the Minnesota Certified Building Official designated by the city pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Chapter 326B. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Program established
children.text: Pursuant to the authority provided in Minn. Statutes, Chapter 463, the City of Minneapolis hereby establishes a program intended to help ensure that properties within the city are maintained in a safe and sanitary condition. This program shall be known as certificate of code compliance and shall apply to all buildings. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Certificate of code compliance
children.text: A certificate of code compliance is hereby established. The purpose of the certificate is to document that an inspection process has been completed for a building and the intent of city ordinances created to preserve the safety and health of its citizens has been met. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: When certificate is required
Application
children.text: The owner of a building which becomes subject to the requirements of this program shall cause application to be made for the code compliance process on the form provided by the city. All information necessary to complete the code compliance process shall be provided by the applicant. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Code compliance permit
children.text: A code compliance permit shall be required to initiate the code compliance process. Upon proper application and payment of the code compliance inspection fee a code compliance permit shall be issued. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Code compliance inspection
children.text: After the code compliance permit has been issued the building official shall cause the building to be inspected for safety and sanitation with respect to its general construction, plumbing and mechanical installations, and other requirements of this Code. The applicant shall be required to hire the services of a licensed electrician to determine code compliance of the electrical system. The standards for the code compliance inspection shall be those minimum requirements of this Code which are applicable to existing buildings. All areas of the building shall be made accessible for the purposes of performing the code compliance inspection. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Failure of building to comply with code
children.text: When the results of the code compliance inspection reveal that the building fails in any respect to comply with the provisions of this Code the building official shall notify the owner to this effect and specify wherein such building fails to comply with the requirements of this Code. The owner shall cause licensed contractors to obtain the required permits to perform corrective work according to requirements of this Code. The building official shall take the necessary action to secure compliance with the provisions of this Code so no immediate hazards to health or safety of the occupants or the public are allowed to continue. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Engineering analysis
children.text: The building official may require the owner to submit an engineering analysis report of the entire or any part of the building or its systems. The report shall be prepared by an engineer certified by the State of Minnesota for the area of concern. When an engineering analysis report is required, no additional permit shall be issued pursuant to this Code prior to completion of the engineering analysis report requirement. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Deposit
children.text: As a condition of the code compliance process, the applicant shall deposit with the city four thousand dollars ($4,000.00) by cashier check. Such monies shall be deposited with the city treasurer to be held without interest until said monies are refunded to the applicant or forfeited to the city when a certificate of code compliance is not issued within nine (9) months from the date the deposit was received by the city or within the time limitation set forth in Chapter 249 of this Code. One (1) three (3) month extension beyond the initial nine (9) month time limitation may be requested by the owner if the work is more than fifty (50) percent complete and unforeseen circumstances have caused delays in the work. In the event the building is restored to habitable condition, and a certificate of code compliance is obtained within the time limits set out herein, the deposit shall be refunded to the payee by the Minneapolis city treasurer. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permits and licensing
children.text: Plumbing and mechanical permits required to perform corrective work shall be obtained by properly licensed professionals pursuant to Chapters 85 and 278 of this Code. Electrical permits and contractor licensing shall be according to the state of Minnesota. Building permits required for corrective work shall be obtained by properly licensed professionals according to State of Minnesota contractor licensing requirements. If no state licensing requirements apply the city may require Minneapolis licensing or verification of continued ownership of the building. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Exempt work
children.text: Rehabilitation work undertaken by community planning and economic development (CPED) or its sponsorship may be exempt from requirements of this article deemed non-essential by the building official. All such exempt rehabilitation work shall be in compliance with the requirements of this Code when completed. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Issuance of certificate
children.text: Upon completion of all corrective work required the owner of the building shall cause a request for the necessary inspections to occur in order to verify that the general construction, plumbing, mechanical, and electrical systems have been improved to a satisfactory condition. Compliance with any housing or zoning requirements shall also be verified. When the necessary inspections have been approved, the building official shall issue a certificate of code compliance. The certificate of code compliance shall authorize occupancy of the building except for moved buildings which shall comply with Minn. Rule Part 1300.0220. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Temporary certificate
children.text: The building official may issue a temporary certificate of code compliance prior to completion of exterior, non-life-safety improvements required by this Code when completion of the exterior requirements is substantially hindered by weather. All interior and life-safety code compliance requirements of this Code must be completed, inspected, and approved before a temporary certificate can be issued. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee
children.text: Fees for the certificate of code compliance process shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Program established
children.text: Pursuant to the Minn. State Plumbing Code Minn. Rule 4714, Chapter 6, a program is hereby established to monitor the installation, removal, replacement, relocation, and maintenance of regulated backflow assemblies. The program shall be known as regulated backflow assemblies. The intent of the program is to protect the public health and sanitation from potential contamination of the public water system. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Regulated backflow assemblies
children.text: Regulated backflow assemblies subject to this program shall be those identified in the Minn. State Plumbing Code Minn. Rule 4714. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit required
children.text: A permit shall be required for regulated work performed on a regulated backflow assembly. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: Permit fees for a regulated backflow assembly permit shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Inspection required
children.text: After initial installation, removal, replacement, or relocation of a regulated backflow assembly the city shall be notified to inspect such regulated backflow assembly by the permit applicant to ensure that the work performed was completed according to code requirements. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Periodic inspection and testing
children.text: The owner of a regulated backflow assembly shall ensure the assembly is maintained in proper working order and shall cause the assembly to be inspected and tested periodically to ensure the assembly is functioning as intended. Testing intervals shall not exceed one (1) year. If unusual circumstances exist for any regulated backflow assembly the city may require more frequent testing. A test and inspection tag shall be affixed to the regulated backflow assembly, and a copy of the test report shall be submitted to the city within fourteen (14) days of the test date. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Licensing and certification
children.text: Licensing and certification required for work on regulated backflow assemblies shall be pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Section 326B.437. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Definitions
children.text:
For the purposes of this article, the following shall have the meanings stated:

Building Official. The Minnesota Certified Building Official designated by the city pursuant to Minnesota Statutes, Section 326B.133.

Department. Construction code services section of the community planning and economic development (CPED) department.

Parking ramp. A building or structure, or part thereof, in which a structural level, other than a slab on grade, is used for parking, storage, or maintenance of motor vehicles.

Parking ramp license. A city-issued business license for operation of a parking ramp.

Parking ramp operating certificate. A city-issued document that affirms that the owner of a parking ramp has completed the requirements of this Code for operation of a parking ramp.

Qualified civil or structural engineer. A person registered by the state of Minnesota as a professional engineer whose field of practice is civil or structural engineering. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Certificate required
children.text: No person, firm, corporation, governmental entity or other entity shall own or operate a parking ramp which has been in operation for five (5) years or more, without having first applied for and obtained an operating certificate. Such certificate shall be granted by the building official as provided in this article. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Application for certificate; fee established
children.text: The fee for a parking ramp operating certificate shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.900 of this Code. Application for a parking ramp operating certificate shall be filed with the department on forms provided by the department. The application shall contain the name, business address and telephone number of the owner of the ramp; the address of the parking ramp; the number of parking spaces; the year in which the ramp was constructed; and such other information as the building official may require. The application shall also state the name, address and telephone number of the person or firm which operates the parking ramp, if different from the owner. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Certificate expiration; renewal
children.text: Unless sooner revoked, a parking ramp operating certificate shall expire on the expiration date of any insurance policy required in section 87.370 of this Code. An applicant who wishes to renew the operating certificate shall, at least thirty (30) days before the expiration date, file an application for renewal on forms provided by the department and shall submit proof of inspection services performed by a qualified civil or structural engineer. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Annual inspection required
children.text: No parking ramp operating certificate shall be issued or renewed unless the owner or operator has caused the parking ramp to be inspected annually by a qualified civil or structural engineer as required by this article. The inspection shall consist of an annual on-site field inspection and, every third year, a sufficient number of destructive or equivalent tests and nondestructive tests to properly determine the structural condition of the parking ramp. Tests shall include, but not be limited to, chain-dragging or coring or chloride testing or equivalent tests. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Affidavit and engineer's report required
children.text: Upon application for or renewal of the required operating certificate, the owner or operator of a parking ramp shall file with the building official an affidavit stating that the parking ramp has been inspected in accordance with section 87.340 of this Code by a qualified civil or structural engineer. The owner or operator shall file with the affidavit a copy of the engineer's inspection report. The report shall contain the engineer's findings and shall indicate whether the structure is capable of supporting the loads for which it is used. The report shall contain a statement by the engineer whose field of practice is civil or structural engineering and that said engineer carries professional liability insurance in the amount of two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000.00). (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Certificate nonrenewal; revocation; transfer
children.text:
(a) No operating certificate shall be issued or renewed unless the owner or operator of the parking ramp has obtained the annual inspections required by section 87.340 of this Code and filed the annual affidavits and reports required by section 87.350 of this Code.

(b) If the owner or operator of a parking ramp fails to file the annual affidavit and report required by section 87.350 of this Code, the building official may revoke the certificate. A decision to revoke the certificate may be appealed in writing within twenty-one (21) days of mailing of the building official's decision.

(c) An existing operating certificate may be transferred to a new owner upon receipt by the city of any required application(s) and supporting documentation. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Insurance required for parking ramp operation
children.text:
No operating certificate shall be granted unless the owner or operator shall carry liability insurance with an insurance company authorized to do business in the state of Minnesota. The liability insurance for the premises and operations of the ramp, which shall include coverage for any injury or loss caused by explosion or collapse, shall be in the sum of at least one million five hundred thousand dollars ($1,500,000.00).

The owner or operator of an automobile service facility, which provides less than one hundred (100) parking spaces in the service facility structure, shall carry liability insurance with an insurance company authorized to do business in the state of Minnesota. The liability insurance for the premises and operation of the ramp, which shall include coverage for any injury or loss caused by explosion or collapse, shall be in the sum of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000.00).

If the owner takes possession of the keys, and has care, custody and control of a vehicle, then the owner shall also provide garage-keepers legal liability insurance in the sum of at least three thousand five hundred dollars ($3,500.00) per stall, or two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000.00) as minimum policy limits. The required certificates of insurance shall be kept current and valid at the corporate headquarters and copies shall be maintained at each parking ramp office. Such certificates shall be produced immediately upon demand of the building official or designee, or any member of the public. Self-insured government entities shall be exempt from the requirements of this section. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Operating certificate to be posted
children.text: Every owner or operator of a parking ramp required to obtain an operating certificate shall post said certificate in a conspicuous location in the office or main collection booth of the parking ramp. In the event such notice is not posted, the building official or designee may require that all motor vehicles be removed from the parking ramp and that no further parking of vehicles be allowed until the required operating certificate has been obtained and posted. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Penalty for failure to obtain or renew operating certificate
children.text: Should any person, firm, corporation, governmental entity or other entity operate a parking ramp without first having a valid operating certificate as required by this article, the owner or operator shall, when subsequently securing such certificate, be required to pay double the fee established in section 87.320 of this Code. The building official or designee may also issue or cause to be issued an administrative citation to the owner or operator for violation of any of the provisions of this article. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.text:
