children.title: Purpose
children.text: The requirements in this chapter are established to provide additional information and protections in the city for various activities. Requirements shall be administered by the appropriate agency or agencies charged with that administration. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Purpose
children.text: For the purposes of minimizing negative impacts that construction activities can have on surrounding areas, including but not limited to wrecking, major remodeling, and new construction, a Minneapolis Construction Management Agreement shall be required. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Requirements and standards
children.text:
In addition to all other applicable requirements of this Code, the building code, and state statutes and rules, the requirements herein shall apply to certain construction projects for dwellings from one (1) to four (4) dwelling units. Construction activities for other buildings that the city determines may have negative impacts to surrounding areas shall also be subject to those requirements herein that the city determines are necessary.

(1) Contact information. Prior to any work being done on the permit site, a sign must be posted identifying the nature of the construction activity, the permit holder, a contact name and phone number, the site address, and a contact phone number at the city to report problems. The sign shall be twenty-four (24) inches by thirty-six (36) inches in size with readable lettering as viewed from the street. All information must remain current, and the sign must be posted without obstruction in the front yard until completion of the work.

(2) Neighbor notification. At least fifteen (15) calendar days before any construction begins on the permit site, the permit holder shall provide mailed notice to all property owners within three hundred fifty (350) feet of the permit site inviting them to a neighborhood informational meeting. The meeting shall be held at least five (5) days before any construction commences and shall be held within three (3) miles of the permit site. Topics discussed must include the construction plans, hours of operation, work schedule, estimated completion date, erosion and sediment control, dumpster location, noise mitigation, dust control, portable bathroom location, debris removal schedule, and site placement for building materials and equipment. The permit holder shall maintain a copy of the written meeting notice, the agenda, and a confirmed attendance list, which shall be available for review by the city.

(3) Work site and surrounding property maintenance. The site must be maintained in a neat and orderly condition. Prior to leaving the construction site at the end of each day, the Contractor must remove empty cans, paper, plastic and other material that is not needed for construction from the site or deposit them in a dumpster. The contractor must keep streets, sidewalks, boulevard areas and adjacent properties clean from waste, materials or refuse resulting from operations on the site. Inoperable equipment and equipment not being used on the site must be removed within twenty-four (24) hours after it becomes inoperable or is no longer in use. Where work on any project lies within areas of pedestrian traffic or vehicular traffic, the project area must be cleaned and swept and all materials related to the project must be stockpiled in appropriate areas. Debris must be contained on the project site. No material may be deposited or stockpiled on the public streets, boulevards, sidewalks or adjacent property.

(4) Dumpster placement, maintenance, and street use. Dumpsters shall be located entirely on the permit site and not on public property. Minnesota state law requires a five (5) foot parking setback from driveways and a thirty (30) foot setback from intersections. Dumpsters must be covered during all non-work hours, and the area around the dumpster shall be kept neat and orderly. If placement requires street use, permits will be issued in thirty (30) day increments only and may be renewed up to a total of one hundred twenty (120) days. Street use permits may be obtained on-line. A copy of the permit must be placed with the building permit on-site, and a readable copy of the permit must be attached to the dumpster with active dates visible.

(5) Portable restroom placement. Portable toilets shall be located to the rear of the project site and not within fifteen (15) feet of an adjacent property. No portable toilets shall be placed on a public street, sidewalk, or boulevard area without obtaining the proper permit from the city. The permit holder is responsible for the security and maintenance of the portable toilet.

(6) Dust control. Dust control is the responsibility of the permit holder. The permit holder must address dust problems immediately upon receiving notice from the city. When feasible, the Contractor shall keep all debris thoroughly dampened with water to minimize dust and particles from flying around the neighborhood. Alternative dust control measures may be required during below-freezing temperatures.

(7) Drive entrance. A drive entrance pad or its equivalent shall consist of an all-weather, large aggregate material capable of minimizing the tracking of dirt from the permit site. The location of the construction drive entrance shall be approved by the city and noted in the on-site construction plans.

(8) Tree protection. The city may order the installation of protective fencing around boulevard trees and trees that will not be removed during construction. The city may also require the submission of a tree preservation plan.

(9) Damage to public property. The permit holder must repair any damage to public property, streets, and sidewalks. Upon request, the permit holder shall furnish photographs of the existing condition of the property, curbs, sidewalks, streets, boulevard, and trees adjacent to the permit site prior to commencing any work. If damage occurs to the foregoing, it must be repaired within three (3) working days after the damage occurs, unless the permit holder has received written permission from the city to delay repairs to a later specified date. The city may require the submission of a soils investigation report and/or shoring plan.

(10) Protection of adjoining property. Adjoining property shall be protected from damage during any construction work on the permit site. Excavations for any purpose shall not remove lateral support from any footing or foundation without first protecting the footing or foundation against settlement or lateral translation. The city may require the submission of a soils investigation report and/or shoring plan.

(11) Surface drainage, erosion and sediment control. The contractor shall protect all storm drain inlets with sediment capture devices prior to soil disruption during the project when soil disturbing activities may result in sediment-laden storm water runoff entering the inlet. The contractor shall provide effective storm drain inlet protection during the duration of the project until all surfaces with the potential for discharging sediment to an inlet have been stabilized.

(12) Survey requirement. Prior to any construction activity, an as-built survey and topographic survey must be submitted as part of the site plan review and is required to note the front and side yard setbacks on directly contiguous properties on the sides of the home. For properties on corner lots, contiguous properties must be included in the survey. As-built surveys are required to be submitted during construction as follows:

a. An as-built survey indicating the floor level of the existing home at the main entry must be submitted with an application for a demolition permit.

b. An as-built survey indicating the top of foundation and structure setbacks must be submitted prior to foundation inspection.

c. An as-built survey indicating actual site conditions, including all structures and contours must be submitted prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy.

(13) Written notification of excavation or wrecking. Adjoining public and private property shall be protected from damage during excavation and demolition activities. Protection must be provided for all parts of adjoining structures and landscaping. Provisions shall be made to control water runoff and erosion during excavation or demolition activities. The person making or causing an excavation or demolition to be made shall provide written notice to the owners of property adjacent to the permit site advising them that the excavation or demolition is to be made and that the adjoining property should be protected. Said notification shall be delivered not less than ten (10) days prior to the scheduled starting date of the excavation or demolition. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Definitions
children.text:
For the purposes of Title 5, the following terms shall have the stated meanings:

Portable swimming pool. Any rubber or plastic swimming pool which can be erected without permanent support.

Private residential swimming pool. Any constructed or assembled swimming pool or portable swimming pool which is used or intended to be used as a swimming pool in connection with one- and two-family dwellings as defined in the building code, and available only to the family of the owner and guests.

Swimming pool. Any structure, basin, chamber or tank constructed or designed to contain an artificial body of water for swimming, diving, relaxation or recreational bathing, and having a depth of two (2) feet or more at any point. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit required
children.text: No person shall construct or erect a private residential swimming pool or reconstruct any such pool or do any alteration, addition, remodeling or repair to such swimming pool that exceeds the value of one hundred dollars ($100.00) without first obtaining a permit from the building official. A permit shall be required for the re-erection of any such swimming pool which was once erected with permit or which was in existence at the date of the enactment of this article, and then disassembled, and which is not re-erected in the same location. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Plans to be submitted
children.text:
Plans and specifications and pertinent explanatory data shall be submitted with the application for a permit. No new plan shall be required for the re-erection of a pool according to a plan previously submitted. The plans shall be reviewed relative to design, operation and maintenance insofar as health and safety features are concerned in accordance with the standards prescribed in this Code. The plans shall be drawn to a scale of not less than one-fourth inch per foot. The plans shall include the following data and such other information as may be reasonably requested by the building official:

(1) The general layout of the entire building lot on which the pool is to be located, including the distances of the pool from the lot lines, the location of all utilities, and the location of any source of contamination within fifty (50) feet of the pool;

(2) The dimensions of the pool, including the effective length and width of the pool and other similar items; and

(3) The source of water supply and method of drainage, including all pipes, inlets, outlets and waste and discharge lines. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Construction in accordance with approved plans; deviations
children.text: Swimming pools, appurtenances, water supply and drainage systems and other features shall be constructed in conformity with the approved plans. If any deviations from such plans are desired, a supplementary plan covering that portion of the work involved shall be filed for approval and shall conform to the provisions of this article. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit fee
children.text: Permit fees shall be pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Design and construction requirements
children.text:
The design and construction of all private residential swimming pools shall comply with the following:

(1) Structural design. The pool structure shall be engineered and designed to withstand the expected forces to which it will be subjected.

(2) Overflow and surface drainage. The pool and surrounding area shall be constructed and arranged in such a manner that no splash or overflow water shall return to the pool. No surface or roof drainage shall be permitted to enter the pool.

(3) Finish. Pool floor and walls shall have a cleanable, white or similar light-colored and impermeable surface.

(4) Handholds. Handholds shall be provided and shall not be more than nine (9) inches above the normal water line and shall extend around the entire periphery of the pool.

(5) Pool deck. Unobstructed deck areas not less than forty-eight (48) inches wide shall be provided to extend entirely around the pool. The deck surface shall be such as to be smooth and easily cleaned and of nonslip construction. The deck shall have a pitch of at least one-fourth (¼) inch to the foot, designed so as to prevent back drainage into the pool. If deck drains are provided, drain pipe lines shall be at least two (2) inches in diameter and drain openings shall have an open area of at least four (4) times the cross-sectional area of the drain pipe. The deck drain system shall have indirect connection to the sanitary sewer. The deck drains shall not be connected to the recirculation system piping. No deck, other than the ground surface, shall be required for any pool that is totally above ground and which is less than four (4) feet in height.

(6) Steps or ladders. One (1) or more means of egress in the form of steps or ladders shall be provided from any pool having a water depth of thirty-six (36) inches or more. Treads of steps and ladders shall be equipped with nonslip material.

(7) Plumbing. All plumbing connected to such swimming pool shall be installed in accordance with the Minnesota State Plumbing Code, Minn. Rule 4714.

(8) Water supply. The water supply serving the swimming pool shall be potable water or of a quality otherwise acceptable to the commissioner of health. All portions of the water distribution system serving the swimming pool and auxiliary facilities shall be protected against backflow. Water introduced into the pool, either directly or to the recirculation system, shall be supplied through an air gap. When such connections are not possible, the supply shall be protected by a suitable backflow preventer installed on the discharge side of the last control to the fixture, device or appurtenance.

(9) Drainage. Pools shall be equipped with facilities for completely emptying the pool to the sanitary sewer, or other suitable disposal unit acceptable to the building official.

There shall be no direct physical connection between the sewer system and any drain from the swimming pool or recirculation system. Any swimming pool or gutter drain or overflow from the recirculation system when discharged to the sewer system, storm drain, or other approved natural drainage course shall connect through a suitable air gap or air break so as to preclude the possibility of backup of sewage or waste into the swimming pool piping system.

The water from the pool shall not be drained onto the streets or sidewalk or any other public property or private property not owned by the pool owner.

(10) Heaters. All gas-fired or oil burning swimming pool heaters and boilers shall comply with the plumbing code and heating code of the city. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Electrical requirements
children.text: All electrical installations installed and used in conjunction with a residential swimming pool or portable swimming pool shall conform to the Minn. State Electrical Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Chemical treatment
children.text: Gaseous chlorinating systems shall not be used as a disinfecting method for a private residential swimming pool or portable swimming pool. Below ground pools shall meet the requirements for recirculation, disinfection and water quality maintenance as required for public swimming pools as set forth in the state department of health miscellaneous environmental health rules. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fences
children.text: Outdoor private residential swimming pools shall be protected by a fence, wall, building or other enclosure or any combination thereof. All fence openings or points of entry into the pool area enclosure shall be equipped with gates. The fence and gates shall be at least four (4) feet in height. All gates shall be equipped with self-closing and self-latching devices placed at the top of the gate or otherwise inaccessible to small children and provided with hardware for permanent locking devices. The openings between the bottom of the fence and the ground or other surface shall not be more than four (4) inches. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Approval of other design and equipment
children.text: Any swimming pool, the design and equipment of which incorporates features other than those set forth herein, shall be subject to review and approval by the building official and the commissioner of health in accordance with acceptable standards and in conformance with current public health and safety practices. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Location
children.text: No portion of a swimming pool or appurtenances thereto shall be located from the lot line at a distance less than that required for a side yard, as set forth in the zoning code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19; Ord. No. 2023-035, § 1, 5-25-23)

children.title: Dangers to life and health prohibited
children.text: No private residential swimming pool or portable swimming pool shall be used, kept, maintained or operated in the city if such use, keeping, maintaining or operating shall be the occasion of any nuisance or shall be dangerous to life or detrimental to health. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Retroactivity
children.text: The provisions of this article shall be applicable to all private residential swimming pools existing on September 8, 1972, except that sections 89.110 through 89.140 and 89.200 of this Code shall not apply unless such pool is disassembled. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Enforcement officers specified
children.text: The building official, zoning administrator, and director of environmental health are authorized and directed to administer and enforce the provisions of this article. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: License required
children.text: A person, corporation, or other entity that raises, supports off a foundation, and moves buildings on and over public streets and highways shall be required to obtain a license from the State of Minnesota pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Section 221.81. All work related to the moving of a building shall comply with the applicable requirements of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Report of violations to state of Minnesota
children.text: The building official shall report all violations of this article to the Minnesota Commissioner of Transportation for possible revocation or suspension of the building mover's state license. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permits required
children.text:
Before initiating any work related to raising, supporting off a foundation, or moving a building, the licensed building mover shall obtain a moving permit required by the city. Moving permits shall be for moving buildings within the city, moving buildings out of the city, or moving buildings outside the city into the city. Permits issued by the city do not authorize any work outside the city limits.

In addition to the moving permit for the moving contractor, it shall be required for any person, contractor, or other entity hired to perform work on the existing site or the new site, when either is in the city, to obtain the required permits for that work. Permits that may be required include but are not limited to wrecking, building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and code compliance. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Moving buildings within the city
Moving buildings out of the city
children.text:
When moving a building out of the city, the licensed building mover shall obtain a moving permit to raise, hold, and move the building. The following shall be completed before a moving permit will be issued:

(1) Notify the public works department of the city of the intent to utilize city streets and comply with any requirements; and

(2) The contractor responsible for the restoration of the site where the building currently exists shall obtain a wrecking permit for removal of the existing foundation, termination of existing utilities, and restoration of the site. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Moving buildings from outside the city into the city
Permit fees
children.text: Fees for moving permits shall be pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Moving through streets
children.text: The building mover shall obtain any required permits and permission to move on city streets from the Minneapolis Public Works Department. The building mover shall not permit the building or equipment to be in violation of any requirements of this Code. When moving a building, the building mover shall make every effort to avoid damage to any public or private property. Any damage that does occur shall be repaired to the same or better condition as previously existed in a timely manner. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Prerequisites to permit
children.text:
No permits shall be issued for the moving of any building until satisfactory evidence is provided that all utility bills, taxes, and other services for the property have been paid, and that all utility connections have been properly disconnected and removed. In addition, the following shall apply before any permits will be issued:

(1) No permit shall be issued as herein provided for the removal of any building until satisfactory evidence is furnished by the city engineer that all sewer charges and water bills chargeable against the property sought to be moved have been paid, and that all sewer and water connections have been plugged or discontinued at the curb line or at the main, as shall be determined by the city engineer, and that satisfactory evidence is presented of the payment of all taxes chargeable against such property. No permit shall be issued until satisfactory evidence is furnished that all public utility companies furnishing services to the premises have been notified in writing by the building mover not less than two (2) business days prior to the raising, holding or moving of the building. The public utility company shall remove its equipment and service within the time set forth in such written notice or promptly notify the building mover and the building official if a longer time period is necessary to remove their equipment and service so as not to constitute a hazard. The building official then may withhold the issuance of the permit when in the city's opinion a longer time period is necessary for the removal of utility equipment and service so as to protect the public health, safety and welfare.

(2) However, in lieu of evidence of payment of taxes, the building official may accept a certificate from the State of Minnesota, any of its agencies or political subdivisions, or a body public and corporate, that it is the owner of such property, and that such moving is being done by it, its contractor or agent.

(3) Further, no permit shall be issued as herein provided for the moving of any building until satisfactory evidence is furnished by a certificate from the commissioner of health that a licensed pest control company has satisfactorily exterminated all nuisance pests from the structure and premises.

(4) Further, no permit shall be issued as herein provided for the moving of any building until satisfactory evidence is furnished in writing that said move or moving has approval of the heritage preservation commission as established in Chapter 34 of this Code.

(5) Further, no moving permit shall be issued as herein provided for the moving of any building until satisfactory evidence is furnished in writing from the owner that all remaining foundation walls, footings, columns, floor slabs, piping, heating equipment, fuel storage tanks, and other debris shall be removed from the premises. The excavation remaining after the moving of a building or structure shall be filled to the level of the surrounding grade, with clean, granular-type fill material. Further, this shall be properly compacted and graded to provide drainage to prevent ponding of water. There shall be a topping of a sufficient depth and quality so as to enable groundcover to grow. Suitable groundcover shall be provided no later than ninety (90) days after permit issuance to comply with section 244.1570. Fencing not less than four (4) feet high shall be placed entirely around the perimeter of the excavation if it is more than thirty (30) inches deep at any point.

(6) Further, no permit shall be issued as herein provided for the moving of any building to a site within the city unless application has also been made by the owner of such building for a certificate of code compliance, as set out in Chapter 87, Article II of this Code, to be performed when the building has been placed on its new site. New construction standards of the state building code shall apply to the construction, alteration, repair or rehabilitation necessitated by such inspection for any building moved to a site within the city. No such building shall be used for human occupancy until the certificate of code compliance relating to that building has been issued.

(7) As a condition of the issuance of any permits, including the permit for moving required by this chapter, the applicant must deposit with the building official two thousand dollars ($2,000.00) in cash or negotiable instrument. Such monies shall be deposited with the city treasurer to be held without interest until such time as said monies are refunded to the applicant or forfeited to the city in the event that the work required by this subsection and a certificate of code compliance is not issued within six (6) months from the date of the code compliance inspection. One (1) three-month extension beyond the initial six-month time limitation may be requested by the owner if it can be shown that the code compliance work is proceeding expeditiously and is more than fifty (50) percent complete, or if unforeseen conditions have had a significant schedule impact on the completion of the work. In the event the building is restored to habitable condition and a certificate of code compliance is obtained within the time limits set out herein, the two thousand dollar ($2,000.00) cash deposit shall be refunded to the payee by the Minneapolis city finance officer.

Rehabilitation undertaken by the community planning and economic development (CPED) department or under its sponsorship shall be exempt from the requirement of a cash deposit. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Wire displacement
children.text:
(a) In every case in which a permit shall be issued, as herein provided, for the moving of a building, when such moving requires the displacement of any overhead electrical or other wires, the person owning, operating or controlling such wires shall remove or displace the same, so far as the same may be necessary to affect the moving of said building to the point to which the removal thereof shall be authorized by such permit.

(b) The person to who said permit shall have been issued shall notify the person owning, operating or controlling said wires to remove or displace the same to facilitate the removal of said building, and shall, at the same time, exhibit to said person the properly issued permit authorizing the moving of said building. Thereupon, said person, within twenty-four (24) hours thereafter, shall remove or displace said wires sufficiently to allow the passage of said building along the street over which said wires are suspended.

(c) The displacement of exterior electrical wires shall be pursuant to any applicable requirements of Chapter 99, Articles IV, V, and VI of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Additional regulations
children.text:
(a) In addition to all other requirements herein, building movers shall observe the following rules:

(1) All building moving shall be done in a manner and during those hours and on the dates designated by the city engineer.

(2) All movements of buildings once started shall continue until completed, and no building shall be parked along the route unless deemed an emergency and approved by the city engineer. The building mover shall promptly notify the licensing official of such approval.

(3) Movers shall provide a front and rear escort for all movements and the outline of the building shall be readily defined by lights. Said escort and lighting shall be as specified by the city engineer. Not more than one (1) building shall be moved over a bridge or a street at any one (1) time. Every building mover shall notify the affected utilities and the licensing official at least two (2) business days, but not more than ten (10) business days, prior to the date of movement. The city engineer shall have the right and authority to deny or change the requested movement depending upon the number of buildings to be moved in a particular area on a given day and to regulate such movements.

(4) The traffic engineering division of the city engineer's department shall issue for a fee "No Parking" signs to be posted by the mover along affected streets. The mover shall notify the city engineer of the streets or areas to be so posted by the mover. All such signs shall be posted not less than twenty-four (24) hours nor more than thirty (30) hours before the move is to be made and the date and day of such move shall be legibly imprinted thereon, together with the name, address and telephone number of the building mover. All such signs shall be removed by the mover immediately after the building has passed a posted location.

(5) All laws pertaining to tampering with private property and vehicles on the streets shall be obeyed by the building mover during all moves.

(6) It shall be unlawful for any mover to use any other route than the one (1) approved by the park and recreation board, the city engineer's office and/or the Minnesota State Highway Department.

(7) The moving permit must be posted on each building being moved during the entire move. The permit must be posted at a point not to exceed eight (8) feet above grade level when the building is loaded.

(b) Two (2) signs must be attached to the building. Each of these signs must be not smaller than twenty-four (24) inches by eighteen (18) inches in size and of a permanent material (not paper or cardboard). One sign must be attached to each side of the building so that it is visible from the curb while the building is being moved, and must remain in place until the building has reached its final destination. Each sign must show, in letters not smaller than one and one-half (1½) inches in height, the licensee's name and telephone number. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Definition
children.text: For the purposes of Title 5, 'wrecking' shall mean the complete removal of a structure including all footings, foundations, accessory structures, and utilities serving the structure. Upon completion of the wrecking of a structure the property shall be restored to a condition that will allow new development or if the property remains undeveloped it shall be restored to a condition that is not a nuisance or a danger to public safety. Partial wrecking of a structure will be evaluated by the city for purposes of determining the licenses and permits that will be required to complete the work. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: License required
children.text: No person, corporation, or other entity shall commence any work related to the wrecking of any building or structure without having first obtained a license pursuant to Chapter 277, Article XII of this Code, unless exempted by said Article XII. All work related to the wrecking of any building or structure shall comply with the applicable requirements of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permits required
children.text: No person, corporation, or other entity shall commence any work related to the wrecking of any building or structure without having first obtained a wrecking permit. Any person, corporation, or other entity hired to perform work related to the wrecking of any building or structure shall obtain required licenses and permits before commencing work. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19; Ord. No. 2025-056, § 1, 12-11-25)

children.title: Permit exception
children.text: No wrecking permit shall be required for the wrecking of a private garage, shed, or other such accessory building or structure not exceeding one thousand (1,000) square feet of total floor area. If such accessory building includes an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) a permit may be required. Floor area shall be determined by the person, corporation, or other entity that will perform the wrecking and be approved by the city. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit fees
children.text: Fees for wrecking permits shall be pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Prerequisites to permit
children.text:
(a) No permit shall be issued as herein provided until satisfactory evidence is furnished by a certificate of the city engineer that all sewer charges and water bills chargeable against the property sought to be wrecked have been paid and that all water and sewer connections have been plugged or discontinued at the curb line or at the main, as shall be determined by the city engineer, and that satisfactory evidence is presented of the payment of all taxes chargeable against such property. A fee for the sewer plug inspection by the city engineer shall be paid to the city finance department prior to the issuance of the permit. The fee amount shall be pursuant to the current fee schedule of the public works department. In addition, no such permit shall be issued until satisfactory evidence is furnished that all public utility companies furnishing services to the premises have been notified in writing by the person applying for the wrecking permit not less than two (2) business days prior to proceeding with the wrecking of the building. The public utility company shall remove its equipment and service within the time set forth in such written notice or promptly notify the building wrecker and the building official if a longer time-period is necessary to remove their equipment and service so as not to constitute a hazard. The building official may then withhold the issuance of the wrecking permit when, in the building official's opinion, a longer time-period is necessary for the removal of utility equipment and service so as to protect the public health, safety and welfare.

(b) In lieu of evidence of payment of taxes, the building official may accept a certificate from the state of Minnesota, any of its agencies or political subdivisions, or a body public and corporate, that it is the owner of such property, and that such wrecking is being done by it, its contractor or agent.

(c) No permit shall be issued as herein provided for the wrecking of any building or structure in the city until satisfactory evidence is furnished by a certificate from the commissioner of health that a licensed pest control company has exterminated all nuisance pests from the structure and premises.

(d) No permit shall be issued as herein provided for the wrecking, of a building or structure in the city until satisfactory evidence is furnished in writing that said wrecking, has the approval of the heritage preservation commission as established in Chapter 34 of this Code.

(e) No permit shall be issued as herein provided for the wrecking of any building or structure in the city that has been determined to meet one (1) or more of the qualifying criteria in section 89.555 until an environmental mitigation plan has been submitted to and approved by the Minneapolis Health Department. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19; Ord. No. 2025-056, § 2, 12-11-25)

children.title: Environmental mitigation plan
children.text:
(a) An environmental mitigation plan may be required for the wrecking of a building or structure in the city that meets one (1) or more of the following criteria:

(1) The facility holds or held a state air emissions permit from the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, unless determined by the health commissioner or the commissioner's designee that the permit does not relate to an activity, process or material that may create a heightened risk of environmental impact upon wrecking of the building or structure;

(2) Hazardous waste or materials have been stored on the site; or

(3) The building or structure is located in the United States Environmental Protection Agency South Minneapolis Residential Soil Contamination Site boundary.

(b) The environmental mitigation plan shall outline how the contractor will mitigate offsite impacts of wrecking activities. Environmental mitigation plan contents shall include at minimum the following:

(1) Methods to assure adequate and continuous dust suppression at the site, including at freezing temperatures; and

(2) Other requirements as determined by the health commissioner or the commissioner's designee.

(Ord. No. 2025-056, § 3, 12-11-25)

children.title: Sign required
children.text: Before such work is commenced, and throughout the progress of the same until the completion thereof, the licensee shall place and maintain in a conspicuous place on the premises where the same can be observed by the public, a sign not less than three (3) by three (3) feet square, on which shall be posted in such a way as to be legible to the public, a statement as to who is doing the wrecking, giving the name of the person doing the work. Said sign shall be removed immediately upon completion of the work. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Notification required
children.text:
(a) At least fifteen (15) calendar days before any wrecking begins on the permit site, the permit holder shall provide mailed notice to the city council ward office, any local official neighborhood organization, and all property owners within three hundred fifty (350) feet of the permit site of the upcoming demolition of the site. Tax fee holders must notify any tenants of the wrecking activity upon receiving such notice.

(b) Wrecking permit applicants required to submit an environmental mitigation plan pursuant to section 89.555 shall hold a meeting for neighbors at least five (5) calendar days before any wrecking begins on the permit site at an accessible location within three (3) miles of the permit site.

(Ord. No. 2025-056, § 4, 12-11-25)

children.title: Supervision by the building official
children.text: All wrecking of buildings or structures within the city shall be subject to the supervision of the building official and to such reasonable requirements and restrictions as may be imposed to minimize public safety hazards and nuisances. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Required wrecking procedures
children.text: The wrecking of any building or structure shall be complete and include the wrecking and removal of all foundations, footings, and floor slabs. All piping, heating plants, fuel storage tanks, appliances, and other such debris shall be removed from the premises. The excavation remaining after the removal of a building or structure shall be filled to the level of the surrounding grade with clean granular-type fill material to provide for proper drainage. The person doing the wrecking shall remove all steps, stoops, private sidewalks, accessory buildings, and hard-surface driveways unless such removal is specifically exempted by the building official. Further, the person doing the wrecking and filling shall provide a topping of soil of a sufficient depth and quality so as to enable ground cover to grow. Suitable groundcover shall be provided no later than ninety (90) days after permit issuance to comply with section 244.1570 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Protection of adjoining property
children.text: The licensed contractor responsible for the wrecking of any building or structure shall provide protection for adjoining public or private property. Protection of adjoining property shall comply with the International Building Code (IBC) Chapter 33. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Sidewalk cover
children.text: Whenever any building or structure two (2) stories or more in height abutting upon or within ten (10) feet of any public street within the city is to be wrecked, it shall be the duty of the person wrecking such building or structure, or of the owner thereof, to erect a good and substantial covering of heavy planking or timber decking, over the adjacent sidewalk, at least six (6) feet in width and ten (10) feet in height, to be approved by the building official. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Inspections required
children.text:
(a) For wrecking of any building or structure in the city that has been determined to meet one (1) or more of the qualifying criteria in section 89.555, additional inspections shall be performed by environmental inspectors from the Minneapolis Health Department to ensure that public nuisances are mitigated and the contractor is following the intent of the environmental mitigation plan.

(b) In addition to the inspections required for the wrecking process, a final inspection shall be required. Upon completion of the wrecking of any building or structure and any related work, the contractor responsible for the work shall request a final inspection to be completed by the city to ensure all work has been completed according to the requirements of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19; Ord. No. 2025-056, § 5, 12-11-25)

children.title: Prevention of nuisances
children.text: Each person engaged in the wrecking of any building or structure within the city shall conduct said work in such a manner as not to create a nuisance to persons on public streets or on neighboring property. Materials removed from the structure shall not be permitted to fall into streets, alleys or adjacent property or otherwise create a nuisance. All debris occasioned by such wrecking shall be thoroughly dampened with water so as to prevent the dust therefrom flying around the neighborhood. No wrecking work shall occur if wind speeds are above fifteen (15) miles per hour unless an emergency dictates that work must proceed. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19; Ord. No. 2025-056, § 6, 12-11-25)

children.title: Stop work orders
children.text: The building official may stop the work of the wrecking of any building or structure if it is determined that the work is being done in an unsafe manner or in violation of the requirements of this Code, in the opinion of the building official, by issuance of a stop work order. A stop work order may be issued to the responsible person, corporation, or other entity pursuant to section 85.120 of this Code. Any person, corporation, or other entity shall comply with the requirements of the stop order. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Continued violations
children.text: The continued violation of any provisions of this article may be considered a separate offense for each day such violation shall continue. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Definitions
children.text:
The following terms shall have the following definitions for the purpose of this article:

Additions. Any extension or expansion of an existing building footprint, including any increase of year-round habitable indoor space, occupancy or use.

Annual contour map. The map of noise contours depicting city blocks with homes that are within or touched by the DNL 60-64 contours based on noise contours developed annually pursuant to section 8.1(d) of the original consent decree and pursuant to the first amendment to consent decree or pursuant to any other legally binding document designed or intended to supplement or add to the noise mitigation required under the original consent decree.

Appurtenance. The visible, functional, or ornamental objects accessory to and part of a building not normally occupied by people including garages and accessory buildings; and other unconditioned spaces including screen porches, gazebos, decks.

Central air conditioning. An air conditioning system which uses ducts to distribute cooled and/or dehumidified air to more than one (1) room, or uses pipes to distribute chilled water to heat exchangers in more than one (1) room, and which is not plugged into a standard electrical outlet. With a typical split system, the compressor and condenser are located in an outdoor unit; the evaporator is mounted in the air handling unit (which is often a forced air furnace). With a package system, all components are located in a single outdoor unit that may be located on the ground or roof.

Consent decree. The consent decree signed on October 19, 2007, by Judge Stephen C. Aldrich of the Minnesota District Court, 4th Judicial District in that action entitled City of Minneapolis et al v. Metropolitan Airports Commission et al., the first amendment to consent decree, and any amendments thereto or any subsequent consent decree or other document designed or intended to supplement or add to the noise mitigation provided under the original consent decree, unless the context clearly indicates a different meaning.

dBA. A unit of sound pressure level weighted by use of the A metering characteristics and weighting as specified in the American national standards institute specification for sound level meters (ANSI S1.4-1983), which is hereby incorporated by reference. "dBA" is also referred to as an A-weighted decibel.

DNL. The day-night average level, or the twenty-four (24) hour equivalent continuous sound level (time averaged A-weighted sound level) from midnight to midnight, obtained after the addition of ten (10) dBA to sound levels measured from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.

First amendment to consent decree. The document that was entered into by the parties to the original Consent Decree in May 2013 and signed on September 25, 2013, by Judge Ivy S. Bernhardson of the Minnesota District Court, 4th Judicial District in that action entitled City of Minneapolis et al v. Metropolitan Airports Commission et al. which provides for additional noise mitigation based on the annual contour map.

Infill development. A vacant parcel or parcels of land proposed for development of uses similar to or less noise sensitive than the surrounding developed parcels including, but not limited to a new house on a vacant lot in a residential neighborhood.

Major development. A parcel of land greater than two and one-half (2.5) acres with existing structures which are proposed to be extensively rehabilitated or demolished for different uses. For example, demolition of an entire block of old residential, office and hotel buildings for new housing, office, commercial uses or conversion of warehouse to office and commercial uses.

Mechanical ventilation. Controlled, purposeful introduction of outdoor air to the conditioned space. The primary purpose of a whole-house mechanical ventilation system in a home is to provide, throughout the habitable and conditioned space, a controlled amount of unpolluted outside air for indoor pollutant dilution and removal, for the sensory satisfaction of occupants and to control interior moisture and indoor air quality.

New development. A vacant parcel or parcels of land in excess of one (1) acre or requested to be rezoned for development. For example, a residential subdivision, industrial park or shopping center.

Noise attenuation. The reduction in sound level which occurs between the source and receiver by means of construction methods and materials.

Reconstruction of existing structures. Replacing an existing building to accommodate the same use that existed before destruction or reconstruction, including indoor occupancy and use.

Sound transmission class (STC). A single number rating for describing the degree of sound transmission loss specified for a wall, window, partition or other building element based on laboratory testing. The higher the STC, the more attenuation the building element will afford. Sound transmission loss performance shall be tested per American Society of Testing Materials (ASTM) E90 and STC rating method per ASTM E413. The same data shall be used to determine the A-weighted Noise Level Reduction (ANLR). The testing laboratory shall be certified by the National Institute of Science and Technology's 'National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program' (NVLAP). (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Noise attenuation
children.text:
It is in the best interests of the city and of current and future residents that the integrity of all residential structures which have received a five (5) dB or other sound insulation package from the Metropolitan Airports Commission be maintained subject to the following:

(1) Noise attenuation required—Expansion. Whenever construction of a habitable addition to a dwelling unit is undertaken which expands the habitable area of a dwelling unit which had previously received a five (5) dB sound insulation package from the Metropolitan Airports Commission pursuant to the consent decree or pursuant to previous noise mitigation programs of the Metropolitan Airports Commission, the construction must include installation of central air conditioning or mechanical ventilation for the expanded area. Such construction shall utilize materials with a sound transmission class (STC) rating of at least forty (40) in order to achieve similar noise attenuation in the expansion of the structure as existed in the principal structure prior to expansion.

(2) Noise attenuation required—Infill or tear down/rebuild residential construction. Infill construction or rebuilding of residential structures after tearing down the original structure which takes place within blocks or between structures that had previously received a five (5) dB sound insulation package pursuant to the consent decree or pursuant to previous noise mitigation programs of the Metropolitan Airports Commission shall utilize building materials with a sound transmission class (STC) rating of at least forty (40) and shall include installation of central air conditioning or mechanical ventilation throughout the habitable areas of the structure.

(3) Requirement within the 60—62 contours. Construction of new single-family homes located in blocks or between structures that have received noise attenuation pursuant to the consent decree that are in the 60 to 62 DNL contours as defined in the consent decree shall include installation of central air conditioning or mechanical ventilation throughout the habitable portion of the structure.

(4) Requirement for multiple-family homes within the 60—64 contour. Construction of new multiple-family homes in blocks that have received noise attenuation pursuant to the consent decree or which are between structures which have received noise attenuation pursuant to the consent decree or pursuant to previous noise mitigation programs of the Metropolitan Airports Commission shall install central air conditioning or mechanical ventilation throughout the habitable portions of the structure. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Application of provisions
children.text: The provisions of section 119.20 shall apply to all new development, major redevelopment, infill development, construction and reconstruction of a building, and any habitable additions or expansions of an existing building requiring a building permit after January 1, 2009. This chapter shall not apply to remodeling or rehabilitation of an existing residential building; construction of decks, swimming pools, breezeways, three-season porches or the construction of an appurtenance to an existing residential building. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee procedure
children.text:
The fees established and set forth in this chapter shall be collected by the city before the issuance of any permit or any service to be provided for which fees are required under the provisions of Title 5 of this Code. Every person applying to the city for any permit or service under the provisions of Title 5 shall complete all forms furnished by the city for that purpose. All information required under this Code shall be provided by the applicant. Upon completion of the forms, the applicant shall sign the forms which shall be considered as a statement that the facts and representations therein made are true and correct, and that the applicant is the owner of the property where the work will be performed or has been authorized by the owner or the entity they represent to apply for such work. Upon such forms being submitted, completion of any required review by the city, and payment to the city by the applicant of the required fees, the building official shall authorize issuance of such permit. Work shall not begin until all fees have been paid and a valid permit has been issued. Work shall not proceed beyond the scope of an issued permit. The building official shall determine exemption from permit and fee requirements pursuant to federal and state law and this Code.

Information submitted by an applicant as to the extent of work, materials used or number of items used to calculate fees for permits shall be subject to review for accuracy. If it is found that fees were incorrectly calculated for any reason, a re-calculation of the fee shall be performed and any additional permit fees or penalty fees shall be paid by the applicant. The calculation of fees for permits may also be subject to review in the event the amount of a fee is questioned by the applicant. Modifications of fees shall be approved by the building official. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee refunds
children.text:
(a) Refunds of any permit-related fees collected by the city in accordance with Title 5 are as follows:

(1) Full refunds may be granted due to community planning and economic development (CPED) department errors.

(2) If none of the work authorized by a permit has started, a fifty dollar ($50.00) processing fee will be retained by the city. The remainder of the fees will be refunded to the permit applicant.

(3) If any of the work authorized by a permit has started, the department may retain a percentage of the fee for such permit equal to the percentage of work completed in addition to the processing fee.

(b) All claims for refunds of permit fees in accordance with this section shall be made to the building official within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the payment of said fees.

(c) The building official shall cause to be placed in the office where permits are to be obtained notices of such size and readability that persons making application for permits and paying the fees therefor shall be notified of the refund policies of the department.

(d) Refunds due under the foregoing provisions shall be made upon written request of the permit applicant. The city finance officer shall refund such monies by issuing a check to the applicant for the refund amount due, upon receipt of a check request approved by the building official. Said request shall contain the name and address of the permit applicant, the permit number, and the amount of refund due under this section. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Minimum fee
children.text: For any work to be done for which a permit is required, and for which a fee has not been established by some other section of this Code, statute, rule or ordinance, the minimum fee shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Working without a permit
children.text: Should any person begin work for which a permit from the city is required by this Code without having secured the necessary permit therefor from the city, that person, when subsequently securing such permit, may be required to pay an investigation and/or penalty fee provided for such permit, and shall be subject to all the penal provisions of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: State surcharge
children.text: A state surcharge shall be required for permits issued pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Chapter 326B. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Plan review fee for other than building permits
children.text: When a plan is required for review as part of the submittal for permits other than building permits, a plan review fee may be required. The plan review fee shall be calculated as up to sixty-five (65) percent of the calculated permit fee and shall be in addition to any other required fees. The plan review fee for building permits shall be pursuant to section 91.230 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Inspection fee
children.text: A portion of the fees paid for a permit normally cover the cost of inspector time to perform inspections. When inspections are required and are not provided for by a permit fee, the fee for those inspections shall be as established herein. The fee for inspections of a transitory project, including but not limited to carnivals, festivals, and special events, for other inspections to be performed during hours other than the normal working hours established by the city, for any inspection requested when no permit is issued, or for any inspection requested or required for which no specific fee is otherwise established shall be based on an hourly fee as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code, including any minimum specified fee, such fees to be paid by the contractor, building owner or agent, or any other person requesting the inspection before any inspections are performed. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Re-inspection fee
children.text: Any person doing work, for which a permit has been issued, in a manner so as to require additional inspections over and above the normal inspections required by the building code and its amendments, shall be required to pay a re-inspection fee as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code for each and every additional inspection required to be made until all such work is found to be in compliance with the applicable code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Temporary certificate of occupancy fee
children.text: The fee for a temporary certificate of occupancy shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Title 5 fee schedule established; annual adjustments
children.text: The city shall publish, maintain and make available to the public via all readily available means a schedule of all such fees referenced in Title 5. Such schedule shall be known as the Title 5 fee schedule and shall be updated by the building official on April 1 of each year. Any update that changes fees in the Title 5 fee schedule shall be determined by using established cost index standards including but not limited to the construction cost index (CCI), the consumer price index (CPI), and any other such standard used for construction or consumer cost estimating. Different adjustments may be made to the various fees in the Title 5 fee schedule if the city determines that such differences are justified. Adjustments to the Title 5 fee schedule shall be made available to the public a minimum of thirty (30) days before becoming effective. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.heading: ARTICLE II.
children.title: BUILDING PERMIT AND PLAN REVIEW FEES
Definitions
children.text: For the purposes of calculating fees, building work shall mean any work that includes but is not limited to excavation, concrete, steel, wood, plastic, insulation, glass, roof covering, finishing, wrecking, moving, and other materials or activities common in construction. Specific definitions of building work can be found in Minn. Rule 1300.0050 including but not limited to Chapters 1305, 1309, 1311, 1322, 1323, and 1341. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: The building official, before issuing any permit for building work, shall require the payment by the applicant for such permit of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for building permits
children.text:
For any permit for the construction, alteration, addition, repair, wrecking or moving of a structure regulated by the building code, the fee charged shall be based on the value of the work to be performed. The valuation determination shall be pursuant to the building code. The fee charged shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code based on the following valuation categories:

Valuation Categories

$1.00 to $500.00

$501.00 to $2,000.00

$2,001.00 to $25,000.00

$25,001.00 to $50,000.00

$50,001.00 to $100,000.00

$100,001.00 to $500,000.00

$500,001.00 to $1,000,000.00

$1,000,001.00 and up.

(Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for building permit plan review
children.text: For any proposed building work that requires a plan to be submitted and reviewed, a plan review fee shall be required to be paid at the time of payment for the building permit. The plan review fee shall be calculated as sixty-five (65) percent of the building permit fee determined in section 91.220 of this Code. The plan review fee for permits other than building permits shall be pursuant to section 91.60. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fees to state of Minnesota
children.text: Electrical permits are issued by the state of Minnesota. Fees shall be paid to the state according to the current state fee schedule. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.heading: ARTICLE IV.
children.title: RESERVED
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (7) ---

Editor's note— Ord. No. 2021-007, § 3, adopted Feb. 26, 2021, repealed Art. IV, §§ 91.400—91.430, which pertained to elevator and conveyance device permit fees and derived from Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19.

children.title: Definitions
children.text: For the purposes of calculating fees, mechanical work shall mean any work that includes fuel gas, heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, refrigeration or high-pressure piping, including any equipment and accessories, regulated by the building code. Definitions for specific mechanical terminology can be found in Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050 including but not limited to Chapters 1346 and 5230. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: The building official, before issuing any permit for mechanical work, shall require the payment by the applicant for such permit of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for gas burner permits
children.text:
(a) For any permit for installing mechanical equipment with a gas burner regulated by the building code including but not limited to boilers, furnaces, kitchen appliances, water heaters, fireplaces, and process equipment, the fee charged shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code for each device included in such permit based on the following categories:

Input

Not exceeding 399,999 Btu.

400,000 Btu and over.

(b) Where more than one (1) gas burner or multiple gas burners are to be installed in a single gas burning device, they shall, for purposes of establishing permit fees therefore, be considered as a single burner with the fee based on the combined total Btu capacity.

(c) For any permit for alterations or repairs to any existing gas burner or gas burner equipment or the installation of piping for a propane tank, or for any permit for gas piping, the fee shall be based on the valuation table contained in section 91.530 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning permits
children.text:
The building official, before issuing any permit for the construction, installation, alteration, addition or repair of any furnace, boiler, heating or power plant or system, or any device or equipment connected therewith, or for any other device connected or to be connected with any chimney or stack, or for the construction, installation, alteration, addition or repair of any air-conditioning system or ventilation system or sheet metal ductwork or equipment connected therewith, shall require the payment by the applicant for such permit of the fee or fees in the amount established herein. Such permit fees shall be published and maintained in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code and shall be based on the following valuation categories:

Not exceeding $50,000.00.

$50,001.00 and over.

The fee for heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning work in existing one- and two-family dwellings shall be fixed according to the fee established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for refrigeration system permits
children.text:
The building official, before issuing any permit for the construction or installation of a new refrigeration system, shall require the payment by the applicant for such permit of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code based on the following categories:

Not exceeding 36,000 Btu.

Each additional 36,000 Btu or fraction thereof.

(Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for alterations to existing refrigeration systems
children.text: The fee for alterations, additions, and repairs to existing refrigeration systems shall be based on the valuation table established in section 91.530 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Permit fees for mechanical work utilizing alternative sources of energy
children.text: The building official, before issuing any permit for the construction, installation, alteration, addition or repair of any regulated mechanical system or equipment which utilizes an alternative source of energy, shall require the payment by the applicant for such permit of the fee or fees in the amount herein established. The fee shall be determined by the building official. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Definitions
children.text: For the purposes of calculating fees, plumbing work shall include work that is regulated by the building code. Specific definitions of plumbing terminology can be found in Minn. Rule Part 1300.0050 including but not limited to Chapter 4714 and Minn. Statutes, Chapter 326B. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: The building official, before issuing any permit for the installation of any plumbing, plumbing system, plumbing fixture, plumbing appliance, or plumbing appurtenance, shall require the payment by the applicant of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee calculation for plumbing permits
Fee calculation for other plumbing alterations
children.text: For any plumbing alteration work not covered by an established fee, the fee shall be calculated by using the mechanical HVAC permit valuation table in section 91.530 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: The building official, before issuing any certificate of code compliance or making any prerequisite inspection, shall require the payment by the applicant for such certificate of code compliance of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: One- and two-family dwellings
children.text: The fee for a one- or two-family dwelling shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Multiple-family dwellings
children.text: The fee for multiple-family dwellings such as apartment buildings, shared-bath dwellings, rooming houses, boardinghouses, dormitories, fraternity and sorority houses, any building containing combinations of the above types of occupancy, and other similar type buildings shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code for the first dwelling, shared-bath or rooming unit, plus an additional fee as specified for each additional dwelling or shared-bath unit, and a separate specified fee for each additional rooming unit. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Commercial or industrial buildings
children.text: The fee for commercial or industrial buildings shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code for the first one thousand (1,000) square feet, or fraction thereof, of floor area, plus an additional specified fee for each additional one thousand (1,000) square feet of floor area, or fraction thereof. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee for temporary certificate of code compliance
children.text: The fee for any temporary certificate of code compliance shall be as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code, and compliance with section 87.140 of this Code shall be required. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: The building official, before issuing any permit for the installation, removal, replacement, relocation, or maintenance of any regulated backflow assembly, shall require the payment by the applicant of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Fee required
children.text: The building official, before issuing any parking ramp operating certificate, shall require the payment by the applicant of the fee or fees established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Returned check fee
children.text: For each check returned as nonnegotiable due to insufficient funds, closed account or other reason, a returned check fee shall be collected together with the face amount of the returned check pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Section 604.113, subd. 2(a), as amended. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Penalty fee
children.text: Violations of the requirements of this Code shall be subject to a determination of the applicability of a penalty fee as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Investigation fee
children.text: Investigations required due to violations of the requirements of this Code shall be subject to a determination of the applicability of an investigation fee as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Request for service fee
children.text: A request for service that is not covered by any other established fee shall be subject to a determination of the applicability of a request for service fee as established in the Title 5 fee schedule pursuant to section 91.100 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Sewer service availability fee
children.text: A service availability charge (SAC) shall be collected for each building permit when so required by the Metropolitan Council Environmental Services Division pursuant to Resolution 2010R-239 of the City Council of the City of Minneapolis. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Street permit fee
children.text:
(a) The city, before issuing any permit for the use or occupancy of any street pursuant to section 430.30 of this Code or otherwise as required by this Code shall require the payment by the applicant for such permit of a fee as established pursuant to this Code.

(b) No person shall place or allow to be placed on any street, boulevard or alley any container which has a capacity of more than five (5) cubic feet, and which is designed or utilized for the collection of building debris, solid waste or any other material without first obtaining the appropriate permit. The permit shall be attached to the exterior of the container with a copy retained by the permit holder and as otherwise required by section 89.30 of this Code, if applicable.

(1) Permits for solid waste containers may only be issued to those persons licensed as a Minneapolis Solid Waste Hauler as required by section 225.290 of this Code or as a Class A or B wrecker of buildings as required by section 277.2270 of this Code.

(c) Permits for storage containers may only be issued to the company which is responsible for the delivery and pickup of the storage container.

(1) Storage containers shall mean a storage container that is contracted to be delivered to a residence and used to store personal items and then picked up by a hauler and stored at a facility until it is requested to be delivered back to the residence so that the personal items may be retrieved or a storage container that is used for the purpose of moving personal items from or to a residence as part of a change of residence. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.title: Utility location fee
children.text: When any work for which a permit is required pursuant to the building code is to include any excavation as defined in the Minnesota One-Call Excavation Notice System pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Chapter 216D, there shall be paid, in addition to all other permit fees for the work, a surcharge pursuant to Chapter 91 of this Code to compensate the city in respect to its locating and marking of utilities pursuant to Minn. Statutes, Chapter 216D. (Ord. No. 2019-034, § 1, 8-23-19)

children.heading: CHAPTER 95.
children.title: PROJECTIONS AND ENCROACHMENTS
children.text:
