children.title: Purpose and policy statement
children.text:
The City of Minneapolis declares that the rights to self-determination, bodily autonomy, and access to gender-affirming and reproductive healthcare are fundamental human rights. Protecting the lives and rights of Two-Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, and the other identities and experiences that fit within these communities (collectively "2SLGBTQIA+") is necessary for the city's public peace, health, and safety. The city has a long history of welcoming the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, and 2SLGBTQIA+ people will always be welcomed, loved, and appreciated in Minneapolis. The city's civil rights ordinance banned discrimination based on sexual orientation in 1974. In 1975, the city amended its civil rights ordinance and became the first city in the United States to ban discrimination based on gender identity.

In 2022 the city and in 2023 the State of Minnesota issued executive orders to protect and support the rights of Minnesota's 2SLGBTQIA+ community members to safely seek and receive gender affirming healthcare services. Our 2SLGBTQIA+ community members both locally and nationally continue to be negatively impacted by the proliferation of executive and legislative attacks that perpetuate a culture of discrimination, harassment, and barriers to equal opportunities for the community.

Studies suggest that 2SLGBTQIA+ people are over-represented in Minnesota's unhoused population. 2SLGBTQIA+ over-representation increases to almost one-quarter for youth experiencing homelessness.

Minneapolis is home to people from diverse racial, ethnic, and gender identities and backgrounds and a place of refuge for people coming from places that do not have the same policies and protections. All residents and visitors, regardless of their gender identity, expression, or medical history, are valued and integral to our social, cultural, and economic community. The city is unwavering in its ongoing commitment to creating a welcoming and respectful atmosphere where everyone is accepted, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity, and sexual orientation. To further this commitment, the city values equal protection and equitable treatment for all residents and visitors. The city rejects and condemns in the strongest possible terms the horrific and discriminatory efforts to use government to erase the identity of 2SLGBTQIA+ people and drive them out of public life.

The city prioritizes using its limited resources to improve the health and safety of its residents and visitors. Gender-affirming care takes many forms, is evidence-based, and supported by peer-reviewed science and the lived experiences of transgender and gender expansive people. The city firmly rejects any attempts to weaponize government resources to disenfranchise or criminalize individuals for seeking or providing life-saving care that is legal in Minnesota. (Ord. No. 2026-019, § 1, 6-25-26)

children.title: Gender-Affirming and Intersex Care
children.text:
(a) Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following definitions apply:

(1) Gender-Affirming Care means all medical, surgical, counseling, or referral services, including telehealth services, that an individual may receive to support and affirm the individual's gender identity or gender expression and that are legal under the laws of Minnesota.

(2) Intersex Care means all medical, surgical, counseling, or referral services, including telehealth services, that an individual may receive related to natural differences or variations in sex characteristics or reproductive anatomy and that are legal under the laws of Minnesota.

(b) The city is a safe-haven for gender-affirming and intersex care. The city acknowledges that minors living independently may consent to their own gender-affirming or intersex care. No city personnel may use a person's age or parental status as a basis to cooperate with anyone seeking to prevent or punish legal healthcare.

(c) Unless required by law, city employees, representatives, and contractors may not use city facilities, property, moneys, equipment, data technology (e.g. license plate recognition, surveillance video, computers) ("city resources"), or city personnel to interfere with the ability of any person to receive gender-affirming or intersex care, to interfere with the ability of any person to advocate for another person to receive gender-affirming care, or for enforcing federal laws that prevent or limit gender-affirming or intersex care.

(d) Unless required by law, city personnel may not disclose any private data, medical information, or surveillance data, including but not limited to traffic or security camera footage, regarding a person's gender-affirming or intersex care.

(e) The city will not enter into any agreements requiring it to share data or resources to interfere with, enforce bans upon, or criminalize gender-affirming or intersex care.

(f) To the extent permitted by law, the city's employee health insurance plan must offer coverage for all eligible city employees and their dependents that includes gender-affirming care benefits.

(g) The administration must ensure that the city's employee health insurance plan offers coverage that addresses the healthcare needs of the intersex community. (Ord. No. 2026-019, § 1, 6-25-26)

children.title: City funds, facilities, and data
Outreach and engagement
children.text:
(a) The administration must report annually to the appropriate committee of the city council on its outreach and engagement efforts to the 2SLGBTQIA+ community. The report should include at a minimum a description of the administration's outreach and engagement efforts and any metrics on the effectiveness and results of those efforts.

(b) After the report is presented to the city council, the commission on civil rights must review the annual report.

(c) If the City Council creates an advisory body that focuses on the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, that body must review the annual report after the report is presented to the city council and may provide the administration, the city council, and the public with feedback on the report and the administration's outreach and engagement efforts. (Ord. No. 2026-019, § 1, 6-25-26)

children.title: Complaints, discipline, and reporting
children.text:
(a) Violations of sections 145.20 or 145.30 (d) of this chapter by employees are subject to disciplinary action.

(b) Summary data about the number and disposition of complaints must be reported to the city council by June 30 and December 31 each year.

(c) If a complaint is filed alleging a violation of sections 145.20 or 145.30 (d), in the course of investigating the alleged violation, no complainant or witness may be compelled by the city investigating authority to provide their gender identity or sexual orientation.

(d) The city must preserve all data related to complaints under this section for at least twelve (12) months after the complaint is closed.

(e) The administration must ensure there is a mechanism for the public to report alleged violations of this chapter by employees. (Ord. No. 2026-019, § 1, 6-25-26)

children.heading: Title 8
children.title: CONSUMER PROTECTION
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (1) ---

Cross reference— Truth in sale of housing, Ch. 248; licenses and business regulations, Title 13; misrepresentation of permitted uses of real estate, property or structure, § 385.250; false advertising with respect to gasoline, § 385.330; advertising sexual remedies, § 385.360.

State Law reference— Regulation of manufacturers and sales, M.S. Ch. 325D.

children.title: Method of sale of commodities generally
Method of sale of meat, poultry, cheese and seafood
children.text: All meat, meat products, poultry (whole or parts), cheese and all seafood, except shellfish, offered for sale or sold as food, shall be offered for sale or sold by weight. Meat, poultry, cheese or seafood combined with or associated with some other food element or elements to form either a distinctive food product or a food combination shall be sold by weight, and the quantity representation may be the total weight of the product or combination. This section shall not apply to prepared meat, poultry, cheese or seafood sold for immediate consumption on or off the premises. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.020)

children.title: Method of sale of packages
children.text:
Commodities in package form offered or displayed for sale to the public shall bear on the outside of the package a definite, plain and conspicuous declaration of the:

(1) Identity of the commodity in the package, unless the same can easily be identified through the wrapper or container;

(2) Net quantity of the contents in terms of weight, measure or count, and not qualified by any term tending to exaggerate the amount of quantity in the package; and

(3) In the case of any package offered or displayed for sale, or sold any place other than on the premises where packed, the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.030)

children.title: Declarations of unit price at random
children.text: In addition to the declarations required by section 152.30, any commodity in package form, the package being one of a lot containing random weights, measures or counts of the same commodity and bearing the total selling price of the package, shall bear on the outside of the package a plain and conspicuous declaration of the price per single unit of weight, measure or count. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.040)

children.title: Unit pricing of commodities
children.text:
(a) No person shall sell or offer or expose for sale at retail any commodity as defined in subsection (b) herein, unless a unit price label containing a description of the item, the selling price, the quantity, and the unit price is affixed by attachment of a stamp, tag or label directly adjacent to the commodity on the display shelf, or on the commodity itself; except where the commodity is not in a conspicuously visible place, a list bearing such price information shall be placed near the place of procurement. "Unit price" means the price per usual unit of quantity of a commodity expressed to the nearest one-tenth of one cent.

(b) The following commodities are governed by the provisions of this section:

(1) Canned, bottled and frozen vegetables.

(2) Canned, bottled and frozen fruits.

(3) Canned, bottled, real and imitation, vegetable and fruit juices.

(4) Frozen vegetable and fruit juice concentrates.

(5) Canned and bottled baby foods.

(6) Cooking and salad oils, and shortening.

(7) Canned and bottled fish and meats.

(8) Canned and bottled tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, tomato puree and other related tomato products.

(9) Ketchups, mustards and other sauces.

(10) Jams, jellies and preserves.

(11) Peanut butter and sandwich spreads.

(12) Flour and sugar.

(13) Coffee, instant and regular, and cocoa and tea.

(14) Dog and cat foods.

(15) Breakfast cereals and instant breakfast foods.

(16) Macaroni, spaghetti and other dry pasta products (does not include prepared convenience pasta foods).

(17) Salad dressings.

(18) Dishwashing and laundry soaps and detergents.

(19) Scouring powders.

(20) Dentifrices, mouthwashes, deodorants, bath soaps, shampoos.

(21) Household cleaning products.

(c) This section does not apply to any brand of any regulated commodity unless there are two (2) or more sizes of the same quality of that brand sold or offered or exposed for sale at an establishment.

(d) This section does not apply to an establishment with total retail sales of less than seven hundred fifty thousand dollars ($750,000.00) per year. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.050)

children.title: Misleading packages
children.text: No commodity in package form shall be so wrapped, nor shall it be in a container so made, formed or filled as to mislead the purchaser as to quantity of the contents of the package, and the contents of a container shall not fall below such reasonable standard of fill. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.060)

children.title: Advertising packages for sale
children.text: Whenever a commodity in package form is advertised in any manner and the retail price of the package is stated in the advertisement, there shall be closely and conspicuously associated with such statement of price a declaration of the basic quantity of contents of the package as is required by this chapter to appear on the package; provided that where the law or regulation requires a dual declaration of net quantity to appear on the package, only the declaration that sets forth the quantity in terms of the smaller unit of weight or measure (the declaration that is required to appear first and without parentheses on the package) need appear in the advertisement; and provided further that there shall not be included as part of the declaration required under this section such qualifying terms as "when packed," "minimum," "not less than," or any other terms of similar import; nor any term qualifying a unit of weight, measure or count (for example: "jumbo," "giant," "full," and the like), that tends to exaggerate the amount of commodity in the package. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.070)

children.title: Misleading advertisements prohibited
children.text:
(a) No person shall advertise or cause to be advertised in any newspaper or other publication, or any advertising device, or by any other manner or means whatever, any assertion, representation or statement of fact, concerning real or personal property or services, professional or otherwise, or concerning any circumstances or matter of fact connected with the proposed performance or disposition thereof, which is untrue or misleading and which is known, or which, by the exercise of reasonable care, should be known to be untrue or misleading.

(b) No person shall, by means of exaggerated variations in the comparative size, location or position of letters, figures or other markings or characters on any price tag, sign, poster, notice, display or advertisement or other public representation of any nature whatsoever, mislead or deceive, or attempt to mislead or deceive, the public, as to the true nature, price, quantity, quality, brand or character of any goods, wares, merchandise, service, facilities or accommodations, or as to the nature of, or the reason, if any is offered, for the sale or offering for sale, so being made to the public.

(c) No person shall advertise property or services for sale with the word "wholesale" when the property or services are available for purchase by the general public.

(d) No person shall advertise or otherwise represent to the public in any manner whatsoever:

(1) A representation of brand, quality, quantity, trade name or other character of any property or services that is untrue or misleading; or

(2) A sale or gift or an offer for sale or gift of any property or services which is contingent upon the concurrent purchase of any other property or service, unless clearly spelled out in the advertising.

(e) This section does not apply to any publisher of a newspaper, magazine or other publication, or the owner or operator of a radio or television station, or any other owner or operator of a medium primarily devoted to advertising, who publishes, broadcasts or otherwise disseminates an advertisement in good faith without knowledge of its false, deceptive or misleading character. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.080)

children.title: Exempt commodities
children.text: Any commodity which is regulated by a federal or state law or regulation relating to the subject matters of the preceding sections of this chapter shall be exempted from those provisions. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.090)

children.title: Meat advertising; USDA marking requirements
Complete price; representations; official terms
children.text:
No person shall advertise or otherwise represent to the public in any manner whatsoever:

(a) A price or price reference of a commodity, service or other thing of value unless such price representation is the complete cash purchase price, which shall be unconditioned and include all charges except taxes levied at the retail level. The prominence or emphasis of the complete price shall be primary to any other related price quotations such as a payment or trade provision.

(b) A representation in any manner of brand, quality, quantity, trade name, or other character of any property or service that is untrue or misleading.

(c) Terms such as "Public Notice," "Public Sale," "Ordered Sold," or other similar phrase, unless there is an official act by a governmental agency concerning the subject or application for such terms. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.110)

children.title: Misrepresentation of price
children.text: Whenever any commodity or service is sold, or is offered, exposed or advertised for sale, by weight, measure or count, the price shall not be misrepresented, nor shall the price be represented in any manner calculated or tending to mislead or deceive an actual or prospective purchaser. Whenever an advertised, posted or labeled price per unit of weight, measure or count includes a fraction of a cent, all elements of the fraction shall be prominently displayed and the numeral or numerals expressing the fraction shall be immediately adjacent to and of the same general design and style as, and at least one-half the height and width of, the numeral representing the whole cents. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.120)

children.title: Scales for checkweighing of prepackaged commodities required
children.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to prepackage and sell food products at retail on the store premises without providing an accessible price computing scale for customer checkweighing usage or to refuse to reweigh such food product in the presence of a prospective customer when so requested. Decimal pound conversion charts or tables shall be provided where markings on packages are designated in the decimal system showing equivalents of the decimal pounds (100 divisions) to be customary ounce divisions, reduced to quarter-ounce fractions thereof (64 divisions). (Code 1960, As Amend., § 838.130)

children.title: Sale of garbage cans; notice required
children.text: No person shall offer for sale any receptacle designed for holding garbage or trash, of a capacity of at least twenty (20) gallons and less than one hundred (100) gallons without displaying next to that receptacle a sign measuring not less than one foot by one foot, on which is written in a legible manner the following: "Minneapolis Code section 225.580 requires that all garbage cans for outdoor use be made of metal, have tightfitting covers, have two (2) side handles, and have a capacity of thirty-two (32) gallons or less." (78-Or-134, § 1, 7-28-78)

children.title: Sale of household batteries; notice required
children.text:
(a) No person shall offer for sale any household battery without displaying on the portion of the shelf or display rack on which such battery is displayed a printed sign plainly visible to customers which reads as follows:

"The improper disposal of used batteries is an environmental hazard. Used batteries should be deposited in Minneapolis recycling containers in a separate transparent plastic bag or in containers located at local police stations, fire stations, or park buildings."

(b) For purposes of this section, the term "household battery" shall mean and include disposable or rechargeable dry cells commonly used as power sources for household or consumer products including, but not limited to, nickel-cadmium, alkaline, mercuric oxide, silver oxide, zinc oxide, lithium and carbon zinc batteries, but excluding lead acid batteries.

(c) This section shall take effect thirty (30) days after the date that the city institutes and operates a program for the collection of discarded household batteries. Prior notice of the effective date of this section shall be published and broadcast in the printed and broadcast media.

(d) This section shall be deemed repealed and of no further force and effect at such time as the city, having instituted and operated a program for the collection of household batteries, terminates such program and ceases to collect such batteries. (90-Or-142, § 1, 5-25-90; 90-Or-240, § 1, 9-14-90)

children.title: Established
children.text: There is hereby established a consumer affairs division under the supervision of the licensing official, who shall serve as director. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.010; Pet. No. 250069, § 2, 8-11-89; 2013-Or-132, § 1, 12-6-13)

children.title: Authority to investigate and enforce
children.text: The director shall receive and investigate all consumer complaints regarding violations of Chapters 152, 156 and 158. The investigation shall include inquiries of the alleged violator. In addition, the consumer affairs division may investigate and enforce the provisions of said chapters. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.020; Ord. of 6-28-74, § 1)

children.title: Authority to issue violation tags
children.text: All duly appointed inspectors assigned to the division are empowered, authorized and directed to issue violation tags for violations of the following provisions: Sections 152.10, 152.50, 152.70, 152.100—152.130, 158.70 and 152.150. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.020; Ord. of 6-28-74, § 1; 89-Or-226, § 1, 11-22-89)

children.title: Notice of complaint
children.text: If the director, after investigation of a consumer complaint, believes a probable violation exists, he or she shall serve personally, or by registered mail, a notice of complaint on the alleged violator. Said notice shall set forth the acts complained of and shall inform the respondent of his or her right to a settlement hearing before the director or the director's designee. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.020; Ord. of 6-28-74, § 1; Pet. No. 250069, § 3, 8-11-89)

children.title: Settlement
children.text: If the dispute can be conciliated, such settlement shall include written assurance of the discontinuance of any act or practice in violation of Chapters 152, 156 or 158, and may include restitution to consumers of money, property or other things received from them in connection with a violation of those chapters. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.020; Ord. of 6-28-74, § 1)

children.title: Findings of director
children.text: The director, if no settlement is made, shall make findings based upon his or her investigation and hearing, if held. A copy of said findings shall be served by registered mail on the respondent. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.020; Ord. of 6-28-74, § 1; Pet. No. 250069, § 4, 8-11-89)

children.title: Referral for prosecution
children.text: The director shall, upon finding that a violation exists, refer his or her findings to the city attorney for prosecution. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 839.020; Ord. of 6-28-74, § 1; Pet. No. 250069, § 5, 8-11-89)

children.heading: CHAPTER 156.
children.title: DECEPTIVE PRACTICES
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (2) ---

State Law reference— Deceptive trade practices, M.S. § 325D.43 et seq.

children.title: Definitions
Acts prohibited
children.text: No person shall act, use or employ any deception, fraud, false pretense, false promise, misrepresentation, misleading statement or deceptive practice, or omit any material fact, with the intent that others rely thereon, in connection with the sale, lease, rental or loan of any goods or services, whether or not any consumer has in fact been misled, deceived or damaged thereby. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 837.020)

children.title: Suspension or revocation of license
children.text: Any trade or activity license issued by the city to a person who violates any provision of this chapter, when engaged in such trade or activity, may be revoked or suspended by the city council. Such revocation or suspension is in addition to any other penalty imposed for violation of this Code. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 837.030)

children.title: "Repairs" defined
children.text: As used in this chapter, "repairs" includes mechanical repairs, alterations, maintenance and the additions of equipment, supplies or parts to any type of item including, but not limited to, motor vehicles, appliances, homes and furniture. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.010)

children.title: Acts prohibited
children.text: No person shall knowingly charge for any services which are not actually performed in repairing an item or knowingly misinform a customer concerning what is wrong with the item or fraudulently substitute parts when such substitution has no relation to the repairing or servicing of the item. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.020)

children.title: Estimate required
Detailed invoice required
children.text: All work done by a person engaged in the business of making repairs shall be recorded on an invoice with the name and address of the business thereon, detailing and describing all services or work performed and all parts supplied and the exact charge for each part or service. In addition, if any used or rebuilt parts are supplied, the invoice shall clearly identify such part and state that fact. One copy of such invoice shall be given to the customer upon completion of the repair work. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.040; Ord. of 5-30-75, § 2)

children.title: Notification of customer of additional charges
children.text: In the event that a determination is made that the actual charges for the repairs to be made will exceed the total written estimate for repairs given under section 158.30, by the sum of ten (10) per cent of the total written estimate, the customer shall be immediately notified by telephone, telegram, mail or written notice of the new estimate charges. Such notification shall be at the expense of the person engaged in the business of making repairs. A customer so notified may authorize the repairs based upon the new estimate charges or may cancel the order for repairs. When the repairs are authorized a revised estimate shall be provided the customer; provided, the parties may agree that the repair work may commence prior to receipt of the revised estimate. If the order for repair is canceled by the customer the unrepaired or partially repaired item shall be released immediately, in reasonable like condition as and where received for repair and upon payment of whatever charge is imposed for the release of the unrepaired item in an amount not to exceed the estimate therefor, as provided in section 158.30 if such estimate was included in the written estimate of repairs. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.050)

children.title: Failure to notify of additional charges
children.text: In the event the customer is not notified of any additional charges for repair, the repaired item must be released upon payment by the customer of not more than an amount equal to the original written estimate plus ten (10) per cent of the original written estimate. In no event shall a customer be required to pay more than the above amount if the customer did not receive notification of a change in the estimate. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.060; Pet. No. 250069, § 7, 8-11-89)

children.title: Notice to customers to be posted
children.text:
All business establishments which engage in making repairs shall post, in a conspicuous place, a sign measuring not less than one foot by one foot, written in a legible manner as follows:

Under the provisions of Minneapolis Code of Ordinances, Chapter 158, a customer may request a written estimate before repair work is begun. This business must comply with the terms of that chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.070)

children.title: Deceptive practices
children.text:
It is an unlawful deceptive practice for anyone engaged in the business of making repairs to:

(a) Fail, in the case of an in-shop repair, to secure a signed work order from the customer to repair a specific item and deliver a copy of the signed work order to the customer, before repair work is begun;

(b) Fail, in the case of an in-home service call where the customer has initially contacted the repair supplier, to disclose, before the repairman goes to the customer's home, if a service or minimum charge will be imposed, and the amount of such charge, even though no repairs may be effected;

(c) Fail, in the case of an in-shop repair, to offer to deliver to the customer any part(s) replaced. Exhibit and tender of a replaced part to the customer is sufficient where the part:

(1) Is too large to be easily moved; or

(2) Must be returned to the manufacturer if the customer wishes to take advantage of a parts warranty; or

(3) Can be rebuilt and the repairman purchases it from the customer for that purpose. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 840.080; Ord. of 5-30-75, § 3; Pet. No. 250069, § 8, 8-11-89)

children.heading: CHAPTER 160.
children.title: WEIGHTS AND MEASURES
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (3) ---

Charter reference— Authority to provide for city sealers, inspectors, weighers and gaugers, Ch. 4, § 5(24).

Cross reference— Ordinance violations bureau to assist court in disposing of violations of Code relating to weights and measures and procedure in case of such violations, Ch. 26.

State Law reference— Weights and measures generally, M.S. Ch. 239.

children.title: Minnesota standards adopted
children.text:
The standards of weights and measures for the city shall be those prescribed by the statutes of Minnesota. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.010)

Cross reference— Standard bread loaf, § 192.20.

children.title: Devices to conform to standards
children.text: No person shall use, maintain or operate, in measuring or weighing any commodity or article of merchandise, any weight, measure, scale-beam, patent balance, steelyard or other instrument that is not conformable to the standards of this state, or use in weighing as aforesaid any scale-beam, patent balance, steelyard or other instrument that is out of order or incorrect, or that does not balance. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.030)

children.title: Misrepresentation of weight or measure
children.text: No person shall sell or offer for sale any commodity or article of merchandise in any quantity of less weight, or measure, or enumeration than the weight, or measure, or enumeration represented by the vendor upon such sale or offer for sale. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.020)

children.title: Duty to submit devices for inspection
children.text: No person maintaining or operating weights, measures, scale-beams, patent balances, steelyards or other instruments shall refuse to exhibit the same to employees of the director of the consumer affairs division authorized to perform the duties of deputy weighmasters or inspectors of weights and measures, for the purpose of inspection or examination when such officials request exhibition of same for the purpose of inspection or examination. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.040; 2013-Or-133, § 1, 12-6-13)

children.title: General powers and duties of inspectors
children.text: The said inspectors of the consumer affairs division shall be special police officers and shall from time to time weigh or measure and inspect packages or amounts of commodities of whatever kind kept within the corporate limits of the city for the purpose of sale or in the process of delivery in the city, in order to determine whether the same contain the amounts represented and whether they are offered for sale or sold in accordance with the statutes of the State of Minnesota or ordinances of the city in relation to weights and measures. Such inspectors may, for the purposes above mentioned, and in the general performance of their official duties, enter and go into or upon any stand, place or premises, or stop any vehicle or conveyance delivering any commodity and require the person in charge thereof, if necessary, to go to some convenient place which the inspectors may specify for the purpose of making proper test. The inspectors shall enforce the ordinances of the city and the statutes of Minnesota regulating the size, weight and loads of motor vehicles. The inspectors may arrest, with or without formal warrant, any violator of the statutes of Minnesota or ordinances of the city in relation to weights or measures. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.050; 99-Or-003, § 1, 1-8-99; 2013-Or-133, § 2, 12-6-13)

children.title: Confiscation of foodstuffs
children.text: The inspectors may seize, with or without formal warrant, any food exposed or offered for sale, or had in possession with intent to sell, contrary to the provisions of the statutes of the State of Minnesota or ordinances of the city. Any food offered or exposed for sale contrary to the provisions of said statutes or ordinances shall be subject to confiscation, and the inspector, in all cases where the owner or person in possession thereof has been convicted of violating any law or ordinance relating to the sale of foodstuffs in quantities less than represented by the seller thereof, shall deliver to the city council, for the use and benefit of the poor of the city, all such articles of foodstuffs so taken or seized by them. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.060)

children.title: Interfering with inspectors
children.text: No person shall, in any way, hinder, impede or obstruct the inspectors of the consumer affairs division in the performance of their official duties. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.070; 2013-Or-133, § 3, 12-6-13)

children.title: General regulations concerning scales
children.text: Hanging spring scales shall be suspended from a stationary support so as to permit accurate reading of the dial by the customer, and so suspended that the top or inside of plate, scoop or pan shall be in clear view of the customer, no higher than five and one-half (5½) feet and no lower than four and one-half (4½) feet from the ground or floor. A scale or other weighing device used in the premises when the customer and seller are on opposite sides of the counter shall be so placed that it is between the customer and the merchant. No part of any scale or weighing device shall, at any time while being used to weigh any merchandise or commodity, be obstructed from the full and plain view of the customer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 830.080)

children.title: Complaints of violation
children.text: Whenever the consumer affairs division shall have knowledge of any violation of the provisions of this chapter, or of any other requirement for the use of sealed weights and measures, it shall make complaint to the district court against the party or parties guilty of such violation. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 831.090; Pet. No. 250069, § 9, 8-11-89; 2013-Or-133, § 4, 12-6-13)

children.title: False certificates prohibited
children.text: No owner or keeper of any scale-beam, steelyard, weight or measure, nor such person's employee, shall make or give a certificate of weight or measure which includes the weight of a person or thing other than the principal load weighed or measured, for which the certificate is issued. Any person who violates the provisions of this chapter shall forfeit the right to use and operate such scale-beam, steelyard, weight or measure. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 832.010; Pet. No. 250069, § 10, 8-11-89)

children.title: Deputy weighers of fuel; bond
children.text: There shall be appointed to serve under the consumer affairs division, one (1) or more deputy weighers for each licensed fuel dealer. Such deputy shall be a licensed fuel dealer or a competent employee of such dealer, and shall hold office until such appointment is revoked. Deputy weighers, before entering upon the duties of their office, shall give bond to the city in the sum of five hundred dollars ($500.00), with sureties to be approved by the city council, conditioned for the faithful performance of the duties of their office, and they shall serve without pay from the city and shall not be construed to be employees thereof. The same person may be appointed as a deputy weigher for one (1) or more licensed dealers, and if for more than one (1), only one bond (1) shall be required. (78-Or-049, § 1, 4-14-78; 2013-Or-133, § 5, 12-6-13)

children.title: City to have standard weights and measures
children.text: The consumer affairs division shall procure, at the expense of the city, a complete set of weights and measures, which shall be tried, proved and sealed by the state; and when so sealed and certified, such weights and measures shall be the city's standard. Such weights and measures shall be tried, proved and sealed by the county standard once in every two (2) years. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 831.020; 2013-Or-133, § 6, 12-6-13)

children.title: Tests required and authorized
children.text: A representative of the consumer affairs division shall visit the places of business of every person engaged in any business, trade or occupation requiring the use of weights and measures; and then and there try, prove and seal all scale-beams, steelyards, weights and measures; and when not found to be accurate, shall take the same into possession and prevent the further use thereof. The division shall keep a record, which shall be open for public inspection, and which shall contain entries, under proper headings, of all scale-beams, steelyards, weights and measures sealed, together with the owners' names, and dates when so sealed. The division may try and prove any scale-beams, steelyards, weights and measures in use within the city at any and all times when it shall deem it necessary for the purpose of detecting inaccuracies in such scale-beams, steelyards, weights and measures. For the tests hereinbefore provided for no fees shall be charged. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 831.030; Pet. No. 250069, § 11, 8-11-89; 2013-Or-133, § 7, 12-6-13)

children.title: Tests on request
children.text: The consumer affairs division also may test, upon the request of any person, any scale-beams, steelyards, weights or measures used or kept within the city. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 831.040; 2013-Or-133, § 8, 12-6-13)

children.heading: ARTICLE III.
children.title: FUEL
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (4) ---

Cross reference— Fuel dealers, Ch. 291.

children.title: Definitions
children.text:
When used in this article, the following terms shall mean:

Cord: One hundred twenty-eight (128) cubic feet of firewood in four-foot lengths; and if the sale is of "sawed wood" a cord shall mean one hundred ten (110) cubic feet when ranked, or one hundred sixty (160) cubic feet when thrown irregularly or loosely into a conveyance for delivery to the purchaser; and if the sale is of "sawed and split wood," a cord shall mean one hundred twenty (120) cubic feet, when ranked, and one hundred seventy-five (175) cubic feet when thrown irregularly and loosely into a conveyance for delivery.

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 239.33.

Firewood: Any kindling, logs, boards, timbers or other wood, natural or processed, split or not split, advertised, offered for sale or sold for heating purposes but excluding charcoal to be used for cooking.

Fuel: Coal, lignite, briquets, coke, firewood, fuel oil or other similar matter used for heating purposes.

Fuel dealer: A person who sells or offers for sale any fuel, or who by advertising or in any manner holds himself or herself out as one who sells or offers for sale any fuel, but not including solicitors or salesmen of licensed fuel dealers.

Packaged firewood: Firewood put up or packed in any manner in advance [of] sale in units less than three (3) cubic feet.

Representation: Any advertisement, offering, sales certificate, invoice, or the like that pertains to the sale of fuel. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 343.010; 77-Or-074, § 1, 4-29-77; Pet. No. 250069, § 12, 8-11-89)

children.title: Sales certificates
Quantity
children.text:
(a) All firewood shall be advertised, offered for sale and sold only by measure, using the term "cord" and fractional parts of a cord, except that wood, natural or processed, offered for sale or sold in quantities less than three (3) cubic feet shall be sold in packaged form and shall display the quantity in terms of weight or cubic feet and fractions of cubic feet. Packaged firewood shall comply with all applicable provisions of Chapter 152 relating to sale of commodities.

(b) All coal, coke, lignite or briquets shall be advertised, offered for sale and sold only by weight. In all contracts for the sale of such commodities the term "ton" shall mean two thousand (2,000) pounds. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 833.030; 77-Or-074, § 3, 4-29-77)

children.title: Prohibition of terms
children.text: The terms "face cord," "stove cord," "rick," "rack," "pile," "truckload," or terms of similar import, shall not be used when advertising, offering for sale or selling firewood. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 833.040; 77-Or-074, § 4, 4-29-77)

children.title: Sales certificates to be numbered
children.text: In all sales of any kind of fuel, regardless of quantity, a sales certificate, as required by the terms of this article, shall be delivered to the purchaser at the time of delivery of said fuel, whether the same be delivered by the vendor or is hauled or carried by the vendee. Each such certificate required shall be numbered serially and each duplicate or copy thereof shall bear the same number as the original. Every licensed dealer, in all cases of sales of fuel to another dealer for delivery to a consumer upon the certificate of the vendee in such sales, shall print, write or stamp upon the certificate to be delivered to the consumer, as herein required, the number of the sales certificate and the license number of the dealer who makes such sale to such other dealer for delivery to a consumer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 833.050; Pet. No. 250069, § 13, 8-11-89)

children.title: Representations pertaining to the sale of firewood
children.text: Every representation pertaining to the sale of firewood shall contain a statement as to whether such firewood is "seasoned" or "green," and a declaration of the true name and percentage of each constituent species group within ten (10) per cent accuracy. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 833.070; 77-Or-074, § 5, 4-29-77)

children.title: Records of dealers
children.text: Every licensed fuel dealer shall keep a complete record of all sales or deliveries of fuel and of all advertisements for the sale thereof, for a period of six (6) months after the date of such sale, delivery or advertisement, and such records shall at all reasonable times be open to the inspection of employees of the consumer affairs division. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 833.080; 2013-Or-133, § 9, 12-6-13)

children.title: False certificates
children.text: No person shall issue or sign any certificate required by this article if the same contains any false or misleading statement as to any facts required to be stated therein. No licensed fuel dealer shall suffer, permit or allow any certificate required by this article to be signed or issued or to be delivered to the vendee or other person as required herein if the same contains any false or misleading statement as to any facts required to be stated therein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 833.100)

children.title: Sale, storage and transportation of elmwood or ashwood prohibited
children.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to transport, store or sell within the city any bark bearing elmwood, ashwood or any wood of a tree that has been infected or infested by an invasive species, without having obtained a permit from the park and recreation board as provided by section 399.80 of this Code. (77-Or-074, § 6, 4-29-77; 2009-Or-107, § 1, 10-16-09)

children.title: Liquid fuels
children.text:
(a) Definitions. Whenever used in this section:

(1) "Tank, truck, trailer or other wheeled conveyance" shall mean an assembly used for the delivery of liquids, comprising a tank, which may or may not be subdivided into two (2) or more compartments, mounted upon a wagon, automobile, truck or trailer, together with its accessory piping, valves, meters, etc.

(2) "Liquid fuels" shall include fuel in liquid form, which can or may be used for heating purposes and which has an American Petroleum Institute gravity nominally greater than twenty-two (22) and a Saybolt Universal viscosity of fifty (50) seconds at one hundred (100) degrees Fahrenheit, or less.

(b) Methods of measuring. No person shall sell, offer for sale, deliver or attempt to deliver any petroleum product or other liquid to be used for fuel for heating purposes, hereinbefore defined as "liquid fuels," by tank, truck, trailer or other wheeled conveyance, unless measured at the place of delivery by standard liquid gallon or five-gallon measure, or by a meter which has been tested, approved and sealed by the Minnesota Division of Weights and Measures. No deliveries of liquid fuels on a meter basis shall be made when a meter is broken and out-of-order, or the seal has been broken or tampered with, defaced or otherwise mutilated. If any meter used upon such tank, truck, trailer or other wheeled conveyance shall become out-of-order, or for any reason inaccurately measured liquid fuel, the person using the same shall immediately report such fact to the consumer affairs division, which division may issue a written permit to sell and deliver liquid fuel from compartments which have been calibrated, and whose indicators have been sealed by the Minnesota Division of Weights and Measures, in lieu thereof, for not to exceed forty-eight (48) hours. This section shall not apply to the delivery of liquid fuel by one (1) dealer to another. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 834.020; 2013-Or-133, § 10, 12-6-13)

children.title: Avoirdupois net weight
children.text: Every person engaged in the business of selling crushed rock, sand, gravel or any mixture thereof shall sell and deliver the same within the city by avoirdupois net weight, and in no other manner. The avoirdupois net weight of any such materials shall mean the avoirdupois net weight thereof, assuming the same to be free from moisture. The seller thereof shall ascertain the true percentage of moisture, if any, contained in such materials at the time of delivery thereof and shall indicate such percentage of moisture on the certificate of weight hereinafter required, and deduct the amount thereof from the gross weight, so as to show the true avoirdupois net weight, assuming said materials to be free from moisture. All such crushed rock, sand, gravel or mixture thereof so sold or delivered shall be weighed on a scale that has been inspected and sealed, as provided by law, by the division of weights and measures of the State of Minnesota. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 835.010)

children.title: Certificate of weight
children.text: Every person engaged in the business of selling crushed rock, sand, gravel or any mixture thereof, and selling and delivering the same within the city, shall furnish to the purchaser thereof with each load of said materials so sold and delivered a written or printed certificate showing the date of weighing, the correct gross weight, the correct tare weight, the net weight of said materials assuming them to be free from moisture, the name and address of the seller and purchaser of said materials, the number of the conveyance in which said materials are delivered, if numbered, and the name of the person in charge of such conveyance. In case such conveyance contains or transports more than one kind of said materials, said certificate shall show the net weight of each kind thereof being so sold, transported or carried. The certificate herein required shall at all times be subject to examination and inspection by the inspectors of the department of licenses and consumer services or any police officer of the city. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 835.020)

children.title: Exception
children.text: Nothing in this article shall apply to motor vehicles equipped with tanks or bodies and machinery used for the purpose of transporting mixed concrete, or concrete being mixed in transit, ready for use in building construction upon delivery thereof. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 835.030)

children.title: Dry quart measure
children.text: The standard measure by which berries and small fruits are sold by the quart shall be that commonly known as dry measure, and the quart shall be one-thirty-second part of the United States standard bushel. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 836.010)

children.title: Standard size boxes
children.text: Square boxes four and one-half (4½) inches in length and breadth and three and five-sixteenths (3 5/16 ) inches in depth may be used, and shall be deemed sufficient to contain one quart when sales are made by single quarts. Square boxes three and one-fourth (3¼) inches in length and breadth and three and three-sixteenths (3 3/16 ) inches in depth may be used and shall be a sufficient measure of one pint. No person shall sell or expose for sale any berries or small fruit in boxes other than those described in this section unless such boxes shall be sealed by the city sealer of weights and measures and the contents of such boxes plainly marked thereon. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 836.020)

children.title: Ward boundaries designated
children.text:
Pursuant to the city charter, the boundaries of the wards of the city shall be as shown on the map set out in Appendix B of this Code, which is hereby made a part hereof. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 470.010)
