children.text: Editor's note— 2003-Or-010, § 4, adopted Jan 31, 2003, repealed § 363.280 which pertained to when application to be published. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2016-070, § 3, adopted Oct. 7, 2016, repealed § 363.290, which pertained to hearings on application; § 1 of said ordinance enacted a new § 360.200 pertaining to similar subject matter. See the Code Comparative Table for derivation.

children.title: On sale wine licenses in proximity to residentially zoned property
children.text:
(a) On sale licenses for new premises, in which the main entrance is within three hundred (300) feet from an adjacent residential use located in an urban neighborhood or residential mixed use district shall be issued only for premises which qualify as a "restaurant" as defined in section 360.10 and have a maximum bar area of not more than thirty (30) percent of the total public premises and which comply with the following requirements:

(1) It is the policy of the city council that establishments operating under this section are intended primarily for the service of patrons at tables and for the consumption of alcoholic beverages in conjunction with food service that is prepared on-site. The minimum seating capacity of an on sale wine establishment shall be twenty-five (25) persons.

(2) The city council may further restrict the days, hours, nature, volume, and other aspects of entertainment in any establishment, including a prohibition against all forms of entertainment, to protect the public interest, safety, repose, and welfare of residents, businesses and other uses near the establishment.

(3) Establishments licensed for the sale of beverage alcohol shall monitor and be responsible for the activity of employees and patrons so as to prevent negative secondary effects directly attributable to the existence of the business. License holders shall monitor all sound levels, so as to comply with state and city noise standards, generated by amplification devices employed by the establishment; patron generated sound levels, nuisance activities, criminal activities occurring on the premises; and loitering activities associated with the licensed premises, so as to protect the safety, repose, and welfare of residents, businesses and other uses near the establishment.

(b) Violations of this section and other sections of this Code or other laws where there is an admission that the violation occurred by satisfaction of the citation, or findings issued regarding violations that are adjudicated by a district, state or federal court of law, or a neutral administrative hearing officer, shall be deemed to constitute a sufficient basis for the city council to impose reasonable conditions or other adverse license action on any license or permit, including but not limited to a reduction in hours of operation, a reduction in bar area, a reduction in the levels of live entertainment allowed, amendments to security plans, or a reduction in the size of outdoor premises. (2014-Or-069, § 10, 9-19-14; Ord. No. 2018-059, § 9, 11-2-18; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 15, 10-9-25)

children.title: Renewal procedure
children.text: If the application shall be for the renewal of an existing license, the licensing official shall immediately transmit the same to the appropriate committee of the city council, whereupon the application may be summarily acted upon by said committee and referred to the city council for immediate action. (78-Or-068, § 27, 4-28-78; 2013-Or-220, § 9, 12-6-13)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2002-Or-079, § 7, adopted Aug. 9, 2002, repealed § 363.310, which pertained to transfer of licenses. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Qualifications of applicant
children.text:
No license shall be issued to any applicant who does not meet the following qualifications:

(1) The applicant must be the actual owner of the premises or the business at the licensed premises. In case of a corporation, applicant must be the manager of such premises or business.

(2) The applicant cannot have been convicted, within five (5) years of the date of the application, of any felony, or of any two (2) crimes other than a felony related to alcohol, or of any willful violation of any law dealing with the sale, possession, manufacture or transportation of liquor, wine or beer. If such conviction within the United States shall have resulted in a forfeiture of civil rights, the five-year period shall begin to run at the date of the restoration of civil rights.

(3) An individual applicant must be a resident of the State of Minnesota. If the applicant is a partnership, the managing partner must be a resident of the State of Minnesota. If the applicant is a corporation, the manager or person in charge must be a resident of the State of Minnesota or reside within seventy-five (75) miles of Minneapolis City Hall. Such residency requirements shall mean being a resident continuously while the license is in effect.

(4) If the applicant is a corporation, it must be authorized to do business in Minnesota. If the applicant is a partnership, all partners must qualify in the same manner as individuals, except that residency requirements shall be governed by subsection 363.320(c).

(5) No license shall be issued or transferred to any person who has had an intoxicating liquor or wine license revoked within five (5) years prior to the date of application under the terms of this chapter or the statutes of the State of Minnesota; nor shall any license be issued or transferred to the spouse of such person. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 78-Or-192, § 4, 9-29-78; 83-Or-302, § 7, 12-16-83; 92-Or-038, § 1, 3-27-92; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 16, 10-9-25)

children.title: Licensing of corporations
children.text: The provisions of section 362.330 of this Code are adopted by reference as though fully set forth, and shall govern the licensing of corporations holding wine licenses. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 78-Or-192, § 5, 9-29-78; 83-Or-302, § 9, 12-16-83)

children.title: Revocation of license generally
children.text: Except as otherwise provided by this Code, any license issued under this chapter may be revoked by the city council for any violation of this chapter or the laws of the State of Minnesota relative to the sale of liquor or to the conduct of the business of the licensee. Such revocation by the city council may be made for cause after notice to the licensee and hearing, and an opportunity of the licensee to be heard. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 90-Or-038, § 3, 1-26-90)

children.title: Revocation of erroneously issued license
children.text: Any license issued to a person not entitled to receive the same under this chapter or any law of the State of Minnesota shall be revoked by the city council at any time after notice and public hearing. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 90-Or-038, § 4, 1-26-90)

children.title: Suspension, revocation and other adverse license action
children.text: Upon a finding by the city council that the licensee, or any agent or employee of said licensee, has failed to comply with any of the provisions of law relating to the sale, purchase, distribution, possession, manufacture or transportation of wine or beer upon the premises of the licensee operated under said license, all licenses of the licensee shall be subject to adverse action pursuant to Minn. Statute Section 340A.415 and as otherwise provided by this Code. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 2013-Or-220, § 10, 12-6-13)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2006-Or-046, § 1, adopted May 12, 2006, repealed § 363.370, which pertained to payment of taxes prerequisite to license. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2025-046, § 17, adopted October 9, 2025, repealed § 363.380, which pertained to health and welfare benefits must be paid and derived from Ord. No 79-Or-093, § 1, adopted June 25, 1976; Ord. No. 78-Or-068, § 3, adopted April 28, 1978 and Ord. No. 2013-Or-220, § 10 adopted December 6, 2013.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 94-Or-138, adopted Sept. 30, 1994, repealed §§ 363.390 and 363.400, which pertained to distance from schools and churches and exception to distance requirements. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Issuance and posting of license
children.text: Upon the approval by the city council of the application, and approval by the liquor control commissioner, a license shall be issued by the licensing official containing the name and address of the license and a description of the premises for which such license is granted, which license shall be signed by the licensing official, and the same shall be kept posted at all times in a conspicuous place in the premises for which license is issued. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 2013-Or-220, § 11, 12-6-13)

children.title: Death of licensee
children.text: The duly appointed, qualified and acting personal representative of the estate of a deceased licensee may operate under any license issued to the deceased licensee, for not more than ninety (90) days after the death of such licensee, upon the filing by said personal representative with the licensing official of a certified copy of appointment as such. The qualifications of an applicant for an original license under this chapter shall also apply to such personal representative, except insofar as such qualifications shall also be required by any other law. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 82-Or-008, § 1, 1-15-82; Pet. No. 251179, § 31, 12-29-89; 2013-Or-220, § 12, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 18, 10-9-25)

children.title: Military service of licensee
children.text: Any person licensed to sell wine who shall enter any of the services of the Armed Forces of the United States may continue as holder of such license, and may have the same renewed, together with any food license held in connection with the conduct of the business, by designating a person with power of attorney to manage and conduct the business while said licensee is in the armed forces, and to apply for renewals of all such licenses for and on behalf of such licensee. Such power of attorney shall state that such licensee has entered the Armed Forces of the United States and shall designate the particular branch thereof. In addition to the authority and power to manage and conduct the business, such power of attorney, if the licensee shall so desire, may also provide for the authority to sell and dispose of such business. Any application for the renewal of any such license shall be made by the person holding such power of attorney for and on behalf of the licensee, but all information required in the license application shall pertain to the person so appointed to manage and conduct the business of the licensee, and no person not qualified under this chapter to hold or obtain such license shall be authorized to conduct or manage such business under said power of attorney, nor shall the application of any such person be accepted. Furthermore, the provisions of this chapter shall not apply unless the person appointed power of attorney shall notify the licensing official within thirty (30) days of the time the licensee entered the Armed Forces. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; Pet. No. 251179, § 32, 12-29-89; 2013-Or-220, § 13, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 19, 10-9-25)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2014-Or-069, § 11, adopted September 19, 2014, repealed § 363.430 which pertained to certified copy of audit required. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Premises to be open to inspection
children.text: The premises named in any license shall at all times while open to the public be open also to inspection and examination by the licensing official or any police, fire, regulatory code official or inspector, or health officer of the city. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; 2013-Or-220, § 14, 12-6-13)

children.title: Compliance with state law
children.text: No license shall be issued in violation of any of the laws of the State of Minnesota, and any violation of any law of the State of Minnesota relating to the sale and distribution of liquor shall be considered a violation of this Code. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78)

children.title: Applicability of other chapters of Code
children.text: All of the provisions of Chapters 360, 364 (except section 364.80) and 370 shall apply herein. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78)

children.title: Council discretion
children.text: The city council may exercise its judgment and discretion, to the fullest extent permitted by law, to grant or deny any application in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, title and any other applicable statute, rule or law. (76-Or-093, § 1, 6-25-76; 78-Or-068, § 3, 4-28-78; Ord. No. 2018-062, § 3, 11-2-18)

children.title: Furnishing to minors
children.text: No holder of an "off sale" liquor license, nor any agent or employee of such license holder, shall deliver any intoxicating liquor to any person under twenty-one (21) years of age. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.010; 80-Or-280, § 1, 11-26-80; 86-Or-191, § 1, 8-8-86; 90-Or-039, § 1, 1-26-90)

children.title: Receipt for deliveries
children.text: No holder of an "off sale" liquor license, his or her agent or employee, shall deliver any such intoxicating liquor to or at any place or premises other than those for which such license shall have been issued, without obtaining a receipt therefor, in duplicate, signed by the person receiving such liquor, in plain and legible writing and bearing the time and date of such delivery, and address of the place, including number of room or apartment, if any, where such liquor is delivered. The original of such receipt shall be kept in the files of the licensee for a period of at least one year from and after the date of such delivery, and all such files and receipts shall be kept available for inspection by the police department at all hours during which such place of business may be open under the terms of this chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.010; Pet. No. 251179, § 33, 12-29-89)

children.title: Sales to obviously intoxicated persons
children.text:
No person may sell, give, furnish, or in any way procure for another alcoholic beverages for the use of an obviously intoxicated person. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.020; Pet. No. 251179, § 34, 12-29-89; 2002-Or-153, §§ 1, 2, 10-11-02)

Editor's note— Ord. No. 2002-Or-153, § 1, adopted Oct. 11, 2002, repealed former § 364.30 which pertained to sales to incompetents or drunkards. Section 2 of said ordinance enacted provisions designated as a new § 364.30 to read as herein set out. See the Code Comparative Table.

State Law reference— Sales to intoxicated persons, M.S. § 340A.502.

children.title: Consuming in public
children.text:
(a) No person shall consume intoxicating liquor as defined by Minn. Statute, Section 340A.101, Subdivision 14, or nonintoxicating malt liquor as defined by Minn. Statute, Section 340A.101, Subdivision 19, while (1) on a public street, highway, alley, sidewalk, boulevard, or any place frequented by the public; (2) on any private property without the consent of the owner of such property; or (3) while in a vehicle upon a public highway. This section shall not prohibit the consumption of such beverages at duly licensed on-sale premises, or if otherwise authorized by law.

(b) Within the premises of the property known as the Downtown East Commons, bounded by 4th Street South, Park Avenue, 5th Street South, and 5th Avenue South, but not including any public street or sidewalk or any portion of the premises operating under the provisions of an on sale alcohol license or permit issued by the licensing official, the city council may, by resolution or ordinance, adopt rules, regulations, and limitations allowing for the possession and consumption of alcoholic beverages. Such rules, regulations, and limitations may address any matters associated with such possession and consumption of beverage alcohol, including, but not limited to, permitted times, hours, events, locations, beverage classes and types, behavior, and containers. Any violation of such a duly-adopted and posted rule, regulation, or limitation shall constitute a violation of this section. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.030; 80-Or-268, § 1, 11-14-80; Pet. No. 251179, § 35, 12-29-89; Ord. No. 2017-016, § 1, 4-28-17)

Cross reference— Authority to operate sidewalk café, notwithstanding provisions of above section, § 265.280.

children.title: Loitering in possession of open bottle
children.text:
No person shall loiter in any public street, highway, alley, sidewalk, boulevard or any other public property, or on any private property without consent of the owner of such property, while in possession of any bottle or other receptacle containing intoxicating liquor or non-intoxicating malt liquor which has been opened, or the seal broken, or the contents partially removed, with intent to consume such intoxicating liquor or non-intoxicating malt liquor.

This section shall not prohibit the possession of alcoholic beverages at duly licensed on-sale premises if otherwise authorized by law.

(93-Or-011, § 1, 1-29-93)

children.title: Taking liquor to another liquor or beer place
children.text: No person shall take or carry any liquor to or into any building or place, or consume any liquor purchased elsewhere, in any building or place operated under an "on sale" license or under a beer license granted by the city council; nor shall any "off sale" licensee knowingly sell or permit to be sold to any person any liquor for transportation to or consumption in any such place operated under an "on sale" license or beer license. This section shall not apply to hotels, except to such parts thereof as are primarily used for the sale of liquor or beer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.040)

children.title: Sales in hotel rooms
children.text: No sale of liquor shall be made to or in guest rooms of hotels, unless the rules of such hotel provide for the service of meals in guest rooms; nor unless the sale of such liquor is made in the manner "on sales" are required to be made; nor unless the rules of such hotel and the description, location and number of such guest rooms are fully set out in the application for a license; provided, however, that hotels may install and operate mechanical dispensing systems for alcoholic beverages which have been specifically approved by the state liquor control commissioner. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.050; Ord. of 9-12-74, § 1)

children.title: Bars
children.text: No public bar, other than a service bar, shall be permitted in any place licensed under "on sale" license, unless it is equipped for the service of food and drink and unless such service is to patrons in full view of and conducted as a part of the service of the dining room or one of the additional rooms of a hotel, restaurant, café or club in which the sale of intoxicating liquor has been authorized by the license. This section shall not apply to establishments for the sale of "on sale" liquor exclusively. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.060)

children.title: Hours, days regulated
Consumption in on-sale liquor or wine premises; hours regulated
children.text:
(a) No person, including the licensee and his or her employees and agents, shall consume liquor or beer in any on-sale liquor or wine premises between 1:30 a.m. and 8:00 a.m.

(b) An establishment that has obtained a permit from the commissioner of public safety under Minnesota Statute Section 340A.504 subd. 7 may not allow consumption of liquor, wine or beer, including the licensee and his or her employees and agents, in any on-sale liquor, wine or beer premises between 2:30 a.m. and 8:00 a.m.

(c) During said hours, no person shall be allowed to be or remain upon or within such room, place or premises for any purpose whatever, except that the owner or licensee, his or her agents, servants or employees may remain therein for the purpose only of cleaning, preparation of meals, necessary repairs or other work therein and in connection therewith, or as guards.

(d) During said hours, beverage alcohol must be removed from all public areas of the establishment including tables and bar areas. (87-Or-181, § 1, 10-9-87; 89-Or-172, § 2, 9-15-89; Pet. No. 251179, § 36, 12-29-89; 2003-Or-084, § 2, 6-20-03; 2009-Or-115, § 2, 10-30-09)

children.title: Storage of liquor in establishment with other business
children.text: The proprietor of any store possessing an "off sale" liquor license who conducts on the premises covered by said license a place for the sale of groceries shall keep all liquors for sale under said "off sale" liquor license in a separate compartment, which shall be in full view of persons entering said store, except that liquors may be stored in a room or rooms provided that such storage rooms shall be locked and kept locked under time lock during the hours when the "off sale" of liquor is prohibited. The requirements of this section shall not apply to the proprietor of any store possessing an "off sale" liquor license where all the businesses on the licensed premises are closed during the hours when the "off-sale" of liquor is prohibited. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.080; 80-Or-033, § 1, 2-29-80; Pet. No. 251179, § 37, 12-29-89)

children.title: "On sale" premises without special licenses to close certain hours
children.text: Every room, place or premises where any liquor is permitted to be or is sold, including the café, restaurant or dining room operated in connection therewith, or as a part thereof, and in which such liquor is sold or served by the licensee thereof pursuant to an "on sale" license, shall be closed and kept closed to the public between the hours of 1:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m., unless the licensee has obtained a permit from the commissioner of public safety under Minnesota Statute Section 340A.504 subd. 7 where they shall be closed and kept closed to the public between 2:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m., unless they are the holder of a special late hours license provided for in sections 360.70, 360.75, and 360.80. During said hours, if the licensee is not the holder of a special late hours license, no person shall be allowed to be or remain upon or within such room, place or premises for any purpose whatever, except that the owner or licensee, his or her agents, servants or employees may remain therein for the purpose only of cleaning, preparation of meals, necessary repairs or other work therein and in connection therewith, or as guards. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.090; 85-Or-195, § 1, 10-11-85; Pet. No. 251179, § 38, 12-29-89; 93-Or-192, § 1, 12-30-93; 2000-Or-072, § 1, 7-28-00; 2003-Or-084, § 3, 6-20-03; 2009-Or-115, § 3, 10-30-09)

children.title: Restroom facilities required
children.text: In each establishment wherein liquor or beer is sold pursuant to an "on sale" license, there shall be installed and maintained proper restroom facilities which comply with all requirements of any applicable code, statute, rule or regulation and a properly installed and maintained floor drain sufficient at all times to keep such floor dry and in a sanitary condition. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 853.100; 2014-Or-071, § 1, 9-19-14)

children.title: Hearing protection devices
children.text: All Class A and Class B on-sale liquor, wine and beer establishments with general entertainment as defined in section 360.50(a)(1) of this Code shall have and make available, free of charge, hearing protection devices to all patrons and employees. Such single-use earplugs must have a Noise Reduction Rating (NRR) of at least twelve (12) decibels. The requirement imposed by this section shall not apply unless the license official has identified a source or supplier of such hearing protection devices to provide sufficient devices free of charge to all such establishments. (2014-Or-015, § 1, 4-11-14; Ord. No. 2018-059, § 10, 11-2-18)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2002-Or-153, § 3, adopted Oct. 11, 2002, repealed former § 364.120, which pertained to blood alcohol chart required. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.heading: CHAPTER 366.
children.title: BEER LICENSES
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (5) ---

State Law reference— Nonintoxicating liquor licenses, M.S. § 340A.403.

children.title: License required
children.text:
No person shall sell, exchange, barter, dispose of or keep for sale any beer, as defined in section 360.10, without first having obtained one or more of the licenses herein provided for. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.010; 2009-Or-179, § 1, 11-13-09)

Cross reference— Permit for sidewalk cafés and authority to licensees under this chapter to obtain such permits, § 265.280 et seq.

children.title: When licenses expire
children.text: All licenses issued under this chapter shall expire on April first each year. (2009-Or-179, § 2, 11-13-09)

children.title: Use of basement or upper floors
children.text: No license shall be issued for the "on sale" of beer in basements or above the first floor of any building unless the application for such license shall clearly state the area to be covered by the license. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.020)

children.title: Licensed premises
children.text: An "on sale" license to sell beer only permits the "on sale" of beer in the premises designated in the license application. Prior to the sale of beer by an "on sale" licensee in expanded premises, an application to expand the licensed premises shall be submitted. (81-Or-308, § 1, 12-28-81)

children.title: Issuance of additional on sale beer licenses prohibited
children.text:
Effective January 1, 2026, no additional on sale beer licenses shall be issued, other than temporary on sale beer licenses pursuant to section 366.40. Any person, partnership, firm, or corporation holding an on sale beer license as of January 1, 2026 may continue to apply to renew such license by paying a fee to the city for on sale beer as established in the License Fee Schedule. The payment of such fee to be evidenced by a receipt from the licensing official, a copy of which shall be filed with such application.

(Ord. No. 2025-046, § 20, 10-9-25)

children.title: Temporary "on sale" beer license
children.text:
(a) A club or charitable, religious or nonprofit organization not included within the term "bona fide" club as defined in section 360.10 may obtain a temporary "on sale" license to sell beer on premises specified in the license, including school buildings and school grounds. The fee for such license shall be as established in the License Fee Schedule.

(b) Application for a temporary "on sale" beer license shall be made in conformance with the provisions of section 366.110(a).

(c) The application for such temporary "on sale" beer license shall contain the following:

(1) The name and address of the organization;

(2) The purpose for which the organization is organized;

(3) The purpose for which the temporary "on sale" beer license is desired;

(4) The address of the place where beer is to be sold; and

(5) The dates and hours at which beer is to be sold.

(d) A temporary "on sale" beer license shall be issued subject to the following conditions:

(1) No individual organization shall be granted such license more than twelve (12) total days per calendar year.

(2) No such license shall be issued for the sale of beer on K-12 school grounds or in K-12 school buildings or within three hundred (300) feet thereof when regularly scheduled classes are being held in such school.

(3) No more than twelve (12) total days of licenses shall be granted in any one (1) calendar year at any location, except for the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Parade Stadium.

(4) In the case of an event to be held upon publicly owned property, or where projected attendance is in excess of one thousand (1,000) persons; a certificate that there is in effect for the license period an insurance policy or pool providing at least fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) of coverage because of bodily injury to any one (1) person in any one (1) occurrence, three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000.00) because of bodily injury to two (2) or more persons in any one (1) occurrence, ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) because of injury to or destruction of property of others in any one (1) occurrence, fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) for loss of means of support of any one (1) person in any one (1) occurrence, and three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000.00) for loss of means of support of two (2) or more persons in any one (1) occurrence. An annual aggregate policy limit for dramshop liability of not less than three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000.00) per policy period may be included in the policy provisions. The policy shall cover all liability imposed by Section 340A.801, Minn. Statute. In the case of property owned or controlled by the City of Minneapolis, the city shall be named as an additional insured.

(e) When an application for a license for temporary on-sale beer has been filed, the licensing official may issue the license if the application is complete, the fee including a fifty (50) percent late fee has been paid, if applicable, and the required conditions listed above have been met. The licensing official may also deny, suspend, or revoke those licenses which have been issued or applied for based on the reasons listed above or for good cause. The issuance of a temporary on-sale beer license is subject to compliance with all applicable health and safety laws. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.035; Ord. of 9-12-74, § 1; 77-Or-147, § 1, 7-15-77; 78-Or-253, § 1, 12-8-78; 79-Or-139, § 1, 6-29-79; 80-Or-117, § 1, 5-9-80; 81-Or-114, § 1, 4-24-81; 86-Or-151, § 1, 7-11-86; 90-Or-014, § 1, 1-26-90; 91-Or-049, § 1, 3-29-91; 98-Or-046, § 1, 5-22-98; 2001-Or-081, § 1, 7-13-01; 2002-Or-023, § 1, 4-5-02; 2002-Or-080, § 1, 8-9-02; 2013-Or-221, § 1, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2017-037, § 7, 8-4-17; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 21, 10-9-25)

children.title: Scope of "off sale" license
children.text: An "off sale" license shall permit the licensee to sell three and two-tenths (3.2) beer in original packages not to be consumed upon the licensed premises. An "off sale" license may be issued to premises licensed for "on sale" beer or "on sale" wine or "on sale" liquor at no further cost. Notwithstanding any other language contained in this section, if such "on sale" liquor premises are located within the Central Commercial District, as defined in section 360.10, such sales shall be prohibited. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.040; 78-Or-262, § 4, 12-22-78; 2000-Or-054, § 1, 6-23-00)

children.title: License fees established
children.text:
The annual fees for the license required by this chapter shall be as established in Appendix J, License Fee Schedule.

The fee shall be paid annually in advance and shall be subject to all provisions in this chapter regarding penalties and prorating. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.060; Ord. of 10-11-74, § 2; 77-Or-147, § 1, 7-15-77; 78-Or-253, § 1, 12-8-78; 80-Or-118, § 1, 5-9-80; 83-Or-251, §§ 1, 2, 10-14-83; 83-Or-304, § 3, 12-16-83; 86-Or-139, § 2, 6-12-86; 86-Or-041, § 1, 3-14-86; 90-Or-014, § 1, 1-26-90; 91-Or-049, § 1, 3-29-91; 98-Or-046, § 1, 5-22-98; 2002-Or-023, § 1, 4-5-02; 2002-Or-080, § 2, 8-9-02)

children.title: Payment and receipt for fee
children.text:
(a) The applicant shall, on or before the filing of such application, pay to the licensing official the license fee required for the kind of license applied for, and the licensing official shall give to such applicant a report in duplicate, a copy of which receipt shall be filed with such application.

(b) Notwithstanding the provisions of any other ordinance, if an application for an "on sale" license is denied by the city council or withdrawn by the applicant, the amount as established in Appendix J, License Fee Schedule, shall be retained from any money deposited by the applicant, to defray the costs of the city in processing and investigating the application and any sum over the amount established in Appendix J may be refunded to the applicant. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.070; Ord. of 9-14-73, § 1; Ord. of 11-8-74, § 1; 77-Or-147, § 1, 7-15-77; 78-Or-252, § 1, 12-8-78; 86-Or-041, § 1, 3-14-86; Pet. No. 251179, § 39, 12-29-89; 2002-Or-080, § 3, 8-9-02; 2013-Or-221, § 2, 12-6-13)

children.title: Prorating of fee
children.text: Where the application for the license shall be for the unexpired portion of a license year, the fee shall be a pro rata share of the annual license fee determined in the manner provided by section 261.40 of this Code. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.080; Pet. No. 251179, § 40, 12-29-89)

children.title: Penalty for late renewal
children.text: In the event any such application is granted which has not been filed on or before thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the license year, before the license can be issued the applicant shall pay an additional fee in the amount as established in Appendix J, License Fee Schedule, in addition to the regular license fee. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.090; 77-Or-147, § 1, 7-15-77; 78-Or-253, § 1, 12-8-78; 81-Or-308, § 1, 12-28-81; 86-Or-025, § 1, 2-14-86; 2002-Or-080, § 4, 8-9-02)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 86-Or-026, § 1, adopted Feb. 14, 1986, repealed § 366.100, concerning the penalty for late installment payments on the license, as derived from Code 1960, § 852.100; 77-Or-147, adopted July 15, 1977; 78-Or-253, adopted Dec. 8, 1978; and 81-Or-308, adopted Dec. 28, 1981.

children.title: Application forms and procedures
children.text:
Every application for a license to sell beer, including applications for changes in ownership or expansion of premises, shall be made only upon forms furnished by the licensing official and, when completed by the applicant, shall be filed and a record of the same made therein. An application for a change in ownership or expansion of an "on sale" premises shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable investigation fee as established in Appendix J, License Fee Schedule. A licensee holding an "off sale" beer license shall not be required to make application for an expansion of premises. Notwithstanding the above-stated requirements, a licensee which is a publicly held corporation or a wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly held corporation need not file an application nor pay an investigation fee for changes in shareholders of the publicly held corporations nor changes in officers of either the publicly held corporation or the wholly owned subsidiary. An application and investigation fee must be submitted for changes in shareholders of the wholly owned subsidiary corporation and/or changes in managers. An application and investigation fee must be submitted for a change in manager when the licensee is a nonresident individual.

The application for an "on sale" beer license shall then be referred to the license inspector of the police department, who upon having completed investigation thereof, shall direct the same to the licensing official. The application for a new "off sale" beer license or for the renewal of an "off sale" beer license shall be recorded and investigated by the licensing official. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.110; 81-Or-308, § 4, 12-28-81; 83-Or-041, § 1, 2-25-83; 83-Or-251, § 3, 10-14-83; 83-Or-303, § 1, 12-16-83; Pet. No. 251179, § 41, 12-29-89; 2002-Or-080, § 5, 8-9-02; 2003-Or-011, § 1, 1-31-03; 2009-Or-179, § 3, 11-13-09; 2013-Or-221, § 3, 12-6-13)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 209-Or-179, § 4, adopted November 13, 2009, repealed § 366.120, which pertained to renewal form. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Contents of application
children.text:
The application shall contain the following:

(1) The true name, place and date of birth, and residence street address of the applicant.

(2) Whether the applicant is married or single. If married, the true name, place and date of birth, and residence street address of the applicant's spouse.

(3) Whether the applicant and spouse maintain their principal place of abode in the State of Minnesota.

(4) Whether the applicant is a natural person, corporation, partnership or unincorporated association.

(5) If the applicant is other than a natural person, the name of the manager or proprietor of the premises to be licensed, giving all the information about said manager or proprietor as is required by (1) through (4) above. In addition, corporations shall file with the application two (2) certified copies of the bylaws, articles of incorporation, and minutes of the meeting setting forth the officers of the corporation. They will also submit two (2) copies of the minutes of the meeting authorizing the issuance of stock and a list of all people holding stocks and the number of shares held by each of them.

(6) If a permit from the federal government is required, the application shall state whether such permit has been issued, and if so, in what name.

(7) The exact legal description of the premises to be licensed.

(8) A statement as to whether all real estate and personal property taxes for the premises to be licensed are fully paid, and if not paid, the years and amounts of delinquency.

(9) Such other information as the licensing official may require.

(10) An applicant for any "on sale" beer license shall file with the application, a notarized agreement that in consideration of the granting of such a license the applicant will, in the event the applicant ever hires any off-duty city employee to work at the licensed premises, hold the city harmless and assume the defense of the city against any claim or lawsuit against it, by reason of the licensee's employee also being an off-duty city employee, and that during all periods of employment of an off-duty city employee, the applicant will maintain in force and effect an insurance policy written by a company authorized to do business in the State of Minnesota, insuring against public liability or damages in the sum of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) for injury or death to one person, and three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000.00) for each accident or occurrence, and fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) property damage, with the city and any off-duty city employee so employed as additional named assureds, and further that during such periods of employment the applicant will maintain in effect an insurance policy with workers' compensation coverage, fully covering the off-duty city employee during periods of employment by the licensee. The granting of a license shall be deemed to be acceptance of the agreement by the city, causing it to be in full force and effect during the license period.

(11) Evidence that notification of the application has been mailed or delivered to the ward council member, the neighborhood group(s), and the business associations(s), of any, for the area in which the premises is located. The neighborhood group(s) and the business association(s) to be notified are those organizations that appear on a list maintained for this purpose by the licensing official. Where the premises for which the license is sought is located on a public street that acts as a boundary between two (2) or more such neighborhood or business organizations, the notification shall be provided to the organizations that represent the adjacent area(s). The notification shall include the following information:

a. The type of license applied for.

b. The address of the premises for which the license is sought.

c. The applicant's name, address, email address, and telephone number.

d. The type of entertainment, if any, that the applicant intends to conduct on the premises. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.130; Ord. of 2-23-73, § 1; 83-Or-304, §§ 4, 5, 12-16-83; 85-Or-019, § 1, 1-25-85; Pet. No. 251179, § 42, 12-19-89; 2003-Or-011, § 2, 1-31-03; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 22, 10-9-25)

children.title: Execution of application
children.text: If the application is by a natural person, it shall be signed and sworn to by such person; if by a corporation, by an officer thereof; if by a partnership, by one of the partners; and if an unincorporated association or club, by the manager or managing officer thereof. If the applicant is a partnership, the application and license shall be made and issued in the name of all the partners of such partnership, but the application may be signed by but one of such partners; provided, however, if the application is for an "on sale" license to a hotel to be owned or operated by it, the application and license shall be made and issued in the partnership name. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.140)

children.title: Investigation of application
children.text: The police license inspector shall investigate into the truthfulness of the statements set forth in all "on sale" beer applications, and into any other matters considered relevant to the application, and shall endorse the findings thereof. All "off sale" beer applications shall be investigated by the licensing official. The applicant shall furnish to the proper investigator such evidence as the investigator may reasonably require in support of the statements set forth in said application. Upon completion of the report, the application shall be filed with the licensing official. (Code. 1960, As Amend., § 852.150; 83-Or-303, § 2, 12-16-83; 2003-Or-011, § 3, 1-31-03; 2013-Or-221, § 4, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 23, 10-9-25)

children.title: False statements in application
children.text: No person shall make any material false statement in any written application, and in addition to all other penalties, the license shall be revoked by the city council for a violation of this section after notice to the licensee and hearing and an opportunity of the licensee to be heard. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.160; 90-Or-040, § 2, 1-26-90)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 2003-Or-011, § 4, adopted Jan. 31, 2003, repealed § 366.170, which pertained to when application to be published. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2016-070, § 4, adopted Oct. 7, 2016, repealed § 366.180, which pertained to hearings on application; § 1 of said ordinance enacted a new § 360.200 pertaining to similar subject matter. See the Code Comparative Table for derivation.

children.title: Action on "off sale" applications
children.text: If the application shall be one (1) for "off sale" beer license, such application, upon being investigated by the licensing official, shall be presented to the appropriate committee at its next regular meeting. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.190; 83-Or-303, § 3, 12-16-83; 2013-Or-221, § 6, 12-6-13)

children.title: Renewal procedure
children.text: If the application shall be for the renewal of an existing license, the licensing official shall immediately transmit the same to the appropriate committee of the city council, and cause the council member of the ward wherein such business establishment is located to be notified; whereupon the application may be summarily acted upon by the committee and referred to the city council for immediate action. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.200; Pet. No. 251179, § 43, 12-29-89; 2013-Or-221, § 7, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 24, 10-9-25)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2002-Or-080, § 6, adopted Aug. 9, 2002, repealed § 366.210, which pertained to transfer of license. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Qualifications of applicant
children.text:
No license shall be issued to any applicant who does not meet the following qualifications:

(1) The applicant must be the actual owner of the premises or the business at the licensed premises. In the case of a corporation, the applicant must be the manager of such premises or business.

(2) The applicant cannot have been convicted, within five (5) years of the date of the application, of any felony, or of any two (2) crimes other than a felony related to alcohol, or of any willful violation of any law dealing with the sale, possession, manufacture or transportation of liquor or beer. If such conviction within the United States shall have resulted in a forfeiture of civil rights, the five-year period shall begin to run at the date of restoration of civil rights.

(3) An individual applicant must be a resident of the State of Minnesota. If the applicant is a partnership, the managing partner must be a resident of the State of Minnesota. If the applicant is a corporation, the manager or person in charge must be a resident of the State of Minnesota or reside within seventy-five (75) miles of Minneapolis City Hall. Such residency requirements shall mean being a resident continuously while the license is in effect.

(4) If the applicant is a corporation, it must be authorized to do business in Minnesota. If the applicant is a partnership, all partners must qualify in the same manner as individuals, except that residency requirements shall be governed by subsection 366.220(c). (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.220; Ord. of 2-23-73, § 2; 83-Or-041, §§ 2, 3, 2-25-83; 83-Or-304, § 7, 12-16-83; 92-Or-039, § 1, 3-27-92; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 25, 10-9-25)

State Law reference— Persons eligible for state license, M.S. § 340A.402.

children.title: Licensing of corporations
children.text: The provisions of section 362.330 are incorporated by reference as though fully set forth and shall govern the licensing of corporations holding beer licenses. (83-Or-304, § 8, 2-16-83)

children.title: Revocation of licenses generally
children.text: Except as otherwise provided by this Code, any licenses issued under this chapter may be revoked by the city council for any violation of Chapters 360 through 370 or the laws of the State of Minnesota relative to the sale of beer or to the conduct of the business of the licensee. Such revocation by the city council may be made for cause after notice to the licensee and hearing and an opportunity of the licensee to be heard. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.230; 90-Or-040, § 3, 1-26-90)

children.title: Revocation of erroneously issued license
children.text: Any license issued to a person not entitled to receive the same under any provisions of this chapter shall be revoked by the city council at any time after notice and public hearing. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.240; 90-Or-040, § 4, 1-26-90)

children.title: Suspension, revocation and other adverse license action
children.text: Upon a finding by the city council that the licensee, or any agent or employee of said licensee, has failed to comply with any of the provisions of law relating to the sale, purchase, distribution, possession, manufacture or transportation of beer upon the premises of the licensee operated under said license, all licenses of the licensee shall be subject to adverse action pursuant to Minn. Statute Section 340A.415 and as otherwise provided by this Code. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.250; 2013-Or-221, § 8, 12-6-13)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2006-Or-047, § 1, adopted May 12, 2006, repealed § 366.260, which pertained to taxes must be paid. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 94-Or-139, §§ 1—3, adopted Sept. 30, 1994, repealed §§ 366.270—366.290, which pertained to distance from schools, churches and exceptions to distance requirements. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Exception to distance requirement when beer not primary business
children.text: The distance limitations for off sale beer shall be one hundred fifty (150) feet for any business in which the sale of beer is incidental to the primary business purpose.(Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.305; 94-Or-139, § 4, 9-30-94; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 26, 10-9-25)

children.title: Businesses entitled to "on sale" licenses
children.text: "On sale" licenses shall be granted only to licensed restaurants, hotels, bona fide clubs (as defined in section 360.10), drugstores which maintain and operate restaurants or lunchrooms in connection therewith, and establishments for the sale of beer, cigars, cigarettes, all forms of tobacco, beverages and soft drinks at retail. A club or charitable, religious or nonprofit organization may be issued a temporary "on sale" license for the sale of beer in accordance with section 366.40. No manufacturer, distributor, or wholesaler of beer shall have any ownership in whole or in part in the business of any licensee operating under an "on sale" license, except that a manufacturer, wholesaler or distributor may be granted one license. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.310; Ord. of 9-12-74, § 2)

children.title: Issuance and posting of license
children.text: Upon the granting by the city council of the application, a license shall be issued by the licensing official containing the name and address of the licensee and a description of the premises for which such license is granted, which license shall be signed by the licensing official and shall have attached thereto the seal of the city, and the same shall be kept posted at all times in a conspicuous place in the premises for which license is issued. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.320; 2013-Or-221, § 9, 12-6-13)

children.title: Death of licensee
children.text: The duly appointed, qualified and personal representative of the estate of a licensee may conduct the business authorized by any license issued under the terms of this chapter to the deceased licensee, for not more than ninety (90) days after the death of such licensee, upon filing by said personal representative with the licensing official, of a certified copy of appointment as such. The qualifications of an applicant for an original license under this chapter shall also apply to such personal representative, except insofar as such qualifications shall also be required by any other law. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.330; 82-Or-009, § 1, 1-15-82; 2013-Or-221, § 10, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 27, 10-9-25)

children.title: Military service of licensee
children.text: Any person licensed to sell beer who shall enter any of the services of the Armed Forces of the United States may continue as holder of such license, and may have the same renewed, together with any food license held in connection with the conduct of the business, by designating a person with power of attorney to manage and conduct the business while said licensee is in the armed forces and to apply for renewals of all such licenses for and on behalf of such licensee. Such power of attorney shall state that such licensee has entered the Armed Forces of the United States, and shall designate the particular branch thereof. In addition to the authority and power to manage and conduct the business, such power of attorney, if the licensee shall so desire, may also provide for the authority to sell and dispose of such business. Any application for the renewal of any such license shall be made by the person holding such power of attorney, for and on behalf of the licensee but all information required in the license application shall pertain to the person so appointed to manage and conduct the business of the licensee, and no person not qualified under this chapter to hold or obtain such license, shall be authorized to conduct or manage such business under said power of attorney, nor shall the application of any such person be accepted. Furthermore, the provisions of this chapter shall not apply unless the person appointed power of attorney shall notify the licensing official within thirty (30) days of the time the licensee entered the Armed Forces. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.340; Pet. No. 251179, § 45, 12-29-89; 2013-Or-221, § 11, 12-6-13; Ord. No. 2025-046, § 28, 10-9-25)

children.title: Premises to be open to inspection
children.text: The premises named in any license shall at all times while open to the public be open also to inspection and examination by the licensing official or any police, fire, regulatory code official or inspector, or health officer of the city. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.350; 2013-Or-221, § 12, 12-6-13)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2025-046, § 29, adopted October 9, 2025, repealed § 366.370, which pertained to permits to certain organizations and derived from Code 1960, as amend., § 852.360.

children.title: Discretion of council
children.text: The city council may exercise its judgment and discretion, to the fullest extent permitted by law, to grant or deny any application in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, title and any other applicable statute, rule or law. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 852.370; Ord. No. 2018-062, § 4, 11-2-18)

children.title: Liquor on beer-licensed premises
children.text:
(a) Every holder of any beer license shall prevent the consumption of liquor on the premises, and every licensee who shall knowingly permit liquor to be consumed on the premises shall have his or her license revoked, unless such licensee shall also be licensed to sell liquor pursuant to an "on sale" license issued by the city council for such premises. No person shall take or carry any liquor to or into any building or place, or consume any liquor in any building or place operated under a beer license granted by the city council, unless such licensee shall also be licensed to sell liquor pursuant to an "on sale" license issued by the city council. Provided, that this shall not prohibit possession by a manufacturer, wholesaler or distributor for the purpose of sale or deliveries of liquor by wholesalers to said premises while there is in full force and effect an "off sale" license to sell liquor upon said premises.

(b) No licensee, agent, proprietor, manager or person in charge of any premises licensed to sell beer shall keep, store, have under his or her control, or permit any person to keep or store upon such premises, any liquor of any kind, unless the licensee shall hold an unrevoked "on sale" or "off sale" license to sell liquor pursuant to chapter 362 of this Code. The presence of liquor in or on the licensed premises, unless the licensee possesses an unrevoked license to sell liquor "on sale" or "off sale", shall be prima facie evidence that said liquor is being kept or stored on said premises in violation of the provisions of this chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., §§ 854.020, 854.190; Pet. No. 251179, § 46, 12-29-89)

children.title: "Spiking" prohibited
children.text: No holder of any beer license shall mix or sell for the purpose of mixing, any beer, or suffer or permit upon the premises any mixing or spiking of beer, soft drinks, or any other liquor or beverage by adding to or with the same any alcohol or other intoxicating liquor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.030)

children.title: Free food or drink prohibited
children.text: No holder of any "on sale" license shall furnish free any food or drink at the licensed premises. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.040)

children.title: Drinking on highways
children.text:
No beer shall be sold or served for consumption, or consumed, upon any public highway or in any vehicle upon any public highway. No person shall transport or convey beer in any vehicle except in the original package with cap or seal unbroken. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.060)

Cross reference— Authority to operate sidewalk café notwithstanding provisions of above section, § 265.280.

children.title: Club sales to nonmembers
children.text: No club shall sell any beer to any person not a member thereof. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.070)

children.title: Hours generally
children.text:
No "off-sale" beer licensee shall sell or serve, or permit to be served, sold or consumed on the premises named in the license any beer on any Sunday between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 12:00 noon; no "on-sale" beer licensee shall sell or serve, or permit to be served, sold or consumed on the premises named in the license any beer on any Sunday between the hours of 1:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m.; nor any other day between the hours of 1:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.080; 84-Or-058, § 1, 4-13-84; 90-Or-041, § 1, 1-26-90; 2003-Or-085, § 1, 6-20-03; 2005-Or-079, § 1, 9-23-05; 2009-Or-116, § 1, 10-30-09)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 340A.504.

children.title: 2:00 a.m. sales permit
children.text:
(a) An establishment that has obtained a permit from the commissioner of public safety under Minnesota Statute Section 340A.504 subd. 7 may sell or serve beer until 2:00 a.m.

(b) An establishment that has obtained a permit from the commissioner of public safety under Minnesota Statute Section 340A.504 subd. 7 must be closed and kept closed to the public between the hours of 2:30 a.m. and 8:00 a.m.

(c) During said hours, beverage alcohol must be removed from all public areas of the establishment including tables and bar areas. (2009-Or-116, § 2, 10-30-09)

children.title: Premises without special license to close certain hours
children.text: Every room, place or premises wherein beer is permitted to be or is sold, including the café, restaurant or dining room operated in connection therewith or as a part thereof, and in which such beer is sold or served by the licensee thereof pursuant to an "on sale" or "off sale" license, shall be closed and kept closed to the public between the hours of 1:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless the licensee is the holder of a permit from the commissioner of public safety under Minnesota Statute Section 340A.504 subd. 7 and must be closed and kept closed to the public between the hours of 2:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m., or a special late hours license provided for in sections 360.70, 360.75, and 360.80. During said hours, if the licensee is not the holder of a special late hours license, no person or persons shall be allowed to be or remain upon or within such room, place or premises for any purpose whatever, except that the owner or licensee, his or her agents, servants or employees may remain therein for the purpose only of cleaning, preparation of meals, necessary repairs or other work therein and in connection therewith, or as guards. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.090; 90-Or-041, § 1, 1-26-90; 93-Or-193, § 1, 12-30-93; 2000-Or-073, § 1, 7-28-00; 2003-Or-085, § 2, 6-20-03; 2009-Or-116, § 3, 10-30-09)

children.title: Equipment for cleaning utensils
children.text: Every place where beer is sold shall be equipped with proper sinks or other equipment, and provided with running hot and cold water for sterilizing and rinsing cups, glasses, mugs or other utensils in which such beer is served, and the sink or other equipment for such sterilizing and rinsing shall be conveniently located to the spigots from which such beverages are drawn. In bars or fountains, such sinks or other equipment for sterilizing and rinsing shall be of the two-compartment type. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.160)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2014-Or-072, § 1, adopted September 19, 2014, repealed § 368.90, which pertained to restroom facilities. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Possession of federal liquor stamp
children.text: No person holding an "on sale" beer license, except persons also holding an "on sale" liquor license under Chapter 362, shall possess any federal license, stamp tax or revenue receipt evidencing payment to the federal government for a license or tax covering the sale of intoxicating liquor. Any holder of an "on sale" beer license who shall possess any federal license, stamp tax or revenue receipt shall be deemed to be engaged in the sale of liquor contrary to the provisions of this chapter, and his or her license shall be canceled and revoked. No renewal of license shall be granted such person. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.180; Pet. No. 251179, § 47, 12-29-89)

children.title: Exceptions
children.text: The provisions of sections 368.100 and 368.10(b) shall not apply to persons holding a federal license for the sale of liquors for medicinal purposes only. The provisions of section 368.10(b) shall not apply to a bottle club having valid permits issued pursuant to Chapter 372 and Minn. Statute, Section 340A.414. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 854.200; Ord. of 5-10-74, § 1; Pet. No. 251179, § 48, 12-29-89)

children.title: Sale to minors
children.text:
No person licensed under Chapters 362, 363 or 366, or such licensee's agent or employees, shall serve, authorize another to serve or dispense upon the licensed premises any liquor or beer to any person under the age of twenty-one (21) years; nor shall such licensee, or the licensee's agent or employee, permit any person under the age of twenty-one (21) years to be furnished with any liquor or beer on the licensed premises. For purposes of this section, the term "authorize another to serve" means:

(1) Verbally affirming or otherwise representing to another agent or employee of the licensee that a person under the age of twenty-one (21) years may be served any liquor or beer upon the licensed premises; or

(2) Affirming to another agent or employee of the licensee, by means of granting admittance to the licensed premises or affixing, placing or directing the affixing or placing of a mark, stamp, wristband or other identifiable sign, symbol or object upon a person under the age of twenty-one (21) years that said person may be served any liquor or beer upon the licensed premises. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 855.010; Ord. of 5-25-73, § 1; 76-Or-129, § 1, 8-13-76; 86-Or-193, § 1, 8-8-86; 2006-Or-025, § 1, 3-31-06)

State Law reference— Sales to persons under nineteen, M.S. § 340A.503.

children.title: Sales or service by minors
children.text: No person licensed under Chapters 362, 363 or 366 shall permit any person under eighteen (18) years of age to sell or serve liquor or beer on the licensed premises. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 855.020; Ord. of 5-25-73, § 1; 76-Or-129, § 2, 8-13-76; 86-Or-193, § 2 8-8-86)

children.title: Purchases, consumption by minors
children.text: No person under twenty-one (21) years of age shall enter any premises licensed for the retail sale of liquor or beer for the purpose of purchasing or having served or delivered to him or her any liquor or beer, nor shall any person under twenty-one (21) years of age consume any liquor or beer on the licensed premises, nor purchase, attempt to purchase or have another person purchase for him or her any liquor or beer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 855.030; Ord. of 5-25-73, § 1; 76-Or-129, § 3, 8-13-76; 86-Or-193, § 3, 8-8-86; Pet. No. 251179, § 49, 12-29-89)

children.title: Possession by minors
children.text: No person under the age of twenty-one (21) years shall consume or have in his or her possession, at any place other than the household of the person's parent or guardian, any liquor or beer with intent to consume the same, and possession thereof shall be prima facie evidence of intent to unlawfully consume the same. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 855.040; Ord. of 5-25-73, § 1; 76-Or-129, § 4, 8-13-76; 86-Or-193, § 4, 8-8-86)

children.title: Social host
children.text:
(a) Purpose and findings. The city council seeks to reduce underage possession and consumption of alcohol by imposing criminal penalties on those person(s) who host events or gatherings where persons under twenty-one (21) years of age possess or consume alcohol.

The city council finds that:

(1) Alcohol is an addictive drug, which, if used irresponsibly, could have drastic effects on those who use it as well as those who are affected by the actions of the irresponsible user.

(2) Events and gatherings held on private or public property where alcohol is possessed or consumed by persons under the age of twenty-one (21) are harmful to those persons and constitute a potential threat to public health, safety and welfare requiring prevention or abatement.

(3) Holding persons criminally responsible for hosting or permitting an event or gathering where underage possession or consumption of alcohol occurs will help deter underage consumption.

(b) Definitions.

(1) Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl or spirits of wine, liqueur, cordials, whiskey, rum, brandy, gin, or any other distilled spirits including dilutions and mixtures thereof from whatever source or by whatever process produced.

(2) Alcoholic beverage means alcohol, spirits, liquor, wine, beer, and every liquid or solid containing alcohol, spirits, wine or beer and which contains one-half (½) of one (1) percent or more of alcohol by volume and which is fit for beverage purposes either alone or when diluted, mixed or combined with other substances.

(3) Adult means any person eighteen (18) years of age or older.

(4) Underage person means any person under the age of twenty-one (21) years.

(5) Parent means any person having legal custody of a juvenile as a natural parent, adoptive parent, step parent, legal guardian, or a person to whom legal custody has been given by order of the court.

(6) Person means any individual, partnership, co-partnership, corporation, or any association of one (1) or more individuals.

(7) Host means to permit, aid, conduct, entertain, organize, supervise, or control an event or gathering.

(8) Event or gathering means any group of three (3) or more persons who have assembled or gathered together for a social occasion or other activity. An event or gathering shall not include assemblies or gatherings occurring on the licensed property of a retail intoxicating liquor or three and two-tenths (3.2) percent malt liquor licensee, municipal liquor store, or bottle club permit holder who is regulated by Minn. Stat. § 340A.503.

(9) Residence or premises means any home, yard, field, land, apartment, condominium, hotel or motel room, or other dwelling unit, or a hall or meeting room, park or any other place of assembly, public or private, whether occupied on a temporary or permanent basis, whether occupied as a dwelling or specifically for a party or other social function, and whether owned, leased, rented, or used with or without permission or compensation.

(c) Prohibited acts.

(1) It is unlawful for any person(s) to:

a. Host an event or gathering;

b. At any residence, premises, or on any other private or public property;

c. Where alcohol or alcoholic beverages are present; and

d. When the person knows or has reason to know that an underage person will or does:

1. Consume any alcohol or alcoholic beverage; or

2. Possess any alcohol or alcoholic beverage with the intent to consume it.

(2) It is a violation of section (c) if the person intentionally aids, advises, hires, counsels, or conspires with another or otherwise procures another to commit the prohibited act.

(3) A person who hosts an event or gathering does not have to be present at the event or gathering to be criminally responsible for a violation of section (c).

(d) Penalty. A violation of this section is a misdemeanor.

(e) Exceptions.

(1) It shall be an affirmative defense to a violation of section (c) that the defendant is the parent of the underage person and that the defendant gave or furnished the alcoholic beverage to that person solely for consumption in the defendant's household.

(2) It shall be an affirmative defense to a violation of section (c) that the conduct was part of a legally protected religious observance.

(f) Severability.  If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, part, provision, phrase, word, or other portion of this section is, for any reason, held to be unconstitutional or invalid, in whole or in part by any court of competent jurisdiction, such portion shall be deemed severable, and such unconstitutionality or invalidity shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this chapter, which remaining portions shall continue in full force and effect.

(2010-Or-005, § 1, 2-12-10)

children.title: Misrepresentation of age
children.text: No person shall misrepresent or misstate his or her age, or the age of another person, for the purpose of inducing any licensee or employee to sell, serve or deliver any liquor or beer to a person under twenty-one (21) years of age. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 855.050; Ord. of 5-25-73, § 1; 76-Or-129, § 5, 8-13-76; 86-Or-193, § 5, 8-8-86)

children.title: Proof of age
children.text: Any person who may appear to the licensee or to the licensee's employees or agents to be under twenty-one (21) years of age shall, upon demand of the licensee or the licensee's employees or agents, produce and permit to be examined appropriate identification as provided for by applicable state statutes. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 855.060; Ord. of 5-25-73, § 2; 76-Or-129, § 6, 8-13-76; 86-Or-193, § 6, 8-8-86)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-042, § 1, adopted Jan. 26, 1990, repealed § 370.70. Said section pertained to certain persons excepted from the regulations herein, and was derived from 86-Or-193, § 7, adopted Aug. 8, 1986.

children.heading: CHAPTER 372.
children.title: BOTTLE CLUBS
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (6) ---

State Law reference— Bottle clubs, M.S. § 340A.414.

children.title: Statement of intent and purpose
children.text:
In the adoption of this article, and as aids in the construction, interpretation and enforcement of this article, the city council finds:

(a) That there has been an increase in the number of so-called private locker or bottle clubs where intoxicating liquor has been kept, stored and used.

(b) That there is an increasing tendency to establish such locker or bottle clubs in conjunction with public cafés and restaurants not having licenses to sell intoxicating liquors situated in residential areas, and frequented by both adults and children.

(c) That the unlicensed and unregulated consumption of liquor leads to violations of law and is detrimental to the public health, welfare and morals, and may degenerate into a public nuisance.

(d) That many public cafés and restaurants are located near theaters, stores and other public places where children may and do congregate and that drunkenness and disobedience of law would adversely affect the morals and welfare of such children and others.

(e) That in many instances the creation of bottle or locker clubs by public cafés and restaurants is merely a scheme or device to circumvent the laws regulating the licensing and regulation of liquor establishments, placing liquor places in prohibited areas, and the payment of license fees.

(f) That such practices tend to cause inconvenience and annoyance to the public generally and are detrimental to the good order, health, morals and welfare of the community as a whole.

For the foregoing reasons it is the intent and purpose of this article to prohibit any connection whatsoever between the so-called private bottle or locker clubs and public cafés and restaurants, and to prevent the use of any trick, artifice or evasion to circumvent the declared policy of the state and of the city in regulating the dispensing of intoxicating liquors in public places, by prohibiting the existence of such private bottle or locker clubs in a space, room or area leased to or made available to such private bottle or locker clubs by the erection of or the closing of a door or other exit, and prohibiting the existence of such clubs on floors other than those occupied by the restaurant in the same building. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 857.010)

children.title: Restaurants not to have bottle clubs or permit display or consumption of liquor or beer
children.text: No public restaurant or café not having a license for the "on sale" of liquor shall have or maintain, or permit to be established or maintained, any so-called private bottle or locker club wherein members keep or have liquor or beer in any room or other area or space connected with or readily accessible to said café or restaurant, or on the same premises as the café or restaurant. Nor shall such restaurant or café permit the consumption or display of any liquor or beer in any room or other area or space connected with or readily accessible to said café or restaurant or on the same premises as the café or restaurant. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 857.020)

children.title: "Set-ups" prohibited
children.text: No owner, proprietor, manager or licensee of any such restaurant or café, by himself or by any agents, servants or employees, shall serve or furnish to such so-called bottle or locker clubs any beverage, ice or so-called set-ups to be mixed with or compounded with any intoxicating liquor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 857.030)

children.title: Renting to bottle clubs prohibited
children.text: No proprietor, owner, licensee or manager of any such restaurant or café shall make or participate in any transaction whereby any room, area or space connected with, controlled by, or adjacent to such café or restaurant may be leased to or made available to any such locker or bottle club, or whereby any such locker or bottle club is granted use of any room or space connected with or under control of the restaurant or café, with or without consideration. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 857.040)

children.title: Issuance of additional bottle club permits prohibited
children.text: Effective November 3, 1995, no additional bottle club permits shall be issued. Any person, partnership, firm or corporation holding a bottle club permit as of November 3, 1995, may continue to apply to renew such permit in conjunction with the renewal of their consumption and display permit issued by the liquor control commissioner of the state pursuant to the provisions of Minn. Statute, Section 340A.414, by paying a fee to the city for on-sale liquor and for on-sale beer as established in Appendix J, License Fee Schedule, the payment of such fee to be evidenced by a receipt from the city finance officer. Such receipt shall at all times be displayed in a prominent place in the premises for which the permit is issued by the liquor control commissioner. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 859.010; Pet. No. 251179, § 50, 12-29-89; 90-Or-014, § 1, 1-26-90; 95-Or-147, § 1, 10-27-95; 98-Or-046, § 1, 5-22-98; 2002-Or-081, § 1, 8-9-02)

children.title: Approval of city council
children.text: Upon receipt of an application for renewal of a bottle club permit the department shall refer the application to the police license inspector who, upon having completed investigation thereof, shall make a report to the city council. The city council may approve or disapprove said application for renewal provided no application for renewal shall be disapproved except for cause and after a hearing thereon with ten (10) days' notice to the applicant. (76-Or-130, § 1, 8-13-76; Pet. No. 251179, § 51, 12-29-89; 95-Or-147, § 2, 10-27-95)

children.title: Inspection
children.text: Any private club or public place allowing the consumption or display of intoxicating liquor shall be open at all reasonable hours for inspection by the liquor control commissioner, his or her designated agents and all duly authorized peace officers of the city. Refusal to permit such inspections shall be a violation of this article. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 859.020; Pet. No. 251179, § 52, 12-29-89)

children.title: Revocation of licenses
children.text: In addition to all other penalties for a violation of this article, the city council may revoke all licenses issued by the city to such private club or public place. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 859.030)

children.title: Other ordinances not affected
children.text: The adoption of this article shall not be construed to repeal, suspend or modify the provisions of any other ordinance relating to the consumption or display of intoxicating liquor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 859.040)

children.heading: CHAPTER 374.
children.title: MINNEAPOLIS CONVENTION CENTER LIQUOR LICENSE
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (7) ---

Editor's note— 89-Or-073, § 1, adopted April 28, 1989, amended Ch. 374 in its entirety to read as herein set forth. Prior to such amendment, Ch. 374, §§ 374.10—374.70, pertained to dispensing at the Minneapolis Convention Hall—Auditorium, and were derived from Code 1960, As Amend., §§ 860.010—860.070; ordinance of Oct. 19, 1973, § 1; ordinance of Feb. 28, 1975, § 1; and 86-Or-033, § 1, adopted Feb. 28, 1986.

It should be noted that § 2 of 89-Or-073 provides as follows: "This ordinance shall be effective upon approval by the city council of Laws of Minnesota 1989, Chapter 40, Section 2, pursuant to Minn. Statute, Section 645.021."

Special law reference—Laws 1989, Chapter 40, § 2, authorizing an on-sale liquor license for the Minneapolis Convention Center, was accepted by 89-R-167 on April 28, 1989.

children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall mean:

Convention center. The Minneapolis Convention Center located at 1301 Second Avenue South, and all expansions and additions thereto.

Convention center manager. The person designated by the City of Minneapolis to manage the convention center, or such manager's duly authorized representative. (89-Or-073, § 1, 4-28-89)

children.title: On-sale license authorized
children.text:
The city council may issue an on-sale liquor license to an alcoholic beverage caterer to dispense alcoholic beverages at the convention center.

The holder of the on-sale liquor license for the convention center shall comply with all provisions of statutes, ordinances, and regulations governing the retail sale of alcoholic beverages. (89-Or-073, § 1, 4-28-89)

children.title: Restrictions
children.text:
(a) The dispensing of alcoholic beverages at the convention center shall be further regulated and restricted by the terms of any contract between the City of Minneapolis and the holder of the on-sale license regarding the catering of alcoholic beverages and food at the convention center.

(b) No alcoholic beverages shall be sold or dispensed at the convention center except by the license holder as provided in this chapter.

(c) No alcoholic beverages may be sold or dispensed under the provisions of this chapter by any person other than a person legally employed by the licensee nor at any location in the convention center except as authorized by the convention center manager.

(d) The licensee may dispense intoxicating liquor only at events held by persons or organizations permitted to use the convention center premises, and may dispense intoxicating liquor only to persons attending such events. The licensee may not dispense intoxicating liquor to persons attending or participating in any amateur event held on the premises. (89-Or-073, § 1, 4-28-89)

children.title: Special provisions
children.text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this title, the term "restaurant," as used in section 362.425 and for purposes of Sunday sales license requirements, shall include the facilities available to and operated by the on-sale license holder at the convention center. (89-Or-073, § 1, 4-28-89; 2002-Or-048, § 1, 6-7-02)
