children.title: Responsibility of persons other than driver
children.text: No person having possession or control of a motor vehicle shall knowingly authorize or allow the same to be driven or operated by any person prohibited from driving or operating such vehicle. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 402.100)

children.title: Exemptions for working on the highway
children.text: The provisions of sections 466.230 and 474.240 shall not apply to persons, motor vehicles, and other equipment while actually engaged in work upon streets, avenues, roadways, or highways. (2009-Or-045, § 1, 5-22-09)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Sections 3—8 of 90-Or-126, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 466.60—466.110. Prior to such repeal, said sections pertained to applicability of traffic code to public vehicles and to street maintenance vehicles, emergency vehicles, animals and animal-drawn vehicles, owners of vehicles obeying regulations, and persons responsible for violations, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 421.070, 421.080, 421.130—421.150, 425.110, 640.232.

children.title: Police to enforce code
children.text: The chief of police, except as otherwise provided, shall enforce all the regulations and requirements of the traffic code. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.010)

children.title: Obedience to police officers
children.text: No person shall willfully fail or refuse to comply with any lawful order or direction of a peace officer invested by law with authority to direct, control or regulate traffic. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.110)

children.title: Only authorized persons to regulate traffic
children.text: No unauthorized person shall regulate or attempt to regulate traffic upon the streets and highways of the city. Police officers are authorized to regulate traffic upon the streets and highways of the city. Traffic control agents while working for the city are authorized to regulate traffic upon the streets and highways of the city. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.020; 81-Or-309, § 1, 12-28-81; 2008-Or-064, § 1, 8-22-08)

children.title: When signs required
children.text:
No part of this title designating particular streets as one-way streets, and requiring that all vehicles thereon be moved in one specific direction; or designating any street or highway as a thru street or highway and requiring that all vehicles stop before entering or crossing the same; or designating any intersection as a stop intersection and requiring all vehicles to stop at one or more entrances to such intersections; or restricting the use of highways as authorized shall be effective until signs giving notice of such traffic regulations are posted upon and kept posted upon or at the entrance to the street or highway or part affected thereof as may be most appropriate. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.200)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.04.

children.title: Obedience to traffic-control devices
children.text: No driver of a vehicle, or pedestrian, or person riding an animal or bicycle shall disobey the instructions of any official traffic-control device, sign, signal or marking upon any street or highway, unless at the time otherwise directed by a police officer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 407.190)

children.title: Unauthorized signs, signals, etc
children.text:
No person shall place, maintain or display upon or in view of any street or highway any unauthorized sign, signal, marking or device which purports to be or is an imitation of or resembles any official traffic-control device or railroad sign or signal, or which attempts to direct the movement of traffic or which hides from view or interferes with the effectiveness of any official traffic-control device or railroad sign or signal. No person shall place or maintain nor shall any public authority permit upon any street or highway any traffic signal or signal bearing thereon any commercial advertising. This shall not be deemed to prohibit the erection upon private property adjacent to streets or highways of signs giving useful directional information and of a type that cannot be mistaken for official signs. Every such prohibited sign, signal or marking is declared to be a public nuisance and the city engineer's department may remove the same or cause it to be removed without notice. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.050)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.07.

children.title: Unauthorized lights
children.text:
(a) No person shall use red, green or amber lights on the highways for advertising or for signaling purposes, except as provided in the traffic code.

(b) No person or corporation shall place, maintain or display any red, green or amber light or sign, signal or lighting device or maintain the same in view of any highway or any line of railroad on or over which trains are operated in such a way as to interfere with the effectiveness or efficiency of any highway traffic-control device or signals or devices used in the operation of a railroad.

(c) Where such prohibited light, sign, signal or device interferes with the effectiveness or efficiency of any highway traffic-control device or signal the city engineer shall have authority to cause the removal of the same upon written notice to such person or corporation.

(d) No person or corporation shall continue to maintain or display any such light, sign, signal or device after written notice from the city engineer that said light, sign, signal or device constitutes a traffic hazard and ordering the removal thereof. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.060)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.073.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Sections 9—12 of 90-Or-126, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 466.190—466.220. Prior to such repeal, said sections pertained to molesting traffic signs or devices, record of conviction not admissible in civil action, convictions not to affect credibility as witness, and violation as prima facie evidence of negligence, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 421.040, 425.120—425.140.

children.title: Obstructing traffic with vehicle
children.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to so drive and operate or park a vehicle upon the streets or highways in the city as to needlessly, unnecessarily and unwarrantedly block, obstruct or interfere with the orderly flow of traffic on said streets. Proof that such traffic was blocked, obstructed or interfered with shall be prima facie evidence that such blocking, obstructing and interference was needless, unnecessary and unwarranted. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.170)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.15.

children.title: Assemblies obstructing pedestrian or vehicular traffic
children.text:
(a) No person or group of persons shall assemble or cause others to assemble on any sidewalk so as to obstruct the free passage of pedestrians thereon or interfere with the use thereof.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person individually or as a member of any group of persons to loiter, stand, sit, lie or remain upon or within any street, sidewalk, crosswalk or other public way or otherwise occupy any portion thereof with the intent or purpose to block, obstruct or interfere with the free passage of any pedestrian thereon or the orderly free flow of vehicular traffic on said street or public way.

(c) This section shall not be interpreted to restrict the lawful exercise of freedom of speech and assembly.

(d) Violation of this section is a petit misdemeanor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 408.090; 84-Or-069, § 1, 4-27-84)

Cross reference— For similar provisions relative to obstructing passage of pedestrians, § 427.220.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-126, §§ 13—15, adopted May 11, 1989, repealed §§ 466.250—466.270. Said former sections pertained to obstructing driver's view or control, following or parking near fire apparatus and driving near fire stations, and parking near hydrants or fire stations, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 421.090, 421.160, 640.230, 640.231.

children.title: Using vehicle for advertising
children.text: No person shall operate or park on any street a vehicle for the primary purpose of advertising. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.260; 99-Or-100, § 1, 9-17-99)

children.title: Tampering with vehicles
children.text: Except as provided in sections 478.170, 478.180 and 478.240, no person shall molest or tamper with a motor vehicle without the permission of the owner, or without authority of the person in charge, climb upon or into any automobile, whether the same is in motion or at rest, or hurl stones or any other missiles at the same, or the occupants thereof, or while such motor vehicle is at rest and unattended, attempt to manipulate any of the levers, starting devices, brakes or machinery thereof, or set such motor vehicle in motion, or otherwise damage or interfere with the same, or place upon any street, avenue or highway of the state any glass, tacks, nails or other articles tending to injure automobile tires. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.030)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-126, § 16, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed § 466.300, which section pertained to distress signals for handicapped persons, and which was derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 411.280.

children.heading: CHAPTER 468.
children.title: VIOLATION PROCEDURE
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (2) ---

Cross reference— Penalty for traffic violations, § 1.30; park and recreation board traffic code, § PB9-1 et seq.; streets and sidewalks, Title 17, Ch. 427 et seq.; moving of buildings, Ch. 115; requirements for vehicles used for peddling food, § 186.60; requirements for operation of food-vending vehicle, § 188.560; identification of vehicles used for transportation of food, § 188.570; ambulances, § 221.10 et seq.; requirements for vehicles used for collection and transportation of garbage, ashes and refuse, § 225.110 et seq.; § 225.290 et seq.; racetracks, Ch. 273; broadcasting vehicles, Ch. 275; motor scooter leasing, Ch. 311; motor vehicle dealers, Ch. 313; motor vehicle lubricant dealers, Ch. 315; open air motor vehicle parking lots, Ch. 319; inspection of odometer on rental automobiles, Ch. 327; taxicabs, Ch. 341; transportation of handicapped persons other than by ambulance, Ch. 345; used motor vehicle parts dealers, Ch. 348; wreckers and touring services, Ch. 349; restrictions on use of vehicle radios, tape players, etc., § 389.90; vehicular noise control generally, § 389.140 et seq.

children.title: Traffic tag defined
children.text:
The term "traffic tag" means a written or printed notice of a violation of a traffic law or municipal ordinance, charter provision, rule or regulation served upon the person so charged in person, by U.S. Mail, or affixed conspicuously to a motor vehicle operated, parked or standing in violation thereof, which requires appearance before the traffic violations bureau within a specified time. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.010; 2005-Or-048, § 1, 6-17-05)

State Law reference— Uniform traffic ticket, M.S. § 169.99.

children.title: Authority to issue traffic tags in lieu of arrest
children.text: In lieu of taking a person into custody for a violation of the provisions of the traffic code, a police officer or any other person duly authorized by ordinance may serve or authorize to be served a written notice upon such person to appear before the traffic violations bureau of the district court at a time and place fixed in said notice. The notice shall contain the name and address of the person charged with such violation, the license number of the vehicle involved and the offense charged. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.020; 90-Or-127, § 1, 5-11-90; 2005-Or-048, § 2, 6-17-05)

children.title: Form of tags
children.text: Such notice shall indicate in addition to the information called for in section 468.20 the time, date and nature of the violation, and in the case of a motor vehicle, the motor vehicle license number. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.030; 2005-Or-048, § 3, 6-17-05)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Section 2 of 90-Or-127, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed § 468.40. Said section pertained to tickets for airport regulation violations, and was derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 425.031.

children.title: Tags for parked vehicles
children.text: Whenever any motor vehicle without an operator is found parked in violation of any of the parking restrictions of the traffic code, the police officer or any other person duly authorized by ordinance finding it shall take its registration number and any other information displayed on the vehicle which may identify its user, and affix conspicuously to such vehicle a written notice for the operator to appear before the traffic violations bureau of the district court at a time and place fixed in said notice. During periods of duly declared snow emergencies or other officially authorized street maintenance activities, all personnel of the city authorized to issue tags for any purpose, and foremen of the public works office, shall be authorized to issue the written notices herein provided for. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.040; 90-Or-127, § 3, 5-11-90; 2011-Or-099, § 1, 11-4-11)

children.title: Disposition of tags
children.text: The police officer or any other person duly authorized by ordinance serving the written notice provided for in this chapter shall deliver one copy of the notice to the person charged with a violation or affix the copy in a prominent place on or within the vehicle and one copy to the traffic violations bureau of the district court. The notice form referred to shall be identified by a separate serial number for each notice. The city finance officer shall audit all accounts, records, files and papers of the chief of police and the clerk of district court at stated periods, relating to said notices, cash statements and disposition of cases of violation of the provisions of the traffic code. The city finance officer shall furnish to the city council monthly reports of the number of violations, warrants, appeals, cancellations and receipts. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.050; 90-Or-127, § 4, 5-11-90; 2005-Or-048, § 4, 6-17-05)

children.title: Duties of persons tagged
children.text:
A person who receives a traffic tag shall proceed as follows:

(a) If a fine for the violation may be paid at the bureau without appearance before a judge, the person charged may pay the fine in person or by mail to the bureau within the time specified in the tag. Such a payment of the fine shall be deemed to be the entry of a plea of guilty to the violation charged and a consent to the imposition of a sentence for the violation in the amount of the fine paid. A receipt shall be issued to evidence the payment, and receipt so issued shall be complete satisfaction for the violation charged in that traffic tag.

(b) When a fine is not so paid, the person charged must appear at the bureau within the time specified in the tag, state whether he or she desires to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty, arrange for a date for arraignment in court and appear in court for arraignment on a date set by the bureau.

(c) No person upon whom a written notice has been served in the manner provided for in this chapter for a violation of the provisions of the traffic code shall fail to either appear before the traffic violations bureau of the district court at the place and within the time fixed in said notice, or satisfy the violation charged in said tag in the manner provided above. Any person who willfully refuses to give his or her name and address or who gives a false name or address shall be guilty of a violation of this chapter, regardless of the offense with which he or she was originally charged. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.060; 90-Or-127, § 5, 5-11-90)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Section 6 of 90-Or-127, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed § 468.80, which section pertained to when immediate arraignment required, and which was derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 425.070.

children.title: Procedure prescribed not exclusive
children.text: The foregoing provisions of this chapter shall govern all police officers in making arrests without a warrant for violations of the traffic code for offenses committed in their presence, but the procedure prescribed herein shall not otherwise be exclusive of any other method prescribed by law for the arrest and prosecution of a person for an offense of like grade. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.080)

children.title: Prior record to be obtained for nonparking offenses
children.text: Whenever a person is arrested for any violation of the traffic code, other than violation of parking regulations, the court before whom such matter is heard shall obtain the driver's record of such person from the commissioner before pronouncing sentence, and the expense incident to the procurement of such information shall be taxable as costs upon conviction. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.090)

children.title: Driver improvement clinics
children.text:
(a) In conjunction with or in lieu of other penalties provided by law for violation of this chapter, the trial court may in its judgment of conviction order the convicted person to attend and satisfactorily complete a course of study at an approved driver improvement clinic, as defined by, and established pursuant to Minnesota Statutes. Any person who fails to comply with such an order may be adjudged in contempt of court. The requirement of attendance at a driver improvement clinic is not a fine, imprisonment or sentence within the meaning of Minnesota Statutes, Section 609.02. The court may not order a convicted person to attend a driver improvement clinic which is located more than twenty (20) miles from the person's residence. For the purposes of this section, "an approved driver improvement clinic" means a clinic whose curriculum and mode of instruction conform to standards promulgated by the commissioner.

(b) The course of study at a driver improvement clinic may not exceed the cumulative total of hours provided by Minnesota Statutes, and no single class session shall last longer than the maximum time provided by Minnesota Statutes. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.091)

State Law reference— Driver improvement clinics, M.S. § 169.971 et seq.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-127, § 7, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed § 468.120. Said section pertained to abstract of court records to go to department, and was derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 425.100.

children.title: Equipment violation tag authorized
children.text: In lieu of the traffic tag set forth in this chapter, the officer may issue a notice of equipment violations tag for the following violations: Obscured license; unlit rear license; head or rear lights or brake lights not operating or out; turn signals inoperative; windshield wipers, rearview mirror, horn or bumper not in compliance; or lack of or defective license plates. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.220)

children.title: Contents of notice of equipment violation
children.text: The notice of equipment violation shall show the vehicle license, the location at which the violation occurred, the make of vehicle and license number, the name and address of the owner and the name and address of the driver, the name and address of the officer issuing the tag, and shall include a statement that the vehicle was being operated with illegal equipment in violation of Minneapolis traffic ordinances and that the owner or operator of the vehicle must, within five (5) days after the issuance of the tag, repair and correct the equipment violation and submit his vehicle to any police officer for inspection. If proper repairs and replacements have been made, the inspecting officer shall so note on the tag, which shall be filed with the police department and no further action taken thereon. If the owner or operator of such vehicle does not make the necessary equipment corrections and report the same within five (5) days, such driver, owner or operator shall be subject to arrest and prosecution as provided by ordinance. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.230)

children.title: Form of equipment violation tag
children.text: The chief of police shall prescribe the size, style and contents of the equipment violations tag in conformity with the provisions of the foregoing sections. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 425.240)

children.heading: CHAPTER 470.
children.title: TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS BUREAU
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (3) ---

Cross reference— Ordinance violations bureau, Ch. 26.

children.title: "Bureau" defined
children.text: The term "bureau" means the Traffic Violations Bureau of the District Court of Hennepin County. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 422.010; 90-Or-128, § 1, 5-11-90)

children.title: Bureau continued; hours
children.text: The traffic violations bureau established by the judges of the district court to assist the court with the clerical work of traffic cases shall be continued. The bureau shall be open at such hours as the judges of the district court may designate. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 422.020; 90-Or-128, § 2, 5-11-90)

children.title: Judges to set fines
children.text:
The judge or judges of the district court who hear traffic cases shall designate fines to be paid for all offenses, which may be satisfied at the bureau, provided such fines are within the limitations established as penalties for the particular violations. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 422.030; 90-Or-128, § 3, 5-11-90)

Cross reference— Fines for traffic violations, § 1.30.

children.title: Duties
children.text:
The duties of the traffic violations bureau shall be as follows:

(a) It shall accept designated fines, issue receipts and represent in court such violators as are permitted and desire to plead guilty and waive court appearance.

(b) It shall enter the time of appearance of all persons who must, or wish to be heard in court, on the court docket, and notify the arresting officer and witnesses, if any, to be present.

(c) It shall keep an easily accessible record of all violations of which each person has been guilty during the preceding twelve (12) months, whether such guilt was established in court or in the traffic violations bureau.

(d) If a violator of the parking restrictions of the traffic code does not appear as provided in this chapter, the traffic violations bureau shall send to the registered owner of the motor vehicle to which the notice was affixed a letter informing him of the violations and warning him that he will be held responsible for the appearance of the offender, and that in the event such letter is disregarded for a period of three (3) days, a complaint will be filed and a warrant of arrest issued. The traffic violations bureau shall not accept fines from such persons.

(e) If any person who has received a notice or summons as provided in this chapter fails to appear within the specified times, the traffic violations bureau shall forthwith have a complaint entered against him and secure and issue a warrant for his arrest. The traffic violations bureau shall not accept fines from such persons.

(f) The bureau shall keep records and submit summarized monthly reports to the city comptroller-treasurer [finance officer] of all notices issued and arrests made for violations and of all the fines collected by the traffic violations bureau of the court, and of the final disposition or present status of every case of violation. These reports shall be public records. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 422.040)

children.heading: CHAPTER 474.
children.title: VEHICLE OPERATION
children.text: Footnotes:

children.title: Reserved

children.title: Starting and acceleration
children.text: No person shall start or accelerate any motor vehicle with an unnecessary exhibition of speed on any public or private way within the city limits. Prima facie evidence of such unnecessary exhibition of speed shall be unreasonable squealing or screeching sounds emitted by the tires or the throwing of sand or gravel by the tires of said vehicle or both. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 403.025; Ord. of 1-31-75, § 1)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 474.40—474.110. Prior to repeal, said sections pertained to driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, definition of "alcoholic beverage", penalty for driving while intoxicated or drugged, evidence from chemical tests for alcohol, open bottle law, employment of intemperate drivers, minor under seventeen not to drive motor vehicle between certain hours, and crossing fire hose, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 403.030—403.090, 421.100, 640.220.

children.title: Zones of quiet
children.text:
No person in any zone of quiet shall make any unnecessary noise by fast driving, riding, ringing of bells, blowing of horns or whistles, or by cutting out the muffler of any motor vehicle, or in any other way tending to disturb the peace and quiet in said zone. The city engineer shall erect suitable signs to identify said zones. University Avenue Southeast from Eleventh to Eighteenth Avenues is a zone of quiet. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 875.050)

Cross reference— Noise generally, Ch. 389.

children.title: Engine braking
children.text: Pursuant to the authority granted in Minnesota Session Law Chapter 350, Article 1, Section 87 (2008), Engine Brakes; Regulation by Minneapolis, it is prohibited to use an engine brake on motor vehicles along Legislative Route No. 107, also known as marked Interstate Highway 394, beginning at the South Penn Avenue interchange in the City of Minneapolis and thence extending easterly to the terminus of marked Interstate Highway 394. For purposes of this section, "engine brake" means any device that uses the engine and transmission to impede the forward motion of the motor vehicle by compression of the engine. (2014-Or-016, § 1, 4-11-14)

children.title: Unnecessary sounding of horns
children.text:
No person shall sound the horn, siren or other signal or warning device attached to a motor vehicle in a public place between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. This section shall not apply to police, fire or public or private ambulance motor vehicles; and shall not be construed to prevent or prohibit the use or sounding of any such horn, siren, signal or warning device as a danger or warning signal when such use or sounding is necessary in the careful and proper operation of any motor vehicle on the public highways, having due regard to traffic, the condition of the highway, and the safety of persons or property, nor when such use or sounding is required by law or ordinance. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 875.020)

Cross reference— Noise, Ch. 389.

children.title: Backing
children.text: No person in control of a vehicle shall back said vehicle without ample warning, and while backing, care must be exercised not to injure persons or property. No person shall back any vehicle around a corner at an intersection of streets or highways, except as provided in section 474.150. (Code 1960, As Amended., § 410.050)

children.title: Bus wyeing
children.text:
(a) A driver of a bus operating on a fixed route within the city may wye his bus at a particular regularly established terminal following an investigation and report by the city engineer, approval of the intersections at the particular terminal by the city council for such wyeing operation, and posting of notices at said intersections. The city engineer shall investigate the feasibility and safety of requiring the bus to circle a city block as an alternative to wyeing at a street intersection.

(b) The investigation of such an alternative operation shall include a study of the hazard and danger to city property, such as curbs and sidewalks, which may result from the heaving of curbs and sidewalks by reason of the weight of the bus in turning at and near street corners and in the buses running over the curbs and the danger to pedestrians at the crosswalk which may result from such damage to curbs and sidewalks, and may result from the irregularity of the surface of the street at crosswalks which may be caused by ruts created by reason of the weight of the buses, the danger to catch basins, and the effect upon drainage, with the likelihood of the resulting damage to property in the neighborhood. He shall investigate the width of the street, the parking problems involved, the need for eliminating parking of vehicles to permit maneuvering of buses at corners and along streets around said block, the extent of the difficulty of enforcing parking regulations as compared with the enforcement of such regulations at the intersection where the bus would otherwise wye, and the danger to persons and property which might result from the buses traveling around said block.

(c) He shall consider the extent of the lighting furnished at the street intersections and on the streets involved in the proposed movement around the block, and the hazard to persons and property during the nighttime which would result from traveling around the block. He shall investigate the feasibility and comparative safety of permitting the buses to make a "U" turn at street intersections if such an operation is possible with reasonable changes in location of curbs and sidewalks. He shall consider the density of traffic at the corners where wyes are proposed, shall make a study of the experience as to numbers of accidents at such corners to determine whether a particular intersection is accident prone. He shall consider the proximity of public playgrounds and schools and school ground areas. He shall consider the grade of streets where wyeing is proposed and consider the grades of streets on which the buses would travel if the alternative around-the-block operation were followed with particular consideration as to the hazards resulting from such grades. He shall study and consider all other factors which in his judgment enter into a determination of the relative danger or safety of the alternative operations which the buses may follow in reversing their direction at terminals.

(d) In his report the city engineer shall state his conclusions as to the relative safety of the alternative methods of buses reversing their direction at terminals. The city council shall consider the report of the city engineer, and if it concludes and determines on the basis of said report that wyeing at any particular terminal by backing around a corner is safer than the alternative methods, and that such operation should be used in the interest of the public safety, health, convenience and welfare, it shall instruct the city engineer to post signs at such particular intersections, and at such other points along the street approaching said intersection as the city engineer shall deem advisable, giving notice that buses wye at such intersection. Following such investigation, report and determination, and following the posting of such notices, buses are authorized to wye at such intersections by backing around the corner. After intersections for wyeing of buses have been established, the city engineer shall investigate the conditions at each of said intersections from time to time and if he determines that changed conditions affecting safety warrant it, he shall make a report to the city council and recommend a corresponding change in the manner of reversing direction of buses at the terminals involved. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 410.060)

children.title: Reserved

Prior to such repeal, said sections pertained to duty to keep to the right, meeting other vehicles, overtaking and passing, passing on right, and limitation on overtaking and passing on left, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 407.010—407.050.

children.title: One-way streets and alleys established
children.text:
The one-way streets and alleys established by the city council as of July 1, 1960 (Chapters 9:17 and 9:18, 1948 Compilation of Ordinances) are continued in effect, and the council may add to or modify the said routes by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The city traffic engineer shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all one-way streets and alleys, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 443.010)

State Law reference— Authority to designate one-way streets, M.S. § 169.04(4).

children.title: Driving on one-way streets and alleys
children.text: No person shall drive or operate, or cause to be driven or operated, any vehicle on any one-way street or alley except in the direction permitted on said street or alley. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 443.020)

children.title: Authorized emergency vehicle on one-way streets
children.text:
The driver of any authorized emergency vehicle, when responding to an emergency call, may enter against the run of traffic on any one-way street or highway where there is authorized division of traffic, to facilitate traveling to the area in which an emergency has been reported. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 640.233)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.03, Subd. 3.

children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 474.260—474.320. Said sections pertained to rotary islands, driving on multiple-laned highways, following too closely, divided highways and crossovers, slow-moving vehicles, turning at intersections, and u-turns, and was derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 407.070—407.130; and 85-Or-092, § 1, adopted April 26, 1985.

children.title: Driving or operating on public property
children.text: No vehicle other than government vehicles shall be driven or operated on any public property not at the time open to the use of such vehicles. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 407.270; Ord. of 9-28-73, § 2)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 474.340—474.360, which sections pertained to starting a parked vehicle, coasting, and hitching, and which were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 407.140—474.160.

children.title: Jumping rides
children.text: No person shall ride in or jump into or upon any vehicle without the consent of the driver and no person shall, when riding, allow any part of the body to project beyond the limits of any motor vehicle, except when signaling as required, nor shall any person board or alight from, nor hang on to any motor vehicle when such motor vehicle is in motion. This section shall not apply to any person whose employment makes it necessary to ride in or upon a vehicle otherwise than herein provided, when engaged in the necessary duties of such employment. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 407.170)

children.title: Safety zones
children.text:
No vehicle shall at any time be driven through a safety zone. The city engineer may mark pavements and erect signs, indicating the location and extent of safety zones at such places established therefor by the city council. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 407.180)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.25.

children.title: Speed on city streets
children.text:
The city engineer may establish speed limits for city streets under the city's jurisdiction in accordance with the provisions set forth at Minnesota Statutes Section 169.14. A comprehensive listing and the procedures relied upon to establish speed limits under this section 474.420 shall be kept on file by the director of public works, and will be made readily available for public inspection.

(Ord. No. 2019-063, § 1, 12-13-19)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 474.420—474.460. Said repealed sections pertained to basic speed rule, general speed limit, impeding traffic, reduced speed required at hazards, and speed in alleys, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 404.010—404.050.

children.title: Speed on bridges
children.text:
(a) No person shall drive a vehicle over any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a street or highway at a speed which is greater than the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to such bridge or structure, when such structure is signposted as provided in this section.

(b) The city engineer may request the commissioner of highways to conduct an investigation of any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a street or highway, and if the commissioner shall find that such structure cannot with safety to itself withstand vehicles traveling at the speed otherwise permissible he shall determine and declare the maximum speed of vehicles which such structure can withstand, and shall cause or permit suitable signs stating such maximum speed to be erected and maintained at a distance of one hundred (100) feet before each end of such structure.

(c) Upon the trial of any person charged with a violation of this section, proof of said determination of the maximum speed by the commissioner and the existence of said signs shall constitute conclusive evidence of the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to such bridge or structure. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 404.060)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.16.

children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 474.480—474.500, which sections pertained to exemption for emergency vehicles, summons to specify speed, and burden of proof, and which were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 404.070—404.090.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Sections 474.530 and 474.540 were repealed by 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990. Said repealed sections pertained to right-of-way at uncontrolled intersections and vehicles turning left, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 409.010, 409.020.

children.title: Thru streets established
children.text: The thru streets established by the city council as of July 1, 1960 (Chapter 9:19, 1948 Compilation of Ordinances) are continued in effect, and the council may add to or modify the said thru streets by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The city traffic engineer shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all thru streets, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 444.010)

children.title: Obedience to through streets and stop intersections
children.text:
The city council may designate through streets or highways and erect stop or yield signs at entrances thereto or may designate any intersection as a stop or yield intersection by erecting like signs at one or more entrances to such intersection. With reference to state trunk highways, the city council may designate through highway or stop or yield intersections only with the consent of the commissioner.

(a) Every driver of a vehicle shall stop at any such stop sign or at a clearly marked stop line before entering an intersection except when directed to proceed by a police officer or traffic-control signal.

(b) The driver of a vehicle shall stop as required by this section at the entrance to a through highway and shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from the through highway or which are approaching so closely on the through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard, but the driver having so yielded may proceed, and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection on the through highway shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicles so proceeding into or across the through highway.

(c) The driver of a vehicle shall likewise stop in obedience to a stop sign, as required herein, at an intersection where a stop sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto although not a part of a through highway, and shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles not so obliged to stop which are within the intersection or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard, but may then proceed.

(d) The driver of every vehicle on any highway in this city shall bring such vehicle to a complete stop before crossing or entering upon an intersecting highway, where and when there is in place on the approaches to or within such intersecting highway any light, sign, standard or marking upon which appears the word "STOP" or the words "STOP, SCHOOL."

(e) Folding type stop signs erected at any designated school crossing location, may be operated and used to regulate traffic so as to require a stop during the hours between 7:45 a.m. and 4:15 p.m. on those days the school is in session. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 409.030)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.20, Subd. 3.

children.title: Reserved

Prior to such repeal, said sections pertained to obedience to yield signs, duty to yield to emergency vehicles, right-of-way and duties of drivers re funeral processions, stopping and yielding upon emerging from alley or driveway, and controlled access roadways, and were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 409.040—409.080; and 76-Or-103, § 1, adopted July 9, 1976.

children.title: Definitions
Traffic control signal
children.text:
(a) Whenever traffic is controlled by traffic control signals exhibiting different colored lights, or colored lighted arrows, successively one (1) at a time or in combination, only the colors green, red and yellow shall be used except for special pedestrian signals carrying a word legend or symbol. The lights shall indicate and apply to drivers of vehicles as follows:

(1) Green indication:

a. Vehicular traffic facing a circular green signal may proceed straight through or turn right or left unless a sign at such place prohibits either such turn. But vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left, shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time such signal is exhibited.

b. Vehicular traffic facing a green arrow signal, shown alone or in combination with another indication, may cautiously enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by such arrow, or such other movement as is permitted by other indications shown at the same time. Such vehicular traffic shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

(2) Steady yellow indication:

a. Vehicular traffic facing a circular yellow signal is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter when vehicular traffic shall not enter the intersection, except for the continued movement allowed by any green arrow simultaneously indicated.

b. Vehicular traffic facing a steady yellow arrow signal is thereby warned that the protected vehicular movement permitted by the corresponding green arrow indication is being terminated.

(3) Steady red indication:

a. Vehicular traffic facing a circular red signal alone shall stop at a clearly marked line, but if none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection, or if none, then before entering the intersection and shall remain standing until a green indication is shown, except as follows:

1. The driver of a vehicle which is stopped as close as practicable at the entrance to the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if none, then at the entrance to the intersection in obedience to a red or stop signal, and with the intention of making a right turn may make such right turn, after stopping, unless an official sign has been erected prohibiting such movement, but shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and other traffic lawfully proceeding as directed by the signal at said intersection; or

2. The driver of a vehicle on a one-way street which intersects another one-way street on which traffic moves to the left shall stop in obedience to a red or stop signal and may then make a left turn into said one-way street, unless an official sign has been erected prohibiting the movement, but shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at said intersection.

b. Vehicular traffic facing a steady red arrow signal, with the intention of making a movement indicated by the arrow, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, but if none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection, or if none, then before entering the intersection and shall remain standing until a permissive signal indication is displayed. (2004-Or-104, § 2, 9-3-04)

children.title: Violation
children.text: If a motor vehicle is operated in violation of section 474.630 and the violation is detected by a recorded image taken by an automated traffic law enforcement system, the owner of the vehicle or the lessee of the vehicle is guilty of a petty misdemeanor. Notwithstanding any other law, a peace officer may issue a citation to the owner or lessee of the vehicle through the United States mail. (2004-Or-104, § 3, 9-3-04)

children.title: Citation
children.text:
When a violation, as set forth by section 474.640, is detected by an automated traffic law enforcement system, the agency shall, within twenty-one (21) days of the violation, mail to the owner a citation, which shall include:

(1) The name and address of the registered owner of the vehicle.

(2) The registration number of the motor vehicle involved in the violation.

(3) The violation charged.

(4) The location where the violation occurred.

(5) The date and time of the violation.

(6) A copy of the recorded images.

(7) The fine amount and the date by which the fine should be paid.

(8) A signed statement by a technician employed by the agency that, based on inspection of recorded images, the motor vehicle was being operated in violation of a traffic control device.

(9) Information advising the person alleged to be liable under the ordinance:

a. Of the manner, time, and place in which liability as alleged in the citation may be contested in the district court; and

b. Warning that failure to pay the penalty or to contest liability in a timely manner may result in a suspension of the owner's driving privileges. (2004-Or-104, § 4, 9-3-04; 2005-Or-049, 6-17-05)

children.title: Evidence
children.text:
(a) In the prosecution of a violation, as set forth by section 474.640, captured by an automated traffic law enforcement system, prima facie evidence that the vehicle described in the citation was operated in violation of this section, together with proof that the defendant was at the time of such violation the owner or lessee of the vehicle, shall constitute in evidence a rebuttable presumption that such owner or lessee was the person who committed the violation. The presumption shall be rebutted if the owner or lessee:

(1) Provides a sworn affidavit delivered by United States mail to the city or agency that he or she was not the owner or lessee of the vehicle at the time of the alleged violation and provides the name and current address of the person operating the motor vehicle at the time of the violation; or

(2) Submits a copy of a police report showing the vehicle had been reported as stolen in a timely manner before the date of the violation.

(b) If the city or agency finds that the person named in the citation was not operating the vehicle at the time of the violation or receives evidence under paragraph (a)(1) of this section identifying the person driving the vehicle at the time of the violation, the city or agency shall issue a citation to the identified driver through the United State mail, no later than fourteen (14) days after receipt of this information. (2004-Or-104, § 5, 9-3-04)

children.title: Severance
children.text: If any section, sentence, clause or phrase of sections 474.620 to 474.660 is held invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction it shall in no way affect the validity of any remaining portion of these sections. (2004-Or-104, § 6, 9-3-04)

children.text: Editor's note— 90-Or-130, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed §§ 474.710—474.760, which sections pertained to driver's signals, and which were derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 410.010—410.040, 410.070, 410.080.

children.heading: ARTICLE II.
children.title: TRUCKS AND TRUCK ROUTES
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (6) ---

Editor's note— Section 6 of 90-Or-131, adopted May 11, 1990, renumbered Art. VII of Ch. 474 as Art. II herein.

children.title: Definition
children.text: As used in this article, the word "truck" shall include trucks, trailers and semitrailers. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 441.010)

children.title: Routes established
children.text:
The truck routes established by the city council as of July 1, 1960 (Chapter 9:6, 1948 Compilation of Ordinances) are continued in effect and the council may add to or modify the said routes by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The city traffic engineer shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all truck routes, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 441.020)

Charter reference— Authority of council to designate truck routes, Ch. 4, § 5(37).

children.title: Marking of routes
children.text: Truck routes shall be identified by appropriate signs erected and maintained by the city engineer. Further, the city engineer shall post at the city limits, upon all main traffic routes entering the city, signs notifying users of highways that trucks are only permitted to be driven on marked truck routes. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 441.030)

children.title: Duty to use routes
children.text: When any such truck route has been established and identified, any person driving a truck having a gross weight of three (3) tons or more shall drive such truck on such route or routes and none other, except when it is impracticable to do so or where necessary to traverse another street or streets to a destination for the purpose of loading or unloading commodities or for the purpose of towing a disabled or damaged motor vehicle to or from public or private property, and then only by such deviation from the nearest truck route as is reasonably necessary. A truck arriving at the end of any designated truck route may be driven over the most direct course to the nearest truck route which extends in the same general direction. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 414.020)

children.title: Permits for use of other routes
children.text: The city engineer shall have the authority, for cause or upon request, to issue temporary permits for trucks to operate over routes not established as truck routes by the city council, or to otherwise deviate from the provisions of the traffic code. Such action by the city engineer shall be subject to review and modification, or cancellation, by the city council. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 414.030)

children.title: Vehicles excepted
children.text: The provisions of this article shall not apply to emergency vehicles of the police department, fire department or health department, nor to any public utility vehicles where actually engaged in the performance of emergency duties necessary to be performed by said public departments or public utilities, nor to any vehicle owned by or performing work for the United States of America, the State of Minnesota, the University of Minnesota, or the City of Minneapolis. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 441.080)

children.title: Conflict with other provisions
children.text: No designation of a "truck route" which consists in whole or in part of any state trunk highway, federal highway or parkway shall be construed as permitting use of said route in violation of any order or rule of the commissioner of highways or any ordinance or rule of the park board. Further, no designation of any "truck route" shall be construed to permit violation of any state law or provision of this Code regulating the size, weight, capacity, height, length or speed of trucks or other vehicles. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 441.040)

children.title: Trucks following each other
children.text: The driver of any truck or truck-tractor when traveling upon a highway outside of the congested zone shall not follow another truck or truck-tractor within one hundred (100) feet, but this shall not be construed to prevent one truck or tractor overtaking and passing another. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 414.060)

Cross reference— Penalty for parking violations, § 1.30; provisions of park and recreation board traffic code relative to parking, stopping and standing, § PB9-132 et seq.; parking at public market, § 202.210; open air motor vehicle parking lots, Ch. 319; parking vehicles on school property, § 385.320(d); parking on parade route, § 447.120(c).

Special law reference—Special act relating to parking facilities for vehicles using Interstate 394, Laws 1985, Ch. 299.

children.title: To be parallel to curb
children.text:
No person shall stand or park a vehicle in a roadway other than parallel with the edge of the roadway, headed in the direction of traffic, with the curbside wheels of the vehicle within twelve (12) inches of the edge of the roadway, and not closer than four (4) feet to another vehicle parked at the curb, except as provided in section 478.30. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.010)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.35.

children.title: To be parallel to edge of roadway in absence of curb
children.text:
Upon streets and highways not having a curb each vehicle stopped or parked shall be stopped or parked parallel with and to the right of the paved or improved or main-traveled part of the street or highway. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.020)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.35.

children.title: Angle parking
children.text: Upon those streets which have been marked or signed for angle parking, vehicles shall be parked at the angle to the curb indicated by such marks or signs. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.030)

children.title: Manner of parking
children.text: The driver of a vehicle intending to park at the curb of any street or highway at a place about to be vacated by another vehicle shall stop back of said parking space and wait until said vehicle has vacated said parking space. The person so desiring to park shall then move his vehicle to a place immediately in front of said parking space and back into it, and the driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear shall yield the right-of-way to such person for the purpose of parking at said parking space. In case there is no one in position immediately in front of said parking space prepared to back into it, and said parking space is large enough to permit it, the driver of an approaching vehicle may head into said parking space without backing. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.040)

children.title: Vehicles backed to curb
children.text:
(a) No vehicle shall be backed up to the curb in the congested zone to load or unload except between 6:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m., by permit from the police department. Outside the congested zone, a vehicle may be backed up to the curb, but only when the weight or bulk of the load necessitates loading or unloading in this position, and only for the period of time necessary to so load or unload said vehicle.

(b) In places where and at hours when stopping for the loading or unloading of merchandise or materials is permitted, vehicles used for the transportation of merchandise or materials may back into the curb to take on or discharge loads when the owner of such vehicle holds a permit granting him such privilege, and such permit shall be either in the possession of the driver or on the vehicle at the time such vehicle is backed against the curb to take on or discharge a load, and no owner or driver shall violate any of the special terms or conditions of any such special permit. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.050)

children.title: Exception for disabled vehicles
children.text: The provisions of the traffic code relating to stopping, standing and parking shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or improved or main-traveled portion of a street or highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.060)

children.title: Display of vehicle for sale
children.text: No person shall place a vehicle on a highway to display the same for sale or exchange. A vehicle shall be deemed to be displayed in violation of this section when found standing upon a street or highway bearing a sign indicating that it is for sale or exchange. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.070)

children.title: Washing, greasing, repairing
children.text: No person shall wash, grease or repair a vehicle upon a street or highway, except such repairs as are necessitated by an emergency. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.080)

children.title: Parking of unattached trailers prohibited
children.text: No person shall stop, stand or park a trailer which is not attached to a properly licensed and insured motor vehicle on any street or highway except as otherwise specifically exempted by Minneapolis City Ordinances or state law. A "trailer" for the purpose of this section is any vehicle without motor power designed for carrying persons or property and for being drawn by a motor vehicle. For the purposes of this section, "not attached" means a trailer that is not attached to a motor vehicle in such a manner that the motor vehicle and trailer can immediately be operated in a safe and legal manner without further attachment. (92-Or-114, § 1, 9-25-92)

children.title: Prohibited in specified places
Citizen enforcement of parking regulations for the physically disabled
children.text:
The City of Minneapolis authorizes qualified citizen volunteers to issue citations exclusively to vehicles illegally parking in spaces designated for the physically disabled, as set forth in Article IV of this chapter.

Citizen volunteers must submit an application to the chief of police, and must meet the following requirements in order to participate in the enforcement of parking violations:

(1) Volunteers must be eighteen (18) years of age;

(2) Volunteers must have a valid drivers license;

(3) Volunteers must have an acceptable driving and criminal history.

The supervisor of the traffic control unit shall establish a training program which citizen volunteers must successfully complete before they will be authorized to enforce parking violations. The training program shall be designed to instruct the citizen volunteers in the requirements of the law, the method of issuing citations, the geography and city limits of Minneapolis, and other related matters.

Upon completion of the training program, citizen volunteers shall be issued a photo identification card authorizing them to issue citations on behalf of the city. Such citizen volunteers are authorized to issue citations for the parking violations set forth in Article IV of this chapter only while they are on duty, in uniform, utilizing city equipment, and are under the direct supervision of the traffic control supervisor. Citizen volunteers must carry their identification cards during the hours they issue such citations.

All duties and responsibilities granted to citizen volunteers under this section may be revoked at any time by the chief of police. (92-Or-123, § 1, 10-9-92; 2008-Or-065, § 1, 8-22-08)

children.title: General time limits for parking
children.text:
(a) No person shall park a vehicle or permit a vehicle to stand upon any street for a longer period of time than that is shown or displayed on official signs erected and installed.

(b) For the purpose of the regulations relating to limited parking, any vehicle moved a distance of not more than two (2) blocks during the limited parking period shall be deemed to have remained stationary. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.130; Ord. No. 2017-023, § 2, 5-12-17)

children.title: No-stopping zone
children.text: No person shall stop or halt a vehicle, even momentarily, in any place on any street or highway where official signs prohibit stopping, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the direction of a police officer or traffic-control sign or signal. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.150)

children.title: Removal of vehicles for street maintenance, snow removal
children.text: Whenever the director of public works or any of his assistants shall find it necessary, for purposes of facilitating street maintenance operations, such as the removal of snow, ice or street wastes, to move any vehicle standing on any highway, the director of public works, or assistants, or other emergency officials in the discharge of their duties, may move such vehicle to the extent necessary for such purposes. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.160; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 1, 11-3-17)

children.title: Authority to require moving of illegally stopped vehicles
children.text: Whenever a police officer finds a vehicle standing upon a street or highway in violation of any of the provisions of the traffic code, such officer may move such vehicle, or require the driver or other person in charge of the vehicle to remove the same, to a position off the paved or improved or main-traveled part of such street or highway. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.170)

children.title: Duties when leaving vehicle on grade
children.text:
No person driving or in charge of a motor vehicle shall permit it to stand unattended on a grade without effectively setting the brakes thereon and turning the front wheels to the curb or side of the highway. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.180)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.36.

children.title: Duty to lock ignition, remove key
children.text:
Every person parking a passenger automobile on a public street or alley in the city shall lock the ignition, remove the key, and take the same with him.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.190)

children.title: Leaving vehicle with wheels fastened
children.text:
No person shall leave a motor vehicle standing upon a street or highway with the wheels chained, locked or fastened in such a manner that the motor vehicle cannot be easily moved in case of emergency.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.200)

children.title: Use of vehicle theft alarm system
children.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to install, operate or use any vehicle theft alarm system that emits or causes the emission of an audible sound, which is not, or does not become, automatically and completely silenced within five (5) minutes. The time period shall be calculated based upon the emission of the first audible sound and shall end five (5) minutes thereafter notwithstanding any variation or temporary stoppage in the emissions of audible sound.

(95-Or-127, § 1, 8-25-95)

children.title: Parking in alleys
children.text:
Vehicles other than commercial trucks shall not be parked in public alleys, and commercial trucks shall not be so parked for a longer period of time than is necessary to load or unload commodities, and then not to exceed thirty (30) minutes.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.210; Ord. of 9-28-73, § 5)

children.title: Stopping or parking on municipal property
children.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle on any municipal parking lot, parking ramp, garage or other municipal property contrary to the restrictions or regulations imposed for parking on such property.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.215; Ord. of 9-28-73, § 6)

children.title: Double parking
children.text:
Vehicles shall not be double parked on a street or highway, except commercial trucks when calling for or delivering merchandise when access to the curb at or immediately adjacent to the place of delivery is blocked by other vehicles, and then only for such length of time as may be necessary to load or unload, such length of time in any event not to exceed fifteen (15) minutes. No commercial truck shall be double parked in any area designated by the city council as a parking meter area. No truck shall be double parked in any area between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. and between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.220; Ord. of 9-28-73, § 5)

children.title: Impounding of violations
children.text:
Any unoccupied vehicle found in violation of the provisions of the traffic code may be immediately removed and impounded by any police officer or duly authorized person in accordance with this code.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.240)

children.title: Impounding rental vehicles
children.text:
Every person engaging in the business of renting vehicles to persons desiring to drive themselves, commonly known as "drive-yourself" businesses, shall register with the city clerk and the police department the license number of all vehicles which are rented to persons who desire to drive and operate them. In the event any such vehicle shall be found in a place or under circumstances which constitute a violation of any of the provisions of the traffic code, such vehicle shall be impounded, whether said vehicle is occupied or unoccupied, damaged or undamaged, and thereafter its release shall be governed by the provisions of the traffic code permitting the release of impounded vehicles.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.250)

children.title: Exceptions
children.text:
The provisions of this article, or any other ordinance pertaining to parking or stopping, shall not apply to authorized emergency vehicles while used in the regular performance of duties, nor to authorized traffic code enforcement personnel engaged in performance of their duties.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.290)

children.title: Parking of overweight vehicles and commercial vehicles and commercial passenger vehicles
children.text:
(a) No vehicle or hitched or unhitched combination, with or without load, which weighs more than ten thousand (10,000) pounds or is registered for a gross weight of more than twelve thousand (12,000) pounds, nor any commercial vehicle or commercial passenger vehicle which is within or abutting, including across a street or alley from any residential zoning district or residential combination district, including office residential districts, as described in Title 20 of this code shall be permitted to stop, stand or park on any street unless one of the following conditions is met:

(1) Such vehicle is actually and expeditiously engaged in the loading or unloading of passengers or materials from the vehicle; or

(2) Such vehicle is stopped, parked, or standing in compliance with specially posted signals or signs regulating the weight of a vehicle or combination, or at the directions of an authorized traffic control agent or police officer.

(b) No vehicle or hitched or unhitched combination, with or without load, which weighs more than twenty-six thousand (26,000) pounds or is registered for a gross weight of more than twenty-six thousand (26,000) pounds shall be permitted to stop, stand, or park on any street unless one of the following exceptions is met:

(1) Such vehicle is actually and expeditiously engaged in the loading or unloading of passengers or materials from the vehicle; or

(2) Such vehicle is stopped, parked, or standing in compliance with specially posted signals or signs regulating the weight of a vehicle or combination, or at the directions of an authorized traffic control agent or police officer.

(c) If any vehicle or hitched or unhitched combination is stopped, standing, or parked in violation of the terms of this section, either the driver or the owner of the vehicle or combination, or for a leased vehicle or combination, the driver, lessor or lessee of the vehicle or combination, is guilty of the violation and subject to the penalty as provided by subsection (d).

(1) No person may be penalized if another person is penalized, convicted for, or pleads guilty to the violation, or if the vehicle or combination was stolen at the time of the violation.

(2) This section does not apply to a lessor of a motor vehicle if the lessor keeps a record of the name and address of the lessee.

(3) If proven by a preponderance of the evidence, it is an affirmative defense to a violation of this section if the vehicle or hitched or unhitched combination was actually and expeditiously engaged in the providing of bona fide services at the location where parked during the date and time specified in the charging document.

(d) Any violation of the terms of this section shall be subject to a fine of one hundred dollars ($100.00) from January 1, 2022, until December 31, 2022, and one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) from January 1, 2023 until December 31, 2023, and two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) thereafter.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.310; Ord. of 10-26-73, § 1; 78-Or-155, § 1, 8-11-78; 90-Or-319, § 1, 12-28-90; 91-Or-099, § 1, 5-10-91; Ord. No. 2021-038, § 1, 7-23-21)

children.title: Abandoned motor vehicles; penalty
children.text:
(a) No abandoned motor vehicle shall remain upon any street or highway in the city. Any vehicle which is permitted to remain upon any street or highway in the city in excess of seventy-two (72) consecutive hours or any vehicle lacking vital component parts shall be presumed to be abandoned and may be immediately removed and impounded by any police officer or duly authorized person in accordance with this code.

(b) Any person violating the terms of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than twenty-five dollars ($25.00) nor more than one hundred dollars ($100.00).

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 421.190; 79-Or-123, § 1, 6-8-79)

State Law reference— Abandoned vehicles, M.S. Ch. 168B.

children.title: Use of alleys for through traffic prohibited
children.text:
(a) Purpose. The city council declares that the public alleys of the city are constructed and maintained primarily to provide limited access to abutting residential and commercial property, and are not intended or designed for use as through streets. The city council finds that it is necessary to limit access to public alleys in order to address the use of public alleys by operators of motor vehicles who use alleys to avoid traffic congestion on city streets, thereby increasing the risk of bodily injury and property damage by increasing vehicular traffic in alleys which are not designed to safely carry such traffic; to address problems of "cruising" alleys in motor vehicles by persons who do not reside or conduct business in abutting property or who are not invitees to abutting property, which can lead to vandalism, burglary or other criminal activity. The city council finds that the protection of the public health, safety and welfare requires that traffic in public alleys be restricted to protect residential neighborhoods and to insure that use of public alleys by operators of motor vehicles is consistent with the purpose of such alleys as stated in this section.

(b) Use prohibited. No person may operate a motor vehicle on a public alley unless directed to do so by a peace officer, authorized traffic code enforcement personnel or authorized traffic control device, except abutting property owners, tenants their guests or invitees, operating a motor vehicle in an otherwise lawful manner. This section shall not be interpreted to preclude use of alleys by the following:

(1) Persons performing authorized law enforcement activities on behalf of any law enforcement agency;

(2) Persons providing emergency medical or fire services;

(3) Persons performing public service activities or inspections on behalf of state, federal or city regulatory agencies or departments; and

(4) Persons performing installation, maintenance or inspection activities for public or private utility or communications companies.

(93-Or-152, § 1, 10-29-93)

children.title: Violation; penalty for owner or lessee
children.text:
If a motor vehicle is stopped, standing, or parked in violation of any section of this chapter, except any section of Article IV, the owner of the vehicle, or for a leased motor vehicle the lessee of the vehicle, is guilty of the violation and subject to any penalty as provided by this Code.

(1) The owner or lessee may not be penalized if

a. another person is penalized, convicted for, or pleads guilty to, that violation, or

b. the motor vehicle was stolen at the time of the violation.

(2) This section does not apply to a lessor of a motor vehicle if the lessor keeps a record of the name and address of the lessee.

(3) This section does not prohibit or limit the criminal, administrative or civil prosecution of a motor vehicle operator for violating any provision of this chapter.

(2010-Or-076, § 1, 8-20-10)

children.heading: ARTICLE II.
children.title: METERED PARKING
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (9) ---

Editor's note— Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, adopted Nov. 5, 2021, amended the title of Art. II to read as herein set out. The former Art. II title pertained to parking meters.

children.title: Payment
children.text:
As used throughout this chapter, "payment" shall mean coin or currency of the United States, accepted debit card, credit card, or other officially authorized payment service.

(Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Compliance required
children.text:
(a) No vehicle shall be parked on streets designated as metered parking, except pursuant to the terms and conditions regulating parking on said streets as indicated upon signs or payment equipment erected in the area.

(b) The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all vehicles unless exception is made by formal written agreement with city council approval.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.140; 2013-Or-073, § 2, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Installation and function
children.text:
Metered parking payment equipment shall be devices approved by the city council and installed in locations authorized by the council. The devices shall measure the permissible predetermined period of time for which parking shall be permitted.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 440.010; 98-Or-096, § 1, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 3, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Construction of metered parking areas
children.text:
Metered parking areas shall be constructed with instructions that indicate when payment is required, maximum parking duration, and relevant restrictions. Payment equipment or authorized payment services shall clearly set out and continue operation during the hours requiring payment for compliance. Payment equipment and services shall also indicate when the lawful parking period has expired.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 440.020; 98-Or-096, § 2, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 4, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Hours
children.text:
Metered parking shall be in operation during the hours and days indicated except New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day, day after Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day, unless otherwise provided in all areas designated by the city council.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 440.030; 98-Or-096, § 3, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 5, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Use of parking meter spaces
children.text:
Any vehicle parked in a metered parking area shall be parked parallel to the curb, and in a manner that does not infringe upon another metered space. Any vehicle parked in angled metered parking shall be parked entirely within the area designated by lines or markings. Trucks and other commercial vehicles using parking meters shall park in such a manner that the least number of metered spaces are occupied.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 440.050; 79-Or-193, § 1, 9-28-79; 98-Or-096, § 4, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 6, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Duty to deposit payment; overtime parking; physically disabled persons
"Feeding" meters
children.text:
No vehicle may be parked in a metered space where a person has deposited payment for the purpose of increasing or extending the parking time of that vehicle beyond the designated legal parking duration which has been established for the parking space.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.140; 98-Or-096, § 6, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 8, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: False or unapproved payment prohibited
children.text:
No vehicle may be parked in a metered space where a person has deposited or caused to be deposited any false or unapproved form of payment.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.140; 98-Or-096, § 7, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 9, 8-16-13)

children.title: Tampering prohibited
children.text:
No person shall injure, deface, tamper with, or willfully break, destroy, or impair the usefulness of any metered parking payment equipment or signage in the city.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.140; 2013-Or-073, § 10, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Charge declared fee
children.text:
The payments required to be deposited as provided herein are hereby levied and assessed as a fee to cover the costs of inspection, installation, operation, maintenance, replacement, regulation, enforcement, control and use of the following:

(1) Parking spaces, payment equipment, and payment services described herein;

(2) The parking of vehicles in the areas where metered parking does not exist; and

(3) Other street transportation related purposes.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.140; 98-Or-096, § 8, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 11, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Credit to parking fund
children.text:
The metered parking payments shall be deposited to the parking fund.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 440.080; 98-Or-096, § 10, 9-18-98; 2013-Or-073, § 13, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Obstruction permits to hood meters
children.text:
(a) Any person, company, or corporation needing special use of metered space(s) to: promote a civic cause, provide space for construction, or any maintenance or delivery activities deemed proper by the director of public works, shall make application to the director of public works, as provided herein, for a permit to hood, reserve, and/or remove said metered space(s), and any such applicant shall defray the cost to the city for the loss of public use of the metered spaces due to the hooding or disabling. The cost to the city shall be proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by city council resolution.

(b) "Hooding," reserving, and/or removing metered space(s) is to be carried out exclusively by the public works department of the city and other authorized city representatives.

(c) Application for an obstruction permit shall be made to the director of public works' office not less than seventy-two (72) hours prior to the effective date of such permit, and shall:

(1) State the purpose of the obstruction permit.

(2) State the name of the person, persons or the authorized officer of the company or corporation applying for the permit with a twenty-four (24) hour phone number.

(3) The location and number(s) of the metered space(s).

(4) State the specified period of time.

(d) The designated administrative fee for the hooding, reserving, and/or removal of metered parking spaces shall be the amount of money necessary to defray the loss to the city of the use of the parking spaces and whatever necessary costs for administration or enforcement. The administrative fee shall be set by the director of public works.
