The obstruction permit, certificate or insignia issued shall be prominently displayed upon the vehicle parked in the hooded meter area, and shall state thereon, the place, date, and identification of permit holder.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 440.090; 98-Or-096, § 11, 9-18-98; 2006-Or-117, § 1, 10-20-06; 2013-Or-073, § 14, 8-16-13; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 1, 11-5-21)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 98-Or-096, § 12, adopted Sept. 18, 1998, repealed § 478.440, which pertained to twelve-hour zone. See the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Traffic-control unit established
children.text: There is hereby established under the control of the department of regulatory services, a unit to be known as traffic control. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 516.010; Ord. of 12-21-73, § 1; 81-Or-310, § 1, 12-28-81; 2008-Or-065, § 2, 8-22-08; Ord. No. 2016-050, § 1, 7-22-16)

children.title: Inspectors and traffic-control agents and other persons authorized to collect monies and issue violation tags
children.text: In cooperation with the police department of the city, traffic-control agents, all inspectors of the regulatory services department, and other persons determined by the supervisor of the traffic control unit are empowered, authorized and directed to collect monies from parking meters and to issue traffic tags for parking meter and other nonmoving traffic violations, such tags to have the same force and effect as though issued by a duly appointed, qualified and acting police officer or other peace officer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 516.020; Ord. of 12-21-73, § 1; 81-Or-310, § 2, 12-28-81; 2008-Or-065, § 3, 8-22-08)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2008-Or-065, § 4, adopted August 22, 2008, repealed § 478.490, which pertained to meter collectors may issue tags. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.heading: ARTICLE IV.
children.title: PHYSICALLY HANDICAPPED PERSONS
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (10) ---

State Law reference— Provisions similar to this article, M.S. § 169.345.

children.title: Definition of "physically handicapped
children.text: " Physically handicapped as employed herein shall include any person who has sustained an amputation or permanent material disability of either or both arms or legs, or who has been otherwise permanently disabled in any manner rendering it difficult and burdensome for him to walk. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.270)

children.title: Scope of privilege
children.text: Any physically handicapped person who displays prominently upon the automobile parked by him or under his direction and for his use, the distinguishing certificate or insignia specified in section 478.540 shall be entitled to courtesy in the parking of such automobile and be relieved of any liability with respect to parking except as provided in sections 478.90, 478.150 and 478.360 hereof and except where parking is prohibited in order to provide fire lanes, or to accommodate heavy traffic during morning and afternoon rush hours. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.270; 91-Or-186, § 2, 9-13-91)

children.title: Identifying certificate
children.text:
The motor vehicles division in the department of public safety shall issue without charge a special identifying certificate or insignia for a marked motor vehicle to any physically handicapped applicant upon submission by the applicant of a certificate by a qualified physician to the division that he is a physically handicapped person within the meaning of section 478.520.

The commissioner of public safety shall determine the form and size, and promulgate rules and regulations governing their issuance and use, as necessary to carry out the provisions of this article. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.270; 76-Or-206, § 1, 11-12-76)

children.title: Spaces reserved for handicapped parking; penalties
children.text:
(a) No person shall park a motor vehicle in a parking space designated and reserved for the physically handicapped unless:

(1) That person is physically handicapped or is operating the vehicle under the direction and for the use of a physically handicapped person; and

(2) Such vehicle visibly bears or contains a proper identifying certificate.

(b) Failure to obey the above provisions shall constitute a petty misdemeanor. Vehicles in violation may be removed and impounded as provided in Article X of this chapter.

(c) The above provisions shall apply to parking spaces, on both public and private property, which are designated and reserved for physically handicapped persons by state or local law or through the action of persons who own or are in lawful possession of the subject property. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.270; 76-Or-206, § 2, 11-12-76; 2010-Or-076, § 2, 8-20-10)

children.title: Designation of location, description of signs
children.text:
Upon recommendation of the city engineer, zones may be established by the city council providing parking for physically handicapped persons. Notice of such designation of handicapped parking spaces shall be given by the posting of permanent, nonportable signs. Such signs shall be designed in accordance with the requirements of the manual of the commissioner of public safety on uniform traffic-control devices.

No person shall cause to be erected signs reserving or designating parking spaces for physically handicapped persons unless the location, number and method of signing of such spaces is first approved by the city engineer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.270; 76-Or-206, § 3, 11-12-76)

children.title: Established
children.text:
The no parking zones established by the city council as of July 1, 1960 (Chapter 9:23, 1948 Compilation of Ordinances) are continued in effect, and the council may add to or modify the said no parking zones by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The director of public works shall maintain a complete listing of all no-parking zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.010; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 2, 11-3-17; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Parking prohibited; exceptions
children.text:
(a) No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle on any street or highway where there has been established a no-parking zone or a corner clearance zone and such zones are marked by a sign, provided, a driver may stop the vehicle momentarily while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers from the vehicle.

(b) Commercial trucks, commercial vehicles (excluding taxis) and commercial permit vehicles may stop in a no-parking zone while actually engaged in loading or unloading merchandise or freight for a period of time not to exceed thirty (30) minutes.

(c) No commercial truck or commercial permit vehicle shall stop, stand or park at any time in a no-parking zone which has been established for a United States post office drive-up mail collection box, or a traffic turning lane, fire lane or traffic clearance lane, to provide additional traffic lanes during peak traffic hours or street maintenance, or in violation of any provisions of section 478.90.

(Code 1960, As Amend., §§ 411.100, 446.020; Ord. of 9-28-73, § 3; 78-Or-161, § 1, 8-11-78; 96-Or-102, § 2, 9-27-96; 97-Or-035, § 1, 3-28-97; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Hours
children.text:
Said zones shall be in effect twenty-four (24) hours of every day, except as may be otherwise provided with respect to particular zones.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.030)

children.title: Where may be established
children.text:
No parking zones may be established by the city council upon compliance with the conditions stated in this article. The city, county, state or federal government may obtain no parking zones without the payment of any fee therefor upon the filing of the application as herein provided.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.040; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Procedure for establishment
children.text:
Any person desiring that a no parking zone not uniform with the adjacent area be established abutting the premises occupied by such person, shall make written application therefor. Such application shall be referred to the director of public works, who shall make a survey of the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone and recommend either the granting or the denial of such permit. If, in the judgment of the city council, the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone do not justify the issuance of such permit, the same shall not be granted.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.050; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Fees
children.text:
No-parking zone fees shall be proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by city council resolution.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.060; Ord. of 8-11-72, § 1; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Marking
children.text:
When the required fee is paid, the director of public works shall install the necessary signs.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.070; 96-Or-102, § 3, 9-27-96; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Expiration and renewal
children.text:
Permits granted under this article shall expire on December thirty-first of the year in which issued and shall not be transferable. Permits may be renewed from year to year in other than parking meter zones and in parking zones and in parking meter zones when the no-parking zone is used after the hours of parking meter operation upon the payment of a maintenance fee. Permits may be renewed from year to year in parking meter areas upon the payment of maintenance and metered zone fees as set forth in section 478.640. In the event of the failure to pay the annual renewal fee herein specified before February twenty-eighth after the expiration of the year for which the same is issued, the no-parking zone theretofore established shall be removed by the director of public works.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.080; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Changing of zone
children.text:
Any person, firm or corporation desiring that a no-parking zone be changed shall make an application therefor. The same procedure relative to the referring of such application and its granting or denial shall be followed as provided for the application for a new no-parking zone.

The fees for changing no-parking zones shall be determined as set forth in section 478.640.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.090; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Signs declared city property
children.text:
All signs designating no parking zones shall remain the property of the city.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.100)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, adopted Nov. 5, 2021, repealed § 478.690, which pertained to painting clearances and derived from the 1960 Code, as amended, § 446.110.

children.title: Church zones
children.text:
No parking during church service zones shall be established at a fee no more than sufficient to cover the cost of the signs, publication and investigation. No costs representing the replacement of damaged or stolen signs and painting maintenance of curbs or signs shall be incurred by the city, unless the incurring of such cost shall be requested by the religious organization having the privilege of a "No Parking During Church Service" zone. In the event such costs are incurred as hereinabove set forth, the religious organization shall be charged the rates prescribed in this article.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 446.120)

children.title: Critical traffic and parking areas
children.text:
(a) Establishment authorized. The city council may, after recommendation of the director of public works, and after receiving an official written application as specified in this section, designate a critical traffic and parking area consisting of certain streets or parts thereof in a compact and contiguous area. The city council shall also specify special traffic and parking restrictions within each critical traffic and parking area thus established.

(b) Procedure for establishment.

(1) An official written application shall be made to the director of public works. Such application shall be signed by one (1) resident in each of at least seventy-five (75) percent of the dwelling units located within the proposed critical traffic and parking area before the city council may consider the designation of a specified critical traffic and parking area. The applicant is responsible for selecting one (1) of the following alternatives:

a. Permit parking, time limited (residents with permit no limit), general public (subject to posted time limit, days and hours of enforcement).

b. Permit parking, residents with permit only, specified hours/days.

c. Permit parking, resident with permit only anytime.

(2) Complete applications shall be referred to the city clerk to certify whether the application contains the required signatures. Once the application has been certified, it will be transmitted to the appropriate committee of the city council, which may direct the director of public works to conduct a traffic and parking survey of the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone and recommend either the granting or the denial of such designation, based on a verification of proper "findings" and compliance with the following qualifying criteria:

a. Permit parking, time limited. Requires a determination that the number of resident vehicles within the requested critical traffic and parking area exceeds the number of off-street parking spaces in the area.

b. Permit parking, resident with permit only, specified hours/days. Requires a determination that the number of resident vehicles within the requested critical traffic and parking area exceeds the number of off-street parking spaces in the area, or a determination that the number of non-resident parkers during the requested hours/days of enforcement exceeds thirty-three (33) percent of the number of on-street spaces in the area.

c. Permit parking, resident with permit only, anytime. Requires a determination that the number of resident vehicles within the requested critical traffic and parking area exceeds the number of on-street and off-street parking spaces in the area. Minimum size area shall be one (1) block face.

(c) Findings. No critical traffic and parking area may be established unless the city council shall have made the following findings:

(1) The area is detrimentally impacted by parking of commuter, student, customer, or visitor/guest vehicles generated by area businesses, institutions or recreational/entertainment facilities during the proposed hours of restriction;

(2) The area does not have sufficient off-street vehicular parking for the use and convenience of the residents thereof in the vicinity of their homes;

(3) Vehicle noise, pollution or congestion will work unacceptable hardships on the residents of the area if present parking is allowed to continue unregulated; and

(4) The health, safety and welfare of residents of the area and the city as a whole and the attractiveness and livability of specific neighborhoods will be promoted by a system of preferential parking enacted under this section.

(d) Residential parking permit authority. The establishment of a critical traffic and parking area shall provide for the issuance of parking permits subject to the following requirements:

(1) The director of public works shall identify the location, boundaries, size, hours, and days to be regulated by the parking permit procedure.

(2) An application for a permit shall be on a form prepared by the director of public works and shall contain the name and address of the resident, make, model and license number of the vehicle, a government issued ID and such other information as is reasonably necessary to enforce the provisions of this section. This application shall be presented with a government issued ID and such other information as may be necessary to prove residency within the designated critical traffic and parking area. No person shall furnish false information in an application for a vehicle permit. A false application shall be grounds for revocation of the permit and is punishable pursuant to section 1.30 of the Minneapolis City Code.

(3) A non-refundable fee shall accompany each permit application and the fee shall be proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by council resolution.

(4) Each permit shall be assigned to a vehicle using the vehicle's license plate number.

(5) Permits shall be made available on a yearly, renewable basis for those areas recommended in the director of public works' report and authorized by the city council and issued to the following individuals:

a. Residents with a maximum of two (2) permits per licensed driver. A valid driver's license must then be provided for each resident of the dwelling unit with permitted vehicles.

b. An owner, manager, or their designee, of a business, institution, or recreational/entertainment facility located within the designated critical traffic and parking area. Maximum of two (2) permits unless otherwise approved by city council.

(6) Temporary parking permits for bona fide visitor's vehicles or service vehicles shall be available to residents of a critical traffic and parking area. These include two (2) transferable permits issued at a one-year fee to each requesting dwelling unit. Additional temporary permits are available for specific dates or for extended periods of two (2) to thirty (30) days.

(7) The provisions of this chapter shall not abrogate the scope of parking privileges granted handicapped persons as defined in sections 478.520 through 478.560 of this Code or by statutes of the State of Minnesota, or the provisions of the snow emergency ordinance section 478.1000 relating to parking. In addition, the provisions of this chapter shall not abrogate the authority of the city to post temporary or permanent parking restrictions for safety, traffic flow, construction, or maintenance purposes.

(8) Any permit issued is only valid within the specified area for which it was issued.

(9) The following vehicle types are not eligible for residential parking permits:

a. Recreational vehicles;

b. Trailers;

c. Buses;

d. Trucks with ICC or LCC license plates;

e. Taxicabs;

f. Commercial vehicles; and

g. Commercial passenger vehicles as prohibited under section 478.240.

(10) The city council may establish special terms, time limits, day and hours of enforcement, and number of permits after a study and recommendation by the director of public works.

(e) Modification. The city council may modify the streets included in a critical traffic and parking area if it determines that a change of circumstances warrants such modification. The city council member of the ward and appropriate committee may recommend to the city council that time limits and hours of enforcement of a critical traffic and parking area be amended if circumstances warrant such modification and the residents within the area support the change.

(f) Disestablishment. The city council may disestablish a critical traffic and parking area after finding that the circumstances that originally prompted the establishment of the area no longer pertain.

(76-Or-137, § 1, 8-13-76; 80-Or-039, § 1, 3-14-80; 80-Or-151, § 1, 6-27-80; 86-Or-030, § 1, 2-14-86; 93-Or-084, § 1, 6-11-93; 98-Or-060, § 1, 6-26-98; 2004-Or-031, § 1, 4-2-04; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 3, 11-3-17; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.title: Electric vehicle parking zones
children.text:
No vehicle shall be stopped, parked, or left standing in a space signed or otherwise designated as an electric vehicle charging station in the public right-of-way, unless the vehicle is plugged into the charging station. Only "all electric vehicles" and "plug-in hybrid electric vehicles" as defined by Minnesota Statute Section 169.011, subds. 1a(a) and 54a, respectively, are permitted to use charging stations in the public right-of-way, and for charging purposes only. No vehicle can be parked at an electric charging station in the public right-of-way for longer than the maximum period of time posted. An "all-electric vehicle" or a "plug-in hybrid electric vehicle" that is permitted and operated as part of an approved carshare service program is exempt from electric charging station parking restrictions at stations signed as such.

(Ord. No. 2021-051, § 2, 11-5-21)

children.heading: ARTICLE VI.
children.title: LOADING ZONES, TRUCK ZONES, LIMITED PARKING ZONES AND DISABILITY TRANSFER ZONES
Establishment generally
children.text:
(a) The loading zones established by the city council as of July 1, 1960 (Chapter 9:25, 1948 Compilation of Ordinances) are continued in effect, and the council may add to or modify the said zones by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The director of public works shall maintain a complete listing of all loading zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein.

(b) Commercial loading zones, truck zones, limited parking zones, passenger loading zones or handicapped persons transfer zones may be established by the city council at buildings not owned by the county, city, state or federal government upon compliance with conditions stated in this article. The city, county, state or federal government may obtain loading zones, truck zones or limited parking zones without the payment of any fee therefor, upon the filing of the application as herein set forth. No fee shall be charged where a disability transfer zone is established at a residence.

(Code 1960, As Amend., §§ 447.010, 447.040; Ord. of 7-27-72, § 2; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Procedure for establishment
children.text:
Any person desiring that a loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone not uniform with the adjacent area, be established abutting the premises occupied by such person, shall make written application therefor. Such application shall be referred to the director of public works, who shall make a survey of the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone and recommend either the granting or the denial of such permit. If, in the judgment of the city council, the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone do not justify the issuance of such permit, the same shall not be granted. No loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone less than twenty (20) lineal feet shall be established.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.050; Ord. of 5-29-70, § 1; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Fees
children.text:
Zone fees shall be proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by city council resolution.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.060; Ord. of 8-11-72, § 1; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Marking
children.text:
When payment of the required amount is made, the director of public works shall install the necessary signs.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.070; 96-Or-102, § 4, 9-27-96; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Expiration and renewal
children.text:
Permits granted under this article shall expire on December thirty-first of the year in which issued and shall not be transferable. Permits may be renewed from year to year in other than parking meter zones, and in parking meter zones when the loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone is used after the hours of parking meter operation upon the payment of a maintenance fee. Permits may be renewed from year to year in parking meter areas upon the payment of maintenance and metered zone fees as set forth in section 478.740. In the event of the failure to pay the annual renewal fee herein specified before February twenty eighth after the expiration of the year for which the same is issued, the loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone theretofore established shall be abolished, and the director of public works shall remove the signs and obliterate the markings of the same.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.080; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Changing of zone
children.text:
Any person, firm or corporation desiring that a loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone be changed shall make an application therefor. The same procedure relative to the referring of such application and its granting or denial shall be followed as now provided for the application for a new loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone.

The fees for changing loading zones, truck zones or limited parking zones shall be proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by city council resolution.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.090; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Signs declared city property
children.text:
All signs designating loading zones, truck zones or limited parking zones shall remain the property of the city.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.100)

children.title: Hours
children.text:
The hours of operation of all zones herein are set by the director of public works and posted on signs in each zone.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.030; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: General prohibition against parking
children.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park any vehicle in any loading zone, disability transfer zone, truck zone or limited parking zone except in accordance with this article.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.020; Ord. of 7-27-72, § 1; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Use of commercial and truck loading zones generally
children.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle, other than a commercial truck, or other commercial vehicle which complies with and displays special parking permit decals issued pursuant to the provisions of section 478.820, or a truck or other commercial vehicle which has a vehicle license, tag, decal or other identification device issued by the city pursuant to this Code, in any space established by the city council as a commercial or truck loading zone. Such vehicles shall not be parked in commercial or truck loading zones for any purpose or length of time other than the expeditious unloading and delivery or pick-up and loading of materials upon any street or highway during the signed times the zone is in effect. In no case shall the stop for loading and unloading of materials exceed thirty (30) minutes or such other time as may be posted pursuant to action of the city council. Parking of commercial and passenger vehicles in such truck loading zones shall be permitted during hours other than those posted or above specified.

(Code 1960, As Amend., §§ 411.110, 447.130; Ord. of 7-26-74, § 1; Ord. of 1-10-75, § 1; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Special permits to park in truck or commercial loading zones
children.text:
Any vehicle which properly displays Minneapolis special parking permit decals or other permit designation or device as determined by the department and complies with all provisions of this section, shall be entitled to park in commercial truck loading zones in accordance with the provisions of section 478.810 and other areas as specified below. Such special parking permits shall be subject to the following terms and conditions:

(a) Any person engaged in a bona fide commercial business who has need for and desires a special parking permit, may make application therefor to the public works department, transportation division on such forms as required by that department.

(b) Special parking permit decals may be issued by the department for one (1) year beginning July first upon payment of a fee proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by city council resolution.

(c) All applications for such permits shall be promptly reviewed by the director of public works or designee. Any permit issued may subsequently be revoked for cause by the department. Any person aggrieved by the denial of an application or a revocation of a permit, may, within ten (10) days of notice of such denial or revocation, appeal in writing to the city council for a hearing before the appropriate committee regarding such denial or revocation.

(d) Permits shall be issued in the form of special parking permit decals, which shall be permanently affixed to the upper half of the front doors on each side of the vehicle.

(e) When any vehicle for which a special parking permit decal has been issued is disposed of by the business which made original application for such permit, the decal must be removed or destroyed so as to preclude the use of such vehicle and permit by any other person. The permittee shall also notify the public works department, transportation division that such permit is no longer valid. A new decal may be issued to the same business for a replacement vehicle under the original application upon payment of a fee proposed by the director of public works and established from time to time by city council resolution.

(f) Any special parking permit may be revoked by the director of the public works department, transportation division when any driver, owner or other person in charge of any vehicle which has a special parking permit violates any provision of this section or any other provision of this article, or uses or attempts to use the permit privileges for purposes other than the pick-up and delivery of merchandise in commerce or other permitted commercial purpose.

(g) A special parking permit shall entitle the vehicle to the special privileges accorded to commercial vehicles in section 478.600.

(h) All vehicles must meet the following conditions in order to obtain a permit:

(1) The vehicles must be operating under a company registered with the State of Minnesota Department of Transportation as a commercial property transporter or be a private carrier with legitimate delivery needs in the area.

(2) The vehicles must be operating under a company which has current motor carrier insurance or appropriate insurance as a private carrier.

(3) The vehicles must be properly registered, with proper plates, current tabs and with proof of insurance.

(4) Each vehicle must display the entity for which it is operating while using the permit, but such identification may be of a temporary nature if professionally produced and reasonably visible to parking enforcement personnel and in compliance with state requirements.

(i) Commercial vehicles meeting the following requirements may park in commercial zones without first obtaining a permit:

(1) Vehicles with permanent lettering, as defined in section 466.30 of this Code, denoting a commercial delivery business registered with the state department of transportation.

(2) Vehicles with truck plates and permanent lettering having a legitimate business need while making a product delivery.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.320; Ord. of 7-26-74, § 2; Ord. of 3-14-75, § 1; 79-Or-178, § 1, 8-30-79; 79-Or-320, § 1, 11-9-79; 80-Or-048, § 1, 3-28-80; 83-Or-088, § 1, 4-8-83; 84-Or-128, § 1, 7-13-84; 90-Or-014, § 1, 1-26-90; 91-Or-041, § 1, 2-22-91; 91-Or-049, § 1, 3-29-91; 96-Or-102, § 5, 9-27-96; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Use of passenger loading zones
children.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle for any purpose or period of time other than for the expeditious loading or unloading of passengers in any place officially designated and marked as a passenger zone during hours when the regulations applicable to such passenger zone are effective, and then only for a period of not to exceed three (3) minutes.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.120)

children.title: Use of disability transfer zones
children.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle for any purpose or period of time other than for the loading or unloading of passengers who are disabled in any place officially designated and marked as a "Disability Transfer Zone."

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 411.125; Ord. No. 2021-051, § 3, 11-5-21)

children.title: Use of limited parking zones
children.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle for any purpose or period of time longer than for the expeditious loading or unloading of passengers or merchandise and materials in any place officially designated and marked as a limited time parking zone, during the time when the regulations applicable to such zone are effective.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 447.120)

children.title: Establishment
children.text: Angle parking zones may be established by the city council. Any person, firm or corporation desiring that an angle parking zone be established abutting the premises occupied by such person shall make an application therefor. Such application shall be referred to the city engineer who shall make a survey of the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone and recommend either the granting or denial of such zone. If in the judgment of the city council the traffic conditions in the vicinity of the proposed zone prohibit such angle parking, the zone shall not be established. The permission establishing an angle parking zone shall specify the exact width of the street that can be used for angle parking and any other restrictions or conditions that are to apply. Continued violations of the restrictions of the zone shall be grounds for revocation of the permit. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 449.010)

children.title: Fees
children.text:
Upon the granting of the zone, the city engineer shall bill the applicant according to the following schedule to defray the cost of installation and maintenance:

For each lineal foot of curb, per year .....$ 1.00

Each sign, mounted on two-inch post in precast base ..... 23.00

Each sign, mounted on post in place ..... 11.00

Investigation and publication expense ..... 12.00

Provided, that when an applicant for an angle parking zone applies for and is granted at the same time a loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone, to be established within the angle parking zone and to include all or a portion of the same area, only one maintenance fee and publication fee shall be charged to cover both permits. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 449.020)

children.title: Marking
children.text: When the required fee is paid the city engineer shall install the necessary signs to designate such zone. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 449.030; 96-Or-102, § 6, 9-27-96)

children.title: Renewal
children.text: The permission granted under these provisions may be renewed from year to year upon the payment of the maintenance fee of one dollar ($1.00) per lineal foot of curb. In the event of the failure to pay the annual renewal fee herein specified within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the year for which the permit has been granted or renewed the angle parking zone theretofore established shall be abolished and the city engineer shall remove the signs and obliterate the markings thereof. Provided, that when a loading zone, truck zone or limited parking zone has been established which includes all or a portion of the same area of an angle parking zone, only one renewal fee shall be charged. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 449.040)

children.title: Establishment
children.text: The city council may establish no stopping zones and may add to or modify the said no stopping zones by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The city engineer shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all no stopping zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 450.010)

children.title: Hours
children.text: Said no stopping zones shall be in effect for the hours as provided with respect to particular zones. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 450.020)

children.title: Definitions
children.text: As used herein, the terms (a) "vehicle" shall mean every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a street or highway, except devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks; (b) "street" or "highway" is the entire width between boundary lines of any way or place when any part thereof is open to the use of the public, as a matter of right, for purposes of vehicular traffic; (c) "fully plowed" shall mean that snow emergency plowing has been completed to the full width of that side of the street for which parking is prohibited by this chapter; (d) "non-snow emergency route" shall mean all streets and highways other than those posted as a snow emergency route; (e) "winter season" shall mean the period of time beginning November 1st through April 1st of the following calendar year. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 448.010; 2002-Or-165, § 1, 10-25-02; 2011-Or-100, § 1, 11-4-11)

children.title: Declaration
children.text: Whenever in the opinion of the director of public works an emergency exists in the city, or in a section or sections thereof, because of snow, freezing rain, sleet, ice, snowdrifts or other natural phenomena which create, or are likely to create, hazardous road conditions impeding, or likely to impede, the free movement of fire, health, police, emergency or other vehicular traffic, or the safety and welfare of the community, the director of public works may declare an emergency to exist for a period of seventy-two (72) hours, but such emergency may be sooner terminated if conditions permit. Notice of such emergency shall be given by press, radio or television, which news media shall be requested to cooperate with the city officials and, when given, such notice shall constitute due and proper notice. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 448.020; 2011-Or-100, § 2, 11-4-11; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 4, 11-3-17)

children.title: Snow emergency parking restrictions
children.text:
(a) For a period of eleven (11) hours beginning at 9:00 p.m. on the day of the declaration of a snow emergency by the director of public works, no person shall stop, stand, park or leave any vehicle or permit it to stand upon any street or highway which is a posted "snow emergency route" until the street has been fully plowed.

(b) For a period of twelve (12) hours beginning at 8:00 a.m. on the morning following such declaration of a snow emergency or until the street has been fully plowed, vehicle parking on non-snow emergency routes shall be prohibited on the side of the street or highway with even-numbered addresses. This paragraph shall not apply to the Minneapolis Parkway System.

(c) For a period of twelve (12) hours beginning at 8:00 a.m. on the second morning following such declaration of a snow emergency or until the street has been fully plowed, vehicle parking on non-snow emergency routes shall be prohibited on the side of the street or highway with odd-numbered addresses. This paragraph shall not apply to the Minneapolis Parkway System. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 448.040; Ord. of 3-26-76, § 1; 76-Or-191, § 1, 10-29-76; 76-Or-236, § 1, 12-10-76; 79-Or-182, § 1, 9-14-79; 80-Or-264, § 1, 10-31-80; 83-Or-047, § 2, 2-25-83; 86-Or-018, § 1, 1-31-86; 89-Or-203, § 1, 10-13-89; 90-Or-211, § 2, 8-10-90; 91-Or-248, § 1, 12-6-91; 97-Or-014, § 1, 2-7-97; 2002-Or-165, § 2, 10-25-02; 2004-Or-113, § 1, 10-8-04; 2011-Or-100, § 3, 11-4-11; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 5, 11-3-17)

children.title: Winter parking restrictions
children.text:
(a) In any winter season the public works director may impose a continuous winter parking restriction on non-snow emergency routes. Upon the declaration of a winter parking restriction, no person shall stop, stand, park or leave any vehicle or permit it to stand upon the restricted side of any non-snow emergency route. This paragraph shall not apply to the Minneapolis Parkway System.

When imposed under this subdivision, the public works director shall designate one (1) side of all non-snow emergency route streets as restricted. The public works director shall provide notice of the imposition and removal of any winter parking restriction, together with all relevant details. Notice of winter parking restrictions shall be accomplished through the press, radio or television and shall request the news media to cooperate with the city in conveying notice to the public and, when given, such notice shall constitute due and proper notice.

(b) Once imposed under subdivision (a), a winter parking restriction shall remain continuously in effect beginning on the date it becomes effective and for the remaining portion of the winter season, or until the restriction is officially removed. Winter parking restrictions imposed under subdivision (a) shall be temporarily suspended during a declared snow emergency to coincide with section 478.1000 of this Code as follows: commencing at 4:00 p.m. on the first day of the snow emergency, winter parking restrictions will be suspended; at 8:00 a.m. on the third morning following the declaration of the snow emergency, winter parking restrictions will resume. Nothing in this subdivision shall be construed so as to prevent the public works director from imposing a short-term, or temporary winter parking restriction. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 448.060; 2011-Or-100, § 4, 11-4-11)

children.title: Impounding violations
children.text: If any vehicle is parked, abandoned or left standing in violation of the terms of this article, the same may be impounded in accordance with the terms of the motor vehicle impounding ordinances of the city, at the cost and expense of the owner thereof. (2011-Or-100, § 5, 11-4-11)

children.title: Winter parking in special parking districts
children.text:
(a) From time to time the city council may establish, add to, modify or cancel special parking districts. The city engineer shall at all times maintain in his office a complete listing of all such districts, and said listing is hereby incorporated into this Code the same as if fully set forth herein.

(b) A special parking district may be established by the council only after a public hearing and a finding of fact by a committee of the council that there is a need for said special parking district within the area covered. Application for designation of an area as a special parking district shall, if possible, be accompanied by a plan to improve parking in said district.

(c) Those areas designated as special parking districts pursuant to subsection (b) above shall be posted with signs by the city engineer. The signs shall advise that parking is permitted, except during a snow emergency.

(d) Parking shall be prohibited in such special parking districts on that side of the street with even-numbered addresses for a period of twelve (12) hours beginning at 8:00 a.m. on the day following the declaration of a snow emergency or until the street has been fully plowed and shall be prohibited in such special parking districts on that side of the street with odd-numbered addresses for a period of twelve (12) hours beginning at 8:00 a.m. on the second day following the declaration of a snow emergency or until the street has been fully plowed. (82-Or-015, § 1, 1-29-82; 82-Or-032, § 1, 2-12-82; 2011-Or-100, § 6, 11-4-11)

Note— Formerly § 478.1020.

children.heading: ARTICLE X.
children.title: VEHICLE IMPOUNDMENT
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (11) ---

Cross reference— Wreckers and tow trucks, Ch. 349.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 84-Or-064, § 1, adopted April 13, 1984, repealed § 478.1040, authorizing towing of certain vehicles. Said section derived from § 423.010 of the 1960 Code and from 83-Or-009, § 1, adopted Jan. 14, 1983.

children.title: Impoundment defined
children.text: "Impoundment" means removal of a vehicle to a storage facility or impound lot by a contractor for towing in response to an authorization from a police officer, traffic control agent or other agent authorized by the City of Minneapolis. (84-Or-064, § 2, 4-13-84; 2011-Or-087, § 1, 9-23-11)

children.title: When a vehicle may be impounded
children.text: Vehicle impoundment shall proceed pursuant to Minnesota Statutes Chapters 168B and 169 and all other applicable laws. (84-Or-064, § 3, 4-13-84; 2011-Or-087, § 2, 9-23-11)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2011-Or-087, § 3, adopted September 23, 2011, repealed § 478.1043, which pertained to when a vehicle may be impounded after notice. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Notice to owners
children.text:
(a) Not more than seventy-two (72) hours after impoundment of any vehicle, the supervisor of impound and towing, or the designee thereof, shall mail a notice to the registered owner of the vehicle, as may be disclosed by the vehicle license number, if such be obtainable, and to any other person, including lienholders, who claims the right to possession of the vehicle, if such a claim is known. The notice shall be mailed to the registered owner at the address provided by the Motor Vehicle Division of the Minnesota Department of Public Safety or the corresponding agency of any other state or province. If the person mailing the notice has reason to believe that an owner, or one who claims to be an owner, is residing or in custody at some different address, a copy of the notice shall also be mailed or personally delivered to such owner or claimant in a manner designed, as nearly as may be practicable, to give actual notice to him or her. The notice shall contain the full particulars of the impoundment, redemption, and opportunity for a hearing to test the propriety of the impoundment as hereinafter provided. If a vehicle is redeemed prior to the mailing of notice, then notice need not be mailed. Saturdays, Sundays and city holidays are to be excluded from the calculation of the seventy-two-hour period.

(b) Similar notice shall be given to each person who seeks to redeem an impounded vehicle by posting in a conspicuous place at the impound lot a sign describing redemption procedures. (84-Or-064, § 5, 4-13-84; 2011-Or-087, § 4, 9-23-11)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2011-Or-087, § 5, adopted September 23, 2011, repealed § 478.1045, which pertained to impoundment hearings. See also the Code Comparative Table.

children.title: Redemption of impounded vehicles
children.text:
(a) Only the registered owner, a person authorized by the registered owner, a lienholder of record, or one who has purchased a vehicle from the registered owner, who produces proof of ownership or authorization, may redeem an impounded vehicle. Impounded vehicles may be redeemed under the following circumstances:

(1) Upon payment at the impound lot of the towing and storage costs prior to redeeming such vehicle. The impound lot shall accept cash, major bank credit cards, certified bank drafts, money orders, and personal checks in payment for such costs; provided, however, that if such a personal check is offered in payment for such costs, the person so offering the same may be required to show evidence of identity by two (2) pieces of identification which may include a driver's license, Minnesota state identification card, other credit cards, or similar forms of identification; provided further, however, if there is reasonable cause to believe the tendered check is uncollectible, acceptance of such check may be refused; or

(2) Upon a finding by the Supervisor of Impound and Towing or a Claims Investigator of the City of Minneapolis that there was no probable cause to impound the vehicle. Upon such a finding, the towing charges shall be paid by the city in accordance with interdepartmental billing procedures. However, if the vehicle is not redeemed on the same day of such a finding, the person redeeming the vehicle shall be liable for all subsequent storage charges; or

(3) Upon the order of any court of competent jurisdiction.

(b) Towing charges shall be assessed against vehicles impounded as stolen vehicles and vehicles impounded for law enforcement investigatory purposes. Storage charges shall also be assessed against said vehicles unless the supervisor of impound and towing or a claims investigator of the City of Minneapolis determines the storage charges or part thereof to be unreasonable.

(c) Vehicles which are not redeemed are subject to sale as provided in section 478.1150. (84-Or-064, § 7, 4-13-84; 2011-Or-087, § 6, 9-23-11)

children.title: Bids for impound towers required
children.text: The purchasing agent shall advertise for bids by persons, firms or corporations desiring to act as impound towers of vehicles impounded under the provisions of this article. The notice for bids shall describe the district from which vehicles shall be towed. The publication of notice for such bids, the filing of bids, and the procedure in the acceptance of such bids shall be in accordance with the procedures of the purchasing department. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.020; 83-Or-009, § 2, 1-14-83)

children.title: Referral to city council; acceptance of bids
children.text: Such bids, when received, shall be referred to the city council and by it considered. The notice shall recite that the council reserves the right to reject any and all bids. Upon the acceptance of bids in the various districts, each successful bidder shall be the impound tower within the towing district described in the notice for bids. After the acceptance of said bids and the designation of the impound tower in each of the towing districts, any vehicle ordered to be impounded by any police officer, traffic control agent or other agent authorized by the City of Minneapolis shall be immediately towed to the city impound lot or other designated location by the impound tower. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.030; 83-Or-009, § 3, 1-14-83; 84-Or-064, § 8, 4-13-84; 2011-Or-087, § 7, 9-23-11)

children.title: Impound tower to be bonded
children.text: The person, firm or corporation whose bid is accepted shall file with the city finance officer a bond in the sum of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) conditioned upon the proper handling and safekeeping of towed motor vehicles, accessories and personal property, reimbursement of the city and owners for loss thereof. Such bond shall be approved by the city attorney. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.040; 83-Or-009, § 4, 1-14-83; 85-Or-120, 6-14-85)

children.title: Towing and storage charges
children.text: The charge for towing and storage including administration and clerical expenses shall be set by the city. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.050; 83-Or-009, § 5, 1-14-83)

children.title: Charge when owner appears before towing
children.text: Where a police officer, traffic control agent or other agent authorized by the City of Minneapolis has ordered the impoundment of a vehicle from public property and the owner or operator thereof appears before the vehicle has been hooked to the tow truck and the wheels thereof hoisted from the ground, the tow truck operator shall release the said vehicle without payment of any fee or towing charge. Where the owner or operator of a vehicle being towed from public property appears after the vehicle has been hooked to the tow truck and the wheels thereof hoisted from the ground, or appears after a power winch has been used to move the vehicle, or appears after the vehicle has been moved forward but before the vehicle has been removed from the block upon which it was parked, the tow truck operator shall release the vehicle only upon the payment of a service fee not to exceed fifteen dollars ($15.00) from November 15th through April 1st, and not to exceed five dollars ($5.00) during other times of the year. The tow truck operator shall give a receipt for each service fee received. This section shall not apply to vehicles impounded as an abandoned vehicle pursuant to Minn. Statute Chapter 168B or as a scofflaw vehicle pursuant to Minnesota Statute Section 169.041(5)(b)(13). The tow truck operator shall comply with the provisions of section 349.185. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.060; 83-Or-009, § 6, 1-14-83; 84-Or-064, § 9, 4-13-84; 88-Or-198, § 1, 10-28-88; 2011-Or-087, § 8, 9-23-11)

children.title: Licenses and permits required
children.text: An impound tower under contract with the city shall abide by all contractual requirements and all applicable laws, ordinances and regulations. An impound tower shall see to and require that every tow truck operator employed by the impound tower shall have in his possession a driver's registration and identification in a form approved by the supervisor of impound and towing and no person shall act as a tow truck operator in the towing of any vehicle to be impounded without having in his possession such registration and identification, and such tow truck operator shall exhibit such registration and identification to the owner of the vehicle or his agent upon request therefor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.070; 83-Or-009, § 7, 1-14-83; 2011-Or-087, § 9, 9-23-11)

children.title: Notice to owners
children.text: The city will endeavor to notify record owners and lien holders of impounded vehicles not claimed within a reasonable time of said impoundment by U.S. mail upon receipt of records of ownership from the registrar of motor vehicles of the state. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.080; 83-Or-009, § 8, 1-14-83)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Section 10 of 84-Or-064, enacted April 13, 1984, repealed § 478.1110, concerning storage of impounded vehicles, as derived from § 423.090 of the 1960 Code and from 83-Or-009, § 9, adopted Jan. 14, 1983.

children.title: Release form
children.text: Upon return of the vehicle the city shall release the same by a release in writing which shall state the date of such release together with the charges enumerated thereon and the purpose for which such charges were made. The city shall retain the original of such release and shall deliver one copy thereof to the owner of the vehicle. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.100; 83-Or-009, § 10, 1-14-83)

children.title: Soliciting towing; damaged vehicles
children.text: The impound tower shall not solicit, directly or indirectly, the impounding or towing of cars under this article. If any unoccupied vehicle is found upon the streets of the city in such a damaged condition as a result of accident or disrepair that it cannot be driven, and is so located as to constitute an obstruction of the street, the same may be ordered impounded by the police or other authorized official; provided, that if the owner or operator thereof has requested, or does request, that such vehicle be towed, at his own expense, to his own or to any garage or lot other than the city's lot, neither the police department nor anyone else shall order such vehicle to be impounded in any public pound unless the police department considers possession of such car is necessary in the prosecution of any person for violation of law. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.110; 83-Or-009, § 11, 1-14-83)

children.title: Vehicles to be tagged
children.text: Any unoccupied vehicle or damaged car ordered impounded by the police or other authorized official shall immediately be tagged. The tag shall show the disposition of the car and the offense for which impounded. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.120; 83-Or-009, § 12, 1-14-83)

children.title: Sale of vehicle when unclaimed by owner
children.text:
(a) When the city desires to dispose of any such vehicle so impounded or otherwise recovered, it shall mail to the registered owner thereof, and lien holder, if any, as shown by the records of the state registrar of motor vehicles, notice that the city has possession and intends to dispose of said vehicle. If the owner of the vehicle does not obtain the vehicle as provided in this article within fifteen (15) days after the mailing of such notice, the vehicle shall thereafter be sold by the city as follows:

(1) Motor vehicles which in the opinion of the director of public works meet the requirements of state or federal statute or rule presently in force or as may be amended or adopted relating to motor vehicle air pollution control systems, shall be eligible for sale to the highest bidder at a public sale thereof, provided that no person under the age of eighteen (18) years shall be eligible to bid on or purchase such vehicle. No less than three (3) days prior to such sale, notice stating the date, time and place of the sale shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the city. Upon sale and payment of the purchase price, the city shall deliver to the purchaser a bill of sale, if requested, sufficient to allow the vehicle to be registered and/or titled pursuant to state law.

(2) Motor vehicles which are not sold pursuant to subsection (a)(1) above shall be sold at a limited public sale thereof to the highest bidder who is deemed by the director of public works to be qualified to handle, buy, sell or wreck used, secondhand or junked motor vehicles or motor vehicle accessories. A bidder is "qualified" within the meaning of this section based on the possession of licenses or permits issued and/or required by any governmental unit to conduct such operations, or where no licenses or permits are required or available, the bidder possesses the demonstrated ability to conduct such operations. Vehicles sold at this limited sale shall not be made available for resale to the public, except those automobile accessories which are salvaged from the vehicles and then resold as parts.

No less than three (3) days prior to such limited sale, notice stating the date, time and place of the sale shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the city. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.130; 83-Or-009, § 13, 1-14-83; 84-Or-127, § 1, 7-13-84; 88-Or-169, 9-2-88; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 6, 11-3-17)

children.title: Form of tag; report of towing agency
children.text: Red-colored traffic tags shall be used by police officers and other authorized officials when directing the towing and impounding of a vehicle for a parking violation. Such red tag shall be in the form prescribed by the chief of police and shall contain such information as may be deemed necessary including the make and license number of the vehicle so tagged, the date and time of offense and the offense charged, and any further information which the chief of police shall deem necessary and advisable. It shall not be necessary for the person issuing a red tag to await the arrival of a tow truck, and when said vehicle is towed, it shall be the duty of the impound tower or his agent to prepare a written report of the description of the vehicle with an inventory of any personal properties visible therein at the time of the arrival of the tower at the location of the vehicle. The description and inventory must include the make and license number of the motor vehicle, together with a statement of the condition of the vehicle with regard to damaged parts and such other information as may be necessary to adequately describe the vehicle and property. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.140; 83-Or-009, § 14, 1-14-83)

children.title: Report required when vehicle not tagged
children.text: Any police officer directing the impounding of any vehicle on other than a red tag as hereinbefore described shall prepare a written report in duplicate of the description of such vehicle including the following: Make of vehicle; license number; tools and other separate articles of personal property as may be readily discerned by him; the general description of the vehicle with regard to damaged parts, if any; the condition of the vehicle and such other information as may be necessary to adequately describe the vehicle and property delivered to the impound tower. The original copy of said report will be retained by the police department, and duplicate thereof remitted to the city comptroller-treasurer [finance officer]. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.140; 83-Or-009, § 15, 1-14-83)

children.title: Insurance of impound tower
children.text: The impound tower shall provide and maintain in force during the period of any contract for the towing of impounded vehicles, such insurance for general and automobile liability, for fire and extended coverage insurance, for contractual liability insurance, for workers' compensation insurance, and for any other coverages, in such amounts and with such provisions as may be determined and approved by the city council for inclusion in specifications for the advertising for bids for towing of impounded vehicles. Evidence of the existence of such insurance coverages shall be provided by the impound tower and filed with the city in the manner required by such specifications approved by the city council. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.150; 83-Or-009, § 16, 1-14-83)

children.title: Article to be included in bid and contract
children.text: This article shall be and constitute part of any bid advertised by the purchasing agent and of any contract entered into with the city by any impound tower, as fully and to the same effect as if set forth at length in said contract and if any part or portion of any such contract entered into shall be inconsistent with the terms of this article, the provisions hereof shall in all respects prevail. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.160; 83-Or-009, § 17, 1-14-83)

children.title: Tow sheets and receipts
children.text: Every impound tower, operating under the terms of this article pursuant to a contract with the city, shall at all times make and keep a "tow sheet" on all red tag tows which shall show the time and date of towing, the make, license number and general condition of the vehicle towed. All tow sheets shall be consecutively numbered. Upon releasing any vehicle impounded under the terms of this article, the city shall give to the owner or his agent a receipt for any moneys paid by such owner or his agent to the city at the time of the release. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 423.170; 83-Or-009, § 18, 1-14-83)

children.title: Defined
children.text:
The words "car sharing" as used in this chapter shall mean any rental or lending service that:

(1) Allows qualified drivers to temporarily use vehicles available from a fleet in exchange for a fee that is based on mileage and/or duration of use; and

(2) Conducts its vehicle vending from parking spaces located in the public right-of-way. Car sharing does not mean a vehicle rental or lending service using a daily rental charge or requiring a minimum twenty-four (24) hour rental period. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Conformance with governing policy
children.text: Every car sharing operation conducting business in the city shall comply with the provisions of the city's Car Share Policy. "Car Share Policy" as used in this chapter shall mean the city's written car sharing policy approved by and kept on file with the director of public works. The Car Share Policy may be amended by the director of public works on an annual basis, before January 31st of each year. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: License required
children.text: No person shall engage in the business of car sharing in the city without first having obtained a license as required by Chapter 259 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Application
children.text: Any person or business desiring a license to conduct a car sharing operation in the city shall make application therefor to the licensing official, upon forms to be furnished by such licensing official, and such application shall, among other things, contain the name and address of the applicant, and the name and address of the car sharing operation. After filing of such application the same shall be referred to the director of public works for investigation and report as to the suitability and sustainability of the proposed car sharing operation for which a license is sought. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Control of right-of-way
children.text: Licenses and permits issued pursuant to Chapter 259 and this Chapter 478, Article XI shall not operate so as to transfer ownership or control of the public right-of-way to car sharing operators, or to any other party. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Compliance with laws
children.text: Car sharing operators shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws as they may be amended from time to time. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.title: Enforcement
children.text: In addition to any other remedy available at equity or law, failure to comply with the provisions of Chapter 259, or this Chapter 478, Article XI, including but not limited to the governing policy referenced herein, may result in license suspension or cancellation as provided in Title 13 of this Code, and/or administrative fines, restrictions, or penalties as provided in Chapter 2 of this Code. (Ord. No. 2016-006, § 1, 2-12-16)

children.heading: CHAPTER 480.
children.title: RESERVED
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (12) ---

Editor's note— 90-Or-133, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed Ch. 480. Prior to such repeal, Ch. 480, §§ 480.10—480.100, pertained to accidents, and was derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 418.010—418.100.

children.heading: CHAPTER 482.
children.title: BUSES AND TAXICABS
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (13) ---

Cross reference— Taxicabs generally, Ch. 341; operation of buses on parkways and park boulevards, § PB5-1 et seq.

children.title: Taxi stands established
children.text: The taxi stands established by the city council as of July 1, 1960 (Chapter 9:21, 1948 Compilation of Ordinances) are continued in effect, and the council may add to or modify the said taxi stands by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The city engineer shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all taxi stands, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 445.010; Ord. No. 2017-067, § 7, 11-3-17)

children.title: Duty to use stand or stop
children.text:
The driver of a bus or taxicab shall not stand or park upon a street in any business district at a place other than a bus stop or taxicab stand, respectively, except that this provision shall not prevent the driver of any such vehicle from temporarily stopping in accordance with other stopping or parking regulations at any place for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading passengers. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 412.010)

Cross reference— Parking restrictions on taxicabs within specified area, § 341.210.

children.title: Use regulations
children.text:
(a) Use of stand or stop by others. No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle other than a bus in a bus stop or other than a taxicab in a taxicab stand when any such stop or stand has been officially designated and appropriately signposted, except that the driver of a passenger vehicle may temporarily stop therein for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading passengers when such stopping does not interfere with any bus or taxicab waiting to enter or about to enter such zone.

(b) Unattended taxicab in taxicab stand. No person shall stop, stand or park a taxicab in a taxicab stand without remaining in the vehicle. Nothing in this subsection shall prohibit a person from leaving the vehicle for the purpose of assisting a passenger into or out of the vehicle. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 412.020; 86-Or-146, § 1, 6-12-86)

children.title: Buses obstructing traffic
children.text: No bus shall be permitted to stand or lie over on any highway in this city except as, when and where authorized by the city council. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 412.030)

children.title: Bus doors to be kept closed
children.text: The gates or doors of every bus upon a highway shall be kept closed at all times except when receiving or discharging passengers. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 412.040)

children.title: Buses to obey traffic devices
children.text: The operator of every bus shall obey the directions given by signs, signals and markings placed and maintained on the highways of this city by authority of the city council for the purpose of guiding, informing, warning or controlling traffic. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 412.050)

children.heading: CHAPTER 484.
children.title: RESERVED
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (14) ---

Editor's note— 90-Or-134, § 1, adopted May 11, 1990, repealed Ch. 484. Formerly, Ch. 484, §§ 484.10—484.100, pertained to pedestrians, and was derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 408.010—408.080, 408.100, 937.020.

children.heading: CHAPTER 486.
children.title: VEHICLE SIZE, WEIGHT AND LOAD
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (15) ---

Cross reference— Size and weight of buses operated on parkways and park boulevards, § PB5-4.

children.title: Applicability
children.text: No person shall drive or move, nor shall the owner cause or knowingly permit to be driven or moved on any street or highway any vehicle of a size exceeding the limitations stated in this article. The provisions of this article shall not apply to fire apparatus, or to implements of husbandry temporarily moved upon a highway, or to loads of loose hay or corn stalks if transported by horse-drawn vehicle or drawn by a farm tractor, or to a vehicle operated under the terms of a special permit issued as provided in Article II of this chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 415.010)

children.title: Outside width
children.text:
The total outside width of any vehicle or the load thereon shall not exceed eight (8) feet, except that the outside width of a farm tractor shall not exceed twelve (12) feet, and except as otherwise provided in this section.

The total outside width of a passenger motor bus, operated exclusively in the city, or contiguous cities, shall not exceed nine (9) feet. A passenger motor bus, not exceeding eight and one-half (8½) feet in width, may operate between the separated facilities of a college or university if part of the facilities are located within one of the foregoing areas and part are located outside but not more than five (5) miles from the area.

The total outside width of loads of forest products when loaded crossways shall not exceed one hundred (100) inches, provided the load is securely bound with a chain attached to front and rear of the loading platform of the vehicle so as to hold the load securely in place. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 415.020)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.80, Subd. 2.

children.title: Projecting load on passenger vehicles
children.text:
No passenger type vehicle shall be operated on any street or highway with a load carried thereon extending beyond the line of the fenders on the left side of such vehicle nor extending more than six (6) inches beyond the line of the fenders on the right side thereof. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 415.030)

State Law reference— Load projecting over front bumper, M.S. § 169.81, Subd. 4.

children.title: Height of vehicles
children.text:
No vehicle unloaded or with load shall exceed a height of thirteen (13) feet, six (6) inches. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 415.040)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.81, Subd. 1.

children.title: Length of vehicles
children.text:
(a) No vehicle shall exceed a length of fifty-five (55) feet extreme overall dimensions, inclusive of front and rear bumper. A truck-tractor and semi-trailer shall be regarded as one vehicle for the purpose of determining lawful length.

(b) No combination of vehicles coupled together including truck-tractors and semitrailers shall consist of more than two (2) units, and no such combination of vehicles shall exceed a total length of fifty-five (55) feet, provided that such vehicles shall not use the area bounded by Third Street, First Avenue North, Tenth Street, and Park Avenue between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. and between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. This limitation as to length and hours when such vehicles are prohibited from using the streets, shall not apply to the transportation of telegraph poles, telephone poles, electric light and power poles, or piling, or pole length pulpwood. Said length limitations shall not apply to:

(1) Vehicles when transporting pipe or other objects by a public utility when required for emergency or repair of public service facilities or when operated under special permit as provided in Article II of this chapter, but in respect to night transportation every such vehicle and load thereon shall be equipped with a sufficient number of clearance lamps and marker lamps on both sides and upon the extreme ends of any projecting load to clearly mark the dimensions of such load;

(2) House trailers or mobile homes when coupled with a motor vehicle, but such combinations shall not exceed fifty-five (55) feet in length; provided further that two (2) vehicles in transit by the drive-away method in saddle mount combinations may be drawn, but such combinations may not exceed fifty (50) feet in length.

(c) The load upon any vehicle operated alone, or the load upon the front vehicle of a combination of vehicles, shall not extend more than three (3) feet beyond the front wheels of such vehicle or the front bumper of such vehicle if it is equipped with such a bumper, nor shall such load extend more than ten (10) feet to the rear beyond the bed or body of such vehicle, except under the conditions of a special permit issued as provided in Article II of this chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 415.050)

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— 81-Or-286, § 1, adopted Nov. 13, 1981, repealed § 486.60, which section enumerated streets upon which vehicles could operate in exception to length restrictions. The repealed section derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 415.060; an ordinance of March 29, 1974, § 1; an ordinance of Sept. 27, 1974, § 1; 78-Or-270, § 1, enacted Dec. 22, 1978; and 79-Or-243, § 1, enacted Nov. 21, 1979.

children.title: Generally
children.text:
No vehicle or combination of vehicles equipped with pneumatic tires shall be operated upon the streets or highways in the city:

(a) Where the gross weight on any wheels exceeds nine thousand (9,000) pounds;

(b) Where the gross weight on any single axle exceeds eighteen thousand (18,000) pounds. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 416.010)

State Law reference— Similar provisions, M.S. § 169.825.
