(1) If said tax delinquent lands are or have been sold pursuant to Minn. Stats. § 282.01 through § 282.12, and the proceeds of said sale are insufficient to meet the balance of said assessments due and deferred, including penalties and interest, said property owner or person in possession shall pay said balance before tapping or connecting to any public water or sewer main or issuance of a permit for the same. The balance shall be determined by the city engineer from the records of said sale and the assessment proceeding in which said assessments were levied; and

(2) In case property abutting upon any water or sewer main was or is now subject to assessment at the time such water or sewer main was or is constructed, either by reason of the fact that said property was or is tax delinquent land forfeited to the state or otherwise exempt from assessment, and the property owner or person in possession of such abutting property shall make application for permit to tap such water or sewer main, no such permit shall be granted nor shall such property owner or person in possession be permitted to use, tap or make connection with any such water or sewer main unless such person shall first pay into the city treasury the cost of the construction of said water or sewer main, together with interest from the date of construction to the date of payment, a sum of money equal to such amount per front foot as shall have been determined at the time such water or sewer main was or is constructed and assessed against other property then subject to assessment. Said payment shall be determined by the city engineer, but shall not exceed (in case of tapping a water main) the cost of laying a street water main six (6) inches in diameter in front of said premises, nor (in case of tapping a sewer) the cost of laying a street sewer two (2) feet in diameter in front of said premises.

(b) The director shall calculate the amount to be paid and provide such amount to the city finance officer, who shall issue an invoice and credit the revenue to the fund from which the dollars for the water or sewer main construction were disbursed. Upon payment of the amount indicated by said invoice, a permit shall be issued in the manner otherwise provided by this Code of Ordinances.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 3, 5-26-22)

children.title: Revocation of certificate of competency for violations
children.text:
In accordance with Code of Ordinances Title 13, Chapter 278, section 278.510, Denial, revocation, suspension or cancellation of certificate of competency, the city council may revoke the certificate of competency card of any plumber licensed by the city who shall be guilty of any violation of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 3, 5-26-22)

children.title: Definitions
children.text:
For this chapter, the following definitions shall apply:

Backflow means the undesirable reversal of flow of water or mixtures of water and other liquids, gases, or other substances into the distribution pipes of the potable support of water from any source(s).

Bonds means revenue or general obligation bonds, notes, loans, or other debt obligations heretofore or hereafter issued to finance the costs of improvements, operations, and/or maintenance.

City engineer means the city engineer of the City of Minneapolis or their duly authorized designee.

City standards shall mean the current version of the Standard Supplemental Specifications for the Construction of Public Infrastructure in the City of Minneapolis.

Cross-connection means any unprotected actual or potential connection or structural arrangement between a municipal or a private potable water system, and any other source or system through which it is possible to introduce into any part of the potable water system any used water, industrial fluid, gases, solids, or substance other than the intended potable water with which the system is supplied. Cross-connection can also describe a condition where two (2) or more individual water service lines from the municipal source are tied together creating the potential for pollution or contamination from an individual building's plumbing system flowing back into a water main due to a pressure differential between the interconnected water service lines.

Department means the Minneapolis department of public works.

Director means the director of the water treatment and distribution services division of public works.

Division means the water treatment and distribution services division of the public works department.

Enterprise fund means the enterprise fund used to account for the revenues and expenses of the water treatment and distribution services division.

Fiscal year means a twelve-month period commencing on the first day of January of any year or such other twelve-month period adopted as the fiscal year of the city.

Public works director means department head with the ultimate responsibility and authority for the public works department.

Revenues means all rates, fees, assessments, rentals, or other charges or other income received by the water utility in connection with the management and operation of the system, including amounts received from the investment, deposit or monies in any fund or account, as calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting practices.

Spacer pipe means a temporary pipe the same size as the water meter to fill the space for the water meter when the water meter is temporarily removed.

Water meter shall include a metering device connected to the water system of the city for the purpose of measuring the amount of water delivered from the city water main to any private premises, buildings, or structures in the city. It will not include private water meters owned and installed by the property owner or occupant of any premises for the property owner's or occupant's own use and benefit.

Water works means an establishment for treating, storing, and distributing water for community supply.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water treatment and distribution services division; supervision by public works director; appointment of personnel
children.text:
Within the department of public works, there shall be a water treatment and distribution services division. Subject to the direction of the city council and the immediate direction of the director of the department of public works, it shall have charge of:

(1) The construction, maintenance, repair, and management of the city's water works and everything pertaining to the city's water facilities and infrastructure, water treatment, water distribution, and other potable water services;

(2) All new constructions, additions, and alterations to the system of any kind; and

(3) The supervision and direction of the operation of the system and related facilities.

This division shall be under the authority of the public works director who, subject to the direction of the city council, shall do everything regarding the division that may be necessary for the management and protection thereof. The public works director shall appoint all officers of the division.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Division officers
children.text:
In addition to the public works director, the officers of the division shall be the director and such other employees as may be necessary to the efficient management of the division.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Director of public works to have general management
children.text:
The director of public works shall have the general custody, control, and management of the division.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Qualifications, duties of the division director
children.text:
The director, under the direction of the city engineer, shall have charge of the operation, maintenance, and construction of the water works, and shall perform such other duties as may be required by the city engineer. The director shall be skilled in water works matters, shall take charge of all employees of the division, and shall see that all work is done in a workmanlike manner and as directed by the city engineer.

The director shall, under the city engineer, have the immediate control and custody of all the property of the division and see that all such property is properly stored and cared for and that a full and complete record and inventory of the same is kept.

The director shall see that all hydrants, gates, valves, and other parts of the division are in order, all leaks are promptly repaired, and full and accurate reports are kept of all work done.

Under the direction of the city engineer, the director shall have general supervision of the:

(1) Intakes, pumping stations, pumps, motors, machinery, equipment, and tools therein and of all employees connected therewith;

(2) Mains, gates, hydrants, valves, and all other devices and appurtenances; and

(3) Reservoirs, purification plants, laboratories and employees connected therewith.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Division records and accounts
children.text:
The director shall keep a full set of records which shall show in detail the location and measurements for all water mains, hydrants, valves, curb stop boxes, water service shutoff valves, tees, crosses, and such other measurements and records as may be necessary. The director shall keep a record of at least two (2) measurements taken from two (2) separate permanent points or the x, y coordinate data for each curb stop box and each water service tap made in the water mains and water service lines.

The director shall issue all permits for tapping mains.

The director shall keep a record of all water service taps and water service lines, their size, and their location.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 4, 2-27-25)

children.title: Supervision of employees; duties of water utility operators
children.text:
The director shall have the immediate charge of all employees necessary to the proper conduct of the division. Division employees designated by the director as water utility operators shall have charge of inspecting the premises entered by water service lines, examining the condition of all water meters and other fixtures, and shall be vigilant to detect and warn against all abuses, whether from waste or other improper use of water. Each water utility operator shall at once report all infringements of the regulations to the director. Said water utility operators shall also make and keep a true record of each water meter in use.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Departure from rules governing the division
children.text:
The director, at their discretion and upon approval of the public works director, may depart from the rules set forth for the government of the division when special written application is made for the purpose which may be deemed proper.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Access to buildings
children.text:
The officers of the division, personally, and persons delegated by them for that purpose, shall, to the maximum extent that it is constitutionally permitted, have free access at proper hours of the day, to all parts of every building in which water is consumed, and to the property in which water piping resides.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Authority to inspect plumbing
children.text:
The water utility operators of the division shall be permitted to examine all plumbing work, materials, and fixtures to the maximum extent it is constitutionally permitted.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Identification of division staff
children.text:
Division staff shall be provided with identification cards which must be shown on demand.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: City not liable for water shortage; authority to shut off
children.text:
The city shall not be liable for any deficiency or failure in the supply of water to consumers, whether occasioned by shutting the water off for the purpose of making repairs or connections, or for any other cause whatever. In case of fire or alarm of fire, or in making repairs, or constructing new works, the director may shut off the water at any time and keep it shut off so long as the director shall deem necessary.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Procuring grounds and diverting water
children.text:
The city council may exercise its power of eminent domain, or proceed under any applicable state law granting or governing proper authority whenever the city council shall consider it necessary to:

(1) Procure grounds for water works, any water-power for water works, or the right to take from any dam, pond, reservoir, or other part or portion of the waters of the Mississippi River, whether the same be private or public property or rights, any and all water necessary or convenient for the purpose of being forced through the conduits, aqueducts, pipes, water mains, or water service lines in the City of Minneapolis, or through any part thereof, for the benefit and use of the inhabitants and people residing at or being in the City of Minneapolis, and for the use of said city;

(2) Lay intake pipes from any pump station in the City of Minneapolis belonging to said water works, through any mill dam, mill pond, whether above, through, or below water, or through the bed or bottom of any such mill dam or mill pond, or through any private real estate, whether same be water or land, or interests in any water power or water reservoir, and to lay and maintain said intake pipe or pipes, and to construct the necessary cribs and other protections of every kind necessary to lay or to protect any such intake pipe or pipes anywhere in the Mississippi River or the islands therein or land adjoining thereto; and

(3) Construct dams, reservoirs, and wing dams, anywhere in said river, whether within or above other dams, ponds, or reservoirs.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Assessment for water mains
children.text:
Whenever water mains shall be laid, re-laid, or extended through any street or alley of the city, or any portion thereof, the city council shall have the authority, and it shall be its duty, to levy and collect the cost or expense thereof or a portion thereof, including pipe, hydrants, valves, and all necessary system components by a special assessment upon the property on both sides of the street fronting upon such improvement.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Services outside the city
children.text:
Where division facilities or water mains of the city have been, or shall be extended to or constructed, in any road, street, alley, or public highway adjacent to or outside of the corporate limits of the city, each request from prospective consumers to connect to the city water mains shall be reviewed by the director to ascertain compliance with this Code of Ordinances and applicable design criteria.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Supervision of work on mains
children.text:
The work of laying, re-laying, or repairing any water main, or making any connection with any water main, for any private person, within the limits of any street or public ground in the city, shall be done under the direction of the director or the director's authorized designee.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Work on water mains under city contract
children.text:
Any person having a contract with the city for laying, re-laying or repairing water mains, or setting hydrants shall have the right to excavate in the streets or alleys for the purpose of laying water mains provided for or needed in the completion of such contract. Said excavation may be done without a permit from the city engineer provided said contract indemnifies the city against any loss or damage caused by neglect or carelessness on the part of the contractor and its agents, employees, or servants in the progress of work done under said contract.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Permits for excavations issued by the division
children.text:
The director, or any person having the authority from the director, may open any street or public ground without permits from the city engineer for the purpose of laying, re-laying, or repairing any water main or water service line when the circumstances require immediate action but such permit must be obtained as soon as possible thereafter. In all other cases, permits for the opening of any street or public ground shall be given by the city engineer to the director.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Damage to division infrastructure or other property
children.text:
Any person who shall, without authority from the city council, willfully break, remove, or in any way injure, damage, or interfere with any division infrastructure or property including, but not limited to the water main, water meter, water service lines, intake pipes, aqueduct, dam, bulkhead reservoir, pump station, gate, gate house, valve, conduit, air vent, air box, air box cover, main pipe or cover, hydrant, storage tank, or any part of the machinery, equipment, infrastructure, or other property of the city; or who shall fill up or partially fill up any excavation, or raise or open any gate, break down or force open any doors, or breach any fences or any city property, or who shall perforate or bore, or cause to be perforated or bored, any main, distributing pipe, branch pipe, aqueduct, or other pipes of any kind, or cause to be made any connections or communications with any such main, distributing pipe, branch pipe, aqueduct, or other pipes, or do any act to pollute the water in any river, creek, or channel anywhere in the city limits of the city, or the Mississippi River within three (3) miles above the north line of the city, or do any act to pollute any reservoir, pipe, main, aqueduct, intake pipe, storage tank, or other place for collecting water for use for the city's water distribution and transmission services, on conviction thereof shall be subject to be punished as provided by section 1.30 of this Code of Ordinances, in addition to being subject to any other penalties or remedies, civil or criminal, provided by local, state, or federal law.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Interference with hydrants, gate valves
children.text:
No person shall open or interfere with any of the hydrants or gate valves of the city, except city employees with proper authorization to do so and other persons with the proper permits from the division.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.heading: ARTICLE II.
children.title: WATER TREATMENT AND DISTRIBUTION SERVICES ENTERPRISE FUND
Financial management
children.text:
(a) The city shall maintain a separate enterprise fund for the division. The enterprise fund shall be used to record all moneys paid and payable to the city as and for water rates, rents, and all other miscellaneous moneys payable or paid to, or received by, the city finance officer from any source whatsoever to the credit of the division. The enterprise fund shall also be used to record all moneys appropriated by the city council for division purposes.

(b) All special assessments levied upon abutting property for the laying of water mains, shall when and as fast as collected, be credited to the enterprise fund. The city shall proceed to lay mains in advance of the collection of special assessments thereof, whenever there shall be sufficient moneys in the enterprise fund in excess of other necessary or estimated demands thereon to enable advances to be made from the fund.

(c) No contract negotiated by the city council shall be binding upon the city until the same shall be countersigned by the finance officer; subject to the same rules respecting the possession of funds to meet such contracts as in case of other contracts entered into on behalf of the city; but the city shall have the right to make such contract for anything pertaining to water treatment and distribution services of the city in anticipation of the sale of any bonds which the city shall have been authorized to sell, the proceeds of which are required to be set apart to the credit of the enterprise fund.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Payments on bonds
children.text:
Interest and principal requirements for all bonds, and for all bonds issued to refund bonds, shall be paid from the enterprise fund.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Budget
Accounting and financial officer
Repairs, use of other funds
children.text:
If it shall be necessary to make repairs, additions, or alterations to any pumping stations, treatment facilities, equipment, water mains, or other facilities of any kind related to water treatment or distribution, when there shall not be sufficient money in the enterprise fund to defray the costs thereof, the city council may appropriate sufficient money from the general fund of the city to the enterprise fund to insure repairs.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Provisions governing
children.text:
All service connections made to any water main or pipe transporting unmetered city water, wherever located, shall be governed by the rules, regulations, and charges provided in this chapter.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Ownership and responsibility
children.text:
(a) The water service line shall consist of:

(1) A water service tap; a gate valve and maintenance hole, a gate cone at the main, or a curb stop box and water service shutoff valve; and

(2) Shut off valves at the water meter; and

(3) The water service line between the water main and the water meter.

(b) The water service line shall be owned by the property it serves, and each piece of the water service line shall be maintained and kept in good operating condition by the property owner. Failure to do so may result in the division issuing a written notice to the owner of the property setting forth the correction or repair required to be done and the date on which such repair is to be completed. Such completion date shall not exceed fifteen (15) calendar days after the date of said notice. If the deficiency is not corrected within the stipulated time frame, the division shall have the necessary corrections made and the cost thereof will be applied to the property owner's utility bill and, if not paid promptly, with the property as a special assessment on the tax rolls. If applied as a special assessment, the procedures used will be as outlined in Section 590.610.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2023-026, § 1, 4-27-23; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 5, 2-27-25)

children.title: Application for permit for connection
children.text:
All permit applications shall be made in writing by the owner of the property, or the duly authorized agent of the property owner, and approved by the division. No permit shall authorize anything not stated in the application. For any misrepresentation in such application, the permit may be suspended, and the property owner fined; and if the misrepresentation appears to be willful, the permit will be revoked.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Permits required
children.text:
No person shall lay, re-lay, or repair any branch or water service line, or tap or make any connection with any water main, without first having obtained a permit to do the same. Excavation permits are also required, as described in Chapter 429, Right-of-way administration if the branch or water service line work requires necessary openings in any street or public ground.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Permit to tap required
children.text:
No person other than a division employee shall tap or make any perforation or opening of any kind in any water main, or any public or private water service line within the boundaries of any street or public ground without first having obtained a permit to do the same.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Permit issuance; contents; compliance therewith
children.text:
If laying, re-laying, repairing, tapping, or making such connection is deemed necessary and proper, the division shall grant a permit to a licensed plumber. The permit shall describe the exact location at which laying, re-laying, repairing, tapping, or making of such connection shall be done. Permitted locations must not be departed from in any degree. If the location is changed, a new permit must be issued.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Inspection and excavation fees
children.text:
Before the issuance of any permit, the permit holder authorized to excavate in the streets, avenues, alleys, or public grounds shall deposit with the city finance department the designated amount of money to cover the expense of inspection of such work and the restoration of the street.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Expense for street restoration
children.text:
The amount for the street restoration shall be as estimated by the city engineer. After the refilling has been done and the work completed, the city finance department shall return to said permit holder such amount that the deposit made with the finance department exceeds the total certified expenses; when the street restoration expenses exceed the amount of deposit made with the city finance department, such excess shall be paid to the city finance officer by the permit holder.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Pipes subject to inspection
children.text:
All water pipes which shall be laid, re-laid, or repaired on any private premises shall be subject to the inspection of the city engineer. The person who is causing the same to be laid, re-laid or repaired as well as the person laying, re-laying or repairing the same shall give the city engineer all reasonable facilities for so inspecting the laying, re-laying, or repairing of the same. All work in connection therewith, and the same shall be laid, re-laid, or repaired according to the directions of the city engineer, where the same has not been prescribed by the city council.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Separation of pipes
children.text:
No water pipes shall be put into any opening with any gas or other pipe, but each of said pipes must be far enough from all others to permit the repair, removal, or re-laying of any one without disturbing the other one in accordance with city standards.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Refusal of water for nonpayment of fees
children.text:
The director of water treatment and distribution services shall refuse to turn on water for any person who has had a connection made with any of the water mains or service pipes of the city, or with any private water service line, who shall refuse or neglect to pay to the city finance officer any balance which may be due the city after exhausting the deposit made to pay the expense of inspection and repaving.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Revocation of certificate of competency card for violations
children.text:
In accordance with Code of Ordinances Title 13, Chapter 278, section 278.510, Denial, revocation, suspension, or cancellation of certificate of competency, the city council may revoke the certificate of competency card of any plumber licensed by the city who shall be guilty of any violation of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Charges for tapping mains
children.text:
A fee shall be charged for the tapping and making connections with the city's water mains. This fee must be paid before a permit shall be issued.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Materials and weights for water service lines
children.text:
Size and weights for water service line pipe and water meter sets shall be according to the city standards.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Flared joints required
children.text:
Service line joints should be minimized when possible. All connections to copper tubing between the water main and the water meter shall be mechanical flared joints, except, to comply with the Minnesota plumbing code, one (1) brazed joint with a wrought copper fitting will be permitted on service line tubing if the joint is made inside the foundation of a building and the joint must be located under a concrete slab. A brazed joint shall be left exposed and pressurized for inspection by a City of Minneapolis Plumbing Inspector prior to being backfilled.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 6, 2-27-25)

children.title: Water service tap installation
children.text:
The water service tap inserted in the water main must be of the size specified in the permit and shall be installed exclusively by division employees. Every water service line and water service tap must be placed in accordance with city standards.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Entrance to building; curb stop boxes
children.text:
The water service line must extend from the main to the inside of the building or other fixtures which it is intended to supply. In all cases, a water service tap shall be completed with a gate cone or maintenance hole at the main, or a water service shutoff valve must be placed outside in a curb stop box according to city standards. All curb stop boxes must be set in front of the building or that part of the building intended to be supplied, not to exceed two (2) feet from the line of said building or part thereof.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 7, 2-27-25)

children.title: Rules for domestic supply from one or more water service lines
children.text:
(a) Buildings with frontage to the public right-of-way shall be supplied by a single metered water service line connected directly to the public water main.

(b) Buildings without frontage to the public right-of-way shall be serviced from the primary structure or from a private water main within the shared land managed by the owners' association.

(c) If the division grants approval for more than one (1) domestic water service line to a structure, a registered backflow device shall be installed on each line after the meter and within three (3) feet of the meter set.

(d) If a structure is renovated and additional domestic water service lines are added, all water service lines must be retrofitted with registered backflow protection devices.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Combination fire protection and domestic water service lines
children.text:
To maintain potable water quality in buildings, combination lines (i.e., single water service lines that provide both domestic water service and fire protection service) larger than two (2) inches in diameter are not allowed.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Proximity to sewers
children.text:
No water pipe shall be laid in the same trench with a building drain or sewer pipe in the city street. The water pipe shall not be closer than ten (10) feet to a sewer pipe at any point horizontally, and when the water and sewer cross each other, there shall be at least eighteen (18) inches of vertical separation from the bottom of the water pipe to the top of the sewer pipe, all in accordance with city standards.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Repair of leaks
children.text:
If a property owner fails to repair a leak in their water service line within fifteen (15) days following issuance of verbal or written notice upon the premises, the water may be shut off and will not be turned on until all applicable fees have been paid and the leak has been remedied. When the waste of water is great or when damage is likely to result from the leak or a hazard has been created, the water may be shut off immediately.

If work is done on a water service line and any part of that water service line is made of lead, then all parts of the water service line that are lead must be replaced with copper. In cases where the line is lead from the water service tap, a new water service tap must be installed. Any new water service line installation, repair, or replacement thereto, shall not connect to materials known to contain lead or to contain galvanized iron.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Assessment for repairs to water service lines
children.text:
(a) The owner of any property having a water service line in need of repair or replacement may request and authorize the city to make all necessary repairs and replacements to the water service line. Such authorization by the property owner to the city shall:

(1) Give the city and/or its designated agents the right to enter upon the premises as may be necessary to make such repairs and replacements;

(2) Indemnify the city for all claims and damages arising from the making of such repairs and replacements; and

(3) Include the consent of the property owner to any unpaid charges for such work to be collected as a special assessment against the property as provided herein.

The city, upon receiving authorization from the property owner, may immediately cause the repairs or replacement of the water service line to be done under its direction and control. The said repair or replacement costs shall be initially provided for by an advance of funds from the water treatment and distribution services division enterprise fund, to be reimbursed from the collection of such charges. Where there is a risk to persons or property as determined by the director, the repair or replacement may be done immediately under the city's direction and control with or without such authorization.

(b) Upon completion of such work, the city shall notify the property owner of the total amount to be paid to the city as reimbursement for the repair and replacement costs and the date by which payment must be made. This amount may include an administrative fee.

(c) If the charges or any part thereof for any such work is unpaid by the specified date, the city shall prepare a proposed assessment roll listing the amount of the charges unpaid and the benefited property which shall be filed with the city clerk. The city council shall assess and levy and cause to be collected the amount of such costs as a special assessment upon and against the property benefited in the manner provided by Minn. Stats. §§ 429.061, 429.071, and 429.081. The interest rate shall be set annually by the city's finance officer and shall reflect the current interest rate environment, the term of the loan, lost investment earnings, and administrative costs to the city.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water service lines to be discontinued and water service taps closed and plugged
children.text:
When new buildings are erected on the sites of old ones, no connections with the mains shall be given until all the old water service lines, active and inactive, are discontinued and the water service tap is closed and plugged at the water main. Installation of new water service taps or removal of an existing water service tap shall only be performed at the direction of the director. When buildings are demolished or removed, the old water service lines shall be discontinued at the main. If the old water service line is not properly discontinued at the main in accordance with city standards, water to the premises shall be shut off and fines shall be levied against the property. Water service shall not be reinstated until the old water service line has been properly discontinued and inspected.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Size of domestic connections
children.text:
Connections with the mains for domestic water supply shall be calculated by the developer so that the water service line is sized sufficiently for the fixture counts of the intended use but not oversized such that building water quality could be diminished by lack of turnover.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Temporary water supply
children.text:
If water supply is interrupted due to maintenance or repair of the water service line or city water distribution piping, permission to take water from another potable water source may be given by the director with consent of the party controlling the temporary source of potable water.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Discontinuing joint services for nonpayment
children.text:
Where two (2) or more customers take water from the same water service line, and any of them neglect to pay the water rates, the water may be shut off from all.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water service for building construction
children.text:
When a permit is issued for building construction purposes, the water service line must be carried to the inside of the curb, and when the building is completed the water service line must be taken up and the water service tap closed and plugged, unless it is will be extended to supply water service to the building; in which case, application must be made in the usual manner for water service line extensions.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Permit required for changes
children.text:
No person shall make any extension or addition to or alteration of any water service line, meter set, fixture, or plumbing connected with the water system of the city without first having obtained from the director a written permit to do so for each building or place where such work is to be performed. The applicant shall pay a fee to the city before such permit is issued. In case of a second offense by any person in doing the work above mentioned without a permit, the director shall have authority to refuse any further permits to such person.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Tampering with water service line and/or water service shutoff valve
children.text:
Whenever the director shall have caused the water to be shut off and it appears there has been tampering with the water service line and/or water service shutoff valve, the director may cause the water service line to be severed from the water main and the property owner may be charged a tampering penalty.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 8, 2-27-25)

children.title: Costs of ice hazard removal reimbursed from water treatment and distribution services enterprise fund
children.text:
In case of an ice hazard in any storm drain, public street, sidewalk, or alley, resulting from a leak occurring in a public or private water main or water service line, the costs of such ice hazard removal shall be paid out of the general fund of the city, to be reimbursed from the water treatment and distribution services enterprise fund.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Private water service lines
children.text:
(a) The director shall have the authority to negotiate private water service line agreements subject to city council approval. This authority shall include:

(1) Private water service lines may extend into streets which have not been officially graded or paved;

(2) Private water service lines under the streets which have been officially graded or paved;

(3) Private water service lines located on private property; and

(4) Private service lines leading into streets which have no water main.

(b) The materials, fittings, and size of pipe shall be suitable for the water service and possible future demands for water service as determined by the director. Maintenance work that is required for private water service lines shall be defined in the private service line agreement.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Plumbing/gas fitting contractor license required
children.text:
All work to connect water service lines inside buildings must be performed by licensed individuals in accordance with Section 278.133.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 10, 2-27-25)

children.title: Manner of making water main connections
children.text:
The following rules must be observed and carried out in all work relating to water main connections, to laying, to re-laying or to repairing water pipes:

(1) In making connections with the water main, the materials and the installation for water service taps and water service lines, as well as all backfilling, must be in accordance with the requirements of the current publication of the Supplemental Specifications for the Construction of Public Infrastructure in the City of Minneapolis.

(2) All work must be done under the supervision of an inspector named by the city engineer.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Pipe laying bond required
children.text:
All work to lay water service lines from the city water main to the inside of buildings must be performed by a person holding a plumbing bond or be an employee of a person in compliance with Minnesota bond and insurance requirements. Each person performing pipe-laying work shall hold a valid plumbers license or hold a current pipe-layer training card documenting satisfactory training.

(Ord. No. 2025-014, § 10, 2-27-25)

children.title: City ownership of water meters
children.text:
The city will install, own, and maintain all water meters, irrigation meters from a dedicated water service line, and detector assembly fire meters inside and outside the city that are attached to the city's water system. This applies to all new construction and to all new water meter installations in existing structures or on existing properties. This will also apply to a water meter that is relocated within an existing property or structure. Any property owner with an existing water meter that is not owned by the city may elect to give their water meter(s) to the city. The city will then be responsible for the maintenance of such water meter(s). Any property owner who elects to retain ownership of their existing water meter shall maintain it consistent with the requirements of this Code of Ordinances and any rules, regulations, or other direction provided pursuant thereto. The supply of water through each separate water service line shall be recorded by one (1) water meter only, for which only one (1) account will be maintained by the city. If additional or auxiliary water meters are desired for recording the subdivision of a water supply, they must be furnished and set by the property owner or consumer at their expense, and all responsibility for reading and maintaining such water meter(s) shall be assumed by the property owner or customer.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Transfer of title
children.text:
(a) Any owner of a water meter described in section 509.800 may make, execute and deliver to the city, through the director, a statement in writing upon a form to be prepared by the director, transferring title of said water meter to the city. From and after the date of the transfer of the title of said water meter to the city, the city will be the exclusive owner of said water meter.

(b) From and after the date of the transfer of the water meter, the city will, at its own expense, keep said water meter in good and efficient operating condition and will, at its sole expense, make all necessary repairs and adjustments in said water meter, except such repairs as are made necessary by willful damage or negligence of the user or owner. Should any such water meter become so damaged or out of condition that it may not be economically repaired, the city, at its sole expense, will replace such water meter.

(c) In all instances where the ownership of a water meter is not transferred to the city, the cost of removal, repair, or replacement of such water meter will be at the expense of the owner of the premises.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water meter placement
children.text:
The director shall have water meters placed, at city expense, on all premises where deemed necessary. Failure of a bill payer to allow a water meter or water meters to be placed on the premises when notified to do so shall be cause for the water to be shut off and not turned on again until such water meter(s) shall be placed as required. Water meter placement shall include any associated water meter reading device and ancillary equipment as required by the division.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Manner of setting
children.text:
Water meter installations shall be made in such a manner that the water meter, couplings and valves will not be subjected to immersion by ordinary back flooding, house drainage over basement floors, or seepage into water meter pit maintenance holes. Each water meter shall have a shut off valve before the inlet and a shut off valve at the outlet, all in accordance with division requirements.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 11, 2-27-25)

children.title: Water meter setting devices
children.text:
Materials for setting water meters up to and including two (2) inch shall be of copper tubing or brass pipe, and brass fittings from the terminus of the water service line, up to and including the house side valve, and shall be subject to the approval of the city.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Location of; specifications for installations
children.text:
(a) Water meters shall be located and installed as follows:

(1) All water meters shall be set at the point the water service line enters the building. No plumbing connections shall be made prior to the meter. Water meters shall be set in such a manner as to be easily accessible for servicing, removal, and resetting. No water service line within a building ahead of a water meter shall be concealed, except it may be run beneath the lowest floor in the building in accordance with the applicable building code. If the water service line is run beneath the floor, the meter shall be set at the location where the line emerges from the floor.

(2) Meter set materials and configuration shall be according to the city standards.

(3) Couplings and valves shall not be subjected to immersion by ordinary back flooding of the building drainage.

(b) Whenever a condition exists that impedes the servicing, removal, or setting of a water meter, the person(s) whose name(s) appear(s) on the current billing records shall be mailed a notice to correct such conditions. Unless the condition is corrected within fifteen (15) days, the city may shut off the water and the water may remain shut off until the condition is corrected, and all fees and costs are paid.

(c) Whenever a water service line to a building is replaced, the water meter shall be installed in accordance with the provisions of this article.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Fire service assembly water meters
children.text:
Fire service assembly water meters registering water consumption for a combined domestic general supply and fire line, where permitted by the director, will be installed, owned, and maintained by the owner of the premises.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Testing
children.text:
Any person desiring to have their water meter tested by the division may have such test made upon paying to the city finance officer an amount to cover removing, transporting, testing, and replacement of the water meter, plus an amount for sewer and water service provided while the water meter was absent.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water meter removal
children.text:
(a) No person shall:

(1) Connect, disconnect, take apart, or in any manner change, or permit to be changed, any water meter connected to, or used in connection with, the Minneapolis water system.

(2) Interfere with the action or regulation of any water meter connected to, or used in connection with, the Minneapolis water system.

(b) Water meters connected to the Minneapolis water system shall be removed only by an employee of the division, or when authorized by the director. When a water meter is removed for such reason, it shall be reset, or a spacer pipe shall be inserted.

(c) When disconnection of the water meter reading device is required, the division shall be notified immediately. Reconnection of the cable shall be performed by a designee of the director.

(d) Violation of this section shall subject the property owner to a penalty which shall be set by city council resolution. Upon finding a violation of this section, the director may also shut off water service either by closing the water service shutoff valve or by closing the water service tap at the water main if the water service shutoff is inoperable. Should water service be shut off, reestablishment may not be made until:

(1) All outstanding bills for utility services are paid in full;

(2) All charges for water shut off are paid, including penalties and fees, if applicable;

(3) All costs for repair or replacement of the damaged water meter are paid.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 12, 2-27-25)

children.title: Outdoor water meter vaults
children.text:
(a) The use of a water meter vault (for water meter installation outside of a building) will only be allowed with written permission of the division as documented in the division's comments in the city's site plan review. If the construction is not required to go through the city's site plan review process or if the site plan review application may be reviewed administratively, a water meter vault will only be allowed by written permission of the director. Where allowed, the water meter vault shall be constructed in a location approved by the division utilizing materials and a design that meets the requirements of city standards. A water meter reading device approved by the division shall be required and installed on all new water meters.

(b) The property owner shall maintain the condition of and accessibility to the vault, including the removal of snow and ice as necessary, to allow the water meter to be serviced or read. The water meter shall not be submerged, and the water meter vault shall be waterproofed. If necessary, a sump pump system shall be installed to keep the vault interior dry. After proper notice, the division may shut off water service if the property owner fails to comply with the requirements of this section.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Damaged water meters and water meter reading devices
children.text:
(a) No person shall disconnect the cable connecting the water meter to the water meter reading device, unless authorized by the division.

(b) If water meters, water meter reading devices, water metering components, or connecting cable are lost, stolen, or damaged, either through neglect or carelessness of the customer, the cost of repairs, or replacement if the equipment is beyond repair, shall be paid for by the property owner.

(c) Any property owner or customer shall notify the division within one (1) business day of the discovery of any breakage, stoppage, or other irregularity in their water meter, water meter setting, or water meter reading device.

(d) Failure to comply with this ordinance may result in an administrative fee and penalty.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water meter obstruction prohibited
children.text:
No person shall cover or obstruct any water meter or water meter reading device, either permanently or temporarily. The water meters and water meter reading device must be easily accessible with adequate clearances as required in the current publication of the Supplemental Specifications for the Construction of Public Infrastructure in the City of Minneapolis.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water rates
children.text:
(a) Water rates shall be set by city council resolution to be effective beginning January of each year. Water rates may be determined by factoring water meter size, volume of water used, fixed charges, or any combination thereof, or in any other manner authorized by state law.

(b) Charges commence when the water service shutoff valve is turned on for water service. The city council shall fix the time when the charges for water shall be made payable.

(c) The city council shall also fix the water rates for customers outside of the city connected to the city water system.

(d) The city council may enter contracts or otherwise sell water in bulk to cities and other governmental units operating their own water distribution systems.

(e) The director shall have the authority to make and enforce such rules and regulations as the director shall deem appropriate to carry into effect the object and intent of this Code of Ordinances regarding the treatment, distribution, consumption, or other use of city conveyed water and to protect the property, interest, and rights of the city.

(f) The director may make any rules and regulations concerning the tapping of any water mains, branches, or making connections therewith, by any private parties or licensed plumbers as the director deems appropriate. The city council may revoke the certificate of competency card of any plumber licensed by the city who has disregarded the rules and regulations regarding the tapping of any water mains, branches, or making connections therewith in accordance with Code of Ordinances Title 13, Chapter 278, section 278.510, Denial, revocation, suspension, or cancellation of certificate of competency.

(g) The owner of private property, as well as the lessee or occupant of the premises, which has a water service line connected to the city water system shall be liable for the water from the city used upon the premises. The division may shut off the water to any premises where rates are payable and remain unpaid, and the city may recover the rates for all water supplied to a property in an action against such property owner, lessee, occupant, or against any or all of them.

(h) The city engineer shall have the authority to make and enforce such rules and regulations as they deem appropriate to carry into effect the object and intent of this Code of Ordinances regarding the treatment, distribution, consumption, or other use of city conveyed water and to protect the property, interest, and rights of the city.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 13, 2-27-25)

children.title: Net current charges and late charges
children.text:
A utility bill charge that is not paid by the due date displayed on the bill, which is twenty-one (21) days from the bill invoice date, shall be considered late. A five (5) per cent late charge shall be added to the net current charges of the bill at the expiration of the due date. The added late charge will appear on the next bill. After the twenty-one (21) day period, the city finance officer may waive the late charges if the current charges are paid in full, and upon satisfactory evidence the delay in payment was due to circumstances over which the customer had no control.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Rates and special charges when not otherwise provided
children.text:
Rates and special charges not otherwise provided will be determined by the director.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Unmetered water
children.text:
Water usage for certain authorized purposes may be charged a fixed rate as well as a volumetric rate per one hundred (100) cubic feet at a quantity estimated by the director.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Charges when water meter not owned by city
children.text:
The city shall charge for inspection and repairs plus an additional ten (10) per cent of the total of all such items, which shall be an overhead charge on all water meters not owned by the city. Inspections and repair costs shall include all parts plus the cost of labor at the currently hourly rate and the cost of transportation, if any.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Charges
children.text:
The director shall establish a schedule of charges and procedures for services provided which shall reasonably relate to the cost of the service and the materials required.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Shut off for public interest, misuse, waste, or violation
children.text:
Any violation of Chapter 509 may cause water to be shut off. Water may also be shut off if the director determines the use, misuse, or waste of water adversely affects the health, safety, or welfare of the public. No one shall turn water on or shut it off without authority from the director. Whenever water is found on without authority, it may be immediately shut off without further notice.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Permits required to tap water mains for fire protection
children.text:
No person shall tap the city water mains for fire protection without first having obtained a written permit to do the same from the director, or their designee, who may grant permits for tapping the city water mains and connecting fire protection water pipes with a water meter, detector, or a check valve/water meter combination. These shall be used only for fire protection in case of fire.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Fire protection water pipes without a water meter
children.text:
(a) No water shall be drawn from fire service water lines for any purpose except for:

(1) Fire extinguishment; and

(2) Proper testing of the fire protection system in accordance with reasonable professional procedures.

Any use of water other than for the purposes listed above shall be paid for by the property owner at regular rates based upon the division's reasonable estimate of the volume used. Violation of this section shall subject the property owner to a penalty which shall be set by city council resolution.

(b) No person shall tap or allow another person to tap any fire service water line for any purpose other than fire protection. Any illegal tap that is found shall be disconnected immediately at the property owner's expense. Violation of this section shall subject the property owner to a penalty which shall be set by city council resolution.

(c) All valves connected to fire protection water pipes having no water meter connected thereto shall be sealed by the city at the expense of the property owner. In case of a fire, the division shall be notified of the fire and the breaking of the seal by the property owner, tenant, or occupant of the premises within twenty-four (24) hours of breaking such seal. A person shall be subject to, and shall pay a penalty which shall be set by city council resolution if there is a:

(1) Use of water from a connection that has been made for fire purposes only for any purpose other than fighting a fire, or who shall break the seal of any valve connected with any fire protection water pipes, and shall fail to notify the division of same within twenty-four (24) hours, as required above; or

(2) Tap or connect to any fire protection water pipes, without a permit.

(d) Any person subject to a penalty for a violation of the requirements of this section has a right to make an administrative appeal using the procedures and deadlines established in Sections 505.120 and 505.130 of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 14, 2-27-25)

children.title: Fire line rates
children.text:
All rates for unmetered fire standpipes, supply pipes, and automatic sprinkler pipes or for those with detector meters or direct meters, shall be set by city council resolution annually.

When the seal of any of the valves connecting with such fire protection water pipes shall be broken, it shall be resealed by authority of the director. All connections for fire systems must have a post indicator valve installed at the curb, if ordered by the director.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Illegal use of hydrant
children.text:
(a) Except for use by personnel of the fire department and the public works department, hydrants may only be used pursuant to the authority of a permit issued by the division. All water taken from a hydrant must be metered. Any other person found using water from a hydrant, other than pursuant to the authority of a permit issued by the division, shall be subject to the following:

(1) A penalty which shall be set by city council resolution, for every hydrant opened without the proper authority; and

(2) Liability for the cost of the water taken from the hydrant at regular rates, based upon a reasonable estimate by the division.

(b) The division will take custody of all hydrant nozzle adaptors and appurtenances found attached to Minneapolis hydrants or adjacent thereto in violation of this Code of Ordinances. Such adaptors and appurtenances shall become the property of the City of Minneapolis.

(c) Any person who objects to a determination made pursuant to this section may make an administrative appeal using the procedures and deadlines established in Sections 505.120 and 505.130 of this title.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 15, 2-27-25)

children.title: Control and protection of supply is required
children.text:
Every building intended for human occupancy or use shall be provided with an ample supply of potable water. All plumbing systems, water sources, and distribution systems shall be constructed and maintained to prevent contamination, pollution, or cross-connections with non-potable water sources as required by the Minnesota Plumbing Code, Minnesota Department of Health standards, and the Division's Cross-Connection Control Program. Any backflow prevention devices or other protective measures required by these authorities must be installed and maintained in good working order to protect the public water supply from contamination.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 16, 2-27-25)

children.title: Inspection of supply
children.text:
The city shall inspect the installation of, extension to, or any alterations in, all water service lines, water supply, or water distribution piping system in all buildings, structures, and premises in the city, or outside the city if the property is connected to the City of Minneapolis water supply system. Authorized city personnel shall have free entry and access to any building, structure, or premises, or part thereof, whether complete or in the process of erection, for the purpose of determining compliance with the provisions of this article. The city may shut off the water supply to any property where the property owner has refused to give access to the affected property.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Connection to another water system
children.text:
No connections shall be permitted between the city water supply and any other system that draws water from a different source where there is a risk that the city water supply could be contaminated by the other source. All properties that have State-approved and inspected gray water systems or private wells must have backflow prevention measures that are properly installed and maintained. These measures must ensure there is no risk of backflow into the city water system. Any fire protection system supplied with water from the city water supply shall be supplied exclusively with the city's water supply. No connection shall be made at any time between the fire service water line and the domestic water service line to the premises unless all connections have been approved by the division.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 17, 2-27-25)

children.title: Separation from connected system
children.text:
Wherever cross-connection between the city water supply and any other water system is found to exist, the property owner and the customer shall be notified; and unless the property owner removes or controls the cross-connection as directed, the water shall be discontinued at the connection to the water main, and it will remain discontinued until the cross- connection is removed or controlled. All costs related to discontinuing the water service and removing or controlling the cross-connection will be the responsibility of the property owner. The director may require other immediate action as necessary to protect the public health.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 18, 2-27-25)

children.title: Cross-connections and backflow prevention in potable water system
children.text:
(a) If an on-premises survey is necessary to evaluate cross-connection hazards, the director shall provide written notice to the customer and require the survey to be completed within sixty (60) days. The customer may have the division conduct the survey at no cost or may choose to hire and pay an independent company who utilizes currently accredited ASSE 5120 backflow prevention surveyors.

(b) Both the director and the customer shall be notified of the finding of any on premises cross connection or backflow prevention surveys, including the degree of hazard and the corrective actions to be taken. If there is imminent danger, the cross-connection hazard shall be addressed immediately, and the water service may be shut off until the hazard is eliminated. Other corrective actions shall be taken within sixty (60) days of the survey and reported to the division when complete.

(c) If backflow prevention is required to protect the public water system, the director shall notify the customer and specify the requirements. The customer shall immediately install such backflow prevention. The cost of installing, testing, repairing, and maintaining the backflow assembly shall be the responsibility of the customer and in accordance with Chapter 91 and the current utility rates set by City Council resolution.

(d) If the required backflow prevention is not installed, tested, maintained, and repaired, or if the required backflow prevention is removed or bypassed, penalties may be applied in accordance with the current utility rates set by city council resolution. Noncompliance may result in a water service shut off. Shut off and turn on fees will be charged. Service will not be turned on again until defects are corrected. All violations shall be reported to the Director of Regulatory Services for the purpose of conformance with Chapter 244 of this Code of Ordinances.

(e) Maintenance and repair work on backflow devices shall be performed by a licensed master plumber, or by a licensed journeyman plumber, under the supervision of a master plumber (Minn. Stat. § 326B.46), who is also a certified backflow prevention assembly tester/rebuilder.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 19, 2-27-25)

children.title: Compliance with plumbing code
children.text:
All materials and methods of installation for the water supply system shall be made in accordance with the provision of the Minnesota Plumbing Code and City of Minneapolis regulatory requirements.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Water use limited during emergency period
children.text:
During any period of emergency caused by shortage of water supply or lowering of water pressure in the water mains of the city, no person shall draw or use water from the city water mains or the city water distribution system other than as permitted by the declaration of emergency.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22)

children.title: Declaration of emergency
Violation of declaration of emergency
children.text:
A warning letter will be issued to the bill payor for the first violation of the declaration of emergency. Each subsequent violation will result in a penalty in accordance with the current schedule of utility rates as set by City Council resolution. Penalties will be added to the water bill. Willful and excessive violations, as determined by the director, will result in the water supply to the premises being shut off. A notice of intent to shut off water service posted in a conspicuous place on or near the front entrance of the premises for twenty-four (24) hours shall be considered sufficient notice prior to shutting off the water supply. When the water has been shut off for violation of the declaration of emergency, it may not be turned on again until payment is received for any charges connected with shutting the water off and turning it back on. These charges may include, but are not limited to, the expenses for any repairs necessary to operate the water service shutoff valve, charges for utility services, administrative fees, and fines that are due.

(Ord. No. 2022-024, § 4, 5-26-22; Ord. No. 2025-014, § 20, 2-27-25)

children.heading: CHAPTER 510.
children.title: STORMWATER MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND OPERATION OF A STORMWATER UTILITY
Definitions
children.text:
In addition to the words, terms and phrases elsewhere defined in this chapter, the following words, terms and phrases as used in this chapter shall have the following meanings:

Bonds means revenue or general obligation bonds, notes, loans or other debt obligations heretofore or hereafter issued to finance the costs of improvements and/or operations and maintenance.

Building permit means a permit issued by the director of inspections that permits construction of a structure.

City means City of Minneapolis, Minnesota.

City council means governing body of the city.

City engineer means the city engineer of the City of Minneapolis and his/her duly authorized designee.

Costs of capital improvements means costs incurred in providing capital improvements to the stormwater management system or any portion thereof including, without limitation, the cost of alteration, enlargement, extension, improvement, construction, reconstruction, testing and development of the stormwater management system; insurance premiums for insurance taken out and maintained during construction, professional services and studies connected thereto; principal and interest on bonds heretofore or hereafter issued, acquisition of real and personal property by purchase, lease, donation, condemnation or otherwise for the stormwater management system or for its protection; and costs associated with purchasing equipment, computers, furniture, etc., that are necessary for the operation of the system or the utility.

Debt service means an amount equal to the sum of (i) all interest payable on bonds during a fiscal year, plus (ii) any principal installments payable on the bonds during that fiscal year.

Developed property means real property, other than undisturbed property; provided that, property used for agricultural uses, upon which no dwelling unit is located, shall not constitute developed property for purposes of this chapter.

Director means the department head and has the ultimate responsibility and authority for the public works department.

Dwelling unit means one (1) or more rooms, designed, occupied or intended for occupancy as a separate living quarter, with a single complete kitchen facility, sleeping area and bathroom provided within the unit for the exclusive use of a single household.

Equivalent stormwater unit (ESU) means a unit of measure that is equal to the average impervious area of single-family residential developed property that falls within the medium class, with a single-family detached dwelling unit located thereon and within the city's limits, as established by city council resolution or ordinance, as provided for herein.

Equivalent stormwater unit rate or ESU rate means the storm sewer charge imposed on single-family residential developed property within the medium class, as established by city council resolution or ordinance, as provided herein.

Exempt property means public rights-of-way, public trails, public streets, public alleys, public sidewalks, railroad tracks that are not in railroad yards, and also means public lands and/or easements upon which the stormwater management system is constructed and/or located.

Fiscal year means a twelve-month period commencing on the first day of January of any year or such other twelve-month period adopted as the fiscal year of the city.

Impervious area means the number of square feet of hard surface areas that either prevent or retard the entry of water into the soil matrix, as it entered under natural conditions as undisturbed property, and/or cause water to run off the surface in greater quantities or at an increased rate of flow from that present under natural conditions as undisturbed property, including, but not limited to, roofs, roof extensions, driveways, pavement and athletic courts.

Other residential developed property means developed property upon which two (2) or more family and/or multi-family dwellings are located.

Non-residential developed property means developed property other than single residential developed property and other residential developed property.

Operating budget means the annual stormwater utility operating budget adopted by the city for the succeeding fiscal year.

Operations and maintenance means, without limitation, the current expenses, paid or secured, of operation, maintenance, repair and minor replacement of the system, as calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice. This shall include, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, cost of studies related to the operation of the system; costs of the study performed heretofore in relation to establishing storm sewer charges for the stormwater utility and other start up costs of the stormwater utility; costs related to the national pollutant discharge elimination system permit study, application, negotiation and implementation, including public education and outreach, as mandated by federal and state laws and regulations and the costs of obtaining and complying with all other permits required by law, insurance premiums, administrative expenses, equipment costs, including professional services, labor costs and the cost of materials and supplies used for current operations.

Revenues means all rates, fees, assessments, rentals or other charges or other income received by the stormwater utility in connection with the management and operation of the system, including amounts received from the investment or deposit of monies in any fund or account, as calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting practices.

Runoff coefficients means those numbers approved by the city council that are used to estimate the impervious area for each non-single family classified property. A list of the coefficients used for the city is found in Table 1 that is incorporated herein.

Single-family residential developed property means developed property upon which single-family detached dwellings are located.

Stormwater charge means a charge authorized by this chapter, Minnesota Statutes 2004, Section 444.075, and other applicable law, and further as set forth in resolution or ordinance heretofore or hereafter adopted or hereafter amended by the city council, which is established to pay operation and maintenance, costs of capital improvements, debt service associated with the stormwater management system and other costs included in the operating budget.

Stormwater management system, sewer system or system means storm sewers that exist at the time the ordinance codified in this chapter is adopted or that are hereafter established and all appurtenances necessary in the maintaining and operating of the same, including, but not limited to pumping stations; enclosed storm sewers; outfall sewers; surface drains; street, curb and alley improvements associated with storm or surface water improvements; natural and manmade wetlands; channels; ditches; rivers; streams; wet and dry bottom basins; pocket ponds; multiple pond systems; settling basins; infiltration trenches or basins; filter systems; bioretention areas; dry or wet swales; grass channels; roof top detention; skimming devices; grit chambers and other flood control facilities; and works for the collection, transportation, conveyance, pumping, treatment, controlling, storing, managing, and disposing storm or surface water or pollutants originating from or carried by storm or surface water.

Stormwater utility or utility means the utility created by this chapter to operate, maintain and improve the stormwater management system and for all other purposes set forth in this chapter.

Undisturbed property means real property that has not been altered from its natural condition in a manner that disturbed or altered the topography or soils on the property to the degree that the entrance of water into the soil matrix is prevented or retarded.

Vacant land means real property upon which there is no structure, as shown in the records of the city assessor's office, which is not designed for or regularly used for commercial residential purposes, and which is not used in connection with another piece of property. Vacant land includes undisturbed property and land with no building used as a community garden.

(2004-Or-132, § 1, 11-5-04; Ord. No. 2017-068, §§ 9, 10, 11-3-17)

children.title: Creation of stormwater utility
children.text:
Pursuant to the provisions of Minnesota Statutes 2004, Section 444.075, the city's general home rule powers, its nuisance powers, police powers and all other authorized powers, the city council does establish a stormwater utility and stormwater management system and declares its intention to operate, construct, maintain, repair and replace the stormwater management system and operate the stormwater utility.

(2004-Or-132, § 1, 11-5-04)

children.title: Findings and determinations
children.text:
The city finds that the elements of the stormwater management system that provides for the collection, conveyance, detention/retention, treatment and release of stormwater, the reduction of hazard to property and life resulting from stormwater runoff, improvement in general health and welfare through reduction of undesirable stormwater conditions and improvement to the water quality in the storm and surface water system and its receiving waters are of benefit and provide services to all property within the city. It is further found, determined and declared that this chapter is in furtherance of and implements the goals and strategies of the local surface water management plan, the annual Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) report and the city's National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit.

(2004-Or-132, § 1, 11-5-04)

children.title: Administration
children.text:
The stormwater utility, under the supervision of the director, shall have the power to:

(1) Administer the acquisition, design, construction, maintenance, operation, extension and replacement of the stormwater management system, including real and personal property that is or will become a part of or protect the system.

(2) Prepare regulations, as needed, to implement this chapter, and forward those regulations to the city council for consideration and adoption, and adopt those procedures, as are desirable, to implement adopted regulations or to carry out other responsibilities of the utility.

(3) Administer and enforce this chapter and all regulations, guidelines and procedures adopted relating to the design, construction, maintenance, operation and alteration of the stormwater management system, including, but not limited to, the flow rate, volume, quality and/or velocity of the stormwater conveyed thereby.

a. Advise the city council on matters relating to the stormwater management system.

b. Develop and review plans concerning creation, design, construction, extension and replacement of the system and make recommendations to the city council related thereto.

c. Inspect private systems, as necessary, to determine the compliance of those systems with this chapter and any regulations adopted pursuant hereto.

d.
