Storing of any kind of material, goods, refuse, etc., and the hanging and drying of clothes, etc., is not permitted on land. Refuse must be deposited only in places designated for that purpose. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1035.050)

children.heading: PB4-119.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Section 2 of Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 86-102, adopted July 2, 1986, deleted § PB4-119 in its entirety. Prior to repeal, said section pertained to passenger launches and excursion boats, and was derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1035.060.

children.heading: PB4-120.
children.title: Subject to ordinances governing use of parks; obedience to superintendent
children.text: Boats and their inhabitants at landings come under all other ordinances governing the use of parks. All owners, renters or inhabitants of such boats must comply with the orders of the superintendent or his authorized agents. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1035.070)

children.heading: Chapter 5
children.title: BUSES
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (5) ---

Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, adopted May 16, 2007, amended Ch. 5, in its entirety, to read as herein set out in §§ PB5-1—PB5-15. Prior to inclusion of said ordinance, Ch. 5 pertained to similar subject matter. See also the Park Board Ordinances Code Comparative Table.

children.heading: PB5-1.
children.title: Policy Statement
children.text:
The parkways and park roads under the jurisdiction of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board (MPRB) were not designed or constructed to accommodate use by buses and commercial vehicles. The MPRB is not obligated to provide commercial bus transportation routes on its parkways and park roads. The commercial use of parkways and park roads conflicts with public access and recreational use of the park system. Non-park roads provide sufficient access to accommodate commercial transportation needs within the City of Minneapolis. Restricted commercial use of parkways and park roads is authorized only by permit issued by the MPRB superintendent. Public transit system use is governed by this ordinance.

The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board's facilities have gained national and international fame for their history, beauty, and innovation. As a result of this notoriety, the entire park system is a desired destination for commercial tourism. The MPRB shall strive to balance the interests of commercial tourism with the demand for access to its parks through the permitting process provided under this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-2.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this chapter the following terms shall mean:

Public Transit System: A publicly owned combination of property, structures, improvements, equipment, plants, parking or other facilities, and rights, or any thereof, used or useful for the purposes of public transit.

Public Bus Transportation: Any public transit system operating buses for the benefit of the general public.

Private Bus, Truck, Limousine or Trolley Transportation: Any private person or company controlling, operating, or managing any bus, truck, limousine or trolley for transporting persons.

Motor Vehicle: Every self propelled device used to transport person(s) or property upon any highway, street, parkway, or road. This definition does not include devices used exclusively on stationary rails or tracks, any electronic personal assistance mobility device as defined in Minn. Stat. § 169.01 Subd. 90, nor a device moved solely by human power.

Parkway or Park Road: That portion of a street or highway located within or adjacent to the city that is under the jurisdiction of the MPRB.

Commercial Vehicle: A bus, truck, limousine, trolley or other vehicle as defined within this section.

Buses: Every motor vehicle designed for carrying more than 15 passengers including the driver and used for the transportation of persons.

Trucks: Any of various heavy motor vehicles with a gross vehicle weight of more than 12,000 pounds, designed for carrying or pulling loads of a one ton capacity or more.

Limousines: A large commercial automobile weighing more than 7,000 pounds with a separation by window or screen between chauffer and passenger(s).

Trolleys: A motor vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of less than 8,000 pounds designed for carrying more than 15 passengers including the driver and used for the transportation of persons.

Permit: The documented and displayed authorization by the MPRB superintendent for use of specific parkways and/or park roads by private bus transportation, its subcontractors, or assigns at designated times and/or dates.

MPRB Superintendent: The MPRB appointed chief executive with the authority to oversee and direct the operations and management of the MPRB staff, properties, and programs. The MPRB superintendent is the MPRB designated authority to grant permits and enforce the provisions of this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-3.
children.title: Displayed Permit Required
children.text: Operation of any vehicle by commercial transportation company upon any parkways and/or park roads without a displayed permit issued by the MPRB superintendent is strictly prohibited. Every permit issued by the MPRB superintendent for operation of a commercial vehicle shall be displayed facing outwards from a vehicle window so as to be readily identified as a permitted user by the staff of the MPRB including Minneapolis Park Police authorized to enforce this ordinance. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-4.
children.title: Application For Permit
children.text:
All private bus, truck, limousine or trolley transportation shall apply to the MPRB in writing for a permit to operate on parkways and/or park roads. Each application shall include:

(1) Name, address, and phone number of the applicant including the names, addresses, and phone numbers of owners, if a corporation,

(2) The names, addresses, and phone numbers of any subcontracting parties that may operate under the permit,

(3) Minnesota drivers license information of all drivers who will operate under the permit,

(4) The motor vehicle insurance information for all buses that will operate under the permit,

(5) A description of the route(s), schedule(s), and passenger fares including any contractual and/or sub-contractual arrangements providing revenue to the applicant,

(6) Descriptions of all the vehicles that will operate under the permit including weight, size of tires, outside dimensions, seating capacity, and vehicle license numbers.

(7) The signature(s) of the applicant(s) swearing to the truth and accuracy of the information and representations in the application,

(8) Copies of all current safety certifications of all buses that will operate under the permit, and

(9) Any other information that the staff of the MPRB may request before the issuance of permit.

Upon review of the application, the MPRB superintendent shall determine whether the application is accurate and truthful, whether the applied for use of the parkways and/or park roads interferes with public access to park land or facilities, and/or whether applied for use unduly burdens park resources. Based on these determinations, the MPRB superintendent shall approve or reject the application. Notice of approval or rejection of the application shall be provided to the applicant within 30 days of the date of application. The applicant may appeal the rejection of the application to the MPRB at a regularly scheduled park board meeting. A vote of six members of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board is necessary to - grant approval to the applicant for a permit. A permit shall then be issued to the applicant in accordance to the provisions set forth in PB5-6 of this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-5.
children.title: Size and Weight of Commercial Vehicles
children.text: The type, dimensions and weight of any vehicle operating on any parkways and park roads shall, so far as applicable, comply with the provisions of Minn. Stat. § 169, provided, however, that nothing herein nor in said Minn. Stat. § 169, shall limit the authority of the MPRB to specify the type, dimensions and weight of any motor vehicle which may be used on any parkway or park road or to prohibit the operation of any motor vehicle which may in the opinion of the MPRB occasion unusual wear and tear to the parkways and park roads, and/or may interfere with the quiet, orderly and suitable use and enjoyment of such parkways and park roads by the public. The MPRB has plenary power to impose limitations and conditions upon the use of the parkways and park roads by motor vehicles including private bus, truck, limousine or trolley transportation. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-6.
children.title: Issuance of Permit
children.text: Private Bus, Truck, Limousine, or Trolley Transportation shall apply to the MPRB for a permit to use parkways and/or park roads. If an application is approved, the applicant will be issued a permit upon payment of the required fee and proof of the MPRB as an additional insured under the applicant's motor vehicle insurance policy for the permitted time to the MPRB. Fee schedules shall be set by the MPRB superintendent. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-7.
children.title: Permits Subject to Existing Ordinances and Imposed Conditions
children.text: Any permit granted under this chapter shall be subject to all laws and ordinances and to any special conditions, regulations or limitations imposed by the MPRB in the issuance of or subsequent to the issuance of the granted permit. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-8.
children.title: No Vested Rights Intended
children.text: The MPRB reserves the right to cancel any permit with or without cause. The MPRB shall give notice to the permit holder if a permit is cancelled. Proper notice shall include either verbal or written communication of cancellation to the permit holder. Upon receipt of notice, the permit is immediately revoked and cancelled. If a permit is cancelled without cause, the former permit holder may request, in writing, a partial refund of the permit fee. If refunded, the permit fee refund shall be that part of the permit fee reasonably attributable to the cancelled time on the permit. All rights to use said parkways and park roads terminate when the authorized permitted time expires. No private bus, truck, limousine, or trolley transportation person or company, by reason of the issuance of any permit, shall acquire any franchise or vested right to future use of parkways or park roads, or the issuance of future permits for such use. Nothing in this chapter shall limit the MPRB from granting or prohibiting any commercial use of a motor vehicle on the parkways or park roads. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-9.
children.title: Preservation of Statutory Rights
children.text: All rights and privileges reserved to local municipalities by Minn. Stat. § 471, Minn. Stat. § 415, Minn. Stat. § 169, and Minn. Stat. § 44, shall in no way be waived by any of the provisions of this chapter; nor does the MPRB waive any rights given it by the statutes of the State of Minnesota or the Charter of the city. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-10.
children.title: Indemnification of Board
children.text: Any private bus, truck, limousine or trolley transportation person or company that is granted a permit shall protect, indemnify, and hold harmless the MPRB against any claim, loss, cost, expense or damage of any kind whatsoever which may result, directly or indirectly, from the permitted use on any parkway or park road or any related activity. This indemnification is in addition to the insurance coverage required by the MPRB in PB5-6 of this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB5-11.
children.title: Acceptance of Chapter
children.text: All permits issued under this chapter shall be filed by the MPRB secretary. Any holder of a permit under this chapter acknowledges and submits to the all the terms set forth in this chapter by acceptance of said permit. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-12.
children.title: Authorization by Board
children.text: The board designates the MPRB superintendent as its authority under this ordinance to grant or reject permits and enforce the provisions of this chapter This chapter shall not be repealed or amended except by a vote of at least six (6) members of the board and may be amended or repealed only at a regular meeting subsequent to a regular meeting at which the amendment or repeal is proposed. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-13.
children.title: Revocation for Violations
children.text: Any violation of a permit holder under this chapter shall revoke the permit, without requirement of notice, and does not preclude any other additional penalties provided under law. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-14.
children.title: Public Bus Transportation
children.text: Public Transit Systems may apply to the MPRB for a permit to operate on parkways and park roads if no other suitable non-park roads are available for essential public bus routes. The written application to the MPRB shall set forth the required necessity for the use of park roads by providing an explanation of the insufficiency of non-park roads for the essential public bus routes. The MPRB may, by a two-thirds majority, grant a permit to a Public Transit System if the use of the park roads is the only reasonable alternative for the necessary and essential use by the Public Transit System, and the use does not interfere with the public access to the parks or overburden park resources. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: PB5-15.
children.title: Violations
children.text: Any violation of a provision of this chapter is an administrative offense and subject to any penalties or fines established in accordance with Chapter 14 of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Code of Ordinances. (Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-102, § 1, 5-16-07)

children.heading: Chapter 6
children.title: CONTRACTS FOR IMPROVEMENTS
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (6) ---

Editor's note— Section 1 of Park Board Ord. No. 84-102, adopted July 11, 1984, repealed §§ PB6-1—PB6-4, as derived from Code 1960, as amended, §§ 1023.010—1023.030 and from Park Board Ord. No. 74-103, § 1, adopted June 5, 1974. Section 2 of 84-102 enacted a new Ch. 6.

children.heading: PB6-1.
children.title: Prevailing wage required
children.text: All invitations or requests for proposals and all contracts entered into where, pursuant to ordinance or statute, a formal written contract or performance bond is required to which the park and recreation board is a party, for the construction, alteration and/or repair of park buildings, park lands or parkways and which requires or involves the employment of mechanics and/or laborers shall contain a provision stating that all federal labor standards and prevailing wage provisions applicable to federal contracts in accordance with the federal Davis Bacon and related acts are applicable to this contract as if fully set forth herein and all contractors and subcontractors shall fully comply with such provisions regardless of any contractual relationship which may be alleged to exist between the contractor or subcontractor and their respective employees. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 84-102, § 2, 7-11-84)

children.heading: PB6-2.
children.title: Preaward conference
children.text: Promptly after bid opening and prior to contract award the apparent successful bidder shall submit to the appropriate contract monitoring officer a list of all anticipated subcontractors and the various classes of laborers and mechanics to be employed on the contract work, together with a schedule of wage rates and fringe benefits to be paid to such employees. Such wage rates shall be at least the prevailing rates as required by section PB6-1. Failure to comply with this provision shall be grounds for rejecting the bid. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 84-102, § 2 7-11-84)

children.heading: PB6-3.
children.title: Submission of statements and payroll records
children.text: Upon the request of the appropriate contract monitoring officer, each contractor or subcontractor engaged in work under the contract shall furnish to the appropriate contract monitoring officer within five (5) working days, a copy of payrolls showing wages paid, and a wage compliance statement with respect to wages paid each of its mechanics and laborers employed on the site of the contract work. In the event the contractor fails to supply such statements or if such statements disclose that the required prevailing wage is not being paid, the contract monitoring officer shall promptly notify the city finance officer who shall forthwith withhold payments to the contractor for such periods of noncompliance. During the course of and upon completion of the contract work, the contract monitoring officer shall have the right to require an appropriate audit of contractor's books to determine compliance or noncompliance with the provisions of this chapter. Each contractor and subcontractor shall retain the relevant weekly payrolls for a period of not less than one year after the completion of the work. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 84-102, § 2, 7-11-84)

children.heading: PB6-4.
children.title: Failure to pay prevailing wage
children.text: Every invitation or request for proposals and contracts within the scope of section PB6-1 shall contain the further provision that in the event it is found by the park and recreation board that any laborer, mechanic or employee employed by the contractor or any subcontractor directly on the site of the work covered by the contract has been, or is being, paid a rate of wages and fringe benefits or their cash equivalent less than rates required by this chapter and by the contract, the contract monitoring officer may place the contractor on a suspended or disbarment list and by written notice to the contractor, terminate the right to proceed with the work or such part of the work as to which there has been a failure to pay said required wages and to prosecute the work to completion by contract or otherwise, and the contractor and sureties shall be liable to the park and recreation board for damages sustained thereby. The park and recreation board reserves the right to withhold contract payments to the extent of the underpayment of required wages. Any contractor objecting to being placed on a suspended or disbarment list by the contract monitoring officer shall have the right to appeal in writing to the board of park and recreation commissioners for review of the contract monitoring officer's actions. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 84-102, § 2, 7-11-84)

children.heading: PB6-5.
children.title: Failure to comply bars future contracts
children.text: The contract monitoring officer shall prepare and maintain a list of all persons or firms who are in default under any of the provisions of this chapter in regard to obligations to their employees, and no further contracts shall be awarded or entered into with such persons or firms for so long as they are in default. A current copy of such list shall be provided to the office of the city finance officer and the city purchasing agent. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 84-102, § 2, 7-11-84)

children.heading: Chapter 6.5
children.title: ENFORCEMENT
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (7) ---

Cross reference— General conduct, PB2-1 et seq.

children.heading: PB6.5-1.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this chapter the following terms shall mean:

Municipal ordinance: Any ordinance or resolution of the City of Minneapolis.

Park and recreation board ordinance: Any ordinance or resolution of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board.

Park patrol agent: Any person employed by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board whose services are utilized for purposes including, but not limited to, providing supplementary assistance at special events, traffic or crowd control, or administrative or clerical assistance to Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board police officers or perform duties, including the operation of marked vehicles, at the direction of the superintendent of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board, the captain of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board police, or their designees.

Police officer: Any person employed by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board of the City of Minneapolis who meets the definition of peace officer in Minnesota Statutes Section 624.84, subdivision 1(c).

State law: Any law of the State of Minnesota. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 87-101, § 1, 7-1-87)

children.heading: PB6.5-2.
children.title: Authorization to issue citations
children.text: Park patrol agents are authorized to issue citations for violations of state laws, municipal ordinances and Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board ordinances. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 87-101, § 1, 7-1-87)

children.heading: PB6.5-3.
children.title: Preservation of statutory and common law rights
children.text: The provisions of this ordinance [chapter] shall not limit or impair the statutory or common law right of park patrol agents to make citizen arrests or issue citations for violations of state laws, municipal ordinances and Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board ordinances. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 87-101, § 1, 7-1-87)

children.heading: PB6.5-4.
children.title: Savings clause
children.text: If any provision of this ordinance [chapter] should be adjudged void or of no effect, for any reason whatsoever, such decision shall not affect the validity of any of the other portions of the ordinance [chapter]. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 87-101, § 1, 7-1-87)

children.heading: PB7-1.
children.title: Excavations to comply with chapter
children.text: No person shall make any excavation in the surface of any park or parkway for the purpose of making sewer, water or gas connections, nor for any other purpose except in accordance with and upon compliance with this chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.010)

children.heading: PB7-2.
children.title: Application for excavation permit; deposit
children.text: Anyone desiring to make any opening or excavation in the surface of any park or parkway, for the purpose of making sewer, water or gas connections, or for any other lawful purpose, shall first apply to the secretary of the board for a permit; and in the application shall agree to comply with and perform all the conditions in the permit, and at the time of the application shall deposit in the city treasury twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for each opening in unpaved roadways and fifty dollars ($50.00) for each opening in paved roadways, as security for the performance of such conditions, and to reimburse the board for the expense of the work to be done by it, as hereinafter provided. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.020)

children.heading: PB7-3.
children.title: Excavation permit issuance; terms, signing
children.text: The secretary, upon receiving such application and the city comptroller-treasurer's [finance officer's] receipt for such deposit, shall issue a permit for the making of such opening and excavation, if the purpose thereof is lawful, in which permit it shall be specified and provided that the earth shall be replaced in the excavation, and made as firm and solid by saturating with water and by tamping as before it was removed, and that the macadam, paving or other surface shall be replaced in like manner and made as firm and in as good condition as before it was removed. Such permit shall also provide that the entire work to be done by the applicant shall be completed within a specified number of days after the date thereof. The time so to be limited shall be a reasonable time, considering the extent and character of the work, and the extent and character of the use of the park or parkway and the interruption to travel, but in no case for more than fifteen (15) days. Such permit shall be countersigned by the general superintendent of parks. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.030)

children.heading: PB7-4.
children.title: Supervision, approval of excavation work; nonconforming work
children.text: The superintendent of parks shall observe and inspect the work done during its progress and at its completion and report to the secretary if the work is done in all respects in compliance with the permit. If the terms of the permit are not fully complied with, the superintendent of parks shall refill the excavation and replace the macadam, paving or other surface in the manner provided in the permit and report the cost thereof to the secretary. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.040)

children.heading: PB7-5.
children.title: Safety measures at excavations
children.text: The applicant for an excavation permit shall cause guards to be placed and kept about such opening from the time it is commenced until it is refilled, and the surface entirely restored, and shall cause proper warning lights to be kept burning from sundown until sunrise during every night from the date of the commencement of such opening, until the surface is completely restored, and such lights shall be sufficient in number and so placed as to fully guard and protect all portions of such excavations as well as all portions of the earth or materials which may be piled and adjacent. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.050)

children.heading: PB7-6.
children.title: Excavation applicant to protect city from liability
children.text: The applicant for an excavation permit shall save the city and the park and recreation board harmless from any damage, loss or liability which may directly or indirectly result therefrom. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.050)

children.heading: PB7-7.
children.title: Permit required to move buildings
children.text: No person shall move any building or other structure along, across or upon any parkway without the permission of the park and recreation board or its proper officers. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.070)

children.heading: PB7-8.
children.title: Building materials and obstructions on parkways
children.text: No person shall encumber or obstruct or cause to be encumbered or obstructed, any parkway or part thereof, by placing therein or thereon, any building materials or any article or thing whatsoever, including waste receptacles or storage units. Provided that if any building is under construction so near to a parkway that the construction cannot well be carried on without depositing building material temporarily in the parkway, an application may be made to the park and recreation board for leave to deposit material stating the circumstances of the case, the portion of the parkway which it is desired to occupy, the kind and quantity of materials to be placed thereon, and the length of time which they shall remain, and thereupon the board may, unless in its judgment the public interest will be injured, authorize a permit to be issued for so depositing materials, and in case a permit is authorized by the board, the secretary shall issue such permit, which shall contain provisions requiring the holder to confine materials to the designated portion of the parkway, to remove the same within the time specified and to replace all turf, shrubbery and other improvements which may be injured, and leave the same in as good condition as before; to keep such material guarded during the daytime against falls and accidents, and to place red lights thereon from sunset to sunrise of each night. The person receiving the permit shall endorse thereon an agreement to comply with all the conditions of the permit, and to save the park and recreation board and the city harmless from any loss, damages or liability which may directly or indirectly result therefrom. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.080; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB7-9.
children.title: Warning lights
children.text: Any person having the use of any portion of any parkway pursuant to this chapter, shall cause proper warning lights to be placed in conspicuous places in front of and at each end of the obstruction or excavation from sunset to sunrise each night while such obstruction or excavation remains. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.090)

children.heading: PB7-10.
children.title: Railroad blocking crossings
children.text: No railway company, railroad engineer, train conductor or other person shall cause or allow any locomotive engine, car, cars or train of cars to stop in any park or obstruct any parkway or pathway for a period longer than five (5) minutes at any one time, unless such obstruction results from an accident in which case the obstruction shall be cleared as soon as is reasonably practical. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.100; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 98-102, § 1, 4-22-98)

children.heading: PB7-11.
children.title: Removal and sale of obstructions
children.text: The superintendent of parks shall, and any employee of the board may, remove or cause to be removed from any park or parkway, any obstruction, article or thing therein placed, kept or found contrary to the provisions of this chapter, at the expense of the owner, contractor or other person responsible for such obstruction, and said superintendent of parks may do every act which the chief of police of the city may do by city ordinance under similar circumstances, including the sale or other disposal of articles to be moved. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.110)

children.heading: PB7-12
children.title: Enforcement by police
children.text: Any member of the police force of the city whether appointed by the park and recreation board or otherwise, shall have power to arrest and take before the municipal court, or to imprison between the sessions of said court, any person or persons who shall be found violating any of the provisions of this chapter except PB7-8, which is enforceable as an administrative offense. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1021.120; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB7-13.
children.title: Violations
children.text: Any violation of a provision of PB7-8 of this chapter is an administrative offense and subject to any penalties or fines established in accordance with Chapter 14 of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Code of Ordinances. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: Chapter 7.5
children.title: PATHWAY USE
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (8) ---

Editor's note— With the concurrence of the city, the editor has redesignated as Ch. 7.5 material originally enacted as Ch. 11.

children.heading: PB7.5-1.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall mean:

Biker: Any person riding upright on a wheeled device propelled by human power, having two (2) tandem wheels either of which is over twenty (20) inches in diameter and including a device generally recognized as a bicycle though equipped with two (2) front or two (2) rear wheels to provide greater stability due to the physical disability of the person.

Jogger: Any person afoot and traveling at a rate of speed such that both feet are at intervals not in contact with the ground.

Pathway: That portion of a park or parkway improved, designated or ordinarily used for travel by foot and/or wheeled device.

Roller skater: Any person riding or propelling oneself by human power or gravity on wheeled devices that are worn on a person's feet or stood upon by a person. Such devices specifically include, but are not limited to, roller skates, in-line skates, roller skis and skateboards.

Walker: Any person afoot and traveling at a rate of speed such that one foot is always in contact with the ground. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 89-101, § 1, 5-3-89; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 92-102, § 1, 6-3-92)

children.heading: PB7.5-2.
children.title: Signs posted
children.text: Signs will be posted to designate each pathway in a park as restricted as a pedestrian path for use by or for use as a bicycle path by walkers, bikers and roller skaters, or both. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 89-101, § 1, 5-3-89)

children.heading: PB7.5-3.
children.title: Prohibited use
children.text: No biker shall ride a bicycle and no roller skater shall ride or propel roller skates on any designated pedestrian pathway, except where such pathway is also a designated bicycle pathway. No biker shall ride a bicycle on any pathway, whether improved or not, where the board has erected signs designating such pathway as a "No Biking" pathway. No walker shall walk and no jogger shall jog on any designated bicycle pathway, except where such pathway is also a designated pedestrian pathway. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 96-101, § 1, 4-3-96; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 96-103, § 1, 9-4-96)

children.heading: PB7.5-4.
children.title: Careless use
children.text: No person shall use pathways carelessly, recklessly, or heedlessly in disregard of the rights or the safety of others. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-5.
children.title: Duty to keep to the right
children.text: Persons using the pathways shall remain upon the right half of the pathway except when overtaking and passing another user proceeding in the same direction. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-6.
children.title: Meeting other users
children.text: Persons proceeding in opposite directions shall pass each other to the right and shall give to the other at least one-half of the pathway as nearly as possible. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-7.
children.title: Overtaking and passing
children.text:
Persons overtaking and passing other users proceeding in the same direction shall be governed by the following:

(a) The person overtaking another proceeding in the same direction shall pass to the left thereof at a safe distance and shall not again return to the right side of the pathway until safely clear of the overtaken person.

(b) The person being overtaken shall give way to the right in favor of the overtaking person on audible warning, and shall not increase their speed until completely passed by the overtaking person.

(c) No person shall overtake and pass another using the left side of the pathway unless such left side is clearly visible and is free of oncoming users for a sufficient distance ahead to permit such overtaking and passing to be completed without interfering with the safety of those approaching from the opposite direction. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-8.
children.title: Following too closely
children.text: No person shall follow another more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of oneself and for others upon the pathway. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-9.
children.title: Speed
children.text: No person shall proceed along a pathway at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions and having regard for the actual and potential hazards then existing. In any event, speed shall be so restricted as may be necessary in order to avoid colliding with another and to maintain oneself in the general flow of movement at that time and location. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-10.
children.title: General speed limit
children.text: No person shall propel a wheeled device at a speed greater than the maximum of ten (10) miles per hour on any pathway. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 81-102, § 1, 5-20-81)

children.heading: PB7.5-11.
children.title: One-way pathways
children.text: No biker shall ride a bicycle and no roller skater shall ride or propel roller skates on the designated bicycle pathways at Lake Harriet, Lake Calhoun and Lake of the Isles other than in a one-way clockwise direction. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 82-104, § 1, 6-16-82; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 83-101, § 1, 5-4-83)

children.heading: PB7.5-12.
children.title: Control of animals
children.text: Any person using a pathway while accompanied by a domestic animal shall at all times maintain control over the animal and keep the animal on a leash. Any pathway user with an animal shall at all times yield the right-of-way to other pathway users and shall not interfere or allow the animal to interfere with other pathway users. No walker or jogger may use a pathway while accompanied by more than two (2) animals. No biker or roller skater may use a pathway while accompanied by more than one animal. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 95-101, § 1, 6-7-95)

children.heading: Chapter 8
children.title: SIDEWALK, CURB AND GUTTER CONSTRUCTION
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (9) ---

Charter reference— Authority of park and recreation board relative to sidewalks, curbs and gutters, Ch. 16, § 15.

Special law reference—Special act relating to installment payment of assessments made by park board, under Chapter 16, § 15 of the Charter, for curb and gutter or sidewalks, Laws 1965, Ch. 407.

children.heading: PB8-1.
children.title: Control and supervision
children.text: The superintendent of parks shall have direct control and supervision of the construction and repair of all sidewalks, curb or curb and gutter, and shall so supervise or construct such sidewalk and curb and gutter whenever the same shall be ordered by the park and recreation board. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1022.010)

children.heading: PB8-2.
children.title: Permit required
children.text: No person shall be allowed or permitted to replace or construct any sidewalk, curb or curb and gutter without obtaining a permit from the superintendent of parks. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1022.020)

children.heading: PB8-3.
children.title: Bond and maintenance agreement
children.text: No person shall be granted a permit except he shall file with the superintendent of parks a good and sufficient bond with at least two (2) sureties to guarantee the construction of such sidewalk, curb or curb and gutter in accordance with the specifications on file in the office of the superintendent of parks, and also to indemnify the park and recreation board for any loss or damage that may arise by the obstruction of the parkways or park, or from any other cause and such bond shall also, among other things, contain an agreement and condition that all curbs and gutters laid by the principal in such bond shall be maintained by such principal for the period of two (2) years after the completion of the laying of the same in a good and sufficient condition and free from all defects, settlements and cracks caused by the use of imperfect material or workmanship, or by the proper use of such sidewalks, curbs and curbs and gutters for the purpose intended, or by the action of the elements. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1022.030)

children.heading: PB8-4.
children.title: Identification to be affixed to construction
children.text: Every such principal who replaces or constructs any sidewalk, curb or curb and gutter shall stamp or affix thereon or therein his name and the true date, or dates, on which such sidewalk, curb or curb and gutter was laid or constructed. The date of construction so indicated thereon shall be prima facie evidence of the date of the commencement of the two-year maintenance period required of the said principal under the terms of his bond, as required by this chapter. Such name and date or dates shall be placed in such sidewalk, curb or curb and gutter in at least one place in every fifty (50) lineal feet thereof, or both ends if a lesser number of feet thereof is constructed. The superintendent of parks shall provide in the specifications for sidewalk, curb or curb and gutter construction the style, size of lettering and manner of stamping or affixing the name and date of construction thereof as herein required. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1022.040)

children.heading: Chapter 8.5
children.title: SNOWMOBILES
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (10) ---

State Law reference— Regulation of snowmobiles, M.S. § 84.81 et seq.

children.heading: PB8.5-1.
children.title: Permit required
children.text: No person shall place, have or use a snowmobile on any property under the jurisdiction of the board of park commissioners without first applying for and obtaining a permit for each snowmobile. Said permit shall be subject to revocation by the board of park commissioners for cause. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.010)

children.heading: PB8.5-2.
children.title: Application for permit
children.text: The superintendent of parks, upon a written application being presented and upon a showing that the person so presenting the same is a fit and proper person to operate a snowmobile on designated park property, shall be authorized to issue such permits. Before the issuance of such permit, the person applying therefor shall complete and sign an application setting forth his name, address, description of the snowmobile for which the permit is being issued and shall agree in writing to operate said snowmobile in accordance with all rules and regulations and to indemnify and save the park department harmless from any liability because of injury to person or property arising out of the activity or privilege for which the permit is issued or caused by reason of the negligent, wrongful or unlawful act of any person to whom the permit is granted, or any person acting under the permittee's control or with the permittee's consent. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.110)

children.heading: PB8.5-3.
children.title: Duration
children.text: Such permit so granted by the superintendent of parks shall be in full force and effect, unless revoked for cause, for a period of one season, which shall be considered as beginning when lakes freeze and are declared to be safe and shall be considered to be closed when ice is declared unsafe in the spring. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.120)

children.heading: PB8.5-4.
children.title: Equipment
children.text:
All snowmobiles shall have the following equipment:

(a) Standard mufflers which are properly attached and in constant operation, and which reduce the noise of operation of the motor to the minimum necessary for operation. Mufflers shall comply with Minnesota Regulations Conservation 55 which is hereby adopted by reference as it existed on September 1, 1970. No person shall use a muffler cutout, bypass, straight pipe or similar device on the snowmobile motor, and the exhaust system shall not emit or produce a sharp popping or crackling sound.

(b) At least one head lamp and one tail lamp, and with brakes which conform to the standards prescribed by rule of the commissioner of public safety of Minnesota.

(c) A safety or so-called "dead man" throttle in operating condition; a safety or "dead man" throttle is defined as a device which, when pressure is removed from the accelerator or throttle, causes the motor to be disengaged from the driving track. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.050)

children.heading: PB8.5-5.
children.title: Capacity
children.text: No snowmobile shall be operated with more than two (2) adults or one (1) adult and two (2) minor children in the snowmobile at the same time. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.100)

children.heading: PB8.5-6.
children.title: Hours of operation
children.text: No snowmobile shall be operated at times other than daylight hours, except in supervised areas which the superintendent of parks shall have the authority to designate and to establish the hours of operation; "daylight" is defined as one-half hour before sunrise until one-half hour after sunset. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.070)

children.heading: PB8.5-7.
children.title: Designated areas
children.text: Notwithstanding the prohibitions of this chapter, the superintendent of parks shall have authority to supervise and regulate events or programs conducted by the park department in making available supervised areas for operation of snowmobiles, and shall have authority to designate park areas that he shall deem appropriate for general use by the public under the terms and conditions of this chapter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.080)

children.heading: PB8.5-8.
children.title: Safe operation and speed
children.text: No person shall operate or halt any snowmobile on park property carelessly or needlessly in disregard of the rights or the safety of others, or in a manner so as to endanger or be likely to endanger any person or property and shall travel at a reasonable speed not to exceed twenty (20) miles per hour. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.030)

children.heading: PB8.5-9.
children.title: Restriction on operation in vicinity of other activities
children.text: No snowmobile shall be operated within fifty (50) yards of any fisherman, pedestrian, skating rink or sliding area, or in any other area where the operation would conflict with other activities or endanger other persons or property. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.040)

children.heading: PB8.5-10.
children.title: Unattended snowmobile
children.text: It is unlawful for the owner or operator to leave or allow a snowmobile to be or remain unattended on park property. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.060)

children.heading: PB8.5-11.
children.title: Renting prohibited
children.text: It is unlawful for a person having possession of a snowmobile on park property to lease or attempt to lease or furnish or attempt to furnish same for pay or hire. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1036.090)

children.title: TRAFFIC
children.text:
Art.       I.

In General, §§ PB9-1—PB9-18

Art.       II.

Rules of the Road Generally, §§ PB9-19—PB9-50

Art.       X.

Establishing and Naming Parkways and Park Roads, §§ PB9-300—PB9-304

children.heading: PB9-1.
children.title: Title
children.text: This chapter shall be known as the "Park and Recreation Board Traffic Code." (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1040.010)

children.heading: PB9-2.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this chapter the following terms shall mean:

Driver. Every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle.

Parkway or drive. Any place under jurisdiction of the park and recreation board which is open to the use of the public as a matter of right for vehicular traffic.

Vehicle. Every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a street or highway, except devices moved by human power, or used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1040.020)

children.heading: PB9-3.
children.title: Minneapolis traffic code to apply
children.text: Where not in conflict with this chapter, the Minneapolis Traffic Code, Title 18 of the Minneapolis Code of Ordinances, shall apply. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1040.030)

children.heading: PB9-4.
children.title: When signs required
children.text: No part of this chapter, designating particular parkways, or streets as one-way streets, and requiring that all vehicles thereon be moved in one specific direction; or designating any parkway, street or drive as a through parkway, street or drive and requiring that all vehicles stop before entering or crossing the same, or designating any intersection as a stop intersection and requiring all vehicles to stop at one or more entrances to such intersection; or restricting the use of any parkways as authorized shall be effective until signs giving notice of such traffic regulations are posted upon and kept posted upon or at the entrance to the parkway, street or drive or part affected thereof as may be most appropriate. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1040.040)

children.heading: PB9-5.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-5, which pertained to obedience to police and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1045.020.

children.heading: PB9-6.
children.title: Vehicles prohibited in nondesignated areas
children.text: No vehicle is permitted to be on any footwalk, lawn or any other grounds on parks or parkways not designated for traffic or parking purposes, unless otherwise permitted by the rules, regulations and ordinances of the park and recreation board. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.090)

children.heading: PB9-7.
children.title: Advertising prohibited
children.text: No person shall drive or park any vehicle upon any park or parkway displaying a sign indicating that it is for sale or exchange or otherwise displaying advertising. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.050)

children.heading: PB9-8.
children.title: (OR PB9-19.) Violations
children.text: Any violation of a provision of PB9-6 of this chapter is an administrative offense and subject to any penalties or fines established in accordance with Chapter 14 of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Code of Ordinances. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-102, § 1, 10-5-11)

children.heading: PB9-19.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-19, which pertained to signals by driver and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1041.010.

children.heading: PB9-20.
children.title: Backing
children.text:
No person in control of a vehicle shall back same without giving ample warning, and while backing shall use care not to injure those in the rear.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1041.020)

children.heading: PB9-21.
children.title: Right-of-way generally
children.text:
(a) The driver of a vehicle approaching an intersection shall yield the right-of-way to a vehicle which has entered the intersection.

(b) When two (2) vehicles enter an intersection from different roadways or parkways at approximately the same time, the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.

(c) The driver of any vehicle traveling at an unlawful speed or who fails to obey any traffic signal, shall forfeit any right-of-way which he might otherwise have.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1041.030)

children.title: Reserved

children.heading: PB9-34.
children.title: "Alcoholic beverage" defined
children.text:
For the purpose of this chapter, an "alcoholic beverage" means any liquid containing more than one-half of one per cent of alcohol by volume.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1041.160)

children.heading: PB9-35.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-35, which pertained to penalty for driving under the influence and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1041.170.

children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-36, which pertained to evidence from chemical tests and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1041.180.

children.heading: PB9-37.
children.title: Open bottle law
children.text:
(a) Drinking in vehicle. No person shall drink or consume intoxicating liquors or nonintoxicating malt liquors in any motor vehicle when such vehicle is upon a public highway or in a public parking lot.

(b) Open bottle in vehicles. No person shall have in his possession on his person, while in a private motor vehicle upon a public highway or in a public parking lot, any bottle or receptacle containing intoxicating liquor or nonintoxicating malt liquor which has been opened, or the seal broken, or the contents of which have been partially removed.

(c) Owner's and driver's responsibility. No owner of any private motor vehicle or the driver, if the owner is not present in the motor vehicle, shall keep or allow to be kept in a motor vehicle when such vehicle is upon the public highway or in a public parking lot, any bottle or receptacle containing intoxicating liquors or nonintoxicating malt liquors which has been opened, or the seal broken, or the contents of which have been partially removed, except when such bottle or receptacle shall be kept in the trunk of the motor vehicle when such vehicle is equipped with a trunk, or kept in some other area of the vehicle not normally occupied by the driver or passengers, if the motor vehicle is not equipped with a trunk. A utility compartment or glove compartment shall be deemed to be within the area occupied by the driver and passengers.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1041.190; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 76-103, § 1, 7-21-76)

children.heading: PB9-38.
children.title: Employment of intemperate drivers
children.text:
No persons owning or having control of a coach or vehicle traveling upon any road for the conveyance of passengers shall employ any person to drive the same who is addicted to the excessive use of intoxicating liquors or narcotic drugs.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1041.200)

children.heading: PB9-39.
children.title: Minor under seventeen not to drive motor vehicle between certain hours
children.text:
Any juvenile under the age of seventeen (17) is prohibited from driving a motor vehicle on any parkway or road under the jurisdiction and control of the park and recreation board between the hours of 12:00 midnight and 5:00 a.m., unless accompanied by an adult or in case of an emergency.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1041.210)

children.heading: PB9-51.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-51, which pertained to the requirement of safe speed and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1042.010.

children.heading: PB9-52.
children.title: Speed limit
children.text:
No vehicle shall be driven at more than twenty (20) miles per hour on any parkway or highway on which a different speed has not been established by the commissioner of highways. On any parkway where a different speed zone has been so established, and signs have been posted calling attention to such zone, no vehicle shall be driven at a speed greater than that indicated on such signs.

(Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.020; Ord. No. 2021-102, § 1, 11-3-21)

children.heading: PB9-53.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-53, which pertained to impeding traffic and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1042.030.

children.heading: PB9-53.1.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-53.1, which pertained to reduced speed required and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1042.040.

children.heading: PB9-54.
children.title: Speed in alleys
children.text: No person shall drive on any public alley on park property in the city at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the circumstances, and in no event at more than ten (10) miles per hour. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.050)

children.heading: PB9-55.
children.title: Speed on bridges
children.text: No person shall drive a vehicle over any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of the park system at a speed which is greater than the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to such bridge or structure, when such structure is sign-posted as provided hereafter. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.060)

children.heading: PB9-56.
children.title: Posting of bridges
children.text: The superintendent of parks may request the commissioner of highways to conduct an investigation of any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a parkway or highway, and if the commissioner shall find thereupon that such structure cannot with safety to itself withstand vehicles traveling at the speed otherwise permissible, he shall determine and declare the maximum speed of vehicles which such structure can withstand, and shall cause or permit suitable signs stating such maximum speed to be erected and maintained at a distance of one hundred (100) feet before each end of such structure. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.070)

children.heading: PB9-57.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-57, which pertained to exemption for emergency vehicles and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1042.090.

children.heading: PB9-58.
children.title: Summons to specify speed
children.text: In every charge of violation of any speed regulation the complaint, also the summons or notice to appear, shall specify the speed at which the defendant is alleged to have driven, also the speed limit applicable within the district or at the location. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.100)

children.heading: PB9-59.
children.title: Prosecutions
children.text: Upon the trial of any person charged with a violation of this article, proof of said determination of the maximum speed by the commissioner and the existence of said signs shall constitute conclusive evidence of the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to such bridge or structure. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.080)

children.heading: PB9-60.
children.title: Effect on civil actions
children.text: The provisions of this article declaring speed limitations shall not be construed to relieve the plaintiff in any civil action from the burden of proving negligence on the part of the defendant as to the proximate cause of an accident. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1042.110)

children.heading: PB9-72.
children.title: Authorization of installation
children.text: The superintendent of parks, acting directly or through his duly authorized officers or agents, may authorize the installation or erection of a traffic-control sign, signal or marking upon any parkway or at one or more entrances to the intersection of a parkway, street or drive. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1043.140; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-101, § 1, 3-20-74)

children.heading: PB9-73.
children.title: Unauthorized signals
children.text:
No person shall place, maintain or display upon or in view of any parkway, street or drive any unauthorized sign, signal, marking or device which purports to be or is an imitation of or resembles an official traffic-control device or railroad sign or signal, and no person shall place or maintain nor shall any public authority permit upon any parkway, street or drive any traffic signal or signal bearing thereon any commercial advertising. This shall not be deemed to prohibit the erection upon private property adjacent to parkways, streets or drives of signs giving useful, directional information and of a type that cannot be mistaken for official signs.

Every such prohibited sign, signal or marking is a public nuisance and the superintendent of parks may remove the same or cause it to be removed without notice. (Code 1960, As Amend., §§ 1043.090, 1043.100)

children.heading: PB9-74.
children.title: Obedience to traffic devices
children.text: No driver of a vehicle, pedestrian, persons riding a bicycle or animal or any person whatsoever shall disobey the instructions of any official traffic-control device, signs, markings, or any part of this article, unless at the time otherwise directed by a police officer. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1043.110)

children.heading: PB9-75.
children.title: Obedience to "stop" signs
children.text: The driver of any vehicle shall bring such vehicle to a complete stop where there is in place any light, sign, standard or marking upon which appears the word "stop" or similar forms such as "School Stop." The driver shall stop before entering the nearest crosswalk, or if none, then before entering the intersection or at any stop sign or other sign or markings indicating where to stop. The driver of a vehicle shall stop in obedience to a stop sign, as required herein, at an intersection where a stop sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto, although not a part of a through street, and shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles not so obliged to stop which are within the intersection or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard, but may then proceed. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1043.010)

children.heading: PB9-76.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-76, which pertained to obedience to "yield" signs and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1043.020.

children.heading: PB9-77.
children.title: Obedience to traffic-control signals
children.text:
Whenever traffic is controlled by traffic-control signals exhibiting different colored lights, or colored lighted arrows, successively one at a time, or in combination, only the colors Green, Red and Yellow, shall be used, except for special pedestrian signals carrying a word legend, and said lights shall indicate and apply to drivers of vehicles and pedestrians as follows:

(a) Green indication.

(1) Vehicular traffic facing a circular green signal may proceed straight thru or turn right or left unless a sign at such place prohibits either such turn. But vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left, shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles and to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or adjacent crosswalk at the time such signal is exhibited.

(2) Vehicular traffic facing a green arrow signal, shown alone or in combination with another indication, may cautiously enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by such arrow, or such other movement as is permitted by other indications shown at the same time. Such vehicular traffic shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

(3) Unless otherwise directed by a pedestrian-control signal as provided in section PB9-80, pedestrians facing any green signal, except when the sole green signal is a turn arrow, may proceed across the roadway within any marked or unmarked crosswalk.

(b) Steady yellow indication.

(1) Vehicular traffic facing a steady yellow signal is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter when vehicular traffic shall not enter the intersection.

(2) Pedestrians facing a steady yellow signal, unless otherwise directed by a pedestrian-control signal as provided in section PB9-80, are thereby advised that there is insufficient time to cross the roadway, before a red indication is shown and no pedestrian shall then start to cross the roadway.

(c) Steady red indication.

(1) Vehicular traffic facing a steady red signal shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if none, then before entering the intersection and shall remain standing until a green indication is shown.

(2) Unless otherwise directed by a pedestrian-control signal as provided in section PB9-80, pedestrians facing a steady red signal shall not enter the roadway. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1043.060)

children.heading: PB9-78.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-78, which pertained to traffic-control signal other than at intersection and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1043.070.

children.heading: PB9-79.
children.title: Flashing signals
children.text:
Whenever flashing red or yellow signals are used they shall require obedience by vehicular traffic as follows:

(a) Flashing red (stop signal). When a red lens is illuminated by rapid intermittent flashes, drivers of vehicles shall stop before entering the nearest crosswalk at an intersection or at a limit line when marked, and the right to proceed shall be subject to the rules applicable after making a stop at a stop sign.

(b) Flashing yellow (caution signal). When a yellow lens is illuminated by rapid intermittent flashes, drivers of vehicles may proceed through the intersection or past such signal only with caution. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1043.080)

children.heading: PB9-80.
children.title: Pedestrian-control signals
children.text:
Whenever special pedestrian-control signals exhibiting the words "Walk," "Don't Walk" or "Wait" are in place such signals shall indicate as follows:

(a) "Walk." Pedestrians facing such signals may proceed across the roadway in the direction of the signal and shall be given the right-of-way by the drivers of all vehicles.

(b) "Don't Walk" or "Wait." No pedestrian shall start to cross the roadway in the direction of such signals, but any pedestrian who has partially completed his crossing on the "Walk" signal shall proceed to a sidewalk or safety island while the "Wait" or "Don't Walk" signal is showing. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1043.120)

children.heading: PB9-81.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-81, which pertained to lane-direction-control signals and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1043.130.

children.heading: PB9-93.
children.title: Applicability of traffic laws
children.text:
(a) Every person riding a bicycle upon a parkway or designated bicycle path shall be granted all the rights and shall be subject to all the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle by this chapter, except those provisions which by their nature can have no application.

(b) Every person riding or propelling a bicycle upon any parkway or designated bicycle path shall observe all traffic rules and regulations, applicable thereto, and shall turn only at intersections, signal for all turns, ride at the right-hand side of the parkway or designated bicycle path, pass to left when passing or overtaking vehicles that are slower moving, and shall pass to the right when meeting, and shall observe all traffic signs and signals and stop at all stop signs. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1044.010; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, 5-1-74)

children.heading: PB9-94.
children.title: Riding on designated pedestrian path prohibited; exception
children.text: No person shall ride a bicycle on any designated pedestrian path except where such path is also a designated bicycle path. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1044.020; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, 5-1-74)

children.heading: PB9-95.
children.title: Control, speed and manner of operation
children.text: No person shall ride or propel a bicycle upon a parkway or designated bicycle path except in a prudent and careful manner and unless such person shall be capable of efficient control and operation of such bicycle, and no bicycle shall be ridden faster than is reasonable and proper. Every bicycle shall be operated with reasonable regard to the safety of the operator and other persons upon the parkway and designated bicycle path. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1044.030; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, 5-1-74)

children.heading: PB9-96.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-96, which pertained to manner and number riding bicycles and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1044.040; and Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-97.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-97, which pertained to hitching rides and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1044.050; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-98.
children.title: Duty to keep to right; riding abreast
children.text: Every person operating a bicycle upon a parkway or designated bicycle path shall ride as near the right side of the parkway or designated bicycle path as practicable, exercising due care when passing a standing vehicle or bicycle or one proceeding in the same direction. Persons riding bicycles upon a parkway or designated bicycle path shall not ride two (2) abreast except for parkways when set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1044.060; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, 5-1-74)

children.heading: PB9-99.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Section 1 of Park Board Ord. No. 79-101, adopted April 18, 1979, repealed § PB9-99, concerning duty of bicyclist to use path when available. The repealed section derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1044.070, and Park Board Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-100.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-100, which pertained to carrying articles while bicycle riding and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1044.080; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-101.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-101, which pertained to lighting equipment on bicycles and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1044.090; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-102.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-102, which pertained to brake equipment on bicycles and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1044.100; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-103.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-103, which pertained to audible bell warning equipment on bicycles and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1044.110; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, adopted May 1, 1974.

children.heading: PB9-104.
children.title: Duty to yield to pedestrians
children.text: Any person riding a bicycle upon any combined designated bicycle and pedestrian path or upon any other park land shall yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian thereon. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1044.130; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, 5-1-74)

children.heading: PB9-105.
children.title: Authorization of path designation signs, control signs and marking
children.text: The superintendent of parks, acting directly or through his duly authorized officers or agents, may authorize the installation or erection of pedestrian and/or bicycle path designation signs, control signs or markings upon any paths on or across park lands so as to properly control their use. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1044.140; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 74-102, § 2, 5-1-74)

children.heading: PB9-106.
children.title: Pedestrians on designated bicycle path prohibited; exception
children.text: No pedestrian shall be on any designated bicycle path except where such path is also a designated pedestrian path. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 78-102, § 1, 4-5-78)

children.heading: PB9-117.
children.title: Established
children.text: One-way parkways and boulevards established by the park and recreation board are continued in effect, and the board may add to or modify the said routes by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The secretary of the board shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all one-way parkways and boulevards, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1046.040)

children.heading: PB9-118.
children.title: Posted drives
children.text: Upon a parkway or drive where the park and recreation board has established a one-way drive, and said drive is sign-posted or otherwise marked or indicated, a vehicle shall be driven only in the direction designated; subject, however, to the exception of emergency vehicles. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1046.030)

children.heading: PB9-119.
children.title: Divided parkways
children.text: On all parkways or drives divided by walk, viaduct, grass area or in any other manner, where divisions are sign-posted or otherwise marked or indicated, vehicles shall keep to the right of such divisions. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1046.010)

children.heading: PB9-120.
children.title: Rotary islands
children.text: A vehicle passing around a rotary traffic island shall be driven only to the right of such island. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1046.020)

children.heading: PB9-132.
children.title: Parking on left side of street
children.text: No vehicle shall stop with its left side to the curb except as otherwise provided herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.010)

children.heading: PB9-133.
children.title: Right curb parking required
children.text: No person, unless in an emergency or to allow another vehicle or a pedestrian to cross his path shall stop, park, double park or leave standing any vehicle within any district or section of any park, parkway or drive except in the line next to the right-hand curb thereof unless in accordance with signs or markings providing for such stopping or parking; also except trucks when calling for or delivering merchandise only when access to the curb at or immediately adjacent to the place of delivery is blocked by other vehicles and then only for such length of time as may be necessary to load or unload. Such length of time in any event, not to exceed fifteen (15) minutes. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.020)

children.heading: PB9-134.
children.title: Parking hours
children.text: Unless otherwise posted or authorized by permit issued by the park board, no vehicle shall be parked, and no person shall remain in or upon a parked vehicle along any parkway or in any parking lot under the jurisdiction of the park board between the hours of 12:00 midnight and 6:00 a.m. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1010.010; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 79-102, § 1, 5-2-79; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 89-102, § 1, 7-5-89)

children.heading: PB9-135.
children.title: Six hour limit
children.text: No person in charge of any vehicle shall park or permit said vehicle to stand upon any drive, parkway or park for more than six (6) consecutive hours between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 2:00 a.m. except in an emergency. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.040)

children.heading: PB9-136.
children.title: Blocking crosswalks
children.text: No vehicle shall stop on any crosswalk so as to interfere with the passage of pedestrians. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.030)

children.heading: PB9-137.
children.title: Near alleys, etc
children.text: No person shall park a vehicle or permit it to stand within any district or section of a park, parkway or drive whether attended or unattended except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic in front of or within five (5) feet of any public or private driveway or alley, where it intersects with any park, parkway or drive. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.060)

children.heading: PB9-138.
children.title: No-parking zones established
children.text: The no-parking zones established by the park and recreation board are continued in effect, and the board may add to or modify the said no-parking zones by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The secretary of the park and recreation board shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all no-parking zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this code, the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.011)

children.heading: PB9-139.
children.title: Parking in no-parking zones
children.text: No person shall park a vehicle or permit it to stand within any district or section of a parkway or drive where the park and recreation board has established a "No-Parking Zone" when such zone is marked by yellow curb, sign or otherwise marked or indicated. Parking at regularly designated parking concourses shall be in accordance with such markings and no person shall park his car in any other manner except as so designated. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.010)

children.heading: PB9-140.
children.title: Limited parking zones established
children.text: Limited parking zones indicating two-hour, one-hour or fifteen-minute parking, established by the park and recreation board, are continued in effect, and the park and recreation board may add to or modify said limited parking zones by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The secretary of the board shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all limited parking zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code, the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.032)

children.heading: PB9-141.
children.title: Parking in limited parking zones
children.text: No person shall park any vehicle nor permit it to stand within any district or section of a park, parkway or drive where the board has established a limited parking zone, for more than the allotted time for such zone at any one time, when such zones are marked by sign or otherwise marked or indicated. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.031)

children.heading: PB9-142.
children.title: Taxi stands established
children.text: Taxi stands established by the park and recreation board are continued in effect, and the park and recreation board may add to or modify said taxi stands by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The secretary of the board shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all taxi stands, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code, the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.061)

children.heading: PB9-143.
children.title: Parking in taxi stands
children.text: No person shall park any vehicle or permit it to stand within any district or section of a park, parkway or drive where the board has established a taxicab stand, except vehicles licensed as taxicabs when such zones are marked by sign or otherwise marked or indicated. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.060)

children.heading: PB9-144.
children.title: Truck loading zones established
children.text: Truck loading zones established by the park and recreation board are continued in effect, and the park and recreation board may add to or modify said truck loading zones by appropriate ordinances from time to time. The secretary of the board shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all truck loading zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code, the same as if fully set forth herein. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.071)

children.heading: PB9-145.
children.title: Parking in truck loading zones
children.text: No person shall stop, stand or park any vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle, within any district or section of a park or parkway established by the board as a truck loading zone, when such zones are marked by sign or otherwise marked or indicated. Commercial vehicles shall not be parked in truck loading zones for any purpose or length of time other than the expeditious unloading and delivery or pickup and loading of materials. In no case shall the stop for loading and unloading of materials exceed thirty (30) minutes. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1048.070)

children.heading: PB9-146.
children.title: Pickups of freight or passengers
children.text: When taking up or discharging freight or passengers, vehicles shall be headed in the direction of traffic on the right of the driveway. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.100)

children.heading: PB9-147.
children.title: Pay parking areas
children.text:
"Pay Parking" areas shall be any portion or section of a park, parkway or drive where meters, pay boxes, parking attendants or any other thing or device for collecting a parking fee is installed or present.
