When any vehicle shall enter, remain or park in or on any pay parking area, the driver of said vehicle shall immediately deposit or cause to be deposited in the meter, coin box or any other device present for collecting a parking fee, or pay or cause to be paid to a parking attendant, the parking fee in coins or currency of the United States equal to the sum due as posted or indicated by signs or directions installed or present in the said area. Said driver shall also comply with all the other laws and regulations in existence or posted by sign or otherwise in the said area. (Code 1960, As Amend.,§ 1048.080)

children.heading: PB9-148.
children.title: Lights on parked vehicles
children.text: No vehicle shall be left standing on a drive, parkway or park at night without light; nor unless lights thereon are displayed so as to be visible from the front and rear. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.090)

children.heading: PB9-149.
children.title: Locking of wheels
children.text: No person shall at any time leave any motor vehicle standing upon any parkway or drive with the wheels chained, locked or fastened in such a manner that such motor vehicle cannot be easily moved in case of need. Locking of a motor vehicle so as to permit the vehicle being moved by hand shall be allowed. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.070)

children.heading: PB9-150.
children.title: Shifting parked vehicle
children.text: For the purpose of the regulations relating to limited parking, any vehicle moved within any limited parking zone and not completely removed therefrom, shall be deemed to have remained stationary. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.070)

children.heading: PB9-151.
children.title: Impounding
children.text: Any unoccupied vehicle found in violation of this chapter, may be removed and impounded by any police officer or duly authorized person in accordance with Chapter 478, Article X of the Minneapolis Code of Ordinances. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1047.080)

children.heading: PB9-152.
children.title: Procedure for establishment of parking zones
children.text: The parking zones authorized by Article VII shall be established in accordance with the provisions of this section. Parking zones may be established by the park and recreation board. Parking zones may be established by the superintendent in compliance with standards promulgated by the park and recreation board for the establishment of the zones. Parking zones may be established by the superintendent with the concurrence of the park and recreation board. The secretary of the park and recreation board shall maintain in his office at all times a complete listing of all parking zones, which said listing is hereby incorporated in this Code, the same as fully set forth herein. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 85-101, § 1, 5-1-85)

children.heading: PB9-163.
children.title: Driving near schoolchildren
children.text: No person shall drive a motor vehicle through a column of schoolchildren crossing a street or highway or past a member of a school safety patrol while the member of the school safety patrol is directing the movement of children across a street or highway and while the school safety patrol member is holding his official signal in the stop position. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.030)

children.heading: PB9-164.
children.title: Passing vehicle stopped at crosswalk
children.text: When any vehicle is stopped at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk at any intersection to permit a pedestrian to cross the street or parkway, the driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass the stopped vehicle. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.040)

children.heading: PB9-165.
children.title: Vehicles prohibited off parkways
children.text: No vehicle or machines of any kind, type or character, except such vehicles and machines operated by and for the park and recreation board, shall be permitted to drive on or across park lands and the ice of park lakes, or flooded skating rinks, unless permission is obtained to so drive thereon from the park and recreation board or its proper officers, paying the fees fixed therefor from time to time, and which shall be governed by the rules, regulations and ordinances of the board; and such vehicles or machines shall be of a kind, type or character approved by the board or its proper officers. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.050)

children.heading: PB9-166.
children.title: Washing, greasing, repairing vehicles
children.text: No person shall wash, grease or repair any vehicle on any park, boulevard or parkway except such repairs as are necessitated by an emergency. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.060)

children.heading: PB9-167.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Ord. No. 2019-104, § 1, adopted Oct. 2, 2019, repealed § PB9-167, which pertained to requirement for mufflers and derived from the Code of 1960, as amended, § 1045.160.

children.heading: PB9-168.
children.title: Excessive exhaust
children.text: No person operating a self-propelled vehicle shall permit the motors of same to operate in such a manner as to emit an unreasonable amount of steam, smoke or products of combustion from exhaust pipes or openings. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.110)

children.heading: PB9-169.
children.title: Spotlights
children.text: No person shall operate or manipulate in any park or upon any parkway, any detached or attached spotlight or flashlight, except for the purpose of finding and reading the street numbers on buildings and road and street signs, and for other emergency purposes. This section shall not apply to agents, servants or employees of the hospital, police or fire department of the city when the operation or use of such lights by them are connected with, and necessary to the performance of their duties. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.120)

children.heading: PB9-170.
children.title: Soliciting passengers
children.text: No person shall solicit passengers within or upon any parkway, unless authorized by the board, and only at places specifically designated by the board. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.130)

children.heading: PB9-171.
children.title: Vehicle and weight restrictions
children.text:
(a) General. No truck, or any vehicle licensed as a truck, or any other overweight vehicle shall be allowed in any park or on any parkway.

(b) Access. Where no other means of access to a site exists:

(i) Vehicles governed by this section, other than overweight vehicles, may use a parkway between such site and the nearest intersecting street or alley.

(ii) Overweight vehicles may use a parkway between such site and the nearest intersecting street or alley by permit only.

(c) Permits. Permits for overweight vehicles shall be issued by the board. The board may establish and charge a fee for such permit. The board may also require the permit applicant to pay a deposit or post a bond, in an amount to be determined by the board, to secure reimbursement to the board for any damage to the park or parkway caused by such permitted use. As a condition of such permit, the board may impose reasonable safety and health restrictions or requirements.

(d) Exceptions. This section shall not apply to:

(i) St. Anthony Boulevard from Marshall Street to Fifth Street Northeast, or other routes which may be designated by the board;

(ii) Vehicles operated by the board or under its directions; or

(iii) Vehicles commonly known as one-half-ton pickups or three-quarter-ton pickups, but only if such pickups have no payload and are operated for noncommercial purposes.

(e) Definitions. For the purpose of this section:

(i) Overweight vehicle means any vehicle or combination of vehicles having a gross weight on any single wheel in excess of seven thousand (7,000) pounds, or having a gross weight on any single axle in excess of fourteen thousand (14,000) pounds.

(ii) Gross weight, single wheel, and single axle shall have the meaning defined in Minnesota Statutes section 169.825. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.140; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 76-106, 11-3-76; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 90-101, § 1, 9-5-90)

children.heading: PB9-172.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-172, which pertained to hitching or towing and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1045.150.

children.heading: PB9-173.
children.title: Rights, duties of pedestrians
children.text: The roadbeds of driveways are primarily intended for vehicles, but pedestrians have the right to cross them in safety and all drivers of vehicles shall exercise all proper care not to injure pedestrians. Pedestrians at crossings shall have the right-of-way. Pedestrians when crossing a driveway shall not carelessly or maliciously interfere with the passage of vehicles. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.110)

children.heading: PB9-174.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-174, which pertained to soliciting rides and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1045.180.

children.heading: PB9-175.
children.title: Running, jogging and walking
children.text: No person shall run, jog or walk along the roadbed of a parkway unless they are taking part in an event or competition authorized or licensed by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Department. For the purposes of this section, "roadbed" is defined as the paved surface of a parkway primarily intended for use by motorized vehicles. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.190; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 80-101, § 1, 5-21-80)

children.heading: PB9-176.
children.title: Ingress and egress to parkways
children.text: No person driving any kind of vehicle whatsoever, whether motor driven or horse driven, shall enter upon or drive into any parkway or boulevard in or adjacent to the city at any point other than a regular street intersection except over such alleys, driveways and other means of ingress or egress authorized by the park and recreation board. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1045.200)

children.heading: PB9-177.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2020-103, § 1, adopted Aug. 5, 2020, repealed § PB9-177, which pertained to funeral processions and derived from Code 1960, as amended, § 1045.210.

children.heading: PB9-200.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used herein, the terms:

(a) "Vehicle" shall mean every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a street, boulevard or highway, except devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks.

(b) "Street," "parkway," "boulevard" or "highway" is the entire width between boundary lines of any way or place when any part thereof is open to the use of the public, as a matter of right, for purposes of vehicular traffic. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 82-101, § 1, 2-17-82)

children.heading: PB9-201.
children.title: Declaration
children.text:
Whenever in the opinion of the city engineer and the chief of police an emergency exists in the city, or in a section or sections thereof, because of snow, freezing rain, sleet, ice, snowdrifts or other natural phenomena which create, or are likely to create, hazardous road conditions impeding, or likely to impede, the free movement of fire, health, police, emergency or other vehicular traffic, or the safety and welfare of the community, the city engineer and the chief of police may declare an emergency to exist for a period of seventy-two (72) hours, but such emergency may be sooner terminated if conditions permit. Notice of such emergency shall be given by press, radio or television, which news media shall be requested to cooperate with the city officials and, when given, such notice shall constitute due and proper notice.

The emergency declaration provided for in this section may be limited to the parkways, boulevards and streets designated as snow emergency routes. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 82-101, § 1, 2-17-82)

children.heading: PB9-202.
children.title: Snow emergency parking restrictions
children.text:
Upon the declaration of a snow emergency by the city engineer and the chief of police, no person shall stop, stand, park or leave any vehicle or permit it to stand upon any parkway, boulevard, street or highway as follows:

(a) On all posted "snow emergency routes" for a period of eleven (11) hours from the effective time of the declared snow emergency.

(b) On all other parkways, boulevards, streets and highways from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., or until plowed full width, on the day following the declaration of a snow emergency. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 82-101, § 1, 2-17-82; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 83-107, § 1, 11-2-83)

children.heading: PB9-203.
children.title: Impounding violations
children.text: If any vehicle is parked, abandoned or left standing in violation of the terms of this article, the same may be impounded in accordance with the terms of Chapter 478, Article X, of the motor vehicle impounding ordinances of the city, at the cost and expense of the owner thereof. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 82-101, § 1, 2-17-82)

children.heading: PB9-204.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Section 2 of Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 83-107, adopted Nov. 2, 1983, repealed § PB9-204, concerning winter parking in special snow-removal zones, which section derived from Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 82-101, § 1, adopted Feb. 17, 1982.

children.heading: ARTICLE X.
children.title: ESTABLISHING AND NAMING PARKWAYS AND PARK ROADS

children.heading: PB9-300.
children.title: Purpose
children.text:
The purpose of this article is to establish by ordinance the names of all public parkways and park roads under the jurisdiction of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board.

(Ord. No. 2019-101, § 1, 4-17-19)

children.heading: PB9-301.
children.title: Authority to name and rename parkways and park roads
children.text:
The official name of all public parkways and park roads on land governed, administered, maintained, controlled, owned or held by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board in and adjacent to the City of Minneapolis shall be named and renamed consistent with the article.

(Ord. No. 2019-101, § 1, 4-17-19)

children.heading: PB9-302.
children.title: Names of public parkways and park roads

children.heading: PB9-303.
children.title: Required Vote
children.text:
Any action to name or rename a parkway or a park road requires at least six (6) affirmative votes by park commissioners.

(Ord. No. 2019-101, § 1, 4-17-19)

children.heading: PB9-304.
children.title: Signage
children.text:
The superintendent shall ensure that each parkway or park road is clearly marked for the public.

(Ord. No. 2019-101, § 1, 4-17-19)

children.heading: Chapter 10
children.title: TREES AND VEGETATION
children.text:
Art.       I.

On Streets and Parkways, §§ PB10-1—PB10-20

Art.       II.

Dutch Elm Disease Control, §§ PB10-21—PB10-27

  Footnotes:  --- (11) ---

Editor's note— With the concurrence of the city, the editor has retitled Ch. 10 as set out above and has given the sections which originally constituted Ch. 10 the designation "Art I. On Streets and Parkways," in order to facilitate the inclusion of Park Board Ord. No. 77-102, as amended, as Art. II hereof. Ord. No. 77-102 originally designated that its provisions be codified as Ch. 11.

Charter reference— Authority of park and recreation board relative to trees, Ch. 16, §§ 16, 17.

Cross reference— Park and recreation board to administer ordinance relative to Dutch elm disease, § 399.10; attaching or hitching animals to trees in public places, §§ 74.20, 427.200.

Special law reference—Special act relating to the planting, care, protection, etc., of trees and shrubs on streets and public grounds, Laws 1969, Ch. 593, as amended by Laws 1974, Ch. 108.

children.heading: PB10-1.
children.title: Permit required to plant
children.text: No person shall plant any tree within the limits of any parkway or street of the city without having first obtained a permit from the general superintendent of parks. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.010)

children.heading: PB10-2.
children.title: Permit procedure, scope
children.text: Anyone wishing to plant such tree or trees shall apply to the general superintendent of parks for a permit, stating the variety and precise location proposed for each tree. After the receipt of such an application the general superintendent shall investigate the locality where the tree or trees are to be placed and shall grant a permit only if in his judgment the location is such as to permit the normal growth and development of each tree. The permit shall specify the location, variety and grade of each tree and method of planting, including among other things, the supplying of suitable soil. The permit shall be good only for the season stated on same in the year issued, and no charge shall be made for same. No trees shall be planted except in accordance with its terms. The specifications of the permit shall be such as will secure the suitable location, planting and growth of each tree. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.020)

children.heading: PB10-3.
children.title: Varieties of street trees
children.text: No trees shall be planted as street trees except by permission of the park and recreation board or its proper officers. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.030)

children.heading: PB10-4.
children.title: Suitable planting conditions
children.text: No permit for planting of such trees shall be given where the clear space between the curb and sidewalk is less than three (3) feet. Neither shall a permit be given where the soil is too poor to insure the growth of the trees unless the applicant or the owner agrees to excavate a suitable hole of not less than fifty-four (54) cubic feet and to replace the material removed with suitable good loam. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.040)

children.heading: PB10-5.
children.title: Dimensions
children.text: No such tree shall be planted measuring less than two (2) inches in diameter of trunk one foot above ground. The trunk of each tree shall be without branches eight (8) feet from the ground and the lowest branch shall not be over nine and one-half (9½) feet from the ground. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.050)

children.heading: PB10-6.
children.title: Permit for house moving if trees involved
children.text: No person, whether licensed or otherwise, shall move any building along any street in such a way as to interfere with or injure any tree or shrub in any street or public ground, including parks and parkways, in the city without a special permit obtained from the general superintendent of parks. The application shall specify the building and the proposed route. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.060)

children.heading: PB10-7.
children.title: Deposit for damage to trees
children.text: All moving of trees and shrubs or trimming the branches thereof made necessary for the moving of such building or any other purpose shall be done by the general superintendent of parks, or under his supervision, at the expense of the applicant. Should such moving or replanting cause the death of such trees or shrubs the applicant shall replace same at his expense. Before such permit is granted the applicant shall deposit at least ten dollars ($10.00) per tree, and as much more as the general superintendent may deem necessary to cover the actual expense of removing and replanting, if necessary; to be retained until said tree or its successor is permanently established. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.070)

children.heading: PB10-8.
children.title: Piling against trees
children.text: No building material or any other material of any description shall be piled up against any street tree unless said tree is first sufficiently protected by a proper guard to prevent possible injury, and all instructions issued for that purpose by the general superintendent of parks must be promptly complied with by the owner or constructor. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.080)

children.heading: PB10-9.
children.title: Damaging trees
children.text: No person shall remove, destroy, cut, deface, trim or in any way injure or interfere with any tree or shrub on any of the avenues, streets or public grounds, including parks and parkways, without a permit from the general superintendent of parks. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.090)

children.heading: PB10-10.
children.title: Wires damaging trees
children.text: No person shall place or let be placed any wire conduit or other thing that burns, cuts or chafes any part of any trees, whether trunk, root or branch, in any street or parkway. In case the owner or the person shall fail after three (3) days' written notice to take adequate steps to prevent further injury, the superintendent of parks shall have power to remove the same. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.120)

children.heading: PB10-11.
children.title: Space for trees
children.text: No paving of any description shall be laid or maintained by anyone between sidewalk and curb which will cut off the air and water from any tree. (Code 1960, As Amend., § 1020.130)

children.heading: ARTICLE II.
children.title: CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES TREE PESTS
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (12) ---

Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, adopted November 18, 2009, amended the title of Art. II to read as herein set out. Prior to inclusion of said ordinance, Art. II was entitled, "Dutch Elm Disease Control." See also the Park Board Code Comparative Table.

children.heading: PB10-20.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used herein the terms:

(a) "Invasive Species" means any invertebrate animal, plant pathogen, parasitic plant or similar or allied organism which can cause a tree to be diseased and is determined by either the commissioner of agriculture of the State of Minnesota or the commissioner of the department of natural resources of the State of Minnesota to be a pest causing economic or environmental harm and disease to trees in Minnesota.

(b) "Tree" means deciduous and coniferous trees.

(c) "Pest" means any living agent capable of reproducing itself that causes or may potentially cause economic or environmental harm to trees through infection and/or infestation.

(d) "Disease" means either an infection or an infestation.

(e) "Infection" means a tree that is: (1) contaminated with pathogenic microorganisms; (2) being parasitized; (3) a host or carrier of an infectious, transmissible, or contagious pest; or (4) so exposed to a tree listed in clause (1), (2), or (3) that one of those conditions can reasonably be expected to exist and the tree may pose a risk of contamination to other trees or the environment.

(f) "Infestation" means a tree that has been overrun by pests.

(g) "Park and Recreation Board" means the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: PB10-21.
children.title: Nuisances declared
children.text:
The following things are public nuisances whenever they may be found within the city:

(a) Any living or standing tree or part thereof infected to any degree or infested with any invasive species pest; or

(b) Any dead tree or part thereof, including logs, branches, stumps, firewood or other tree material from which the infected and/or infested part has not been removed and burned or sprayed with an effective pesticide. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: PB10-22.
children.title: Nuisance prohibited
children.text: It is unlawful for any person to permit any public nuisance as defined in section PB10-21 to remain on any premises owned or controlled by said person within the city. Such nuisance may be abated in the manner described in this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: PB10-23.
children.title: Inspections; right to enter
children.text:
(a) All premises and places within the city shall be inspected by employees or agents of the Park and Recreation Board as often as practicable to determine whether any condition described in section PB10-21 exists therein. All reported incidents of an infection or infestation by an invasive species tree pest shall be investigated.

(b) Entry may be made upon private premises by said employees or agents of the Park and Recreation Board at any reasonable time for the purpose of carrying out any of the duties and responsibilities under this chapter.

(c) Upon finding conditions indicating an invasive species tree pest infection and/or infestation, appropriate specimens or samples shall be taken and sent to the commissioner of agriculture (bureau of plant industry), State of Minnesota, for analysis, or such other steps shall be taken for diagnosis as may be recommended by the commissioner of agriculture. No action to remove infected or infested trees or wood shall be taken until positive diagnosis of the disease has been made.

(d) Within five (5) days of receipt of the diagnosis, the owner of the property from which the specimen was obtained shall be notified of the result by personal delivery or first class mail. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 78-103, § 1, 4-19-78; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: PB10-24.
children.title: Abatement on public property
children.text: In abating the nuisances defined in section PB10-21, the infected or infested tree or wood shall be removed and burned or otherwise effectively treated to destroy and prevent as fully as possible the spread of the invasive species tree pest. Such abatement procedures shall be carried out in accordance with the current technical and expert methods and plans as may be designated by the commissioner of agriculture of the State of Minnesota or by the commissioner of natural resources of the State of Minnesota. Specifications for tree removal and disposal methods consistent therewith shall be established by the Director, Park Forestry of the Park and Recreation Board or other appropriate designee of the Park and Recreation Board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: PB10-25.
children.title: Abatement on private property
children.text:
(a) Whenever it is found with reasonable certainty that the infection and/or infestation defined in PB10-21 exists in any tree or wood located on private property, outside of any public way in the city, the owner or person in occupancy or control of such property on which the nuisance is found shall be notified by personal delivery or first class mail of the infection and/or infestation, and be directed that the infection and/or infestation shall be removed and burned, or otherwise effectively treated in a manner as set forth in PB10-24, by such owner or person in occupancy or control within ten (10) days after receipt of such notice. The notice shall also state that if such nuisance shall not have been abated by the owner or person in control of the property within the time provided, the owner or person in charge may be charged with a violation of this chapter for maintaining a nuisance and that the nuisance may be abated by the park and recreation board and the costs of such abatement assesses against the property.

(b) Said notice shall be accompanied by a postcard, returnable to the Park and Recreation Board, upon which the owner or person occupying or in control of the property shall indicate whether he intends to remove and effectively treat the infection and/or infestation.

(c) In the event that said postcard is not returned to the Park and Recreation Board within ten (10) days, the Park and Recreation Board shall post upon the property in a conspicuous place a notice indicating that the infection and/or infestation exists on said property. The posted notice shall contain the same information as set forth in subsection (a) of this section.

(d) If the owner or person occupying or in control of any private premises upon which a tree or wood is situated fails to have such tree or wood so removed and burned or otherwise effectively treated, after having elected to do so himself within ten (10) days after return of the postcard or fails to remove and burn or otherwise effectively treat the tree or wood within ten (10) days of the posting of notice on said property, then the removal and burning or other effective treatment of such tree or wood may be undertaken by the Park and Recreation Board and any expense incurred by Park and Recreation Board in so doing shall be a charge and a lien upon said property and shall be collected as a special assessment in the manner prescribed in Minnesota Statutes Section 429.091 and Minnesota Statutes Section 429.101 (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 78-103, § 2, 4-19-78; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2019-103, § 2, 10-2-19)

children.heading: PB10-26.
children.title: Collection of assessment
children.text: The cost of the abatement of any such nuisance done by the Park and Recreation Board at the election and approval of the owner or person occupying or in control of the private premises and not reimbursed by the owner on or before September 1st of the year shall be reported to the Park and Recreation Board and the Park and Recreation Board shall assess and levy and cause to be collected the amount of such cost as a special assessment upon and against said premises and property upon which said nuisance existed in the manner prescribed in Minnesota Statutes Section 429.091 and Minnesota Statutes Section 429.101. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: PB10-27.
children.title: Interference prohibited
children.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent, delay or interfere with the Park and Recreation Board, its officers, employees or agents while they are engaged inn the performance of duties imposed by this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 77-102, § 1, 7-6-77; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2009-103, § 1, 11-18-09)

children.heading: Chapter 11
children.title: PARK FACILITY CONSTRUCTION AND REDEVELOPMENT
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (13) ---

Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, adopted November 9, 2011, amended the title of Ch. 11 to read as herein set out. Prior to inclusion of said ordinance, Ch. 11 was titled, "Park Facility Construction and Redevelopment Public Participation."

children.heading: PB11-1.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this chapter the following terms shall mean:

Community Engagement: The opportunity for stakeholders to influence decisions that shape the park system, including the intentional effort to create public understanding of MPRB project, programs, and services, and to make certain the MPRB is aware of and responsive to stakeholder needs, concerns and industry trends. Interchangeable terms include: public participation, community involvement, and citizen participation.

Park facility construction and redevelopment: The development of new of redevelopment of existing facilities as approved and budgeted in a Capital Improvement Program for the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board, including construction and redevelopment of facilities approved and budgeted through third party agreement. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-2.
children.title: Community Engagement Policy
children.text: The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board shall create, maintain, and regularly evaluate a community engagement policy that requires all park facility construction and redevelopment projects to have a community engagement plan. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-3.
children.title: Community Engagement Plan
children.text: All park facility construction and redevelopment projects require a community engagement plan. The community engagement plan shall be developed in consultation with established neighborhood organizations. When possible, other representative community groups and under-represented groups shall be involved in the development of the plan. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-4.
children.title: Community Advisory Committee—Creation and Authority
children.text: The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board shall cause a community advisory committee to be created when recommended within a community engagement plan. The community advisory committee shall be balanced and representative of the interests impacted by the proposed park facility construction or redevelopment project. The community advisory committee shall have the authority to make recommendations to the designated Committee of the Board on the proposed park facility construction and redevelopment project. The Board of Commissioners shall have the authority to cause the creation and approve the charge and composition of a community advisory committee for topics of its choosing. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-5.
children.title: Community Advisory Committee—Meetings and Recommendation
children.text: All meetings shall be open to the public. Any person may appear and speak at a meeting either in person or by a duly appointed representative. Upon conclusion of public input, the community advisory committee shall announce its recommendation or shall lay the proposal over to a subsequent meeting. Records shall be kept on file at the Park Board office of attendance, meetings, agendas, handouts and committee actions. All recommendations of the community advisory committee shall be presented at the public hearing of the designated Committee of the Board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-6.
children.title: Committee of the Board Public Hearing
children.text: A Committee of the Board shall hold a public hearing on all project that include recommendations of a community advisory committee. The chair or acting chair may set the parameters of testimony to be received from interested parties. Any person may appear and testify at a hearing either in person or by a duly appointed representative. After reviewing the community advisory committee's recommendations and after the conclusion of public testimony, the Committee of the Board shall announce its decision or shall lay the matter over to a subsequent meeting. The Committee of the Board shall keep records of its public hearing and official actions. Decisions of the Committee of the Board shall be dated and forwarded to the full Board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-7.
children.title: Community Advisory Committee Meeting and Public Hearing Notice
children.text: The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board shall create and maintain a notification process that addresses all community advisory committee meetings and public hearings for a project. This process shall require a ten (10) day notice of the first meeting in a newspaper of general circulation, of park councils and registered neighborhood groups and all owners of records of property located in whole or in part within three (3) city blocks of the project area. The notice shall comply with all other notice requirements of Minnesota's Open Meeting Law. Failure to give mailed notice to all affected parties, or defects in the notice, shall not invalidate the process or proceedings. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 99-1010, § 1, 9-15-99 ; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, 11-9-11)

children.heading: PB11-8, PB11-9.
children.title: Reserved
children.text: Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-103, § 1, adopted November 9, 2011, repealed §§ PB11-8, PB11-9, which pertained to Full Park Board Hearing Notice and Public Hearing of Appeal. See also the Park Board Comparative Table.

children.heading: PB12-1.
children.title: Purpose
children.text: This ordinance is adopted to: enhance and preserve the environmental qualities of surface waters and shoreland areas under the jurisdiction of the MPRB; provide for the reasonable use of such waters and shoreland areas; comply with the requirements of state law regarding the management of shoreland areas; and protect the public health, safety and welfare. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2001-102, § 1, 9-19-01)

children.heading: PB12-2.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
As used in this Article, the following words and phrases shall mean:

"Bluff" means a steep outcropping, hill, cliff or embankment adjacent to a protected water, with an average slope of eighteen percent (18%) or greater measured over a horizontal distance of fifty (50) feet or more, and that rises at least twenty-five (25) feet above the ordinary high water mark of the protected water.

"Floodplain" means an area delineated as a floodplain by the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

"Ordinary high-water mark" means the point of the highest water level, which has existed for a sufficient period of time to leave evidence upon the landscape. The ordinary high-water mark is commonly that point where natural vegetation change from predominantly aquatic to predominantly terrestrial.

"Protected shoreland" means land owned by or under the control of the MPRB that is (a) within one thousand (1,000) feet of the ordinary high water mark of a protected waters; (b) within one thousand (1,000) feet of the top of a steep slope; or (c) on a bluff.

"Protected water" means the following lakes, ponds, streams and rivers and any other public waters or wetlands (as classified by the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources or the United Stated Fish and Wildlife Service) within the jurisdiction of the MPRB: Brownie Lake, Cedar Lake, Lake of the Isles, Lake Calhoun, Lake Harriet, Lake Nokomis, Lake Hiawatha, Diamond Lake, Powderhorn Lake, Spring Lake, Birch Pond, Loring Pond, Webber Pond, Bassett Creek, Minnehaha Creek, Shingle Creek and the Mississippi River.

"Structure" means any building, road, path, walkway, stairs, retaining wall, pier, dock, or other permanent fixture or improvement.

"Steep slope" means land having an average slope of eighteen percent (18%) or greater measured over a horizontal distance of fifty (50) feet or more having a drop from the high point to the low point of at least ten (10) feet that is adjacent to a protected water.

"Top of a steep slope" means the contour at which the slope ceases to be eighteen percent (18%). (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2001-102, § 1, 9-19-01)

children.heading: PB12-3.
children.title: Prohibition Against Structures
children.text: No person shall install or maintain any structure on any floodplain or protected shoreland, unless a permit has been issued to such person by the MPRB. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2001-102, § 1, 9-19-01)

children.heading: PB12-4.
children.title: Permit Criteria

children.heading: PB12-5.
children.title: Vegetation on Protected Shoreland
children.text: No person shall remove or damage any vegetation on any floodplain or protected shoreland, unless a permit has been issued to such person by the MPRB. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2001-102, § 1, 9-19-01)

children.heading: PB12-6.
children.title: Grading and Filling
children.text: No person shall dump any fill material on or grade any floodplain or protected shoreland, unless a permit has been issued to such person by the MPRB. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2001-102, § 1, 9-19-01)

children.heading: PB12-7.
children.title: Environmental Protection
children.text: Nothing herein shall prevent or preclude the MPRB from taking any of the following actions on a floodplain or protected shoreland: building or maintaining any structure; removing vegetation (not including routine mowing of grass and trimming of trees, shrubs, bushes or similar vegetation); or grading or filling. However, upon undertaking any such action, the MPRB shall comply with all applicable state and federal laws and regulations and, to the extent reasonably feasible as determined by the MPRB, shall employ measures to minimize stormwater runoff into protected waters, maximize overland flow and flow distances over surfaces covered with vegetation, employ on-site filtration techniques, replicate predevelopment hydrologic conditions, minimize off-site discharge of pollutants to ground and surface waters, and encourage natural filtration functions. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2001-102, § 1, 9-19-01)

children.heading: PB13-1.
children.title: Findings
children.text: The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board hereby finds that uncontrolled and inadequately planned utility encroachments on Park Board properties adversely affects public access and enjoyment of park lands and further restricts future development for these purposes, and further impairing other beneficial uses of environmental resources and hindering the ability of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board to provide other community services. In addition, extraordinary park expenditures may be required for the administration, recording, and monitoring of utility encroachments on parkland. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-2.
children.title: Purpose
children.text: The purpose of this chapter is to promote, preserve and enhance the natural resources and recreational opportunities within the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board and protect them from adverse effects occasioned by utility encroachments that would have an adverse and potentially irreversible impact on environmentally sensitive land; by minimizing conflicts and encouraging compatibility between encroachment and recreational activities; and by requiring detailed review standards and procedures for utility encroachments, and developing a fair reimbursement for Park Board expenses and land value associated with utility encroachments. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-3.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, the following terms, phrases, words, and their derivatives shall have the meaning stated below. When not inconsistent with the context, words used in the present tense include the future tense, words in the plural number include the singular number, and words in the singular number include the plural number. The word "shall" is always mandatory and not merely directive.

PB13-3-1. Applicant. Any person who wishes to obtain an encroachment permit approval.

PB13-3-2. The Board. The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board (MPRB).

PB13-3-3. Encroachment. Any use or diversion of parkland for purposes other than that for which the lands were acquired.

PB13-3-4. Land disturbing activity. Any activity that results in change of the land surface including removing vegetative cover, excavating, filling, grading, and the construction of any structure.

PB13-3-5. Parks. Any property owned or leased by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board.

PB13-3-6. Park Engineer. The professional engineer designated by the Board as Park Engineer or a representative thereof.

PB13-3-7. Person. Any individual, firm, corporation, partnership, franchisee, association or governmental entity.

PB13-3-8. Structure. Anything manufactured, constructed or erected which is normally attached to or positioned on land, including portable structures, above ground junction boxes, earthen structures, roads, parking lots, and paved storage areas.

PB13-3-9. Utility. Any conveyance or structure associated with public or private municipal infrastructure including but not limited to: water supply, energy supply, communications, stormwater drainage and sanitary sewer installations.

PB13-3-10. Utility Encroachment Fee Policy. The statement of fees associated with utility encroachment permits as approved by the Board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-4.
children.title: Scope and effect
children.text:
PB13-4-1. Applicability. No utility may be placed on or within land owned or leased by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board without first obtaining a utility encroachment permit. Every applicant for a utility encroachment permit approval must submit a completed application form and a utility alignment plan to the Parks Engineer. No utility encroachment approval shall be issued until the utility application and utility alignment plan has been approved by the Board or its designated representative.

Every applicant for a utility encroachment permit must also obtain a construction permit for the land disturbing activities associated with installation of the utility. A construction permit must also be obtained for the land disturbing activities associated with any maintenance subsequent to the initial installation of the utility. The applicant shall supply an as-built drawing upon completion of construction per Section 13-5-2.

PB13-4-2. Exemptions.

(a) The provisions of this chapter do not apply to emergency work to protect life or limb.

(b) Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Projects approved by the Board are exempt from this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-5.
children.title: Utility Encroachment Application Procedures
children.text:
PB13-5-1. Application. A written application for a utility encroachment approval, along with the proposed utility alignment plan, shall be filed with the Parks Engineer and shall include a statement indicating the grounds upon which the approval is requested, and give reasons why the proposed alignment is the only feasible alternative.

Three sets of clearly legible blue or black lined copies of all drawings on bond paper are required. Required information as outlined in Section 13-5-2 shall be submitted to the Parks Engineer and shall be accompanied by a receipt from the Special Services Department evidencing the payment of all required fees for processing and approval as set forth in Section 13-8 of this chapter.

The utility alignment plan drawings shall be prepared to a scale appropriate to the site of the project and suitable for the review to be performed. At a minimum the scale shall be one (1) inch equals fifty (50) feet. Drawing sheets shall be on eleven (11) by seventeen (17) inch sheets.

PB13-5-2. Utility alignment plan and as-built drawing. At a minimum the utility alignment plan and post construction as-built drawing shall contain the following:

A map of existing site conditions showing the site and immediately adjacent areas within one hundred (100) feet, and including:

(a) The names, addresses, telephone numbers, and fax numbers of: the applicant, owner, engineer and contact person.

(b) A north point oriented either up or to the right, date and scale of drawing and number of sheets.

(c) Property parcel lines.

(d) Information regarding the names and numbers of adjoining roads, railroads, utilities, subdivisions, towns and districts or other landmarks.

(e) Location and indication of existing structures, fences, sidewalks, roadways, lights of other park equipment.

(f) Location and indication of demolition, relocation, or abandonment of existing structures.

(g) Existing underground and overhead utilities, easements and rights-of-way.

(h) A delineation of all streams, rivers, ponds, public waters and wetlands.

(i) Vegetative cover such as brush, grass and trees, and clearly delineating any vegetation proposed for removal.

(j) The proposed, or as-built utility alignment, location and elevations, and identification of infrastructure including junction boxes manholes or other installed equipment.

(k) Locations and dimensions of all construction-site erosion control measures.

(l) Schedule of anticipated starting and completion date of each land disturbing activity.

(m) Any other information pertinent to the project, which in the opinion of the applicant or the Parks Engineer is necessary for the review of the project. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-6.
children.title: Permit Approval
children.text:
PB13-6-1. Process. Utility encroachment applications and alignment plans meeting the requirements of Sections 13-6 and 13-7 of this chapter shall be submitted by the Parks Engineer to the Board for review in accordance with the standards of this chapter. The Board shall have the authority to:

(a) Approve,

(b) Approve with conditions,

(c) Ask for additional information, or

(d) Deny the utility alignment plan and utility encroachment permit.

PB13-6-2. Duration. Approval of a utility alignment plan submitted under the provisions of this chapter shall expire one (1) year after the date of approval unless construction has commenced in accordance with the plan.

PB13-6-3. Conditions. A utility alignment plan may be approved subject to compliance with conditions reasonable and necessary to insure that the requirements contained in this chapter are met. Such conditions may, among other matters, limit the size, kind or character of the proposed encroachment, require the construction of structures, landscaping, drainage facilities, and other facilities, require replacement of vegetation, establish required monitoring procedures, stage the work over time, require alteration of the site design to insure buffering.

PB13-6-4. Insurance. Prior to approval of any utility alignment plan, the applicant shall submit proof of liability insurance. Insurance amount limits shall be in accordance with current MPRB standards. The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board must be explicitly named as additionally insured on the certificate.

PB13-6-5. Performance bond. Prior to approval of any utility alignment plan, the applicant shall submit an agreement to comply with such conditions as may have been agreed to. Such agreement shall be accompanied by a bond to cover the amount of the established cost of complying with the agreement. The agreement and bond shall guarantee completion and compliance with conditions within a specific time. The adequacy, conditions and acceptability of any agreement and bond shall be determined by the Board or any official of the Board as may be designated by the Board.

PB13-6-6. As-built drawing. The applicant shall provide the Parks Engineer with an as-built drawing showing the constructed locations and elevations of all installed equipment along with the information required in Section 13-5-2. The performance bond shall be held until the Parks Engineer has approved the as-built drawing.

PB13-6-7. Approval standards. No utility encroachment permit which fails to meet the standards contained in this Section shall be approved by the Board.

PB13-6-7-1. Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Land Policy. MPRB Policy XV Section A, Encroachments on Park Lands shall be adhered to:

A. Encroachments on Park Lands. The Board strongly opposes diversion of park property by any individual, institution or organization, public or private, for any purpose other than that for which the lands were acquired. Where proposed diversions of park property appear to be in the best interest of the Park System or where all other alternatives have been exhausted, and only under these conditions, requests will be taken under consideration by the Board on an individual basis.

In those instances where the Board determines that encroachment on park property may be necessary, easements or permits will be granted which include the following requirements:

A.1

To the greatest extent possible, intrusion will be limited to the periphery of park property, must be unobtrusive in nature, and must minimize the amount of damage to the landscape.

A.2

Restoration of any physical or natural property removed or damaged, or equivalent monetary compensation provided.

A.3

Compensation shall reflect the impact of the intrusion on aesthetic and recreational values of parkland.

PB13-6-7-2. Permit agreement required. To assure compliance with the above policy, a permit agreement signed by the applicant which includes compensation per Section 13-7 for the impact of the encroachment on Park aesthetics, recreational values and staff resources is required. The agreement shall be compiled by the Board's attorney and approved by the Board.

PB13-6-7-3. Site erosion control. Erosion control measures specified in the utility alignment plan must meet all City of Minneapolis, State of Minnesota or Watershed District requirements.

PB13-6-7-4. Wetlands. Plans must meet all Minnesota Wetland Conservation Act requirements for wetland impacts.

PB13-6-7-5. Inspection and maintenance. All utility facilities on Park property shall be designed to minimize the need of maintenance, to provide access for maintenance purposes and to be structurally sound. All utility facilities shall have a plan of operation and maintenance that assures minimum maintenance.

PB13-6-7-6. Other permits or approvals. The applicant shall obtain all permits and approvals required by the City, the State, or other agency and provide copies of permits or written permissions to the Board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-7.
children.title: Utility Encroachment Fees
children.text:
PB13-7-1. Utility encroachment fee established. The Board does hereby establish the utility encroachment fee for the purpose of managing Board-owned property, recouping administrative staff time, and compensating for the impacts of utility encroachment on Park aesthetics and recreational values. The fee is effective the date of adoption of this Ordinance.

PB13-7-2. Operation and Administration. The operation and administration of the Utility encroachment fee will be the responsibility of Board designated MPRB staff.

PB13-7-3. Rules and Regulations. Establishment of operational standards, fees and other rules and regulations established for the purpose of operating this utility encroachment fee are established in the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Utility Encroachment Fee Policy which is adopted here by reference and may be amended by Board resolution as is deemed necessary by the Board.

PB13-7-4. Fees. All applications for utility encroachment permit approval shall be accompanied by a processing fee determined by the Utility Encroachment Fee Policy. An applicant shall also be required to pay a yearly permit fee as per the Utility Encroachment Fee Policy as part of a permit, or other agreement as approved by the Board.

PB13-7-5. Waiver. The Board may waive a utility encroachment fee where it deems it in the best interests of the Park System. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-8.
children.title: Penalty
children.text:
(a) Violation of any provision of this chapter is a misdemeanor.

(b) Board may issue a stop work order halting all construction work, grading, land disturbing activity and/or building construction for noncompliance with this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-9.
children.title: Other Controls
children.text: In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this chapter and the provisions of any other Ordinance adopted by the Board, the more restrictive standard prevails. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13-10.
children.title: Severability
children.text: The provisions of this chapter are severable. If any provision of this chapter or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Chapter, which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2002-101, § 1, 6-12-02)

children.heading: PB13.5-1.
children.title: Purpose
children.text: The Board of Commissioners of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board (hereinafter referred to as "park board") anticipated the increase in requests for non-park uses of land in their stated land policy. The purpose of this chapter is to effectively administrate requests for access for non-park uses that impact parkways or park land. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-2.
children.title: Scope and effect
children.text: Unless otherwise provided in the park board ordinances, temporary access permits are required for any non-park or construction related use of parkways or land owned or leased by the park board. Construction related use means the use of parkways or park land to access a project site on non-park land. Every applicant for a permit under this chapter must submit an application to the assistant superintendent of planning of the park board. The assistant superintendent of planning will review the application to determine if the requirements under this chapter are met prior to granting a temporary access permit. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-3.
children.title: Exemptions
children.text: Approved park board projects are exempt from this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-4.
children.title: Application procedure
children.text:
A written application for permit approval under this chapter must be filed with the assistant superintendent of planning for the park board. All applicants for a construction access permit shall provide the information required on the park board's application for construction permit form. In addition, if not already provided on an application for construction permit form, applications shall provide the following information:

a. The names, addresses, telephone numbers, and fax numbers of the following as applicable: the applicant, owner, organization, contact person, and project manager and engineer.

b. The nature, character, and location of the parkway(s) or park board land for which access is requested.

c. Schedule of anticipated starting and completion date of access to the parkway(s) or park board land.

d. A description and weight of all equipment or materials to be brought onto parkway(s) or park board land.

e. Any other information pertinent to the project, which in the opinion of the assistant superintendent of planning is necessary for the review of the project. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-5.
children.title: Permit approval
children.text:
The park board designates and authorizes its assistant superintendent of planning to approve temporary access permits that satisfy the requirements of this chapter and do not exceed one hundred eighty (180) days. The assistant superintendent of planning will have the authority to:

a. Approve,

b. Approve with conditions,

c. Require additional information for review,

d. Submit the application to the park board for review, consideration, and recommendation, or

e. Deny the permit application.

All temporary access permits approved by the assistant superintendent of planning under this chapter must be reported to the park board within a reasonable time after the date of issuance of the permit but no longer than one (1) month from that date. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-6.
children.title: Duration
children.text: All temporary access permits approved under this chapter must define the authorized time for access and use of parkways or park board property, and in no case will the time exceed one hundred eighty (180) days without express prior approval of the park board. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-7.
children.title: Conditions
children.text: The assistant superintendent of planning for the park board may require a construction or use plan prior to approval of a permit under this chapter. If required, a plan will be subject to the conditions reasonable and necessary to insure that the requirements contained in this chapter are met. Such conditions may, among other matters, limit the size, kind or character of the proposed construction access or use, require conditions on the use of structures or materials, landscaping, drainage facilities, and other facilities, require the replacement of vegetation, establish monitoring procedures, provide a schedule of work reasonably calculated to comply any plan and chapter requirements, and any other conditions the assistant superintendent of planning may require. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-8.
children.title: Insurance
children.text: Prior to approval of any temporary access permit under this chapter, the applicant shall submit proof of liability insurance. Insurance amount limits must be in accordance with standards acceptable to the assistant superintendent of planning for the park board. The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board must be explicitly named as additionally insured on the certificate. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-9.
children.title: Performance bond/letter of credit
children.text: The assistant superintendent of planning for the park board may require a performance bond or letter of credit prior to the approval of any permit under this chapter. If required, the applicant will submit an agreement subject to the conditions required by the assistant superintendent of planning of the park board for the approval of the temporary access permit. Such agreement must be accompanied by a performance bond or letter of credit to cover the amount the assistant superintendent of planning of the park board will establish to comply with the agreement. The agreement must guarantee completion and compliance with the schedule and conditions predetermined by the assistant superintendent of planning for the park board. The adequacy, conditions, and acceptability of any agreement, performance bond, or letter of credit shall be subject to the complete discretion of the assistant superintendent of planning for the park board. The park board authorizes its assistant superintendent of planning to enter into any agreement under this section without prior approval of the park board. Any performance bond or letter of credit agreement required under this section will be incorporated by reference into the approved temporary access permit for the use of parkways or park property. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-10.
children.title: Approval standards
children.text: No permit under this chapter will be approved that fails to meet the conditions under this chapter and any other conditions required by the assistant superintendent of planning under this chapter except for any access and use that is for an emergency purpose as defined under this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-11.
children.title: Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Policy
children.text:
A. The park board strongly opposes diversion of park property by any individual, institution or organization, public or private, for any purpose other than that for which the property were acquired. Where proposed construction access or other uses of park property are not in conflict with the best interests of the park system and where all other alternatives have been exhausted, applications submitted under this chapter will be considered subject to the following general policy statements:

1. To the greatest extent possible, intrusion will be limited to the periphery of park property, be as unobtrusive a possible in nature, and minimize the damage and alteration of the landscape or parkways.

2. To the greatest extent possible any alteration or damage to park property or parkways must be restored to the requirements of the assistant superintendent of planning for the park board. If damage or alteration of park property or parkways cannot be restored, equivalent monetary compensation must be provided.

3. Compensation shall reflect the impact of the intrusion on aesthetic and recreational values of the park property or parkways involved.

B. The Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board institutes this chapter to address the numerous and diverse requests for limited access for construction related use and other uses of its property that it receives on a day to day basis. The authority vested in its assistant superintendent of planning under this chapter is to provide for the efficient and reasonable response to these requests without the prior approval of the park board. The park board shall review all approved permits under this chapter to insure that access authorized by its assistant superintendent of planning complies with the intent of this policy within a reasonable time after the date of issuance of the permit but no longer than one (1) months from that date. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-12.
children.title: Compliance with federal, state and local laws
children.text: No permit under this chapter shall be approved if the construction or use of park property will be in violation of any federal, state, or local laws, ordinances, and rules, and no permit shall be approved prior to the granting of any required additional federal, state, or local agency permit(s). (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-13.
children.title: Permit fees
children.text: The park board does hereby establish a permit fee schedule under this chapter for the purpose of managing park property, recouping administrative staff time, and compensation for the impacts on the aesthetic and recreational value of park property or parkways. The assistant superintendent of planning for the park board shall submit to the park board for approval a temporary access permit fee schedule to be administered under this chapter. The temporary access permit fee schedule may be revised at any time subject to the approval of the park board. All application for temporary access permits under this chapter must be accompanied by a processing fee as provided for by the temporary access permit fee schedule. The park board authorizes and designates its assistant superintendent of planning with the responsibility to insure compliance of with the temporary access permit fee schedule by all applicants under this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-14.
children.title: Waiver
children.text: A temporary access permit fee may be waived by the assistant superintendent of planning for the park board under this chapter where it is deemed in the best interests of the park system. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-15.
children.title: Penalty
children.text:
(a) Violation of any provision of this chapter is a misdemeanor.

(b) Board may issue a stop work order halting all construction work, or any other use for noncompliance with this chapter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-16.
children.title: Other controls
children.text: In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this chapter and the provisions of any other ordinance adopted by the board, the more restrictive standard prevails. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-17.
children.title: Severability
children.text: The provisions of this chapter are severable. If any provision of this chapter or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this chapter, which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB13.5-18.
children.title: Emergency powers
children.text: The board designates and authorizes its superintendent to act with the authority provided under this chapter in response to an emergency that, without such action by the superintendent, detrimental harm to either the public interest or property of the board could not be avoided. The superintendent upon invoking this emergency power shall report to the board at his/her earliest opportunity of such emergency action. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2011-101, § 1, 1-5-11)

children.heading: PB14-1.
children.title: Definitions
children.text: An administrative offense is a violation of a provision of this Code when one commits a prohibited act or fails to act in compliance with this Code. Persons who commit an administrative offense are subject to the administrative penalties set forth in the schedule of offenses and penalties referred to in PB14-6 hereinafter. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2006-101, § 1, 5-3-06)

children.heading: PB14-2.
children.title: Notice
children.text: Any officer of the Minneapolis Park Police and any Park Patrol Agent employed by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board having authority to enforce this Code, shall, upon determining that there has been a violation, notify the violator, or in the case of a vehicular violation, attach to the vehicle a notice of the violation. Said notice shall set forth the nature, date and time of the violation, the name of the official issuing the notice, and the amount of the proscribed penalty. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2006-101, § 1, 5-3-06)

children.heading: PB14-3.
children.title: Payment
children.text: Once such notice is given, the person responsible for the violation shall, within seven (7) days of the time of issuance of the notice, make payment in full of the amount stated on the notice of violation to the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board Finance Department. Payment shall be admission of the violation. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2006-101, § 1, 5-3-06)

children.heading: PB14-4.
children.title: Failure to Pay
children.text: If a violator fails to pay the penalty imposed by this section, violation may be recharged as a petty misdemeanor, misdemeanor or other applicable code violation. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2006-101, § 1, 5-3-06)

children.heading: PB14-5.
children.title: Disposition of Penalties
children.text: All penalties collected pursuant to this chapter shall be paid to the Park Board's Finance Department and be deposited into the General Fund of the Park Board or such other special fund as the Board may designate. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2006-101, § 1, 5-3-06)

children.heading: PB14-6.
children.title: Offenses and Penalties
children.text: Offenses which may be charged as administrative offenses and the penalties for such offenses may be established by resolution of the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board from time to time. Copies of such resolutions shall be maintained in the office of the Superintendent. (Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2006-101, § 1, 5-3-06)

children.heading: Chapter 15
children.title: PARKLAND DEDICATION
children.text:
Footnotes:  --- (14) ---

Editor's note— Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-103, § 1, adopted July 11, 2007, amended the Code by adding provisions designated as a new Ch. 14. Inasmuch as there already exists provisions so designated, Pk. Bd. Ord. 2007-103 has been included herein as a new Ch. 15 at the discretion of the editor. Subsequently, Pk. Bd. Ord. 2010-Or-101, § 1, adopted July 1, 2010, repealed former Ch. 15 and enacted provisions designated as a new Ch. 15 to read as herein set out. Prior to inclusion of said ordinance, Ch. 15 pertained to park dedication. See also the Park Board Code Comparative Table.

children.heading: PB15-1.
children.title: Findings and purpose
children.text:
The City Council of the City of Minneapolis and the Park and Recreation Board of the City of Minneapolis jointly find that the preservation and development of parks, playgrounds, recreational facilities, wetlands, trails, and open space areas within the city are essential to maintaining a healthy and desirable environment for residents and persons employed within the city. The value and attractiveness of residential, commercial, and industrial developments to land owners, developers, purchasers, employers, and employees is significantly enhanced by the presence of park and open space amenities.

The city council and park and recreation board find that the development of land for new residential, commercial, and industrial purposes creates a need for park and recreational land and facilities within the city that exceeds current park resources. The city council and park and recreation board find that:

(1) The National Recreation and Parks Association's guidelines for park system planning are that neighborhood parks have a service area between one-quarter (¼ to one-half (½) mile and that the service area for community parks is between one-half (½) to three (3) miles.

(2) The Urban Land Institute's guidelines have a one-half (½) mile service radius for neighborhood parks and a two (2) mile service radius for community parks.

(3) One (1) of the stated goals of the park board's comprehensive park system plan is to "ensure park access for all residents by providing parks within an easy walk from their homes (no more than six (6) blocks) and achieving a ratio of .01 acres of parkland per household."

(4) The city's current neighborhood and community parks consist of one thousand seven hundred twenty-nine (1,729) acres.

(5) The metropolitan council has projected that by the year 2040, forty-six thousand three hundred and sixty (46,360) new households will be added to the city creating a demand for an additional four hundred sixty-four (464) acres of neighborhood and community parkland.

(6) The metropolitan council projects net new job growth of one hundred thirty-seven thousand three hundred sixty-eight (137,368) by the year 2040, which would create an additional need for three hundred eleven (311) acres of parkland.

It is both appropriate and reasonable that new development contribute to addressing this systemic need in rough proportion to the relative burden it will place upon existing park resources. Park dedication requirements are based on the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board's standard of .01 acres per household for neighborhood and community parks. The average household size for the city as a whole is 2.25 persons per household. The average household size for neighborhoods in the downtown area is smaller with an average household size of 1.48 persons or sixty-six (66) percent of the city's average household size. Parkland dedication for residential development within the downtown area shall be based on sixty-six (66) percent of the land area as that required for the remainder of the city.

Further recognizing that employees of commercial and industrial land uses place demands on parks, albeit to a lower extent than residents, park land dedication for commercial and industrial development is based on one-half (½) the rate of .01 acres per household required for residential uses divided by the average 2.25 persons per household resulting in one hundred (100) square feet per employee.

The city council and park and recreation board find that the requirements of this ordinance are in accordance with the parks and open space goals and policies of the comprehensive plan and park system plan, and are proportionate, fair, and reasonable with respect to the park land and facilities need generated by new development occurring within the city. (2009-Or-030, § 1, 4-10-09; 2010-Or-081, § 1, 9-24-10; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2013-103, § 1, 12-18-13)

children.heading: PB15-2.
children.title: Authority
children.text: Pursuant to Laws of Minnesota 2006, Chapter 269, Laws of Minnesota 2008, Chapter 331, Laws of Minnesota 2008, Chapter 366, Laws of Minnesota 2013, Chapter 85, and other powers granted by law, the city and park and recreation board are jointly authorized to require that a reasonable portion of any new residential, commercial, and industrial development be dedicated to the public for public use as parks, playgrounds, recreational facilities, wetlands, trails, or open space areas, and that the city and park and recreation board may alternatively accept an equivalent amount in cash. (2009-Or-030, § 1, 4-10-09; 2010-Or-081, § 2, 9-24-10; Pk. Bd. Ord. No. 2013-103, § 1, 12-18-13)

children.heading: PB15-3.
children.title: Definitions
children.text:
The following terms whenever used in this article shall have the following respective meanings:

Affordable housing units means:

(1) Residential dwelling units financed in whole or in part by a local, state, or federal government entity for the purpose of creating housing affordable to and occupied by households earning sixty (60) percent or less of the median family income for the Minneapolis/St. Paul metropolitan statistical area, as adjusted for family size;

(2) Residential dwelling units in a project financed in whole or in part by a local, state, or federal government entity for the purpose of creating affordable housing where one hundred (100) percent of the housing project meets the requirements for income averaging under Section 42(g)(1)(c) of the Internal Revenue Code resulting in an average rent for all units in the project that does not exceed sixty (60) percent of Metropolitan Median Income (MMI); or

(3) Residential dwelling units in a project that are affordable to and occupied by households earning sixty (60) percent or less of the MMI as a result of compliance with Minneapolis Code of Ordinances, Article XIV, Inclusionary Housing.

City means the City of Minneapolis.

City staff means the appropriate department head or person designated by that department head to carry out a specific duty or function designated by this ordinance.

Community park means a public park that is a minimum of six (6) acres in size serving the community that may include more specialized or unique features that are not typically provided in a neighborhood park.

Comprehensive plan means the Comprehensive Plan of the City of Minneapolis.

Developer means any person, firm, corporation, sole proprietorship or partnership who seeks to improve property in a manner that would result in a net increase in the number of residential dwelling units on the property or create or expand a commercial or industrial use on the property, and includes any property owner or subdivider of the land. This definition does not include governmental units.

Development employees refers to the approximate number of new or additional employees that will result from the proposed commercial or industrial development or expansion and is equal to the product of (1) the number of square feet of floor area of the new structural improvements in the proposed commercial or industrial development or expansion divided by one thousand (1,000) (or for hotels, the number of hotel rooms) and (2) the average number of employees per one thousand (1,000) square feet of floor area of the proposed type of development (or for hotels, the average number of employees per hotel room) based on data maintained by the department of community planning and economic development. Any conversion of existing commercial or industrial space from one (1) type of use to another that does not result in any additional square footage of usable space shall not result in any new development employees.

Development site refers to a plot of land that is intended or suitable for a proposed servicing of unimproved land or the improvement of previously developed land and for which there is the proposed construction of new buildings or renovation or significant change of existing buildings to accommodate a new land use or increased density of a land use and for which planning approvals are required. Development site does not include an expansion to an existing commercial or industrial building that is less than five thousand (5,000) square feet or the construction of a new commercial or industrial building that is less than five thousand (5,000) square feet.

Downtown area means the geographic area of the city bounded by Interstate 35W, Interstate 94, Plymouth Avenue, and the Mississippi River.
